title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄序
上萬曆之七年天下復當大比士
於鄉巡按陝西監察御史張
〔憲翔〕銜
上命晨夜馳入關無何迫試事乃
以前御史沈〔涵〕禮聘學正〔宗〕
〔湯〕教諭王〔居仁〕爲考試官學
===
正劉〔淑唐〕教諭涂〔案〕方〔思賢〕
薛〔彥卿〕訓導石〔珮〕賔〔中孚〕爲
同考試官提調則左布政使
朱〔炳如〕右布政使張〔國彥〕監
試則副使李〔時漸〕王〔體復〕諸
執事靡弗慎擇充者於是合
河西巡按御史趙〔楫〕提學副
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄序
上萬曆之七年，天下復當大比士於鄉。巡按陝西監察御史張〔憲翔〕銜上命，晨夜馳入關。無何，迫試事，乃以前御史沈〔涵〕禮，聘學正〔宗〕〔湯〕、教諭王〔居仁〕爲考試官，學正劉〔淑唐〕、教諭涂〔案〕、方〔思賢〕、薛〔彥卿〕、訓導石〔珮〕、賔〔中孚〕爲同考試官。提調則左布政使朱〔炳如〕、右布政使張〔國彥〕，監試則副使李〔時漸〕、王〔體復〕，諸執事靡弗慎擇充者。於是合河西巡按御史趙〔楫〕、提學副…
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the seventh year of His Majesty's Wanli reign (1579), it was once again the time for the Empire to hold the great triennial selection of scholars in the provinces. The Regional Inspector of Shaanxi and Investigating Censor Zhang Xianxiang 張憲翔, bearing His Majesty's command, rode day and night into the Passes. Before long, as the examination affairs pressed near, in accordance with the courteous invitations issued by the former Censor Shen Han 沈涵, he engaged the Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies [?] Zong Tang 宗湯 and the County Director of Studies Wang Juren 王居仁 as Examiners, and the Director of Studies Liu Shutang 劉淑唐, the County Directors of Studies Tu An 涂案, Fang Sixian 方思賢, and Xue Yanqing 薛彥卿, and the Assistant Instructors Shi Pei 石珮 and Bin Zhongfu 賔中孚 as Associate Examiners. Serving as Proctors were the Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhu Bingru 朱炳如 and the Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Guoyan 張國彥; serving as Monitoring Officials were the Surveillance Vice Commissioners Li Shijian 李時漸 and Wang Tifu 王體復; and all the other functionaries were carefully chosen to fill their posts. Thereupon, combining the scholars selected by the Hexi Regional Inspector and Censor Zhao Ji 趙楫 and the Education-intendant Surveillance Vice…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
使李〔維楨〕所選士一千九百
有奇三試之遵
制額舉六十五人錄其氏名若
文以
獻〔宗湯〕宜序首簡蓋漢人之言
曰秦形勝之國也帶河阻山
縣隔千里持戟百萬秦得百
二焉秦之雄於天下自古記
之矣〔宗湯〕則請言
===
今日自
國家建都于燕俯而臨天下如
北辰然分野萬里郡縣星列
天下有相制之形而無偏重
之處秦雖大直當之一隅安
punctuated: 使李〔維楨〕所選士一千九百有奇，三試之，遵制額舉六十五人，錄其氏名若文以獻。〔宗湯〕宜序首簡。蓋漢人之言曰：「秦，形勝之國也，帶河阻山，縣隔千里，持戟百萬，秦得百二焉。」秦之雄於天下，自古記之矣。〔宗湯〕則請言今日。自國家建都于燕，俯而臨天下，如北辰然，分野萬里，郡縣星列，天下有相制之形，而無偏重之處。秦雖大，直當之一隅，安
translation_en:
… [Education-intendant Vice] Commissioner Li Weizhen 李維楨, numbering over one thousand nine hundred in all, and tested them in three sessions. In compliance with the statutory quota, sixty-five men were selected as provincial graduates, and their surnames and personal names, together with their essays, have been recorded for presentation to the throne. It falls to me, [Li] Zongtang 李宗湯, to write the preface for the opening pages.

Now, a man of the Han dynasty once said: "Qin is a state of strategic terrain. Girdled by the Yellow River and shielded by mountains, it is suspended a thousand li apart; among a million halberd-bearers, two percent of Qin's match a hundred percent of the other states'." That Qin held supremacy over the realm has been recorded since antiquity. Yet I, Zongtang, beg leave to speak of the present day. Ever since our Dynasty established its capital at Yan, looking down to rule over the realm like the Pole Star, with its allotted territories stretching ten thousand li and its commanderies and counties arrayed like stars, the realm has possessed a configuration of mutual checks and balances, with no region holding disproportionate weight. Vast though Qin is, it merely constitutes a single corner; how…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
所名其雄乎秦不能以其大
而雄天下則將奚以夫人固
有以地重地亦有以人重必
得士焉與天下絜長比大而
秦得百二而後可也今夫天
下非小狹也秦士非益多而
天下非少也有人於此遽而
===
號於衆曰秦之士與天下之
士絜長比大而得百二衆有
不失笑者乎〔宗湯〕請譬之鄧
林之植也不必皆干霄拂雲
蔽青天而蔭原畝之木也然
而求干霄拂雲蔽青天而蔭
原畝之木非鄧林無有也燕
punctuated: 所名其雄乎？秦不能以其大而雄天下，則將奚以？夫人固有以地重，地亦有以人重，必得士焉，與天下絜長比大，而秦得百二，而後可也。今夫天下非小狹也，秦士非益多而天下非少也；有人於此，遽而號於衆曰：「秦之士與天下之士絜長比大而得百二。」衆有不失笑者乎？〔宗湯〕請譬之：鄧林之植也，不必皆干霄拂雲、蔽青天而蔭原畝之木也；然而求干霄拂雲、蔽青天而蔭原畝之木，非鄧林無有也。燕
translation_en: …can it claim its preeminence? If Qin cannot be preeminent in the empire by virtue of its size, then by what means shall it be so? Now, just as men are certainly esteemed because of their land, a land is also esteemed because of its men. It must obtain scholars who, when measuring excellence and comparing greatness with the rest of the empire, give Qin a two-to-a-hundred advantage—only then will it suffice. Now, the empire is not small or narrow, nor are the scholars of Qin increasingly numerous while those of the empire are few. Suppose someone here were suddenly to proclaim to the multitude: "When the scholars of Qin measure excellence and compare greatness with the scholars of the empire, they hold a two-to-a-hundred advantage!" Would anyone in the multitude not burst out laughing? I, [Zongtang], beg to illustrate this with an analogy. Among the trees of the Forest of Deng (Denglin), not all are necessarily trees that pierce the sky and brush the clouds, blotting out the blue heavens and shading the plains and fields; yet if one seeks trees that pierce the sky and brush the clouds, blotting out the blue heavens and shading the plains and fields, they are to be found nowhere if not in the Forest of Deng. Among the [horses] of Yan…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
代之馬不必皆追風掣電一
日而千里然脫有追風掣電
一日而千里者必燕代馬也
秦亦士之鄧林之圃而燕代
之野也渠寧無士昔人之論
曰才過千人謂之豪過萬人
謂之傑夫此一人耳而才度
===
越千萬人則豪傑之名歸焉
矣豪傑之士雖無文王猶興
矧生於文王之鄉而爲思皇
之遺者乎方今
神聖在御日出之地光耀明德治
登乎大猷唯是勸學育才招
延茂異勤於中懷誠幾得豪
punctuated: 代之馬，不必皆追風掣電、一日而千里；然脫有追風掣電、一日而千里者，必燕、代馬也。秦亦士之鄧林之圃，而燕、代之野也，渠寧無士？昔人之論曰：「才過千人謂之豪，過萬人謂之傑。」夫此一人耳，而才度越千萬人，則豪傑之名歸焉矣。豪傑之士，雖無文王猶興，矧生於文王之鄉，而爲思皇之遺者乎？方今神聖在御，日出之地，光耀明德，治登乎大猷，唯是勸學育才，招延茂異，勤於中懷，誠幾得豪
translation_en: … and Dai need not all be steeds that chase the wind and flash like lightning, covering a thousand li in a single day; yet if there happens to be one that chases the wind and flashes like lightning, covering a thousand li in a single day, it will surely be a horse of Yan or Dai. Qin, too, is for scholars what the groves of Denglin and the plains of Yan and Dai are—how could it possibly lack scholars? An ancient saying goes: "One whose talent surpasses a thousand men is called a hero (hao); one who surpasses ten thousand is called a champion (jie)." Now, this is but a single man, yet because his talent far transcends that of thousands or tens of thousands, the title of hero and champion goes to him. Scholars who are heroes and champions rise up even without a King Wen; how much more so those born in the homeland of King Wen, who are the remnant legatees of the "magnificent multitudes" [celebrated in the Odes]? At the present time, a divine sage is on the throne; to the places where the sun rises, his illustrious virtue shines forth, and governance has ascended to the great plan. Only this—encouraging learning and nurturing talent, inviting and welcoming the flourishing and extraordinary—occupies his innermost thoughts, as he earnestly hopes to obtain heroic…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
傑之士而用之士誰有不敬
應者乎秦渠寧無士蓋〔宗湯〕
之初應聘而來也私覩夫挾
策懷器雲翔而待校於車下
者無慮數千百人也進而觀
其所爲文辭陳之以疑以觀
其學雜設之事以觀其才紛
===
難之以觀其識漫引之以觀
其守旁詰射之以觀其辯如
此而不失得六十五人而止
爾夫此六十五人者一旦而
穎脫於數千百人之上若所
謂豪傑云者而言者曰是不
離爾之鄉爾早暮績食偕計
punctuated: 傑之士而用之，士誰有不敬應者乎？秦渠寧無士？蓋〔宗湯〕之初應聘而來也，私覩夫挾策懷器、雲翔而待校於車下者，無慮數千百人也。進而觀其所爲文辭：陳之以疑以觀其學，雜設之事以觀其才，紛難之以觀其識，漫引之以觀其守，旁詰射之以觀其辯。如此而不失，得六十五人而止爾。夫此六十五人者，一旦而穎脫於數千百人之上，若所謂豪傑云者，而言者曰：「是不離爾之鄉爾。」早暮績食偕計，
translation_en: …outstanding men and employ them, what scholar would not reverently respond? How could Qin have no scholars? Indeed, when I, [Zongtang], first arrived in response to the invitation to serve, I privately observed those clasping their books and harboring their talents, gathering like clouds to await examination beneath my carriage—there were easily several thousand or hundred men. Advancing to examine the essays they composed, we presented them with doubtful points to observe their learning, set forth miscellaneous affairs to observe their talent, confounded them with difficulties to observe their insight, drew them out broadly to observe their moral constancy, and questioned and probed them from all sides to observe their powers of argumentation. Tested thus without failing, we obtained sixty-five men and no more. Now, these sixty-five men have in a single day stood out sharp and clear above several thousand or hundred men, just like those who are called outstanding heroes; yet some might say: "This is merely without leaving your own home province." Soon, supplied with provisions to travel with the local tribute reports…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
與四方名下之士角於春官
更進而踐
文石履
赤墀奉
臨軒之制對稱曰予大夫也當此
之時不佞卽不敢過望爾人
人而舉顧豈無絕塵而奔者
===
於其間乎有之謂足當豪傑
非耶而言者又曰是藝止爾
可以爲先資而未可以成信
則所爲豪傑者大略可覩矣
太上立德其次立功其次立
言周召尚矣自周而漢而唐
宋窺前聖之奧樹將相之勳
punctuated: 與四方名下之士角於春官，更進而踐文石、履赤墀，奉臨軒之制對，稱曰「予大夫也」。當此之時，不佞卽不敢過望爾人人而舉，顧豈無絕塵而奔者於其間乎？有之，謂足當豪傑，非耶？而言者又曰：「是藝止爾，可以爲先資，而未可以成信。」則所爲豪傑者，大略可覩矣。太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。周、召尚矣，自周而漢、而唐、宋，窺前聖之奧，樹將相之勳，
translation_en: …and compete at the Ministry of Rites against renowned scholars from all quarters; and advancing even further, tread upon the patterned stones, walk the crimson steps of the palace courtyard, and receive the Emperor's decree in person at the Palace Examination, responding as one whom the sovereign calls, "My grandee!" At that moment, although this unworthy one would not dare expect every single one of you to succeed, could it be that there are none among you who will gallop ahead, leaving the dust behind? If there are such men, would you not say that they are worthy of being called heroes? Yet critics will say again: "This is merely literary skill; it can serve as an initial credential to advance, but it is not enough to establish true trustworthiness." From this, what constitutes a true hero can be seen in general outline. The highest achievement is to establish virtue; the next is to establish功 [meritorious service]; and the next is to establish words. The Dukes of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) and Shao (Shaogong 召公) are of the highest antiquity; from the Zhou down through the Han, and to the Tang and Song, those who peered into the profundities of the former sages, established the meritorious achievements of generals and chief councilors,…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
富名山之藏者何可指數然
太半炳烺於爾秦之圖籍也
爾如不以豪傑自命則可如
以豪傑自命典刑具在奚所
擇而處焉夫遇
光華之旦圖不朽之業修此三
者故全也德不至而功立功
===
不至而言立隨性之所近而
務臻其極流聲無窮者名世
之軌也而總之不在名高而
在致實不在材具而在所養
爾多士勉矣氣欲完神欲定
心欲密才欲練措之為德行
發之為事業擬議之為變化
punctuated: 富名山之藏者，何可指數？然太半炳烺於爾秦之圖籍也。爾如不以豪傑自命則可；如以豪傑自命，典刑具在，奚所擇而處焉？夫遇光華之旦，圖不朽之業，修此三者，故全也。德不至而功立，功不至而言立，隨性之所近而務臻其極，流聲無窮者，名世之軌也。而總之，不在名高而在致實，不在材具而在所養。爾多士勉矣！氣欲完，神欲定，心欲密，才欲練，措之為德行，發之為事業，擬議之為變化，
translation_en: …and enriching the treasures of famous mountains—how could they all be counted on the fingers? Yet the greater half of them shine brilliantly in the records and registers of your Qin region. If you do not regard yourselves as heroes of outstanding talent, then let it be; if you do regard yourselves as heroes of outstanding talent, the exemplars are all here—which among them will you choose to abide in? Now, encountering this glorious dawn and planning for an imperishable enterprise, to cultivate all three of these is indeed perfection. If one does not reach the pinnacle of virtue yet establishes merit, or does not reach the pinnacle of merit yet establishes words—following what one's nature is closest to and striving to reach its utmost so as to leave a reputation without end—this is the path of those renowned in their generation. In sum, it lies not in lofty fame, but in attaining substance; not in mere talent and capability, but in what one nourishes within. Strive on, you many scholars! Your vital energy should be whole, your spirit settled, your mind meticulous, and your talent seasoned—applying them as moral conduct, manifesting them as achievements and enterprises, and deliberating upon them to effect transformation…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
則養盛而實至實至而名隨
之矣上之與周召爲徒次無
墜爾先哲之典刑矣先資成
信而不第爲一鄉士矣昔宋
太宗嘗言士非望拔十得五
得一二人亦可爲致理之具
蓋其難也宗湯不使業以爾
===
多士進多士寧無意乎俾談
者曰三秦豪傑唯爾多士曰
秦無人亦唯爾多士曰豪傑
則以一人而度越千萬人雖
謂秦士於天下得百二亦宜
曰無人則太華誠高洪河誠
深安所託其重于天下耶宗
punctuated: 則養盛而實至，實至而名隨之矣。上之與周、召爲徒，次無墜爾先哲之典刑矣，先資成信，而不第爲一鄉士矣。昔宋太宗嘗言：「士非望拔十得五，得一二人亦可爲致理之具。」蓋其難也。宗湯不使，業以爾多士進，多士寧無意乎？俾談者曰「三秦豪傑」，唯爾多士；曰「秦無人」，亦唯爾多士。曰「豪傑」，則以一人而度越千萬人，雖謂秦士於天下得百二亦宜；曰「無人」，則太華誠高、洪河誠深，安所託其重于天下耶？宗
translation_en: …then your cultivation will be abundant and the substance will be attained, and when the substance is attained, reputation will follow it. At the highest, you will be peers of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao; next, you will not let fall the exemplary models of your former worthies; you will establish trustworthiness in your initial pledge of service, and not merely be scholars of a single locality. In the past, Emperor Taizong of the Song once said: "With scholars, one does not hope to select ten and obtain five; if one obtains even one or two, they can still serve as instruments for bringing about order." Such is the difficulty! Unworthy [不使, for 不佞?] as I, Zongtang, am, I have already presented you many scholars for advancement—how could you many scholars not take this to heart? Whether commentators say "There are heroic talents in the Three Qin," it depends entirely on you many scholars; or whether they say "There are no men in Qin," it likewise depends entirely on you many scholars. If they say "heroic talents," then because a single man surpasses ten million men, even to say that the scholars of Qin possess a two-against-a-hundred advantage over the rest of the realm would be fitting. If they say "there are no men," then though Mount Taihua is truly lofty and the great Yellow River is truly deep, upon what could they entrust their weight in the realm? I, Zong[tang]…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
湯自度淺薄無以相長爾多
士第借形勝之輕重述才賢
之所產明
主上之至意闡豪傑之名實以與
爾多士勗焉多士耳目所覩
記至孰必有能辨此矣是舉
也總督軍務則兵部左侍郎
===
兼右僉都御史郜〔光先久弘〕
文德雅厲士習巡撫陝西地
方則右副都御史近陞戶部
右侍郎傅〔希摯〕風教淪浹今
右僉都御史李〔堯德〕聲猷夙
暨甘肅則兵部右侍郎兼右
僉都御史侯〔東萊〕寧夏則右
punctuated:
湯自度淺薄，無以相長爾多士，第借形勝之輕重，述才賢之所產，明主上之至意，闡豪傑之名實，以與爾多士勗焉。多士耳目所覩記至孰，必有能辨此矣。
是舉也，總督軍務則兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史郜〔光先久弘〕文德，雅厲士習；巡撫陝西地方則右副都御史、近陞戶部右侍郎傅〔希摯〕風教淪浹，今右僉都御史李〔堯德〕聲猷夙暨；甘肅則兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史侯〔東萊〕，寧夏則右
translation_en:
… [Zong]tang, measuring my own shallowness, know that I have nothing with which to foster the growth of you many scholars. I merely draw upon the relative weight of strategic terrain, recount the lands that have produced men of talent and worth, make clear the supreme intent of His Majesty the Sovereign, and elucidate the name and reality of true heroes, so as to encourage you many scholars. What you many scholars have witnessed and remembered with your own eyes and ears is thoroughly familiar to you, and surely there are those among you who can discern this.

In this undertaking: the Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, Left Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Gao [Guangxian 郜光先, who has long broadened] civil virtue and cultivated and spurred the habits of the literati; the Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief recently promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue Fu [Xizhi 傅希摯], whose moral teaching has deeply permeated the region, and the incumbent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li [Yaode 李堯德], whose reputation and statesmanship have long reached here; for Gansu, Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Hou [Donglai 侯東萊]; for Ningxia, Right…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
副都御史羅〔鳳翱〕延綏則右
副都御史宋〔守約〕撫治鄖陽
則先右副都御史徐〔學謨〕今
右僉都御史楊〔俊民〕綏宇右
文巡茶御史先李〔時成〕今羅
〔應鶴〕巡鹽御史先尹〔良任〕今
房〔寰〕秉憲作士而兵科都給
===
事中戴〔光啓〕奉
命閱視四鎮其以督餉至者則戶
部郎中譚〔啓〕高〔時〕其以使事
至者則尚寶司司丞沈〔玄華〕
工部主事王〔謙〕行人司行人
邢〔孔陽〕王〔世揚〕樂觀人文譽
髦感奮其綜理於外者右叅

translation_en: …Vice Censor-in-Chief Luo Feng'ao 羅鳳翱; for Yansui, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Shouyue 宋守約; and as Grand Coordinator for the Pacification and Governance of Yunyang, formerly Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Xuemo 徐學謨 and presently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Yang Junmin 楊俊民, who have pacified the territories and championed civil culture. The Tea-Control Censors, formerly Li Shicheng 李時成 and presently Luo Yinghe 羅應鶴, and the Salt-Control Censors, formerly Yin Liangren 尹良任 and presently Fang Huan 房寰, have upheld the Censorate's laws and encouraged the scholars. Meanwhile, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War Dai Guangqi 戴光啓 received the imperial command to inspect the four defense commands; those who arrived to supervise military supplies were Bureau Directors in the Ministry of Revenue Tan Qi 譚啓 and Gao Shi 高時; and those who arrived on imperial missions were Seal Office Vice Director Shen Xuanhua 沈玄華, Ministry of Works Secretary Wang Qian 王謙, and Messengers of the Messenger Office Xing Kongyang 邢孔陽 and Wang Shiyang 王世揚—all delighted in witnessing the flourishing of literary culture, inspiring the renowned talents to rouse themselves. As for those managing affairs outside the examination compound, Right Administration Vice…

Those who maintained security on the outside were Assistant Regional Commander (參將) He Ji 何極, and Acting Assistant Commissioners-in-Chief of the Regional Military Commission (署都指揮僉事) Bian Yong 卞永, Xin Shouchen 辛守臣, and Zhao Jizu 趙繼祖. Meanwhile, Left Administration Vice Commissioner (左參政) Li Lin 李麟, Surveillance Vice Commissioner (副使) Li Guihe 李貴和, Vice Minister of the Branch Court of the Imperial Stud (行太僕寺少卿) Li Chengxuan 李承選, and Acting Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief of the Regional Military Commission (署都指揮僉事) Xu Deng[ying] 許登…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
瀛以先期按察使孫〔坤〕以先
任皆入賀
萬壽副使王〔湘〕以遷秩僉事咸〔懷〕
〔良〕以調任近方出關皆始事
有勞者得備書云
直隸滁州儒學學正任〔宗〕〔湯〕
謹序
punctuated:
瀛以先期、按察使孫〔坤〕以先任，皆入賀萬壽；副使王〔湘〕以遷秩、僉事咸〔懷〕〔良〕以調任，近方出關。皆始事有勞者，得備書云。
直隸滁州儒學學正任〔宗〕〔湯〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Ying 瀛 because of an earlier departure date, and Surveillance Commissioner Sun Kun 孫〔坤〕 because of a prior appointment, had all gone to court to offer congratulations on the Imperial Birthday; Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Xiang 王〔湘〕 because of a promotion in rank, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xian Huailiang 咸〔懷〕〔良〕 because of a transfer to another post, had recently just departed the pass. All of them having contributed their labor at the inception of the undertaking, it is fitting that they be recorded here in full.

Respectfully prefaced by Ren Zongtang 任〔宗〕〔湯〕, Confucian School Director of Chuzhou 滁州 in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸).

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰吾十有五而志于學三十而立四十
而不惑五十而知天命六十而耳順七
十而從心所欲不踰矩
苟不固聰明聖知達天德者其孰能知之
孟子曰禹惡旨酒而好善言湯執中立賢
無方文王視民如傷望道而未之見武
王不泄邇不忘遠周公思兼三王以施
四事其有不合者仰而思之夜以繼日
幸而得之坐以待旦
===
易
聖人作而萬物覩本乎天者親上本乎地
者親下則各從其類也
王假有家交相愛也
乾知大始坤作成物乾以易知坤以簡能
書
百官以治萬民以察
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
子曰：「吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。」
苟不固聰明聖知達天德者，其孰能知之？
孟子曰：「禹惡旨酒而好善言。湯執中，立賢無方。文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。周公思兼三王，以施四事；其有不合者，仰而思之，夜以繼日；幸而得之，坐以待旦。」

易
聖人作而萬物覩，本乎天者親上，本乎地者親下，則各從其類也。
王假有家，交相愛也。
乾知大始，坤作成物。乾以易知，坤以簡能。

書
百官以治，萬民以察。
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

The Master said: "At fifteen, I set my heart on learning; at thirty, I stood firm; at forty, I had no doubts; at fifty, I knew the decree of Heaven; at sixty, my ear was attuned; at seventy, I followed what my heart desired without transgressing the rule." (Analects 2.4)

Only he who is truly quick in apprehension, clear in discernment, of far-reaching intelligence and all-embracing knowledge, and who has attained to the virtue of Heaven—who else could know him? (Doctrine of the Mean 32)

Mencius said: "Yu hated fine wine and loved good words. Tang held fast to the Mean, and in establishing the worthy in office knew no bias. King Wen looked on the people as if they were wounded, and looked toward the Way as if he had not yet seen it. King Wu did not treat the near with familiarity and did not forget the distant. The Duke of Zhou sought to combine the virtues of the Three Kings in order to carry out these four courses of action. Whenever anything did not accord with them, he looked up and thought about it, continuing through the night what he had begun by day; and when he was fortunate enough to find the answer, he sat waiting for the dawn." (Mencius 4B.20)

Book of Changes (Yijing)

The sage arises and the myriad creatures behold him. What is rooted in heaven draws near to what is above; what is rooted in earth draws near to what is below: thus each follows its own kind. (Hexagram 1, Qian, Commentary on the Words of the Text)

"The king approaches his family": they love one another mutually. (Hexagram 37, Jiaren, Commentary on the Judgments)

Qian directs the great beginning; Kun brings things to completion. Qian knows through the easy; Kun is capable through the simple. (Appended Remarks, Part I, Chapter 1)

Book of Documents (Shujing)

By these all the officials are regulated, and the myriad people are clearly observed. ("Counsels of the Great Yu")

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
野無遺賢萬邦咸寧
有言逆于汝心必求諸道有言遜于汝志
必求諸非道
曰其稽我古人之德矧曰其有能稽謀自
天
小大之臣咸懷忠良其侍御僕從罔匪正
人以旦夕承弼厥辟
詩
南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子福履成之
===
靡室靡家玁狁之故不遑啓居玁狁之故
采薇采薇薇亦柔止曰歸曰歸心亦憂
止憂心烈烈載饑載渴我戍未定靡使
歸聘采薇采薇薇亦剛止曰歸曰歸歲
亦陽止王事靡盬不遑啓處憂心孔疚
我行不來
迺慰迺止迺左迺右迺疆迺理迺宣迺畝
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方
春秋
punctuated:
野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。
有言逆于汝心，必求諸道；有言遜于汝志，必求諸非道。
曰其稽我古人之德，矧曰其有能稽謀自天。
小大之臣，咸懷忠良；其侍御僕從，罔匪正人，以旦夕承弼厥辟。

《詩》
南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。
靡室靡家，玁狁之故；不遑啓居，玁狁之故。采薇采薇，薇亦柔止。曰歸曰歸，心亦憂止。憂心烈烈，載饑載渴。我戍未定，靡使歸聘。采薇采薇，薇亦剛止。曰歸曰歸，歲亦陽止。王事靡盬，不遑啓處。憂心孔疚，我行不來。
迺慰迺止，迺左迺右，迺疆迺理，迺宣迺畝。
儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。

《春秋》
translation_en:
"No worthy men were left neglected in the wilderness, and the myriad states all enjoyed peace."
"When you hear words that go against your heart, you must seek their basis in the Way; when you hear words that conform to your will, you must test whether they deviate from the Way."
"Not only may it be said that he examines the virtue of our ancients, how much more may it be said that he is able to examine counsels from Heaven."
"Let your ministers, great and small, all cherish loyalty and goodness; let your attendants, grooms, and followers all be upright men, so that morning and evening they may assist and correct their sovereign."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"In the south are trees with curving branches, and the creepers and vines twine round them. Happy be the lord, may happiness and dignity make him complete."
"We have no house, no home, because of the Xianyun; we have no leisure to kneel or sit at rest, because of the Xianyun. We gather the thorn-ferns, we gather the thorn-ferns; the thorn-ferns are tender now. We say, 'Let us return, let us return!' and our hearts are full of sorrow. Our sorrowing hearts burn fiercely; we are hungry, we are thirsty. Our garrison duty is not yet settled, and we have no one to send home to inquire after our families. We gather the thorn-ferns, we gather the thorn-ferns; the thorn-ferns are stiff now. We say, 'Let us return, let us return!' and the year is in its tenth month now. The king's business allows no slackening; we have no leisure to kneel or rest. Our sorrowing hearts are deeply pained; we marched forth and have not come back."
"So he comforted them, so he settled them; so he placed them on the left, so he placed them on the right; so he marked out the boundaries, so he divided the land; so he drained the soil, so he laid out the acres."
"Reverently take as pattern and model the statutes of King Wen, and daily pacify the four quarters."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
春正月己卯烝　夏五月丁丑烝〔桓公八〕
〔年〕
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
〔僖公元年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀〔僖公三年〕春王正月公會齊侯宋
公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰
遂伐楚次于陘　楚屈完來盟于師盟
于召陵　齊人執陳轅濤塗　秋及江
人黃人伐陳　冬十有二月公孫兹帥
===
師會齊人宋人衛人鄭人許人曹人侵
陳〔俱僖公四年〕
三月作丘甲〔成公元年〕春用田賦〔哀公十〕
〔有二年〕
春王正月季孫宿叔老會晉士匄齊人宋
人衛人鄭公孫蠆曹人莒人邾人滕人
薛人杞人小邾人會吳于向〔襄公十有〕
〔四年〕
禮記
punctuated:
春正月己卯，烝。夏五月丁丑，烝。〔桓公八年〕
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。〔僖公元年〕秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕春王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。齊人執陳轅濤塗。秋，及江人、黃人伐陳。冬十有二月，公孫兹帥師會齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭人、許人、曹人侵陳。〔俱僖公四年〕
三月，作丘甲。〔成公元年〕春，用田賦。〔哀公十有二年〕
春王正月，季孫宿、叔老會晉士匄、齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭公孫蠆、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人會吳于向。〔襄公十有四年〕
《禮記》
translation_en:
In spring, in the first month, on the jimao day, the winter sacrifice (zheng) was performed. In summer, in the fifth month, on the dingchou day, the winter sacrifice (zheng) was performed. [Eighth year of Duke Huan]
In the eighth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng. [First year of Duke Xi] In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, a representative of Jiang, and a representative of Huang met at Yanggu. [Third year of Duke Xi] In spring, in the King's first month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to make an incursion into Cai; Cai collapsed in rout, and they thereupon attacked Chu, halting at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the armies, and they covenanted at Shaoling. The people of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen. In autumn, together with representatives of Jiang and Huang, we attacked Chen. In winter, in the twelfth month, Gongsun Zi led a force to join representatives of Qi, Song, Wei, Zheng, Xu, and Cao to make an incursion into Chen. [All from the fourth year of Duke Xi]
In the third month, the district armor levy (qiujia) was instituted. [First year of Duke Cheng] In spring, the land tax levy for military service (tianfu) was introduced. [Twelfth year of Duke Ai]
In spring, in the King's first month, Jisun Su and Shu Lao joined Shi Gai of Jin, representatives of Qi, Song, and Wei, Gongsun Chai of Zheng, and representatives of Cao, Ju, Zhu, Teng, Xue, Qi, and Little Zhu in meeting Wu at Xiang. [Fourteenth year of Duke Xiang]
The Record of Rites (Liji)

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
凡爲君使者已受命君言不宿於家
天下大定然後正六律和五聲弦歌詩頌
此之謂德音德音之謂樂
君子之所謂義者貴賤皆有事於天下天
子親耕粢盛秬鬯以事上帝故諸侯勤
以輔事於天子
天下莫不貴者道也
論
第貳場
===
佐贊乾坤化育之功
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢戒俗吏矯飾者詔〔元和二年〕
擬唐以陸贄爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔貞元八年〕
擬河工告成廷臣
賀表
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
punctuated:
凡爲君使者，已受命，君言不宿於家。
天下大定，然後正六律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌，此之謂德音，德音之謂樂。
君子之所謂義者，貴賤皆有事於天下。天子親耕，粢盛秬鬯，以事上帝；故諸侯勤，以輔事於天子。
天下莫不貴者，道也。

第貳場

論
佐贊乾坤化育之功。

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕
擬漢戒俗吏矯飾者詔〔元和二年〕。
擬唐以陸贄爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔貞元八年〕。
擬河工告成廷臣賀表。

判語〔五條〕
官吏給由。
translation_en:
"Whenever one serves as an envoy for the ruler, once he has received his charge, the ruler's words do not stay overnight in his home."
"When all under Heaven was greatly settled, only then did he rectify the six pitch-standards, harmonize the five tones, and sing the Odes and Hymns to string accompaniment. This is called virtuous sound, and virtuous sound is called music."
"What the gentleman calls righteousness is that both the noble and the lowly have their duties in the world. The Son of Heaven plows in person to provide the sacrificial grain and black-millet aromatic wine with which to serve the Lord on High; therefore the feudal lords are diligent in order to assist in serving the Son of Heaven."
"That which nothing in the world fails to prize is the Way."

Second Session

Discourse:
"Assisting in the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth."

Edict, Mandate of Appointment, and Memorial (candidates answer one):
Imitation of a Han-dynasty edict admonishing vulgar officials who engage in pretentious artifice (second year of the Yuanhe era [85 CE]).
Imitation of a Tang-dynasty mandate appointing Lu Zhi 陸贄 as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery (eighth year of the Zhenyuan era [792]).
Imitation of a congratulatory memorial from court officials upon the completion of the Yellow River conservancy works.

Legal Judgments (five items):
Issuing service-record certificates for officials and functionaries.

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
收支留難
禁止迎送
優恤軍屬

第叁場
策五道
問古今稱極治者必曰虞周以今觀之重
華之勲始於釐降二南之化肇自關雎
風敎本原顧不重耶我
===
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇
成祖文皇帝誕膺鴻運創述巍煥流𠒎八埏卽
舜文無異揆焉乃
皇明祖訓
聖學心法二書所以貽厥孫謀者至爲閎具可
指而言與我
高皇后母儀天下嘉言懿行載在方策嗣我
文皇后作內訓以敎宮闈蓋釐降關雎一轍也
略亦可殫述與我
punctuated:
收支留難。
禁止迎送。
優恤軍屬。
帶造段匹。

第叁場
策五道

問：古今稱極治者，必曰虞、周。以今觀之，重華之勲始於釐降，二南之化肇自《關雎》，風敎本原，顧不重耶？我太祖高皇帝肇造區宇，成祖文皇帝誕膺鴻運，創述巍煥，流𠒎八埏，卽舜、文無異揆焉。乃《皇明祖訓》、《聖學心法》二書，所以貽厥孫謀者，至爲閎具，可指而言與？我高皇后母儀天下，嘉言懿行，載在方策；嗣我文皇后作《內訓》以敎宮闈，蓋釐降、《關雎》一轍也，略亦可殫述與？我
translation_en:
Obstruction in receiving and disbursing funds and grain (Shouzhi liunan).
Prohibiting official welcoming and sending-off (Jinzhi yingsong).
Compassionate relief for the dependents of military personnel (Youxu junshu).
Supplementary weaving of silk fabrics (Daizao duanpi).

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: When people past and present speak of the ultimate in good governance, they invariably cite the eras of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou dynasty. Viewed from the present, the meritorious achievements of Chonghua [Emperor Shun] began with the marriage of the two royal daughters sent down to him, and the moral transformation celebrated in the "Two Nan" [sections of the Classic of Poetry] originated with "The Osprey's Cry" (Guanju). Are not the fundamental sources of moral customs and instruction weighty indeed? Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), first founded the realm, and our Accomplished Progenitor, Emperor Wen (Chengzu, the Yongle Emperor), grandly received the great destiny. Their founding and continuation were lofty and resplendent, their flowing blessings [?] reaching the eight extremities of the world, following the very same principles as Shun and King Wen. Now, the two books Ancestral Injunctions of the August Ming (Huang Ming zuxun) and Method of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), by which they bequeathed plans to their descendants, are supremely vast and comprehensive; can you point them out and discuss them? Our Empress Gao (Empress Ma) served as a motherly model for all under Heaven, her admirable words and virtuous deeds recorded in the historical tablets; subsequently, our Empress Wen (Empress Xu) composed the Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun) to teach the palace women—following the exact same track as the royal marriage to Shun and "The Osprey's Cry." Can their general outlines also be fully recounted? Our…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
穆宗莊皇帝睿明恭儉祇續
先猷
仁聖懿安
慈聖宣文
二皇太后貞靜徽柔昭示宮則視我
二祖
二后貽謀規範不先後同符與我
皇上
皇后躬親訓迪今二載于兹矣其熙洽寓內維
===
持陰敎光
祖烈而軼虞周者必有本也願鋪張而揚厲之
以鳴
今日之盛
問秦罷封建置郡縣法甚具也而禁網益
密姦僞萌起漢除秦苛與民約法惟三
章耳而郡若縣兢兢守之何與夫漢法
行漢吏業已稱盛矣乃班之叙傳也僅
僅見五六抑以何道取之與夫定儀攸
punctuated:
穆宗莊皇帝睿明恭儉，祇續先猷；仁聖懿安、慈聖宣文二皇太后貞靜徽柔，昭示宮則：視我二祖、二后貽謀規範，不先後同符與？我皇上、皇后躬親訓迪，今二載于兹矣，其熙洽寓內，維持陰敎，光祖烈而軼虞、周者，必有本也。願鋪張而揚厲之，以鳴今日之盛。
問：秦罷封建，置郡縣，法甚具也，而禁網益密，姦僞萌起；漢除秦苛，與民約法惟三章耳，而郡若縣兢兢守之，何與？夫漢法行，漢吏業已稱盛矣，乃班之叙傳也，僅僅見五六，抑以何道取之與？夫定儀攸
translation_en:
…Emperor Muzong Zhuang (穆宗莊皇帝) was perspicacious, reverent, and frugal, respectfully continuing the plans of his predecessors; the two Empresses Dowager, Rensheng Yi'an (仁聖懿安) and Cisheng Xuanwen (慈聖宣文), are chaste, tranquil, virtuous, and gentle, clearly manifesting the standards for the palace women. Compared to the counsels and models bequeathed by our Two Progenitors and Two Empresses, do they not tally perfectly across time? Our reigning Emperor and Empress have personally received this instruction and guidance for two years now [since their marriage in 1578]; that they bring harmony to all within the realm, uphold the "yin teachings" (female instruction), glorify the achievements of the ancestors, and surpass Yu [Shun] and Zhou must surely have a fundamental root. We wish you to elaborate and extol this in detail, so as to proclaim the flourishing splendor of the present day.

Question: When Qin abolished feudal enfeoffment (fengjian 封建) and established commanderies and counties (junxian 郡縣), its laws were extremely thorough; yet as the net of prohibitions grew ever denser, treachery and deceit sprouted up. Han eliminated the harshness of Qin and made a covenant of law with the people consisting of only three articles, yet the commanderies and counties cautiously and reverently abided by them—why was this? Now, as Han laws were carried out, Han officials were already praised as flourishing; yet when Ban [Gu 班固] composed his collective biographies [of upright officials in the Book of Han], only five or six were included—by what criterion did he select them? As for those who established rituals or relied on…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
籍者聲稱有赫投巫擿伏者民畏如神
而乃不得與五六人竝傳何與士平居
譚治道輒欲姑舍漢吏而近世法令益
修未見超越漢治豈吏之未盡良耶抑
所以馭吏者道未盡也頃言官建白謂
久任不行吏數更易以故鮮實效耳今
任不爲不久矣何效之不可睹與此其
法必有不盡于此者而補偏救弊之說
不可不亟講也諸士習世故亦必有槩
于中矣願相與揚搉之以俟經世者擇
焉
===
問道德文章事功節義士論褒然重之全
雍以姬教穠沃河山鬱蒸才臣碩彥鱗
砌而出諸列在詩書毋贅已嗣是有總
衆職稱上意者參帷幄剖決如流者守
正不阿者忘身徇國者坐困先零者克
復兩京者三傳竝行於世者著書百萬
餘言者有長曆作而春秋之義著西銘
punctuated:
籍者，聲稱有赫；投巫擿伏者，民畏如神；而乃不得與五六人竝傳，何與？士平居譚治道，輒欲姑舍漢吏，而近世法令益修，未見超越漢治，豈吏之未盡良耶？抑所以馭吏者道未盡也？頃言官建白，謂久任不行，吏數更易，以故鮮實效耳。今任不爲不久矣，何效之不可睹與？此其法必有不盡于此者，而補偏救弊之說，不可不亟講也。諸士習世故，亦必有槩于中矣，願相與揚搉之，以俟經世者擇焉。
問：道德、文章、事功、節義，士論褒然重之。全雍以姬教穠沃，河山鬱蒸，才臣碩彥，鱗砌而出。諸列在《詩》、《書》，毋贅已。嗣是有總衆職稱上意者，參帷幄剖決如流者，守正不阿者，忘身徇國者，坐困先零者，克復兩京者，三傳竝行於世者，著書百萬餘言者，有《長曆》作而《春秋》之義著、《西銘》
translation_en:
…registers had illustrious reputations, and those who cast witches into the river or exposed hidden crimes were revered by the people as gods—yet why were they not given biographies alongside those five or six men? In ordinary conversation about the way of governance, scholars always wish to set aside the officials of Han as unworthy of emulation; yet in recent times, although laws and ordinances have been ever more elaborated, we have not seen governance surpass that of the Han. Is this because officials are not yet all good, or because the way of managing officials has not been fully realized? Recently, speaking officials submitted proposals arguing that because long tenure is not practiced and officials are frequently replaced, tangible results are rare. Now tenures cannot be said not to be long—why, then, are no results to be seen? In this matter, the method surely does not stop here alone, and theories for rectifying imbalances and remedying abuses must be urgently discussed. You gentlemen are conversant with worldly affairs and must certainly hold principled views within your minds; I wish to examine and weigh them together with you, awaiting selection by those who order the state.
Question: Moral virtue, literary composition, administrative achievement, and principled integrity—scholarly opinion praises and attaches great weight to these. All of Yongzhou [Shaanxi] was richly nourished by the teachings of the Zhou house, and from the lush vitality of its rivers and mountains, talented ministers and eminent worthies have emerged in dense succession. Those arrayed in the Book of Odes (Shi) and Book of Documents (Shu) need not be recounted further. Thereafter, there were those who supervised the multitude of offices and satisfied the ruler's wishes; those who participated in council within the command tent and decided matters like a flowing stream; those who upheld rectitude without flattery; those who forgot themselves to die for the state; those who sat fast and wore down the Xianlian [Qiang]; those who recovered the Two Capitals; those whose commentaries made all Three Traditions circulate together in the world; those who authored writings of over a million words; those through whose compilation of the Long Calendar (Changli) the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) was made manifest, and through whose Western Inscription (Ximing)…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
出而仁孝之理明者躬耕谷口者牧豕
上林者泉石膏肓雲溪退士者之數子
者於道德文章事功節義可別而言之
與歷時既邈載籍可稽數子嘉言善行
果信然與夫學者談唐虞而述三代率
卑漢唐宋曰勿論也能自得師即嫰惡
錯居亦多砥淑先哲如數子後事標矱
自在吾將以諗諸士之所適
問馬政軍國重務載在周禮纖悉具備今
===
可舉而言之與由周而來言馬政者凡
幾變矣漢初稍爲復古遂致阡陌成羣
唐制府兵貞觀後天下以一縑易一馬
今其法固在可倣而行之與宋初有官
馬戶馬戎馬之設至熙寧吏保馬之法
而民翻以病其視漢唐之制有優劣與
我
國朝馬政計地課駒牧不稱苦馬不稱乏與
周制有異同與弘正嘉隆之間先後有
punctuated:
出而仁孝之理明者，躬耕谷口者，牧豕上林者，泉石膏肓、雲溪退士者。之數子者，於道德、文章、事功、節義，可別而言之與？歷時既邈，載籍可稽，數子嘉言善行，果信然與？夫學者談唐虞而述三代，率卑漢、唐、宋曰「勿論也」。能自得師，即嫰惡錯居，亦多砥淑。先哲如數子，後事標矱自在，吾將以諗諸士之所適。
問：馬政，軍國重務，載在《周禮》，纖悉具備，今可舉而言之與？由周而來，言馬政者凡幾變矣。漢初稍爲復古，遂致阡陌成羣；唐制府兵，貞觀後天下以一縑易一馬，今其法固在，可倣而行之與？宋初有官馬、戶馬、戎馬之設，至熙寧吏保馬之法，而民翻以病，其視漢、唐之制有優劣與？我國朝馬政，計地課駒，牧不稱苦，馬不稱乏，與周制有異同與？弘、正、嘉、隆之間，先後有
translation_en:
… came forth and the principles of benevolence and filial piety were made clear; one who personally plowed at Gukou; one who herded swine in the Shanglin Park; one afflicted with an incurable passion for springs and rocks; and one known as the Retired Scholar of Yunxi (Yunxi tuishi). As for these several gentlemen, can they be distinguished and discussed under the categories of moral virtue, literary achievement, meritorious service, and principled integrity? Though a long time has elapsed, the written records can still be examined: are the admirable words and good deeds of these gentlemen truly credible? Now, scholars who discourse on Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] and recount the Three Dynasties generally look down upon the Han, Tang, and Song, saying, "They are not worth discussing!" Yet if one can find a teacher for oneself, even where the good and bad [?] live intermixed, there is much by which to whet and refine one's virtue. With former worthies such as these several gentlemen, their standards and models for later affairs remain present; through this I shall ascertain what direction you gentlemen choose to follow.

Question: Horse administration is a vital affair of the military and the state. As recorded in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), it was complete in every minute detail; can you cite and discuss it today? From the Zhou onward, discussions and systems of horse administration have undergone several changes. In the early Han, there was a slight restoration of antiquity, which resulted in horses forming herds along the field paths. The Tang established the Garrison Militia (fubing), and after the Zhenguan reign (627–649) the realm traded a single bolt of fine silk for a horse; now that its methods are still on record, can they be imitated and put into practice? In the early Song, there were establishments for government horses (guanma), household horses (huma), and military horses (rongma); by the Xining reign (1068–1077), when the officials changed [?] to the security-group horse method (baoma), the people instead suffered from it. Compared with the systems of the Han and Tang, what were its relative merits and defects? In our Dynasty's horse administration, foals were assessed according to land, so that herders did not complain of hardship and horses were not reported as scarce; how does this compare in similarities and differences with the Zhou system? Between the Hongzhi (1488–1505), Zhengde (1506–1521), Jiajing (1522–1566), and Longqing (1567–1572) reigns, there were successively …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
題屢爲清補屢爲甃壓華未復其舊近牧臣目
擊而條議省臣熟計而
上陳皆亹亹數千言甚爲激切今皆下其議於
所司將次第其要緊者以復舊備
廟堂采擇萬一第不知
國初之舊法尚可復行以濟牧軍之急近日
之節議亦可少損以裨馬政之敝與無
已尚有經國籌邊之略如昔丘文莊李
文正楊文襄之議更酌漢唐宋之中而
上求周官之遺意俾夫有定役地有常
數輸直有規差撥無苦内以重邊關之
勢外以寓制虜之機諸士生長百二之
鄉習聞而籌之熟矣願著于篇將采以
===
轉聞于
上
問北虜爲患中國往牒所載甚詳由周以
降漢唐之强竟莫能摧輪而縶其頸者
豈其時謀國者之馭戎之上策耶迨我
punctuated:
題，屢爲清補，屢爲甃壓，華未復其舊。近牧臣目擊而條議，省臣熟計而上陳，皆亹亹數千言，甚爲激切。今皆下其議於所司，將次第其要緊者以復舊，備廟堂采擇萬一。第不知國初之舊法尚可復行，以濟牧軍之急；近日之節議亦可少損，以裨馬政之敝與？無已，尚有經國籌邊之略，如昔丘文莊、李文正、楊文襄之議，更酌漢、唐、宋之中，而上求《周官》之遺意，俾夫有定役，地有常數，輸直有規，差撥無苦，内以重邊關之勢，外以寓制虜之機。諸士生長百二之鄉，習聞而籌之熟矣，願著于篇，將采以轉聞于上。

問：北虜爲患中國，往牒所載甚詳。由周以降，漢、唐之强，竟莫能摧輪而縶其頸者，豈其時謀國者之馭戎之上策耶？迨我
translation_en:
… memorials, repeatedly clearing up and making good deficits, and repeatedly walling in and suppressing [abuses?] [? 屢爲甃壓，華未復其舊], yet it ultimately has not been restored to its former state. Recently, horse-administration officials have witnessed these conditions firsthand and submitted itemized proposals, while Supervising Secretaries have deliberated thoroughly and presented memorials to the throne—all running tirelessly to several thousand words in the most urgent and earnest terms. Now their proposals have all been referred down to the competent authorities, who will arrange the most essential points in order so as to restore the old system and provide for the court's selection in some small measure. Yet I do not know whether the old regulations of the beginning of our dynasty can still be put back into practice to relieve the urgency of the herd-soldiers, and whether recent proposals for retrenchment [? 節議] can also be slightly curtailed to remedy the abuses of the horse administration? If nothing else will do, is there still some grand strategy for governing the state and planning for the frontiers—such as the proposals of the former Qiu Wenzhuang (Qiu Jun 丘濬), Li Wenzheng (Li Dongyang 李東陽), and Yang Wenxiang (Yang Yiqing 楊一清)—that further strikes a balance among the Han, Tang, and Song systems while reaching back to seek the intent bequeathed by the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), so that adult males have fixed labor services, land has a constant quota, the commutation of payments has regular rules, and assignment and dispatch entail no hardship, internally strengthening the strategic position of the frontier passes and externally embodying the mechanism for controlling the northern caitiffs? You gentlemen were born and raised in this region of "two against a hundred" [Shaanxi], have long heard of these matters, and have planned for them thoroughly. I hope you will set them forth in your essays, which will be selected and transmitted to the notice of His Majesty.

Question: The northern caitiffs have been a menace to China, as is recorded in great detail in past documents. From the Zhou dynasty onward, despite the might of the Han and Tang, they were ultimately unable to smash their chariot wheels and bind their necks—was it because those who planned for the state in those times lacked [? 之 for 乏] the supreme strategy for controlling the western and northern barbarians? Coming down to our…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元
成祖文皇帝三犁虜庭鴻猷駿烈曠古稱盛然
倏順倏叛奄入奄遯虜情桀黠亦未帖
然傾心也邇者俺酋納款輸貢其部落
往來內地我
皇上猶赤子視之邊臣不以塞垣限之豈非千
古一時
國家之極盛哉然狼子野心中懷叵測頃以
禮佛建寺盤據河外往來張掖酒泉威
===
劫屬番脾睨茶馬至亡厭也凡此豈效
順者所宜有耶夫虜所駐足咸爲要塞
儻久此不返猶樗腹而堅前好乎此地
者全陝之屏翰而全陝者九邊之肩背
也諸士生長於茲宜懷請纓之志願詳
言之俟石畫者採焉
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元，成祖文皇帝三犁虜庭，鴻猷駿烈，曠古稱盛。然倏順倏叛，奄入奄遯，虜情桀黠，亦未帖然傾心也。邇者俺酋納款輸貢，其部落往來內地，我皇上猶赤子視之，邊臣不以塞垣限之，豈非千古一時，國家之極盛哉！然狼子野心，中懷叵測，頃以禮佛建寺，盤據河外，往來張掖、酒泉，威劫屬番，脾睨茶馬，至亡厭也。凡此，豈效順者所宜有耶？夫虜所駐足，咸爲要塞，儻久此不返，猶樗腹而堅前好乎？此地者，全陝之屏翰；而全陝者，九邊之肩背也。諸士生長於茲，宜懷請纓之志，願詳言之，俟石畫者採焉。
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, swept away the barbarian Yuan, and Emperor Chengzu, the Cultured Emperor, thrice plowed up the caitiffs' courts. Their grand plans and illustrious achievements are acclaimed as flourishing beyond anything in antiquity. Yet, now submitting and now rebelling, suddenly invading and suddenly fleeing, the caitiffs in their fierce cunning still did not docilely give their allegiance.

Recently, the chieftain Altan Khan (Anqiu 俺酋) has offered submission and presented tribute. His tribes travel back and forth within our interior lands; His Majesty regards them as newborn infants, and our frontier officials do not restrict them behind the border walls. Is this not a once-in-a-millennium moment and the supreme flourishing of the State? Yet with the wild hearts of wolf cubs, they harbor unfathomable intentions within. Of late, on the pretext of worshiping the Buddha and building a monastery, they have entrenched themselves beyond the Yellow River, moving back and forth around Zhangye and Jiuquan, intimidating and plundering our tributary Tibetan tribes (shufan 屬番), and casting greedy eyes on the tea-and-horse trade, utterly without satiation. Are any of these things proper for those who profess allegiance?

Now, the places where the caitiffs have stationed themselves are all strategic strongholds. Should they linger here for long without returning, will they still remain empty-bellied and hold fast to their former amity? This region is the protective screen of all Shaanxi, and all Shaanxi is the shoulders and back of the Nine Frontiers. You gentlemen were born and raised here and ought to cherish the ambition of requesting a long cord to bind the enemy. I hope you will speak of this in detail, awaiting selection by those who devise firm strategic plans.

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人六十五名
第一名劉宇　金州學生　春秋
第二名彪準　西安府學生　易
第三名王守禮　延川縣學生　詩
第四名南企仲　渭南縣學生　禮記
第五名曹思聰　岷州衛學生　書
第六名張鵾　西安府學生　詩
第七名周南　三原縣學附學生　易
===
第八名杜本益　米脂縣學增廣生　春秋
第九名雷益　南鄭縣學生　書
第十名張惟任　潼關衛學生　禮記
第十一名康塡　武功縣學生　詩
第十二名張美　安化縣學生　易
第十三名趙賞瀛　禮縣監生　春秋
第十四名王三策　郃陽縣學生　詩
第十五名高數仞　寶雞縣學生　書
第十六名李賦秀　延安府學生　詩
punctuated:
中式舉人六十五名：
第一名，劉宇，金州學生，《春秋》。
第二名，彪準，西安府學生，《易》。
第三名，王守禮，延川縣學生，《詩》。
第四名，南企仲，渭南縣學生，《禮記》。
第五名，曹思聰，岷州衛學生，《書》。
第六名，張鵾，西安府學生，《詩》。

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰吾十有五而志于學三十而立四十
而不惑五十而知天命六十而耳順七
十而從心所欲不踰矩
劉宇
同考試官學正劉　批〔起處即提出矩字通篇以不踰矩爲作用功夫至七十而化乃能從心所欲耳此特達之見非經生所能說到〕
===
考試官教諭王　批〔格調高古非苟作者〕
考試官學正任　批〔意精詞雅迥異時作〕
聖學所以化由志而日新者也夫所欲即矩則
化矣而必由志學以進焉學之不可已也如是
夫夫子自述以詔後學蓋曰學以理爲矩以不
踰矩爲能守以從心不踰矩爲能化今吾心之
所欲矩自在矣然豈一朝一夕之故哉彼學未
有無志而成者吾昔十有五也志於學焉學雖
未至而志則已定不至於矩之從欲不止矣由
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「子曰：『吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。』」
劉宇
同考試官學正劉　批：〔起處即提出「矩」字，通篇以「不踰矩」爲作用功夫，至七十而化，乃能從心所欲耳。此特達之見，非經生所能說到。〕
考試官教諭王　批：〔格調高古，非苟作者。〕
考試官學正任　批：〔意精詞雅，迥異時作。〕
聖學所以化，由志而日新者也。夫所欲即矩，則化矣，而必由志學以進焉，學之不可已也如是夫！夫子自述以詔後學，蓋曰：學以理爲矩，以不踰矩爲能守，以從心不踰矩爲能化。今吾心之所欲，矩自在矣，然豈一朝一夕之故哉？彼學未有無志而成者。吾昔十有五也，志於學焉。學雖未至，而志則已定，不至於矩之從欲不止矣。由
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books
"The Master said: 'At fifteen, I set my heart on learning. At thirty, I took my stand. At forty, I had no doubts. At fifty, I knew the Mandate of Heaven. At sixty, my ear was attuned. At seventy, I followed what my heart desired without overstepping the carpenter's square.'"
Liu Yu 劉宇
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Liu, comments: [Right from the opening, he highlights the word "square" (ju 矩), and throughout the entire essay he treats "not overstepping the square" as the active effort of self-cultivation; only upon reaching seventy and achieving transformation is one able to follow what the heart desires. This is an insight of exceptional penetration, not something an ordinary student of the Classics could arrive at.]
Examiner, District Instructor (jiaoyu) Wang, comments: [Lofty and antique in style and tone; not the work of a careless writer.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor Ren, comments: [Refined in meaning and elegant in diction, utterly different from contemporary compositions.]
That whereby sage learning achieves transformation is through setting the will and renewing itself daily. Now, when what one desires is itself the square, one has achieved transformation; yet one must advance toward this from having set one's heart on learning—such is the impossibility of ceasing to learn! In recounting his own experience to instruct later learners, the Master was in effect saying: Learning takes principle as its square, takes not overstepping the square as the ability to hold fast, and takes following the heart without overstepping the square as the ability to transform. Now, in whatever my heart desires, the square is naturally present; yet how could this be the result of a single morning or a single evening? Learning has never been brought to completion without first setting the will. In the past, when I was fifteen, I set my heart on learning. Although my learning had not yet reached its goal, my will was already fixed: I would not stop until the square itself followed my desires. From…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
此而三十操存其所志者又十有五年而吾始
可與立也由此而四十研窮其所立者又十年
而吾始能不惑也以所不惑者而上達焉命可
知矣時其在五十乎以所知者而一貫焉耳斯
順矣時其在六十乎夫自志學以來固無敢一
日踰乎矩者而未必從心所欲也今七十矣然
後從其所欲而不踰焉無欲非矩無矩非心吾
之志固如斯而今可無負也已向使未七十而
助長或十五之後而中止焉何以有是哉過此
===
以往吾將終身焉爾亦安知老之至也嘗觀易
曰天行健君子以自强不息夫天豈待積累而
成然非健則造化或幾乎息矣聖人之道猶天
然謂其至七十而後化謂其當十五而即化者
皆非也故志學必稱十五其天人之介乎易之
序卦乾坤屯蒙相次它日又曰後生可畏其旨
深哉
苟不固聰明聖知達天德者其孰能知之
彪準
punctuated:
此而三十，操存其所志者又十有五年，而吾始可與立也。由此而四十，研窮其所立者又十年，而吾始能不惑也。以所不惑者而上達焉，命可知矣，時其在五十乎？以所知者而一貫焉，耳斯順矣，時其在六十乎？夫自志學以來，固無敢一日踰乎矩者，而未必從心所欲也。今七十矣，然後從其所欲而不踰焉。無欲非矩，無矩非心，吾之志固如斯，而今可無負也已。向使未七十而助長，或十五之後而中止焉，何以有是哉？過此以往，吾將終身焉爾，亦安知老之至也！嘗觀《易》曰：「天行健，君子以自强不息。」夫天豈待積累而成？然非健則造化或幾乎息矣。聖人之道猶天，然謂其至七十而後化，謂其當十五而即化者，皆非也。故志學必稱十五，其天人之介乎？《易》之《序卦》，《乾》、《坤》、《屯》、《蒙》相次，它日又曰：「後生可畏。」其旨深哉！
苟不固聰明聖知達天德者，其孰能知之？
彪準
translation_en:
… here to thirty, holding fast to and preserving that upon which I had set my mind for another fifteen years, and only then was I able to take my stand. From here to forty, investigating thoroughly that upon which I had taken my stand for another ten years, and only then was I free from doubts. Taking that about which I had no doubts and reaching upward with it, the Mandate of Heaven could be known—was the time for that not at fifty? Taking what was known and threading it together as one, my ear was thus attuned—was the time for that not at sixty? Now, ever since setting my mind on learning, I certainly never dared for a single day to overstep the square, yet I could not necessarily follow what my heart desired. Now at seventy, only after this do I follow what my heart desires without overstepping it. No desire is not the square, and no square is not the heart; my resolve was originally like this, and now I have not failed it. Had I forced its growth before seventy, or stopped halfway after fifteen, how could I have attained this? Going forward from here, I shall simply continue thus to the end of my life; how would I even know that old age is coming on! I have observed that the Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Heaven's movement is vigorous; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself unceasingly." Does Heaven depend on gradual accumulation to reach completion? Yet without vigor, creative transformation would almost cease. The Way of the sage is like Heaven, yet to say that he undergoes transformation only after reaching seventy, or to say that he undergoes transformation immediately at fifteen, are both wrong. Therefore, in speaking of setting the mind on learning, he necessarily cites fifteen—is this not the boundary between Heaven and man? In the "Sequence of the Hexagrams" (Xugua) of the Book of Changes, Qian, Kun, Zhun, and Meng follow one another in turn; and on another day he also said, "Awe is due to youth." How profound is the meaning!

"Only he who is genuinely quick in apprehension, clear in discernment, of far-reaching intelligence and all-embracing knowledge, and who has attained to the virtue of Heaven—who else can know him?"
Biao Zhun 彪準

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭方　批　〔聖與誠原是一理此作開講節〕
〔說破而開闔變化不出範圍末二股更奇絕不可易及〕
考試官教諭王　批　〔題難下手子顧不著意而發明〕
〔透徹大雅之文也錄之〕
考試官學正任　批　〔別是大家機軸非熟於秦漢文〕
〔字其孰能知之〕
中庸決言至誠之道非至聖不能知也夫聖之
至者以其誠之至也非聖則非誠矣安能知其
道哉中庸之意蓋曰知與能非兩事聖與誠非
===
二物至誠功用能極其盛者謂其有聰明聖知
之資達仁義禮智之德耳是豈可易知哉質之
不敏無足論矣苟質美而非固有之者何以能
窮其神德之不足不待言矣苟德備而非達諸
天者何以能會其妙人曰至誠則大經之經綸
也大本之立也化育之知也且不自知其所以
然而欲人知其所未然誰則能之人非至聖於
仁之肫肫也淵之淵淵也天之浩浩也既不能
其所已能而欲知其所不能無是理矣聲名有
punctuated:
同考試官教諭方　批：〔聖與誠原是一理。此作開講節說破，而開闔變化，不出範圍。末二股更奇絕，不可易及。〕
考試官教諭王　批：〔題難下手，子顧不著意而發明透徹，大雅之文也，錄之。〕
考試官學正任　批：〔別是大家機軸，非熟於秦漢文字，其孰能知之？〕
《中庸》決言至誠之道，非至聖不能知也。夫聖之至者，以其誠之至也；非聖則非誠矣，安能知其道哉？《中庸》之意，蓋曰：知與能非兩事，聖與誠非二物。至誠功用能極其盛者，謂其有聰明聖知之資，達仁義禮智之德耳。是豈可易知哉？質之不敏，無足論矣；苟質美而非固有之者，何以能窮其神？德之不足，不待言矣；苟德備而非達諸天者，何以能會其妙？人曰至誠，則大經之經綸也，大本之立也，化育之知也，且不自知其所以然，而欲人知其所未然，誰則能之？人非至聖，於仁之肫肫也，淵之淵淵也，天之浩浩也，既不能其所已能，而欲知其所不能，無是理矣。聲名有
translation_en:
Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Fang comments: [Sagehood and sincerity are originally a single principle. This composition lays it bare right in the opening section, and in its opening and closing transformations, it never steps outside the bounds. The final two parallel legs are even more marvelously unmatched and cannot easily be equaled.]
Examiner County Director of Studies Wang comments: [The topic is difficult to tackle, yet you bring it out with thorough clarity without strain; it is a piece of great elegance, so we record it for publication.]
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Ren comments: [This has the distinctloom and structure of a great master; unless one is well-versed in Qin and Han prose, who could appreciate it?]
The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) decisively states that the Way of utmost sincerity cannot be known by anyone other than one of utmost sagehood. Now, one who has reached the pinnacle of sagehood is so because he has reached the pinnacle of sincerity; if one is not a sage, one does not possess utmost sincerity—how then could he know its Way? The meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean is roughly to say: knowing and being able are not two separate matters, and sagehood and sincerity are not two separate things. That the functional efficacy of utmost sincerity can reach the height of flourishing means simply that one possesses the endowment of quick apprehension, clear discernment, far-reaching intelligence, and all-embracing knowledge, and penetrates the virtues of humaneness, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom. How could this be easily known? Those whose natural qualities are dull are not worth discussing; yet even if one's natural qualities are fine, if he does not possess them innately, how could he fathom its mysterious workings? Those whose virtue is deficient need not be mentioned; yet even if one's virtue is complete, if he does not penetrate to the level of Heaven, how could he comprehend its subtlety? When speaking of one of utmost sincerity—in his ordering and regulating of the great invariable relations, his establishing of the great foundation, and his understanding of the transforming and nourishing processes—even he himself does not know how it is so; if one wishes others to know what has not yet become so for them, who could be capable of it? If a person is not of utmost sagehood, then with regard to the earnestness of his humaneness, the depth of his abyssal stillness, and the vastness of his Heaven-like nature, since one is already incapable of what the sage is capable of, to wish to know what lies beyond one's capability is contrary to principle. Fame and renown have…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
共仰而所以爲聲名則民可由而不可知有能
知之者必也卽至誠乎尊親有同情而所以可
尊親則百姓日用而不知非天下至聖孰能與
於斯蓋論道之大卽少有所窺謂之不能知固
不可論道之精卽未達一間謂之能知亦不可
大哉誠乎斯其至矣抑夫子以生知爲上學知
爲次孟子亦譬聖知於巧力子思所謂孰能知
者蓋得之夫子而授之孟子非世儒所謂知也
不然何以必曰聰明聖知此豈人力哉雖然性
===
近習遠及其知之一也神而明之存乎其人耳
孟子曰禹惡旨酒而好善言湯執中立賢
無方文王視民如傷望道而未之見武
王不泄邇不忘遠周公思兼三王以施
四事其有不合者仰而思之夜以繼日
幸而得之坐以待旦
王守禮
同考試官訓導石　批〔說理貫徹非泛言者〕
考試官教諭王　批〔詞氣老成踈暢取之〕
punctuated:
共仰，而所以爲聲名，則民可由而不可知；有能知之者，必也卽至誠乎！尊親有同情，而所以可尊親，則百姓日用而不知；非天下至聖，孰能與於斯？蓋論道之大，卽少有所窺，謂之不能知固不可；論道之精，卽未達一間，謂之能知亦不可。大哉誠乎！斯其至矣。抑夫子以生知爲上，學知爲次，孟子亦譬聖知於巧力。子思所謂「孰能知」者，蓋得之夫子而授之孟子，非世儒所謂知也。不然，何以必曰「聰明聖知」？此豈人力哉！雖然，性近習遠，及其知之一也。神而明之，存乎其人耳。
孟子曰：「禹惡旨酒而好善言。湯執中，立賢無方。文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。周公思兼三王，以施四事；其有不合者，仰而思之，夜以繼日；幸而得之，坐以待旦。」
王守禮
同考試官訓導石　批〔說理貫徹，非泛言者。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔詞氣老成踈暢，取之。〕
translation_en:
… universally looked up to, yet as for that whereby his fame and renown come to be, the common people can follow it but cannot know it. If there is anyone capable of knowing it, must he not be one of utmost sincerity himself! Reverence and affection are shared sentiments, yet as for that whereby he is worthy of reverence and affection, the hundred surnames use it daily without knowing it. Unless one possesses the utmost sageliness in the world, who could participate in this? Indeed, speaking of the greatness of the Way, even if one has caught a slight glimpse of it, one certainly cannot be called unable to know it; yet speaking of the subtlety of the Way, even if one falls short by just a single hair's breadth, one likewise cannot be called able to know it. Great indeed is sincerity! This is its ultimate perfection. Moreover, the Master ranked those born with knowledge as the highest and those who know through learning as next, and Mencius likewise compared sagely wisdom to skill and strength. What Zisi meant by "who can know" was in fact received from the Master and transmitted to Mencius; it is not what worldly scholars call knowledge. Otherwise, why would he necessarily say "intelligence, clarity, and sagely wisdom"? Could this be achieved by human effort alone! Even so, by nature men are nearly alike, while by practice they grow wide apart, yet once they attain knowledge, it is one and the same. To comprehend it in spirit and illuminate it rests with the individual alone.

Mencius said: "Yu hated fine wine and loved good words. Tang held fast to the Mean and established the worthy without regard to origin. King Wen looked upon the people as if they were wounded, and gazed toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. King Wu did not treat the near with familiarity, nor did he forget the distant. The Duke of Zhou sought to combine the achievements of the Three Kings in order to carry out their four undertakings. Whenever there was anything that did not accord with his circumstances, he would look up and reflect upon it, continuing from day into night; and when by good fortune he grasped it, he would sit waiting for the dawn."

Wang Shouli 王守禮
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Shi 石 comments: 〔His exposition of principle is thorough and penetrating; he is no speaker of empty generalities.〕
Examiner, Instructor Wang 王 comments: 〔His diction and tone are mature, seasoned, and fluent; select it.〕

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正任　批　〔發明心學不事浮詞宜錄以式〕
觀羣聖不自逸之心可以知道統之傳矣夫聖
人之傳道以心也由三王而周公孰非其不自
逸之心乎孟子之意若謂道出於天而全於聖
精一之統自舜開之而心學有傳矣是故禹受
命於舜者也故嚴於理欲之防旨酒是惡善言
是好儆怠荒而戒滿假蓋舜之所以爲心也已
湯得統於禹者也故謹於人已之際執中弗失
立賢無方昭大德而求哲人蓋禹之所以爲心
===
也已文王繼湯而著丕顯之謨民已安矣道已
至矣猶軫如傷之視焉懷未見之憂焉愛之深
求之切其心何異於湯乎武王繼文而揚丕承
之烈篤乎近矣舉乎遠矣猶敬慎而不泄焉慮
周而不忘焉德之盛仁之至其心何異於文乎
夫三王迭興而四事代作則思兼而施之者固
周公任道之責也故未得而精思求以神會三
王之心焉既得而敏行求以善述三王之事焉
又安知繼日待旦之勞哉夫三王以聖人君天
punctuated:
考試官學正任批：〔發明心學，不事浮詞，宜錄以式。〕

觀羣聖不自逸之心，可以知道統之傳矣。夫聖人之傳道，以心也。由三王而周公，孰非其不自逸之心乎？孟子之意，若謂：道出於天而全於聖，精一之統自舜開之，而心學有傳矣。是故禹，受命於舜者也，故嚴於理欲之防，旨酒是惡，善言是好，儆怠荒而戒滿假，蓋舜之所以爲心也已；湯，得統於禹者也，故謹於人已之際，執中弗失，立賢無方，昭大德而求哲人，蓋禹之所以爲心也已。文王繼湯而著丕顯之謨，民已安矣，道已至矣，猶軫如傷之視焉，懷未見之憂焉，愛之深、求之切，其心何異於湯乎？武王繼文而揚丕承之烈，篤乎近矣，舉乎遠矣，猶敬慎而不泄焉，慮周而不忘焉，德之盛、仁之至，其心何異於文乎？夫三王迭興而四事代作，則思兼而施之者，固周公任道之責也。故未得而精思，求以神會三王之心焉；既得而敏行，求以善述三王之事焉，又安知繼日待旦之勞哉！夫三王，以聖人君天
translation_en:
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Ren comments: [It elucidates the learning of the mind-and-heart (xinxue) without indulging in superficial rhetoric; it is fitting to record it as a model.]

By observing the minds of the sages that never allowed themselves ease, one can understand the transmission of the succession of the Way (daotong). Now, the sages transmit the Way through the mind. From the Three Kings down to the Duke of Zhou, which of them did not possess this mind that never allowed itself ease? The meaning of Mencius is as if to say: The Way originates from Heaven and is perfected in the sages. The succession of refinement and single-mindedness was initiated by Shun, and thus the learning of the mind-and-heart was transmitted. Therefore, Yu was the one who received the mandate from Shun. Hence he was strict in guarding the boundary between principle and desire—detesting fine wine and loving good words, guarding against indolence and neglect while warning against arrogance and presumption; this was indeed what Shun took as his mind. Tang was the one who obtained the succession from Yu. Hence he was cautious in the relationship between others and the self [reading 已 as 己]—holding fast to the Mean without losing it, and establishing the worthy without restriction, manifesting great virtue and seeking wise men; this was indeed what Yu took as his mind. King Wen succeeded Tang and manifested his illustriously bright plans. Though the people were already at peace and the Way was already reached, he still felt the distress of looking upon them as if they were wounded, and harbored the anxiety of not yet having seen the Way. So deep was his love and so earnest his seeking—how did his mind differ from that of Tang? King Wu succeeded King Wen and extolled his grandly inherited achievements. Though he was already devoted to those near and had elevated those far away, he still remained reverent and cautious so as not to treat the near with familiarity, and thoughtful and comprehensive so as not to forget the distant. So abundant was his virtue and so utmost his benevolence—how did his mind differ from that of King Wen? Now, the Three Kings arose in succession and their four undertakings were accomplished in turn; thus, to think of combining and implementing them all was assuredly the responsibility of the Duke of Zhou in taking up the Way. Therefore, before he had grasped it, he pondered deeply, seeking to commune in spirit with the minds of the Three Kings; once he had grasped it, he acted earnestly, seeking to transmit well the undertakings of the Three Kings—how then would he even be conscious of the toil of continuing from night into day and sitting to await the dawn! Now, the Three Kings were sages who ruled the world…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
下者也周公以聖人相天下者也其心皆不敢
自逸焉凡以全此幾希之理耳此道統之所由
傳與雖然三代之治盛矣而其君相不自以爲
盛何哉宜日中而勅時幾憂治世而戒滿盈道
固然也是故禹湯文武周公同此憂勤惕勵之
心乃所以益成其盛也斯義也萬世君相所當
知也
易
聖人作而萬物覩本乎天者親上本乎地
者親下則各從其類也
===
彪準
同考試官教諭方　批〔發明盛治宛然在目而結以眷治推之其臣尤爲有見取之〕
考試官教諭王　批〔說理明切詞氣從容取之〕
考試官學正任　批〔簡潔可誦〕
聖人繫天下之望一類應之常而已夫物莫不
以類相從也然則聖人作於上而天下之覩之
也固宜文言釋乾九五爻義若曰君子觀於聲
punctuated:
下者也，周公以聖人相天下者也，其心皆不敢自逸焉，凡以全此幾希之理耳。此道統之所由傳與！雖然，三代之治盛矣，而其君相不自以爲盛，何哉？宜日中而勅時幾，憂治世而戒滿盈，道固然也。是故禹、湯、文、武、周公同此憂勤惕勵之心，乃所以益成其盛也。斯義也，萬世君相所當知也。

易

「聖人作而萬物覩。本乎天者親上，本乎地者親下，則各從其類也。」

彪準

同考試官教諭方　批〔發明盛治，宛然在目，而結以眷治推之其臣，尤爲有見，取之。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔說理明切，詞氣從容，取之。〕
考試官學正任　批〔簡潔可誦。〕

聖人繫天下之望，一類應之常而已。夫物莫不以類相從也，然則聖人作於上而天下之覩之也，固宜。《文言》釋《乾》九五爻義，若曰：君子觀於聲
translation_en:
… the realm as sages, and the Duke of Zhou assisted in governing the realm as a sage; in their hearts, none of them dared to indulge in ease, all in order to preserve intact this slight distinction of moral principle. Is this not whereby the succession of the Way was transmitted! Even so, the governance of the Three Dynasties was flourishing indeed, yet their rulers and chief ministers did not consider it flourishing themselves—why was this? Keeping fit for the midday sun and cautiously attending to timing and subtle incipient tendencies, worrying over an era of order and guarding against fullness and overflow—such is inherently the Way. Therefore, Yu, Tang, King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou all shared this anxious, diligent, vigilant, and self-exhorting mind, which was precisely how they brought their flourishing governance to even greater perfection. This principle is what rulers and chief ministers for ten thousand generations ought to know.

Classic of Changes (Yijing)

"When the sage arises, the myriad things look up to him. What is rooted in heaven draws near to what is above; what is rooted in earth draws near to what is below: thus each follows its own kind."

Biao Zhun 彪準

Associate Examiner and Instructor Fang 方 comments: [He elucidates flourishing governance so that it appears vividly before one's eyes, and concludes by extending concern for governance to the ministers, which shows particular insight. Selected.]
Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: [His explanation of principle is clear and incisive, and his diction and tone are unhurried and composed. Selected.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Ren 任 comments: [Concise, clean, and worthy of recitation.]

That the sage binds to himself the hopes of the realm is nothing more than the constant norm of response among things of the same kind. Now, among things there are none that do not follow after their own kind; this being so, when the sage arises above, it is naturally fitting that the whole realm looks up to him. title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
應氣求之機水火風雲之理而知感應之爲至
神也何獨於聖人而疑之是故聖人者秉剛健
中正之德而應運以握其符爲仁義禮樂之宗
而得位以行其道是維皇建極旣以一人而撫
萬邦則惟民歸極自以萬物而覩一人仰其乘
龍之猷而觀光於朝者爭快覩其休也荷其御
天之治而觀化於野者咸樂覩其盛也若此者
豈聖人有要於萬物哉亦從其類焉耳夫天以
陽浮於上者也而動物之本乎天者皆仰而親
===
之物何心哉得陽之氣從其類於陽而已地以
陰凝於下者也而植物之本乎地者皆俯而親
之物何心哉得陰之氣從其類於陰而已聖人
之於民亦類也聖人以同然之德感天下而如
天之覆如地之載也天下以同然之心應聖人
而怙之如天依之如地也均之非有所強者也
九五曰飛龍在天利見大人其此之謂乎觀此
可以爲世道慶矣抑是聖人也將裁成天地之
道輔相天地之宜舉親上親下之物而曲成之
punctuated: 應氣求之機，水火風雲之理，而知感應之爲至神也。何獨於聖人而疑之？是故聖人者，秉剛健中正之德，而應運以握其符；爲仁義禮樂之宗，而得位以行其道。是維皇建極，旣以一人而撫萬邦；則惟民歸極，自以萬物而覩一人。仰其乘龍之猷，而觀光於朝者，爭快覩其休也；荷其御天之治，而觀化於野者，咸樂覩其盛也。若此者，豈聖人有要於萬物哉？亦從其類焉耳。夫天以陽浮於上者也，而動物之本乎天者，皆仰而親之，物何心哉？得陽之氣，從其類於陽而已。地以陰凝於下者也，而植物之本乎地者，皆俯而親之，物何心哉？得陰之氣，從其類於陰而已。聖人之於民，亦類也。聖人以同然之德感天下，而如天之覆、如地之載也；天下以同然之心應聖人，而怙之如天、依之如地也。均之非有所強者也。九五曰：「飛龍在天，利見大人。」其此之謂乎！觀此可以爲世道慶矣。抑是聖人也，將裁成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，舉親上親下之物而曲成之
translation_en: …the mechanism by which matching tones respond and like qi seeks its own, and the principle governing water, fire, wind, and clouds, one knows that stimulus and response are supremely marvelous. Why, then, should one doubt this solely in the case of the sage? Therefore, the sage possesses the virtue of firm strength and central correctness, and responds to destiny to grasp the tally of sovereignty; he serves as the exemplar of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, and attains the throne to put his Way into practice. Thus, when the August Sovereign establishes the Supreme Ultimate, already soothing the myriad states as the One Man, the common people turn toward the Supreme Ultimate, naturally beholding the One Man as the myriad things. Those who look up to his dragon-riding plans and behold the splendor of the court vie to eagerly witness his blessings; those who receive his heaven-driving governance and observe his transformation in the countryside all joyously witness his flourishing. That it is like this—how could it be that the sage makes demands upon the myriad things? It is simply that they follow their own kind. Now, Heaven floats above by virtue of yang, and animate creatures that have their origin in Heaven all look up and cleave to it. What conscious intent do creatures have? Having received the qi of yang, they simply follow their kind toward yang. Earth congeals below by virtue of yin, and plants that have their origin in Earth all bow down and cleave to it. What conscious intent do creatures have? Having received the qi of yin, they simply follow their kind toward yin. The relation of the sage to the people is also one of kind. The sage moves the world through their shared virtue, sheltering it like Heaven and supporting it like Earth; the world responds to the sage with a shared heart, relying on him as on Heaven and depending on him as on Earth. In both cases, there is nothing forced. When the Nine in the Fifth Place says, "The flying dragon is in the heavens; it is advantageous to see the great man," is this not what it means? Observing this, one may rejoice for the Way of the world! Moreover, this sage is one who will regulate and complete the Way of Heaven and Earth, assist and guide what is appropriate to Heaven and Earth, and take up all creatures that cleave to what is above and what is below, bringing every one of them to intricate completion…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者也然代天弘化非能獨運於上而調元贊化
不無望於其臣也堯舜在上而四岳九官助之
以致唐虞之治古之明良相與以有成如此故
周公繫乾之九五曰利見而於九二亦云
乾知大始坤作成物乾以易知坤以簡能
周南
同考試官敎諭方　批〔剗去浮言惟發本旨蓋素嘗究〕
〔心易學者取之〕
考試官敎諭王　批〔明白親切無踰此作取之〕
===
考試官學正任　批〔善發乾坤之蘊其學通造化者〕
〔乎取之爲說易者式焉〕
大傳論乾坤功用之盛而因本其無心之妙焉
蓋知始作成乾坤之功用盛矣然不外於易簡
焉其諸無心而成化者歟且夫統萬物而不遺
者天地之全功也鼓萬物而無憂者天地之至
德也善觀造化者觀諸此而已矣何則物必有
始其孰始之惟乾有天道不特成男已也先天
之化宰於是焉則顯仁於藏用之餘而萬有兆
punctuated:
者也。然代天弘化，非能獨運於上，而調元贊化，不無望於其臣也。堯舜在上，而四岳九官助之，以致唐虞之治，古之明良相與以有成如此。故周公繫《乾》之九五曰「利見」，而於九二亦云。

乾知大始，坤作成物。乾以易知，坤以簡能。
周南
同考試官敎諭方　批〔剗去浮言，惟發本旨，蓋素嘗究心《易》學者。取之。〕
考試官敎諭王　批〔明白親切，無踰此作。取之。〕
考試官學正任　批〔善發乾坤之蘊，其學通造化者乎！取之，爲說《易》者式焉。〕

《大傳》論乾坤功用之盛，而因本其無心之妙焉。蓋知始作成，乾坤之功用盛矣，然不外於易簡焉，其諸無心而成化者歟！且夫統萬物而不遺者，天地之全功也；鼓萬物而無憂者，天地之至德也。善觀造化者，觀諸此而已矣。何則？物必有始，其孰始之？惟乾有天道，不特成男已也，先天之化宰於是焉，則顯仁於藏用之餘，而萬有兆
translation_en:
… However, in acting on behalf of Heaven to broaden transformation, he cannot operate alone from above, and in harmonizing the primal forces and assisting in transformation, he cannot but place hopes in his ministers. Yao and Shun were on high, while the Four Peaks and Nine Officials assisted them to bring about the governance of Tang and Yu; such was the way enlightened rulers and worthy ministers worked together to achieve success in antiquity. Therefore, when the Duke of Zhou appended his judgment to the Nine in the Fifth place of the Qian hexagram, he said "It is advantageous to see," and at the Nine in the Second place he said the same.

"Qian directs the great beginnings; Kun acts to bring things to completion. Qian directs through ease; Kun is capable through simplicity."
By Zhou Nan 周南.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Fang 方 comments: 〔Stripping away superficial words, he solely brings out the fundamental meaning; he is surely one who has long devoted his mind to the study of the Book of Changes (Yi). Selected.〕
Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: 〔Clear, direct, and pertinent, nothing surpasses this composition. Selected.〕
Examiner and Director of Studies Ren 任 comments: 〔Skillfully unfolding the profundities of Qian and Kun, is his learning not conversant with the creative transformations of nature? Selected to serve as a model for those who expound the Book of Changes.〕

The Great Treatise (Dazhuan) discusses the abundance of the functions and achievements of Qian and Kun, and thereby traces them to the marvel of their purposelessness. Indeed, in directing beginnings and acting to complete things, the functions and achievements of Qian and Kun are abundant; yet they do not go beyond ease and simplicity—are they not bringing about transformation without conscious purpose? Moreover, encompassing the myriad things without omission is the complete achievement of Heaven and Earth; stirring the myriad things without anxiety is the supreme virtue of Heaven and Earth. Those who are skilled at observing the creative transformations of nature need only observe them in this. Why is this so? Things must have a beginning—who begins them? Only Qian possesses the Way of Heaven; it does not merely form the male. The transformations prior to Heaven are governed by it; thus it manifests benevolence out of the surplus of its hidden function, and the myriad existences show the first signs of…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
開先之漸矣乾非知大始乎物必有成其孰成
之惟坤有地道不特成女已也後天之化賛於
是焉則效法於成象之後而庶類獲各足之休
矣坤非作成物乎夫物莫難於創始而乾盡物
以始之若甚難矣不知乾健而動者也健則發
之者無停機動則出之者有餘力故時至機行
所以鼓萬物之出者自沛然莫之能禦也觀於
其易而主始之妙不可知耶事莫煩於作成而
坤盡物以成之若甚煩矣不知坤順而静者也
===
順則恒委夫獨運之權静則惟守其代終之義
故承天時行所以斂萬物之入者自隤然不見
其迹也觀於其簡而作成之妙不可知耶夫生
成異用者兩之所以化也易簡合德者一之所
以神也神化合一而乾坤寧復有餘藴哉雖然
乾坤者易書之法象也吾心者易書之精藴也
善學者能以吾心而觀易以易而得乾坤之理
則造化爲徒矣不然易爲粗迹而乾坤與我何
相値哉嗚呼學易者惟於心焉求之
punctuated: 開先之漸矣。乾非知大始乎？物必有成，其孰成之？惟坤有地道，不特成女已也。後天之化賛於是焉，則效法於成象之後，而庶類獲各足之休矣。坤非作成物乎？夫物莫難於創始，而乾盡物以始之，若甚難矣。不知乾健而動者也，健則發之者無停機，動則出之者有餘力，故時至機行，所以鼓萬物之出者，自沛然莫之能禦也。觀於其易，而主始之妙不可知耶？事莫煩於作成，而坤盡物以成之，若甚煩矣。不知坤順而静者也，順則恒委夫獨運之權，静則惟守其代終之義，故承天時行，所以斂萬物之入者，自隤然不見其迹也。觀於其簡，而作成之妙不可知耶？夫生成異用者，兩之所以化也；易簡合德者，一之所以神也。神化合一，而乾坤寧復有餘藴哉！雖然，乾坤者，易書之法象也；吾心者，易書之精藴也。善學者能以吾心而觀易，以易而得乾坤之理，則造化爲徒矣。不然，易爲粗迹，而乾坤與我何相値哉！嗚呼！學易者，惟於心焉求之。
translation_en:
…the gradual unfolding of their inception. Does not Qian then "direct the great beginnings"? Things must have a completion; what is it that completes them? Only Kun possesses the Way of Earth, and it does not merely form the female. The transformations that succeed Heaven's initiative are assisted here; thus, by modeling itself after the forms have been manifested, the myriad categories of beings obtain the blessing of each being fully sufficed. Does not Kun then "bring things to completion"?

Now, among things nothing is more difficult than initiating a beginning, and since Qian initiates all things without exception, it would seem exceedingly difficult. Yet one fails to realize that Qian is vigorous and active. Being vigorous, that which it issues forth knows no pausing of its mechanism; being active, that which it brings out possesses a surplus of strength. Therefore, when the season arrives and the mechanism moves, that whereby it stirs the emergence of the myriad things flows forth copiously of itself, so that nothing can check it. Observing its "easiness," can one not understand the subtlety of its presiding over beginnings? Among affairs nothing is more繁 (laborious) than bringing things to completion, and since Kun completes all things without exception, it would seem exceedingly laborious. Yet one fails to realize that Kun is compliant and tranquil. Being compliant, it constantly entrusts the authority of sole operation [to Qian]; being tranquil, it simply abides by the principle of bringing work to completion on another's behalf. Therefore, acting at the proper time in compliance with Heaven, that whereby it gathers in the retreat of the myriad things proceeds with effortless docility of itself, leaving no trace to be seen. Observing its "simplicity," can one not understand the subtlety of its bringing things to completion?

Now, that generation and completion differ in their functions is how the Two carry out transformation; that easiness and simplicity unite in their virtue is how the One achieves spiritual wonder. When spiritual wonder and transformation unite as one, how could Qian and Kun possibly have any further hidden reserves left over! Even so, Qian and Kun are the model-images of the Book of Changes (Yi), whereas our own mind is the essential subtlety of the Book of Changes. One who excels at learning is able to observe the Changes through his own mind, and through the Changes to grasp the principle of Qian and Kun; then he becomes a companion to the creative transformations of nature. Otherwise, the Changes remain mere coarse traces, and what have Qian and Kun to do with me! Alas! Let those who study the Changes seek it only within the mind.

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
書
野無遺賢萬邦咸寧
曹思聰
同考試官教諭涂　批〔講不費詞而題意發明殆盡豈凡筆可到〕
考試官教諭王　批〔以知人安民立說得帝舜推言之旨〕
考試官學正任　批〔體裁整飭詞致秀雅〕
賢盡用而民舉安克艱之效也蓋用賢安民治
===
道之大端也羣賢舉而萬邦寧克艱之效何如
哉帝舜因禹陳謨而推言其效如此若曰君臣
之相與也豈徒然哉凡以爲知人安民計也信
能克致其艱豈止嘉言之罔伏耶彼賢者俟特
于野嘗闢四門以來之矣然未必其無遺也今
惟克艱則君純心于上矣臣引類于下矣由是
切帝臣之思者共立于明良之朝懷奮庸之具
者同升于喜起之會或以修政或以長民濟濟
然九德咸事也覩于野而猶謂側陋之未揚者
punctuated:
書
「野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。」
曹思聰
同考試官教諭涂　批〔講不費詞，而題意發明殆盡，豈凡筆可到。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔以知人、安民立說，得帝舜推言之旨。〕
考試官學正任　批〔體裁整飭，詞致秀雅。〕
賢盡用而民舉安，克艱之效也。蓋用賢、安民，治道之大端也。羣賢舉而萬邦寧，克艱之效何如哉！帝舜因禹陳謨，而推言其效如此。若曰：君臣之相與也，豈徒然哉？凡以爲知人、安民計也。信能克致其艱，豈止嘉言之罔伏耶？彼賢者俟特于野，嘗闢四門以來之矣，然未必其無遺也。今惟克艱，則君純心于上矣，臣引類于下矣。由是切帝臣之思者，共立于明良之朝；懷奮庸之具者，同升于喜起之會。或以修政，或以長民，濟濟然九德咸事也。覩于野，而猶謂側陋之未揚者，
translation_en:
Book of Documents (Shu)
"There will be no neglected worthies in the wilds, and all the myriad states will enjoy peace."
Cao Sicong 曹思聰
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Tu 涂 comments: [The exposition wastes no words, yet brings out the meaning of the theme almost completely—how could an ordinary brush attain this?]
Examiner and County Director of Studies Wang 王 comments: [By framing the argument around knowing men and giving peace to the people, it captures the purport of Emperor Shun's extended reasoning.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Ren 任 comments: [The structure is orderly and disciplined; the phrasing and style are refined and graceful.]

When the worthy are all employed and the people are entirely at peace, such is the efficacy of being able to recognize the difficulty of one's duties. Indeed, employing the worthy and giving peace to the people are the great fundamentals of the way of governance. When all the worthies are elevated and the myriad states enjoy peace, how great is the efficacy of recognizing the difficulty of one's duties! Because Yu 禹 set forth his counsels, Emperor Shun 舜 deduced and spoke of its efficacy in this way. It is as if he said: When sovereign and minister join together, is it in vain? Everything is done for the sake of knowing men and giving peace to the people. If they can truly recognize the full difficulty of their duties, will the result merely be that fine words are not hidden away? Those worthies awaiting exceptional appointment in the wilds—previously the four gates were thrown open to attract them, yet it was not certain that none were left behind. Now, solely through recognizing the difficulty of their duties, the sovereign maintains a pure heart above, and the ministers draw in their own kind below. Consequently, those who earnestly long to be the Emperor's servants stand together in the court of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers; those who possess the wherewithal to exert themselves in meritorious service ascend together at a time of joyful and vigorous endeavor. Some cultivate governance, while others preside over the people; in dignified abundance, the practitioners of all nine virtues are in service. Looking out into the wilds, to still say that men of obscure and humble station have not been raised up…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
無矣蓋朝廷不以易心待天下之賢而賢者忍
自負明時乎萬邦望治于我嘗咨四岳以安之
矣然未必其咸寧也今惟克艱則君奉天子民
矣臣行君之令矣由是交泰以播休風所在露
樂利之澤協恭以昌理道敷天頌熙皡之仁政
無不若德無不懷雍雍乎太和充溢也邦有萬
而猶有一民之怨咨者無矣蓋朝廷不以易心
擾天下之民而民生有不獲自遂乎吁無遺賢
則知人哲矣萬邦寧則安民惠矣克艱之效豈
===
其微哉嘗觀元愷登庸四方風動有虞之治不
啻足矣而舜禹猶拳拳克艱之謨蓋羣賢彙征
尤小人易伺之會而大猷之世民生有隱憂焉
況象庸之典未格于庶頑而有苗弗率猶爲有
外之化乎虞廷君臣蓋非過計也噫此治之所
以益隆也
小大之臣咸懷忠良其侍御僕從罔匪正
人以旦夕承弼厥辟
雷益
punctuated:
無矣。蓋朝廷不以易心待天下之賢，而賢者忍自負明時乎？萬邦望治于我，嘗咨四岳以安之矣，然未必其咸寧也。今惟克艱，則君奉天子民矣，臣行君之令矣。由是交泰以播休風，所在露樂利之澤；協恭以昌理道，敷天頌熙皡之仁。政無不若，德無不懷，雍雍乎太和充溢也，邦有萬而猶有一民之怨咨者無矣。蓋朝廷不以易心擾天下之民，而民生有不獲自遂乎？吁！無遺賢，則知人哲矣；萬邦寧，則安民惠矣。克艱之效，豈其微哉！嘗觀元愷登庸，四方風動，有虞之治不啻足矣；而舜、禹猶拳拳克艱之謨。蓋羣賢彙征，尤小人易伺之會；而大猷之世，民生有隱憂焉。況象庸之典未格于庶頑，而有苗弗率，猶爲有外之化乎？虞廷君臣，蓋非過計也。噫！此治之所以益隆也。

小大之臣咸懷忠良，其侍御僕從罔匪正人，以旦夕承弼厥辟。
雷益
translation_en:
…there are none. For when the court does not treat the worthy men of the empire with a careless heart, how could those worthy men bear to fail such an enlightened age? The myriad states look to us for good governance; we have already consulted the Four Peaks to bring them peace, yet it was not certain that all of them were tranquil. Now, simply by appreciating the difficulty of our responsibilities, the ruler serves Heaven and treats the people as his children, and the ministers carry out the ruler's commands. Consequently, in harmonious communion they spread a fine moral influence, so that everywhere the blessings of joy and benefit are manifest; with united reverence they make the way of order flourish, so that under all Heaven people praise their serene and radiant benevolence. There is no governance that is not compliant, and no virtue that fails to win allegiance; in harmonious concord, supreme harmony overflows, and among the myriad states there is not a single commoner left to complain or sigh. For when the court does not disturb the people of the empire with a careless heart, how could the people fail to fulfill their livelihoods? Ah! When no worthy men are left neglected, that is wisdom in knowing men; when the myriad states are at peace, that is kindness in giving rest to the people. How could the efficacy of appreciating the difficulty of one's task be slight?

When we observe how the Eight Worthies (ba yuan 八元) and Eight Harmonizers (ba kai 八愷) were promoted and employed, and how the four quarters were moved as by the wind, the governance of the Yu 虞 court was more than sufficient; yet Shun 舜 and Yu 禹 still clung earnestly to the counsel of appreciating the difficulty of their responsibilities. This was because the gathering advance of a multitude of worthies is precisely the moment when petty men most easily lie in wait for an opening, and even in an age of grand achievements, the people's livelihood holds hidden worries. How much more so when the statutory emblems of robes and carriages had not yet reformed the顽 [obstinate] multitude, and the ruler of the Miao 苗 was still disobedient, remaining outside the reach of civilizing transformation? The ruler and ministers of the Yu court were certainly not being overly anxious in their calculations. Alas! This was why their governance grew ever more prosperous.

"All his ministers, great and small, cherished loyalty and goodness; his attendants,御 [charioteers/grooms], and personal servants were none of them other than upright men, who morning and night waited upon and assisted their sovereign."
Lei Yi 雷益

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭涂　批〔此題乎講殊非獨此篇起處崩歸重近臣而末講更有警句讀之令人醒目〕
考試官教諭王　批〔清氣逼人自是妙手〕
考試官學正任　批〔簡潔爽朗〕
聖世得人之盛猶藉近臣以養德焉夫人君之
德惟在所養也以文武之得人而猶藉于近臣
如此况後世乎穆王命伯冏之意若曰人君以
一身而立于臣人之上擇人其先務也近臣其
尤要也我觀文武而知所重矣蓋聰明齊聖既
===
開聖作之期而小臣大臣自極一時之選列爵
雖不同而忠植于天者有同懷焉精白承休畢
效乎奉公之節受任雖不一而願爲良臣者無
異懷焉靖恭體國各殫乎毗主之忱夫臣而忠
良所以承弼厥辟者至矣雖無待于近臣可也
乃當時之爲侍御僕從者又皆簡于迪知之日
而非僻之罔干朝夕于王宮若胥倡于忠焉所
以詔其娛而格其非者無時非正人之助也得
于忱恂之餘而憸邪之自遠出入乎禁闥若胥

Associate Examiner Instructor Tu comments: [Flatly expounding on this topic is quite wrong; only this essay right from the opening [?] places the main emphasis on close attendants, and the concluding exposition has even more striking lines that catch the eye upon reading.]
Examiner Instructor Wang comments: [A pure vitality presses upon the reader; naturally a masterly hand.]
