Even with the flourishing abundance of talent obtained in a sage age, one still relied on close attendants to nourish virtue. Now, the virtue of a ruler lies entirely in how it is nourished. If even with the talent obtained by Kings Wen and Wu, they still relied upon close attendants like this, how much more so in later ages! The purport of King Mu's charge to Bo Jiong was as if to say: A ruler stands as a single person above his ministers and people; selecting men is his foremost task, and selecting close attendants is especially crucial. Looking at Kings Wen and Wu, I know where the emphasis lies. For their intelligence, perspicacity, and sagely perfection had already inaugurated an era of sagely creation, and the lesser and greater ministers naturally represented the very finest selection of the age. Though their noble ranks differed, their heaven-implanted loyalty was a shared sentiment; in pure rectitude they received the royal grace, fully devoting themselves to the integrity of public service. Though the charges they received were not uniform, their desire to be good ministers was an identical sentiment; in quiet reverence they identified with the state, each exhausting his sincerity in assisting the sovereign. Now, when ministers are loyal and good, that whereby they attend and correct their sovereign is already complete, so that even without relying on close attendants it would suffice. Yet those who served as attendants and grooms in those days were also all selected at a time of enlightened understanding, so that nothing improper or depraved could intrude; morning and evening in the royal palace, it was as if all led one another in loyalty, and thus in guiding his pleasures and rectifying his faults, there was no time without the assistance of upright men. title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
率干良焉所以美則承而違則弼者隨處皆大
君之資也蓋外臣之勢隔無由效其旦夕之勤
近臣之情親得以廣其薰陶之益故于今頌文
武之盛而遡近臣之功不可誣也以予弗類視
文武爲何如者承弼之責非近臣疇望哉抑考
綴衣武賁列于三事膳夫寺人隸于太宰古之
明君良佐慎于玆選者誠以外庭顯諍較之潛
孚禁近難易蓋什伯矣不然克終允德豈必處
仁遷義而敬義之主固基于不泄邇乎賈生云
習與善人居欲使其爲不善不可得已蓋與伯
冏之書相發與
===
詩
南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子福履成之
王守禮
同考試官訓導石　批
〔塲中作者類多浮泛此篇講樂只及成之俱用本色語形容至咏嘆餘休及於開大運祚尤見學識〕
敬羨
考試官教諭王　批
〔詞理溫然得風人渾厚之體〕
punctuated:
率干良焉，所以美則承而違則弼者，隨處皆大君之資也。蓋外臣之勢隔，無由效其旦夕之勤；近臣之情親，得以廣其薰陶之益。故于今頌文、武之盛，而遡近臣之功，不可誣也。以予弗類，視文、武爲何如者？承弼之責，非近臣疇望哉？抑考綴衣、武賁列于三事，膳夫、寺人隸于太宰，古之明君良佐慎于玆選者，誠以外庭顯諍較之潛孚禁近，難易蓋什伯矣。不然，克終允德豈必處仁遷義，而敬義之主固基于不泄邇乎？賈生云：「習與善人居，欲使其爲不善，不可得已。」蓋與《伯冏》之書相發與！

詩
「南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。」
王守禮
同考試官訓導石　批：〔塲中作者類多浮泛，此篇講「樂只」及「成之」，俱用本色語形容，至咏嘆餘休及於開大運祚，尤見學識。〕敬羨。
考試官教諭王　批：〔詞理溫然，得風人渾厚之體。〕
translation_en:
… lead one another in goodness [reading 干 as 于]; thus, in upholding his virtues and correcting his faults, everywhere they served as an aid to the great sovereign. For outer officials are separated from him by position and have no way to render service morning and evening, whereas close attendants are intimate in feeling and are able to broaden the benefits of their moral influence. Therefore, when today we praise the flourishing age of Kings Wen and Wu and trace back the merits of their close attendants, those merits cannot be denied. Unworthy as I am, how do I compare with Kings Wen and Wu? For the responsibility of assisting and correcting me, upon whom should I rely if not my close attendants?”

Moreover, if we examine how the Keeper of the Robes and the Palace Guards were ranked alongside the Three Ducal Ministers, and how the Grand Provisioner and the Eunuchs were subordinated to the Grand宰 (Minister of State), we see that when wise rulers and good chief ministers of antiquity were so careful in selecting these personnel, it was truly because open remonstrance from the outer court, when compared with quiet moral influence within the palace precincts, is ten or a hundred times more difficult. Otherwise, why would “bringing sincere virtue to completion” necessarily depend on “dwelling in benevolence and moving toward righteousness,” and why would a sovereign of reverence and righteousness indeed lay his foundation in “not being overly familiar with those who are near”? Master Jia [Jia Yi 賈誼] said: “When one is accustomed to living with good men, even if you wished to make him do evil, it could not be done.” Does this not mutually illuminate the document “Bo Jiong” [Charge to Jiong 囧命 in the Book of Documents]?

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
“In the south there are trees with drooping branches, and the creepers and vines entwine them. Happy be our lord [or princely lady], may dignity and fortune bring her to completion.”
By Wang Shouli 王守禮.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Shi: [Most writers in the examination hall tended to be superficial and vague. In explaining “happy be” and “bring to completion,” this essay uses authentic, natural language throughout to describe them; and where it sings the praises of lingering blessings extending to the opening up of a great dynastic destiny, it especially shows erudition and insight.] With respectful admiration.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang: [Its diction and reasoning are gentle and warm, capturing the generous and profound style of the poets of the Airs.]

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正任　批　通篇無一閑語當是作手
詩人與君子之德而以全福願之其所感深矣
夫福以成而全也后妃以德獲之其成之宜矣
斯爲全福乎此衆妾有感而稱願之曰天道祐
德和氣致祥君子之德至矣豈惟福履綏之將
之已哉彼南有樛木若或俯而就也而葛藟縈
之自將依而附焉况我君子幽閑之性植於天
者既純慈愛之心及於人也甚溥吾嘗於始至
而友之矣謂其爲好逑爾已顧逮下之恩施於
===
貫魚不圖可友之至於斯也於既見而樂之矣
謂其爲母儀爾已顧同行之惠廣於羣居不圖
可樂之至於斯也如是而福有不成乎以正中
宫此可以言福履矣然非止一身已也芣苢樂
焉桃夭宜焉王化成於二南與君福之攸降媲
美也餘休所被吾人且求賴之矣豈天將開靈
長之運而特爲厚其祉耶以聽内治此可以爲
福履矣然非止一時已也螽斯徵焉麟趾應焉
王瑞成於百世與君福之聿懷匹休也餘慶所
punctuated:
考試官學正任　批：通篇無一閑語，當是作手。

詩人與君子之德，而以全福願之，其所感深矣。夫福以成而全也，后妃以德獲之，其成之宜矣，斯爲全福乎！此衆妾有感而稱願之曰：天道祐德，和氣致祥，君子之德至矣，豈惟福履綏之、將之已哉？彼南有樛木，若或俯而就也，而葛藟縈之，自將依而附焉。况我君子幽閑之性，植於天者既純；慈愛之心，及於人也甚溥。吾嘗於始至而友之矣，謂其爲好逑爾已，顧逮下之恩施於貫魚，不圖可友之至於斯也；於既見而樂之矣，謂其爲母儀爾已，顧同行之惠廣於羣居，不圖可樂之至於斯也。如是而福有不成乎？以正中宫，此可以言福履矣，然非止一身已也。芣苢樂焉，桃夭宜焉，王化成於二南，與君福之攸降媲美也，餘休所被，吾人且求賴之矣，豈天將開靈長之運，而特爲厚其祉耶？以聽内治，此可以爲福履矣，然非止一時已也。螽斯徵焉，麟趾應焉，王瑞成於百世，與君福之聿懷匹休也，餘慶所
translation_en:
Examiner Ren, Subprefectural Director of Studies, comments: "Throughout the entire piece there is not a single superfluous word; this must be the work of a skilled hand."

The poet praises the virtue of the noble lady and wishes her complete blessings, having been deeply moved by her. Now, blessings become complete through fulfillment; since the queen consort obtains them through her virtue, it is only fitting that they are fulfilled—is this not complete blessing! Thus the many concubines, moved by her, praise and wish her well, saying: The Way of Heaven aids virtue, and a harmonious atmosphere brings about auspiciousness. The virtue of our noble lady is supreme! How could dignified blessings merely comfort her and sustain her, and nothing more? In the south there are trees with drooping branches, as if bending down to accommodate what is below, and the葛 and 藟 vines twine around them, naturally leaning upon and attaching themselves to them. How much more so with our noble lady: her serene and tranquil nature, implanted by Heaven, is already pure, and her compassionate and loving heart reaches others most broadly. When she first arrived, we befriended her with music, thinking only that she was a fine mate for our lord; yet as her grace extending to inferiors was bestowed upon us like a string of fish in orderly progression, we never imagined she would be so worthy of friendship as this! After we had seen her, we rejoiced in her, thinking only that she was a model of maternal deportment; yet as the kindness of her companionship spread widely among us all dwelling together, we never imagined she would bring such joy as this! Being thus, how could her blessings fail to be fulfilled? By rectifying the central palace, this may already be called dignified blessing, yet it does not stop with her own person alone. The gatherers of plantain rejoice in "Fuyi," the young brides harmonize their households in "Taoyao," and the royal transformation is accomplished throughout the two "Nan" sections, matching in beauty the descent of our lady's blessings. Where her surplus grace extends, we ourselves shall seek to rely upon it—could it be that Heaven is about to inaugurate an era of enduring longevity, and therefore specially enriches her felicity? By governing the inner quarters, this may already be considered dignified blessing, yet it does not stop with a single age alone. Prolific descendants are evidenced in "Zhongsi," noble offspring respond in "Linzhi," and royal auspiciousness is fulfilled for a hundred generations, equaling in splendor the blessings our lady draws to herself. title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
及吾人將竝受之矣豈天將大姬籙之傳而特
爲隆其祚耶是知樂只一樛木也福履一葛藟
也觀風人之咏而感應之理可誣哉抑妃匹之
際生民之始萬福之原故讀樛木之詩而知后
妃之感人深也由是小星進御江沱悔迎舉南
國皆樛木之風矣然必有徽柔之聖而後成樂

及，吾人將竝受之矣，豈天將大姬籙之傳而特爲隆其祚耶？是知「樂只」，一樛木也；「福履」，一葛藟也。觀風人之咏，而感應之理可誣哉！抑妃匹之際，生民之始，萬福之原，故讀《樛木》之詩，而知后妃之感人深也。由是《小星》進御，《江沱》悔迎，舉南國皆《樛木》之風矣。然必有徽柔之聖，而後成樂只之賢，成周八百有道之長，不有由哉！

Thus we know that "rejoicing in her" is just like the trees with down-curving branches, and "happiness and dignity" are just like the creepers and vines. Looking at the balladeer's song, how can the principle of stimulus and response be denied! Moreover, the relationship between royal consorts is the beginning of the people and the source of ten thousand blessings. Therefore, upon reading the ode "Trees with Down-Curving Branches" (Jiumu), one knows how deeply the Queen Consort moved people. From this, the concubines in "Small Stars" (Xiaoxing) advanced to attend the lord, and the bride in "The Jiang and the Tuo" (Jiang Tuo) repented and welcomed her companion; the entire southern states were imbued with the ethos of "Trees with Down-Curving Branches." Yet there must first be a sage of admirable gentleness before the worthiness of one who brings joy can be achieved. Did not the eight-hundred-year virtuous longevity of Established Zhou have its cause in this!

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
布在方冊者可考而知也文考有安民之典而
貽于子孫者可循而治也我則幸家法之具存
儀式而不愆凡周南召南之美意皆行之爲定
保之徵幸治法之大備儀刑而不忘凡治岐治
豐之良猷皆守之爲敷錫之凖惠鮮鰥寡典之
所以怙西土也舉而行之日綏四方以惠鮮之
澤而不使之顛連也懷保小民典之所以和有
夏也率而由之日與四方以懷保之仁而必使
之輯寧也幅幀至廣也舉斯典以康濟之則家
===
法之宋遠而四方爲綱之治可期矣以此纘緒
庶克繼其求寧之志也豈專於將享之文乎民
生至衆也推斯典以漸被之則治法之昭明而
四方爲則之化有終矣以此紹述是適慰其觀

translation_en: …what is set forth in the records on wooden and bamboo tablets can be examined and known; our Accomplished Father possessed the statutes for bringing peace to the people, and what was bequeathed to his descendants can be followed to achieve good governance. I am fortunate that the family norms are fully preserved; taking them as models without error, all the fine intentions of the "Zhounan" and "Shaonan" [odes] are put into practice as evidence of stability and protection. I am fortunate that the methods of governance are grandly complete; taking them as patterns without forgetting, all the excellent plans from the governance of Qi and Feng are upheld as standards for廣泛 bestowing blessings. Showing kindness to the destitute, the widower, and the widow was how his statutes sheltered the Western Lands; raising and implementing them, we daily pacify the four quarters with the grace of kindness to the destitute, never allowing them to fall into distress and helplessness. Cherishing and protecting the common people was how his statutes harmonized the Chinese states; following and abiding by them, we daily grant the four quarters the benevolence of cherishing and protecting, ensuring that they are brought to harmony and tranquility. The realm's territory is vast indeed! By raising these statutes to bring peace and relief to it, the family norms will be carried far [? 宋遠], and the governance that serves as the guiding cord for the four quarters can be anticipated. Continuing the line of succession in this manner, we may perhaps succeed in carrying on his ambition to seek tranquility; how could it consist merely in the outward forms of presenting offerings? The multitude of the people is numerosos indeed! By extending these statutes so that they gradually reach them, the methods of governance will be made radiantly clear, and the transformation that serves as the model for the four quarters will be brought to completion. Carrying on his legacy in this manner precisely comforts his heart's desire to see accomplishment; can we not then trust in the constancy of our bright communion with his spirit? Therefore, when our Accomplished Father assists and accepts, Heaven's disposition can be known as well. How true a way the Zhou king [? 周上] had in reaching his ancestor! Moreover, this is the way of benevolence and filial piety. When filial piety does not go against one's parent, benevolence does not go against Heaven. In the sacrifice of the "Wo jiang" [ode], certainty is sought not from Heaven, but from imitating his statutes—this can truly be called serving one's parent as one serves Heaven! With the four quarters daily brought to peace, did not supreme harmony reside throughout the universe of completion-era Zhou? Alas! Had the…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之子孫永守文王之典周至今存可也
春秋
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉〔僖公元年〕
秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰
遂伐楚次于陘
楚屈完來盟于師盟于召陵
齊人執陳轅濤塗
秋及江人黃人伐陳
冬十有二月公孫茲帥師會齊人宋人衛人鄭人許人曹人侵陳〔俱僖公四年〕
===
劉宇
同考試官學正劉　批〔桓仲方與楚盟而遂加於陳驕溢甚矣此篇以始勤終怠譏之當爲確論〕
考試官教諭王　批〔詞嚴義正桓仲當自心服〕
考試官學正任　批〔文有斷制可錄〕
霸者始勤而終怠春秋所不予也此見齊桓服
楚之勤而加于陳者則甚悖矣欲無譏得乎嘗
punctuated:
之子孫永守文王之典，周至今存可也。

《春秋》
「八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。」〔僖公元年〕
「秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。」〔僖公三年〕
「春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。」
「楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。」
「齊人執陳轅濤塗。」
「秋，及江人、黃人伐陳。」
「冬，十有二月，公孫茲帥師會齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭人、許人、曹人侵陳。」〔俱僖公四年〕

劉宇
同考試官學正劉　批：〔桓、仲方與楚盟，而遂加於陳，驕溢甚矣。此篇以始勤終怠譏之，當爲確論。〕
考試官教諭王　批：〔詞嚴義正，桓、仲當自心服。〕
考試官學正任　批：〔文有斷制，可錄。〕

霸者始勤而終怠，《春秋》所不予也。此見齊桓服楚之勤，而加于陳者則甚悖矣，欲無譏得乎？嘗
translation_en:
… descendants had forever preserved the statutes of King Wen, the Zhou dynasty could well have endured to this very day.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In the eighth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and an envoy of Zhu at Cheng." [First year of Duke Xi]
"In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, an envoy of Jiang, and an envoy of Huang met at Yanggu." [Third year of Duke Xi]
"In spring, in the King's first month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to make an incursion into Cai. Cai collapsed in rout, whereupon they attacked Chu and halted at Xing."
"Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army; they covenanted at Shaoling."
"The men of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen."
"In autumn, together with the men of Jiang and the men of Huang, we attacked Chen."
"In winter, in the twelfth month, Gongsun Zi led a force to join the men of Qi, the men of Song, the men of Wei, the men of Zheng, the men of Xu, and the men of Cao in making an incursion into Chen." [All from the fourth year of Duke Xi]

Liu Yu 劉宇
Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies (Xuezheng) Liu: [Just after Duke Huan and Guan Zhong had made a covenant with Chu, they immediately turned their aggression against Chen—their arrogance and excess were extreme! This essay censures them for being diligent at the start and lax at the end, which may rightly be considered a definitive judgment.]
Comment by Examiner and District Director of Schools (Jiaoyu) Wang: [The diction is stern and the reasoning upright; Duke Huan and Guan Zhong themselves would have to submit in their hearts.]
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies Ren: [The essay shows decisive judgment and is worthy of inclusion.]

When a hegemon is diligent at the start yet lax at the end, the Spring and Autumn Annals withholds its approval. Here we see Duke Huan of Qi's diligence in bringing Chu to submission, yet what he subsequently inflicted upon Chen was utterly perverse—how could he possibly escape censure? I have…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
謂霸主之行乎諸侯也不徒始謀之善而貴終
事之臧不徒有匡天下之名而貴有容天下之
量孰意桓仲君臣見不及此方楚人未帖而鄭
患孔殷也于檉有謀諸夏之威振矣而陽穀一
會信復惇于遠人于陘有次文告之詞修矣而
召陵一盟好遂協于敵國此其憂勤惕厲審已
下人念何深而禮何謹也持此心以進善王道
不庶幾哉奈之何楚方盟我不勝其驕溢之私
陳一失謀遽張夫凌虐之慘濤塗執焉若可已
===
也又連兵以問其罪執而伐焉若可已也又掠
境以厚其毒雖軍道之誤法所當懲而國病之
憂情實可憫已則不省而惟人之尤陳已不堪
而怒猶未怠吁亦舛矣吾不知楚人未服之前
何心而楚人既服之後又何心耶蓋量如桓器
如仲能假于取威定霸之日而不能假于外寧
内謐之時恣意妄行不自覺其猖狂至此耳回
視東征而四國是王勝夏而隕淵是懼者何天
壤也哉經于濤塗之執特以人稱罪齊侯也稱
punctuated: 謂霸主之行乎諸侯也，不徒始謀之善，而貴終事之臧；不徒有匡天下之名，而貴有容天下之量。孰意桓、仲君臣見不及此。方楚人未帖而鄭患孔殷也，于檉有謀，諸夏之威振矣，而陽穀一會，信復惇于遠人；于陘有次，文告之詞修矣，而召陵一盟，好遂協于敵國。此其憂勤惕厲、審已下人，念何深而禮何謹也！持此心以進善，王道不庶幾哉？奈之何楚方盟我，不勝其驕溢之私；陳一失謀，遽張夫凌虐之慘。濤塗執焉，若可已也，又連兵以問其罪；執而伐焉，若可已也，又掠境以厚其毒。雖軍道之誤，法所當懲，而國病之憂，情實可憫。已則不省，而惟人之尤；陳已不堪，而怒猶未怠。吁！亦舛矣。吾不知楚人未服之前何心，而楚人既服之後又何心耶？蓋量如桓、器如仲，能假于取威定霸之日，而不能假于外寧内謐之時，恣意妄行，不自覺其猖狂至此耳。回視東征而四國是王、勝夏而隕淵是懼者，何天壤也哉！經于濤塗之執，特以「人」稱，罪齊侯也；稱…
translation_en: …held that in the conduct of a hegemon toward the feudal lords, what is valued is not merely the excellence of his initial planning, but the goodness of how he brings matters to completion; not merely possessing the reputation of rectifying the realm, but possessing the capacity to tolerate the realm. Who would have thought that the ruler and minister, Duke Huan and Guan Zhong, would fail to see this? Just when the people of Chu were not yet submissive and the calamity facing Zheng was most urgent, there was the planning at Cheng, by which the prestige of the Chinese states was roused, and with the single meeting at Yanggu, good faith was once again strengthened with distant peoples; there was the halting of troops at Xing, where the words of the diplomatic declaration were well-crafted, and with the single covenant at Shaoling, amity was thereupon harmonized with a rival state. In this, how anxious, diligent, vigilant, and self-examining they were in humbling themselves before others—how deep was their concern and how circumspect their propriety! Had they maintained this mind to advance toward goodness, would they not have come close to the Kingly Way? How was it that no sooner had Chu made a covenant with us than he could not overcome his selfish arrogance and excess, and as soon as Chen made a single miscalculation in its planning, he suddenly unleashed the cruelty of bullying and oppression? Taotu was seized; it seemed he could have stopped there, yet he again joined forces to call Chen to account for its offense. Having seized him and attacked Chen, it seemed he could have stopped there, yet he again raided its borders to deepen his venom. Although misleading the army's route of march is something the law ought to punish, yet Chen's worry over its state being exhausted was a circumstance truly worthy of pity. He did not examine himself, but only blamed others; Chen could already bear it no longer, yet his anger still did not slacken. Alas, how perverse indeed! I do not know what mind he had before the people of Chu submitted, and what mind he had after the people of Chu had submitted! For with a capacity like Huan's and a vessel like Zhong's, they were able to feign virtue on the day of seizing prestige and establishing hegemony, yet unable to feign it at a time of external peace and internal tranquility; thus they acted willfully and recklessly, not realizing themselves that their unbridled arrogance had reached such an extreme. Looking back by comparison at those who marched east and brought the four quarters to order, or who conquered Xia and felt dread as if on the brink of an abyss—what a difference of heaven and earth! Regarding the seizure of Taotu, the Classic specifically refers to Qi as "people" (ren) in order to condemn the Marquis of Qi; its calling it…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
侵陳者深責之也此此義行無復淺束狹度如唐
莊魏武之爲者垂訓之功大矣哉於乎桓之驕
也以楚服也弦于方城漢水之對楚何嘗帖然
下齊哉況侵蔡而蔡未同勤鄭而鄭巳去荊南
虐焰日甚一日其目中似巳無桓矣何驕之有
雖然尊周攘夷猶幸有召陵之盟在也
春王正月季孫宿叔老會晉士匄齊人宋
人衛人鄭公孫蠆曹人莒人邾人滕人
薛人杞人小邾人會吳于向〔襄公十四年〕
杜本益
===
同考試官學正劉　批〔使介有禮叔老並大□歟□□此作能發明無遺識亦□□在其衍說□斷〕
考試官教諭王　批〔得備詞此□□〕
考試官學正任　批〔深識發後〕
春秋于二臣並使特變文以著其罪焉甚哉使
介之有禮也二臣昧此故春秋罪之向爲會乎
以謀楚也吾聞春秋之例使舉上客季與叔老
punctuated:
侵陳者，深責之也。此此義行，無復淺束狹度如唐莊、魏武之爲者，垂訓之功大矣哉！於乎！桓之驕也，以楚服也。弦于方城、漢水之對，楚何嘗帖然下齊哉？況侵蔡而蔡未同，勤鄭而鄭巳去，荊南虐焰日甚一日，其目中似巳無桓矣，何驕之有？雖然，尊周攘夷，猶幸有召陵之盟在也。

春王正月，季孫宿、叔老會晉士匄、齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭公孫蠆、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人會吳于向。〔襄公十四年〕
杜本益
同考試官學正劉　批〔使介有禮，叔老並大□歟？□□此作能發明無遺，識亦□□，在其衍說□斷。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔得備詞，此□□。〕
考試官學正任　批〔深識發後。〕

《春秋》于二臣並使，特變文以著其罪焉。甚哉，使介之有禮也！二臣昧此，故《春秋》罪之。向爲會乎？以謀楚也。吾聞《春秋》之例，使舉上客，季與叔老
translation_en:
… "invaded Chen" is to censure him deeply. Once this principle is put into practice, there will no longer be narrow-minded and petty actions like those of Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang or Emperor Wu of Wei; how great indeed is its merit in handing down instruction! Alas! Huan's arrogance was because Chu had submitted. Yet looking at [Qu] Wan's [garbled as 弦] reply regarding the Fangcheng mountains and the Han River, when did Chu ever docilely submit to Qi? Moreover, he invaded Cai and Cai did not join him; he labored on behalf of Zheng and Zheng had already departed. The tyrannical flames south of Jing grew fiercer day by day; in their eyes it seemed there was already no Duke Huan—what had he to be arrogant about? Even so, in honoring Zhou and repelling the Yi, it is still fortunate that the covenant of Shaoling remained.

"In spring, in the king's first month, Jisun Su and Shu Lao met with Shi Gai of Jin, a man of Qi, a man of Song, a man of Wei, Gongsun Chai of Zheng, a man of Cao, a man of Ju, a man of Zhu, a man of Teng, a man of Xue, a man of Qi, and a man of Little Zhu to meet Wu at Xiang." [Fourteenth year of Duke Xiang]
By Du Benyi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Liu: [There is ritual propriety between envoy and deputy; were Shu Lao and the other both great [officials?] [?]. This composition is able to elucidate the matter exhaustively; its insight is also [?], lying in its elaboration and [?] judgment.]
Comment by Examiner District Director of Studies Wang: [It achieves complete expression [of the meaning of the text]; this [?].]
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Ren: [Profound insight is brought out in the latter part.]

In the case of two ministers being sent together as envoys, the Spring and Autumn Annals specially alters its wording to make clear their offense. How crucial indeed it is that there is ritual propriety governing the envoy and his deputy! The two ministers were blind to this, and therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns them. Why was there a meeting at Xiang? In order to take counsel against Chu. I have heard that according to the precedent of the Spring and Autumn Annals, in recording a mission only the principal envoy is named. Why then are Jisun [Su] and Shu Lao…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
竝書者何蓋人臣之事君也必體統正而後閫
家之勢常尊必儀位昭而後人臣之分兩得故
卿使則大夫介大夫使則士介茲使人之體一
定而不可移也胡二卿未達此歟一則班序未
明而挾權以自大一則等威弗辨而俛首以相
從季之意豈不曰事大交鄰有邦重務我使而
叔介之無傷也曾不思叔何人哉非與我同爲
魯國之卿者乎竝立于朝廷而降班于壇坫季
何見也乃安于以卿爲介而弗使之免耶叔之
===
意豈不曰通吳制楚中國大事宿使而我介之
無傷也曾不思宿何人哉非與我同秉魯國之
政者乎備位于百乘而自處于三揖叔何見也
乃甘心以介于宿而弗敢避耶要之季可使也
而叔老介焉則外不免于失人君子以爲亢矣
叔可介也而介於宿焉則內不免于失已君子
以爲卑矣脫使在會諸人有能申使介之規而
請魯無勤不識二臣將何辭以對然則今日之
得免于會幸耳雖晉人輕其幣而敬其使何足
punctuated: 竝書者何？蓋人臣之事君也，必體統正而後閫家之勢常尊，必儀位昭而後人臣之分兩得。故卿使則大夫介，大夫使則士介，茲使人之體一定而不可移也。胡二卿未達此歟？一則班序未明，而挾權以自大；一則等威弗辨，而俛首以相從。季之意豈不曰：「事大交鄰，有邦重務，我使而叔介之，無傷也。」曾不思叔何人哉？非與我同爲魯國之卿者乎？竝立于朝廷，而降班于壇坫，季何見也？乃安于以卿爲介，而弗使之免耶？叔之意豈不曰：「通吳制楚，中國大事，宿使而我介之，無傷也。」曾不思宿何人哉？非與我同秉魯國之政者乎？備位于百乘，而自處于三揖，叔何見也？乃甘心以介于宿，而弗敢避耶？要之，季可使也，而叔老介焉，則外不免于失人，君子以爲亢矣；叔可介也，而介於宿焉，則內不免于失已，君子以爲卑矣。脫使在會諸人，有能申使介之規，而請魯無勤，不識二臣將何辭以對？然則今日之得免于會，幸耳！雖晉人輕其幣而敬其使，何足…
translation_en: …are both recorded together—why is this? Indeed, when a minister serves his ruler, the hierarchical system must be rectified before the authority of the state [?] can remain exalted, and ceremonial ranks must be made clear before the proper duties of ministers can be mutually fulfilled. Therefore, when a Chief Minister (qing) goes as envoy, a Grand Master (dafu) serves as his deputy (jie); when a Grand Master goes as envoy, a Servitor (shi) serves as his deputy. This protocol for envoys is fixed and unalterable. How could the two Chief Ministers have failed to understand this? One failed to clarify the order of precedence and presumed upon his power to aggrandize himself; the other failed to distinguish ranks of dignity and bowed his head to follow along. Did not Jisun Su's (季孫宿) thinking go: "Serving a great power and maintaining relations with neighbors are weighty affairs of state; for me to be the envoy and Shulao (叔老) to be my deputy does no harm"? Yet he never paused to consider: who is Shulao? Is he not a fellow Chief Minister of the state of Lu alongside me? They stand as equals at court, yet one is demoted in rank at the diplomatic altar—what was Jisun thinking? How could he comfortably use a Chief Minister as his deputy without excusing him from it? And did not Shulao's thinking go: "Opening relations with Wu to hold Chu in check is a great affair of the Central States; for Su to be the envoy and me to be his deputy does no harm"? Yet he never paused to consider: who is Su? Is he not one who holds the reins of government in the state of Lu alongside me? Holding the rank of a hundred chariots, yet placing himself in the position of advancing at the third bow—what was Shulao thinking? How could he willingly serve as deputy to Su without daring to decline? In sum, Jisun was qualified to be an envoy, but by having Shulao as his deputy, outwardly he could not avoid wronging another, and the gentleman deems him arrogant; Shulao was qualified to be a deputy, but by serving as deputy to Su, inwardly he could not avoiddemeaning himself, and the gentleman deems him base. Suppose that among the participants at the covenant meeting, someone had been able to set forth the regulations governing envoys and deputies and asked Lu not to trouble itself—I do not know with what words the two ministers would have replied! That being so, their managing to escape reproach at the meeting today was sheer luck! Even though the men of Jin treated their gifts lightly while respecting their envoys, how could that suffice to…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
多哉經特竝書于策二臣之罪彰彰明矣嗟夫
人君擅一國之名寵進退出入惟我所制叔季
竝使非也主之者誰歟三軍作而權不在公中
軍舍而季日益肆欲宿之無亢而公室無畀不
可得已叔老何爲噫意中國且覩吳矣列卿且專
會矣奚魯事之足云
禮記
凡爲君使者已受命君言不宿於家
南企仲
===
同考試官教諭薛　批〔格正詞嚴發臣子敬慎專心殆無餘蘊而結復歸重君心尤見體認取之〕
考試官教諭王　批〔簡明古雅宜錄〕
考試官學正任　批〔典則可誦〕
觀使臣奉命之速而其敬可知矣甚矣人臣無
以有已也則夫受命而即行孰非其敬心爲之
哉記曲禮者蓋謂臣道莫大于敬敬君惟本於
心自一心以爲國又一心以顧家則敬始不純
而臣節虧矣凡爲君使者當何如今夫命也者
punctuated:
多哉！經特竝書于策，二臣之罪彰彰明矣。嗟夫！人君擅一國之名寵，進退出入，惟我所制。叔、季竝使，非也，主之者誰歟？三軍作而權不在公，中軍舍而季日益肆，欲宿之無亢而公室無畀，不可得已，叔老何爲？噫！意中國且覩吳矣，列卿且專會矣，奚魯事之足云！

禮記
凡爲君使者，已受命，君言不宿於家。
南企仲
同考試官教諭薛　批〔格正詞嚴，發臣子敬慎專心，殆無餘蘊；而結復歸重君心，尤見體認。取之。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔簡明古雅，宜錄。〕
考試官學正任　批〔典則可誦。〕

觀使臣奉命之速，而其敬可知矣。甚矣，人臣無以有已也！則夫受命而即行，孰非其敬心爲之哉？記《曲禮》者，蓋謂臣道莫大于敬，敬君惟本於心。自一心以爲國，又一心以顧家，則敬始不純，而臣節虧矣。凡爲君使者當何如？今夫命也者，
translation_en:
…be worth praising! By specially recording both of them together in the tablets, the Classic makes the offenses of the two ministers glaringly clear. Alas! The ruler possesses the titles and favors of an entire state; advancement and dismissal, going out and coming in, should be under his sole control. Sending both Shu and Ji as envoys was wrong—yet who was in charge of this decision? Once the three armies were created, authority no longer rested with the duke; once the middle army was abolished, the Ji family grew ever more unrestrained. To wish that Su would not be arrogant and that the ducal house would not cede its power was already impossible; what could Shu Lao do about it? Alas! When one considers that the Central States were about to look up to Wu, and the various ministers were about to conduct interstate meetings on their own authority, how are the affairs of Lu even worth mentioning!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Whenever one serves as an envoy for the ruler, once he has received the command, the ruler's words do not stay overnight at his home."
By Nan Qizhong
Associate Examiner, Instructor Xue, comments: [Its structure is upright and its diction rigorous. It brings out the reverent caution and single-minded devotion of a minister, leaving almost nothing unexpressed; and at the close it returns the emphasis to the ruler's mind, which especially shows personal comprehension. Selected.]
Examiner, Instructor Wang, comments: [Concise, clear, and classically elegant; it ought to be recorded.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Ren, comments: [Canonical in style and worthy of recitation.]

By observing the swiftness with which an envoy carries out his commission, one may know his reverence. Indeed, how true it is that a minister does not regard his person as his own! Thus, in setting out immediately upon receiving a command, what part of this is not driven by a reverent heart? The compiler of the "Summary of the Rules of Propriety" (Quli) meant to say that in the way of a minister, nothing is greater than reverence, and reverence for the ruler is rooted solely in the mind. Once one has one mind to serve the state and yet another mind to look after one's family, reverence ceases to be pure, and ministerial integrity is impaired. How, then, should anyone who serves as an envoy for the ruler conduct himself? Now, a command is that…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
君之所以承天道而鼓舞萬民者也使也者臣
之所以奉君命而致之天下者也當君命未受
之先則吾之家吾之所有也何可以不顧也及
君命已受之後則吾之身迺君之身也胡可以
自私耶殆必念君逸臣勞之分而絲綸下及惟
敬應之弗遑思國爾忘家之義而渙汗方臨斯
欽承之恐後或受命而表正乎萬民則汲汲焉
思以致之民也推其敬事之心即過門不入猶
以爲緩矣尚敢宿之于家乎或受命而輯和乎
===
邦國則遑遑焉思以致之國也即其服勤之念
雖行不俟駕猶以爲後矣尚知家之當恤乎是
何也國爲重則家爲輕緩於家自急於國吾固
諒之素矣况自委質之初而此身此家已捐之
自效矣遲遲吾行可乎哉要之速命正所以敬
命也敬命即所以敬君也否則其不至於辱君
命者幾希雖然唯天子受命於天必爲之君者
正身修德日兢兢焉上畏天命下酌民言凡所
以發號施令者罔有不臧夫然後上天下施自
punctuated: 君之所以承天道而鼓舞萬民者也；使也者，臣之所以奉君命而致之天下者也。當君命未受之先，則吾之家，吾之所有也，何可以不顧也？及君命已受之後，則吾之身，迺君之身也，胡可以自私耶？殆必念君逸臣勞之分，而絲綸下及，惟敬應之弗遑；思國爾忘家之義，而渙汗方臨，斯欽承之恐後。或受命而表正乎萬民，則汲汲焉思以致之民也；推其敬事之心，即過門不入，猶以爲緩矣，尚敢宿之于家乎？或受命而輯和乎邦國，則遑遑焉思以致之國也；即其服勤之念，雖行不俟駕，猶以爲後矣，尚知家之當恤乎？是何也？國爲重則家爲輕，緩於家自急於國，吾固諒之素矣。况自委質之初，而此身此家，已捐之自效矣，遲遲吾行，可乎哉？要之，速命正所以敬命也，敬命即所以敬君也；否則，其不至於辱君命者幾希。雖然，唯天子受命於天，必爲之君者，正身修德，日兢兢焉，上畏天命，下酌民言，凡所以發號施令者，罔有不臧，夫然後上天下施，自
translation_en: … is that by which the ruler upholds the Way of Heaven and rouses the myriad people to action; an embassy is that by which a minister receives the ruler's command and conveys it to the realm. Before the ruler's command has been received, my family is my own possession—how could I not care for it? Yet once the ruler's command has been received, my person is in fact the ruler's person—how could I act out of private interest? Indeed, he must bear in mind the proper distinction between the ruler's ease and the minister's toil, so that when the silken words of the royal decree reach down to him, he has no leisure to do anything but respond with reverence; he must ponder the righteous principle of dedicating oneself to the state and forgetting one's home, so that just as the sovereign's irreversible proclamation arrives, he reverently receives it, fearing only to fall behind. Perhaps he receives a command to set an upright example for the myriad people, and thus anxiously thinks of conveying it to the people; extending his heart of reverent service, even passing by his own door without entering would still seem slow to him—how would he dare to lodge the command at home overnight? Or perhaps he receives a command to bring harmony to the states of the realm, and thus urgently thinks of conveying it to the states; judging by his dedication to diligent service, even setting out without waiting for his carriage to be yoked would still seem belated to him—how would he still be mindful that his family ought to be looked after? Why is this? Because when the state is held as weighty, the family is held as light; being unhurried about one's family naturally comes from being urgent about the state—this I have certainly understood all along. How much more so when, from the very moment one first presented one's pledge of allegiance as a minister, this person and this family were already surrendered in devoted service—how could it be permissible to linger and delay on my way? In sum, acting swiftly upon a command is precisely how one reveres the command, and revering the command is itself how one reveres the ruler; otherwise, rare indeed are those who do not end up disgracing their ruler's command. Even so, only the Son of Heaven receives the Mandate from Heaven. Only when he who acts as ruler rectifies his person and cultivates his virtue, remaining cautious and trembling day by day, revering the Mandate of Heaven above and weighing the words of the people below, so that in all his issuing of orders and commands there is nothing that is not good—only then, modeled on Heaven above and bestowed upon the world below, will there naturally…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
有不行而至不疾而速者在也故曰君命順則
臣有順命有制命之責者其慎諸
天下大定然後正六律和五聲弦歌詩頌
此之謂德音德音之謂樂
張惟任
同考試官教諭薛　批〔發明古樂由盛處純正典雅是〕
〔深於禮者錄之〕
考試官教諭王　批〔氣格簡古〕
考試官學正任　批〔理明詞達可式〕
===
世治而有作古樂之所由名也蓋樂非無因而
強作也聖王當治世而後和樂興焉其斯以爲
盛乎子夏即此以告文侯意豈不曰禮樂本出
於一原君人貴審其所尚王知樂之不同於音
矣抑知其所由作乎是故聖王值大當以正紀
綱而天下至於大定焉則是上有道揆一人建
中和之極下有法守萬邦協底定之休君臣正
於朝舉凡天下之人合者莫不定於義也父子
正於家舉凡天下之恩合者莫不定於仁也斯
punctuated:
有不行而至、不疾而速者在也。故曰：「君命順，則臣有順命。」有制命之責者，其慎諸！

天下大定，然後正六律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌，此之謂德音，德音之謂樂。
張惟任
同考試官教諭薛　批：〔發明古樂由盛處，純正典雅，是深於禮者，錄之。〕
考試官教諭王　批：〔氣格簡古。〕
考試官學正任　批：〔理明詞達，可式。〕

世治而有作，古樂之所由名也。蓋樂非無因而強作也，聖王當治世而後和樂興焉，其斯以爲盛乎！子夏即此以告文侯，意豈不曰：禮樂本出於一原，君人貴審其所尚。王知樂之不同於音矣，抑知其所由作乎？是故聖王值大當，以正紀綱，而天下至於大定焉。則是上有道揆，一人建中和之極；下有法守，萬邦協底定之休。君臣正於朝，舉凡天下之人合者，莫不定於義也；父子正於家，舉凡天下之恩合者，莫不定於仁也。斯
translation_en:
… reaches without walking, and is swift without hurrying. Therefore it is said: "When the ruler's commands are in accordance with right, the ministers will obey the commands." Let those who bear the responsibility of issuing commands be cautious in this!

"When all under Heaven is greatly settled, only then does one rectify the six pitch-standards, harmonize the five tones, and sing the Odes and Hymns to string accompaniment. This is called virtuous sound; virtuous sound is called music." [Classic of Rites, "Record of Music" (Liji, Yueji)]

Zhang Weiren 張惟任
Associate Examiner, Instructor Xue 薛, comments: [He elucidates how ancient music arises from an era of flourishing; pure, orthodox, refined, and elegant—this is someone deeply versed in the Rites. Record it.]
Examiner, Instructor Wang 王, comments: [The spirit and style are concise and antique.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Ren 任, comments: [The reasoning is clear and the diction expressive; it can serve as a model.]

When the world is well-governed and compositions arise, that is whence ancient music derives its name. For music is not forcibly created without cause; only when a sage-king presides over a well-governed world does harmonious music arise therein—is it not for this reason that it is considered flourishing? When Zixia 子夏 spoke of this to Marquis Wen 文侯, was his meaning not to say: Rites and music originally spring from a single source, and one who rules over men must value examining what he esteems. Your Majesty knows that music is not the same as mere sound, but do you also know whence it is created? Therefore, when a sage-king meets with a time of great order, he rectifies the laws and institutions, and all under Heaven reaches a state of great settlement. Thus above, governance is measured by the Way, and the One Man establishes the supreme standard of centrality and harmony; below, the laws are observed, and the myriad states join in the blessings of stabilization. Ruler and minister are rectified at court, so that among all relationships in the world bound by human duty, none fails to be settled in righteousness; father and son are rectified in the family, so that among all relationships in the world bound by affection, none fails to be settled in benevolence. Thus…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
則至禮不讓而天下治矣和樂其可興乎夫然
後審五聲于六律而清濁損益洋洋乎其盈耳
被詩頌于弦歌而抑揚反覆渢渢乎其足聞夫
是音也殆德音之音而今之所謂古樂者播比
之間無非倫理之著而古先聖王所以格神人
和上下者由此其選也其斯以為咸英韶護之
規模乎聲音之變一皆治化之形而自古帝王
所以一天人贊化育者胥此焉出也其斯以為
清廟明堂之氣象乎是則觀德音所由作則紀
===
綱其所急也觀古樂所由名則德化不可誣也
王顧聽之而恐臥焉何哉大抵樂成于治治本
於心唯先王心和則氣和氣和則形和故以此
措之民物則為雍熙之盛治以此見之聲容則
為和平之雅樂否則欲世之大治亦已難矣樂
奚自而和乎故善論樂者固當求于世之治尤
當求夫大聖之心
第貳場
論
punctuated:
則至禮不讓而天下治矣，和樂其可興乎！夫然後審五聲于六律，而清濁損益，洋洋乎其盈耳；被詩頌于弦歌，而抑揚反覆，渢渢乎其足聞。夫是音也，殆德音之音，而今之所謂古樂者。播比之間，無非倫理之著，而古先聖王所以格神人、和上下者，由此其選也，其斯以為咸、英、韶、護之規模乎！聲音之變，一皆治化之形，而自古帝王所以一天人、贊化育者，胥此焉出也，其斯以為清廟、明堂之氣象乎！是則觀德音所由作，則紀綱其所急也；觀古樂所由名，則德化不可誣也。王顧聽之而恐臥焉，何哉？大抵樂成于治，治本於心。唯先王心和則氣和，氣和則形和，故以此措之民物，則為雍熙之盛治；以此見之聲容，則為和平之雅樂。否則，欲世之大治亦已難矣，樂奚自而和乎？故善論樂者，固當求于世之治，尤當求夫大聖之心。

第貳場

論
translation_en:
… then supreme ritual requires no formal yielding and the empire is well governed. May harmonious music then rise up! Only after this are the five notes examined against the six pitch-standards, so that in their clear and turbid tones and their subtractions and additions, how grandly they fill the ears! Odes and hymns are set to strings and song, so that in their rising and falling and their repetitions, how majestically they are worthy of being heard! Now such tones as these are surely the tones of virtuous sound, what is today called ancient music. Between their performance and accompaniment, there is nothing that is not a manifestation of human moral relations; that whereby the ancient sage-kings reached spirits and men and harmonized superiors and inferiors was chosen from this. Is this not the model of the Xian, Ying, Shao, and Hu music? The transformations of sound and tone are one and all the forms of governance and教化 (moral transformation), and that whereby emperors and kings since antiquity have unified Heaven and man and assisted the transforming and nourishing processes of nature all issues forth from this. Is this not thegrand atmosphere of the Pure Temple (Qingmiao) and the Hall of Light (Mingtang)? Thus, if one observes whence virtuous tones arise, the moral and social order is what is most urgent; if one observes whereby ancient music gets its name, moral transformation cannot be falsified. Why is it, then, that Your Majesty listens to it and fears falling asleep?

In general, music is brought to completion through good governance, and governance is rooted in the mind. Only when the former kings' minds were harmonious was their vital energy harmonious, and when their vital energy was harmonious, their outward forms were harmonious. Therefore, when they applied this to the people and things, it became a flourishing rule of harmony and brightness; when they manifested this in sounds and dance movements, it became a refined music of peace and harmony. Otherwise, even to desire that the world be greatly governed is already difficult enough—whence could music become harmonious? Therefore, one who excels at discussing music certainly ought to seek it in the governance of the age, and even more ought to seek it in the mind of the great sage.

Second Session

Discourse (Lun)

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
佐贊乾坤化育之功
彪準
同考試官教諭方　批〔論以均利立說而開闔變化如珠滾盤〕〔觀者眩目驚心謂珠已出盤而珠固自在奇矣奇矣此宇宙〕
內不朽文字藉令陸賈復出當揖讓矣敬服
考試官教諭王　批〔命意遣詞雄渾辯博條貫森然〕
前無古人矣
考試官學正任　批〔玄思雅調詎當以經生視耶〕
天地生聖人以利天下之民而聖人以天地之
===
利利天下天地聖人者交相爲用者也何者天
下之不得其治物之失所也物之不得其所利
之弗均也千金之貲匹夫匹婦相與坐而守之
惟恐或失挈以與人不勝德色彼守之者與與
之者皆一人之利也非治天下之道也蓋萬物
爲體而一夫呰窳則萬物猶疾首矣六合爲家
而野有溝塍則六合猶懸罄矣故恒人利其小
聖人利其大恒人以利爲利聖人以天下爲利
聖人以利與天下而未嘗不獲其利天下受聖
punctuated:
佐贊乾坤化育之功
彪準
同考試官教諭方　批〔論以均利立說，而開闔變化，如珠滾盤。〕〔觀者眩目驚心，謂珠已出盤，而珠固自在。奇矣！奇矣！此宇宙〕內不朽文字，藉令陸賈復出，當揖讓矣，敬服！
考試官教諭王　批〔命意遣詞，雄渾辯博，條貫森然，〕前無古人矣。
考試官學正任　批〔玄思雅調，詎當以經生視耶？〕
天地生聖人以利天下之民，而聖人以天地之利利天下。天地、聖人者，交相爲用者也。何者？天下之不得其治，物之失所也；物之不得其所，利之弗均也。千金之貲，匹夫匹婦相與坐而守之，惟恐或失；挈以與人，不勝德色。彼守之者與與之者，皆一人之利也，非治天下之道也。蓋萬物爲體，而一夫呰窳，則萬物猶疾首矣；六合爲家，而野有溝塍，則六合猶懸罄矣。故恒人利其小，聖人利其大；恒人以利爲利，聖人以天下爲利。聖人以利與天下，而未嘗不獲其利；天下受聖
translation_en:
"[Assisting and Furthering the Transformative and Nurturing Achievement of Heaven and Earth]"

Biao Zhun 彪準

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Fang, comments: 〔This discourse establishes its thesis on equalizing benefit, and its opening, closing, and transitions are like pearls rolling on a tray.〕 〔The reader is dazzled and startled, thinking the pearls have already rolled off the tray, yet the pearls remain right where they are. Marvelous! Marvelous! This is〕 immortal writing within 〔the universe〕. Even if Lu Jia 陸賈 were to appear again, he would have to bow and yield to it. I am filled with admiration!
Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Wang, comments: 〔In conceiving ideas and choosing words, it is vigorous, profound, eloquent, and wide-ranging, with a tightly structured coherence;〕 none of the ancients have surpassed it.
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Ren, comments: 〔With its profound thought and elegant tone, how could one regard its author as a mere examination candidate?〕

Heaven and Earth give birth to the sages in order to benefit the people of the world, and the sages use the benefits of Heaven and Earth to benefit the world. Heaven and Earth and the sages serve one another reciprocally. Why is this? When the world does not attain good governance, it is because things have lost their proper place; when things do not attain their proper place, it is because benefit is not equally distributed. With a fortune of a thousand pieces of gold, a common man and woman sit together guarding it, only fearing lest it be lost; if they take some to give to others, they cannot help wearing a self-satisfied look of benevolence. Both the one who guards it and the one who gives it away are concerned only with the benefit of a single person; this is not the Way of governing the world. Indeed, when the myriad things form a single body, if a single man lives in squalor and misery, it is as though the myriad things all suffer a headache; when the six directions form a single household, if the countryside is divided by ditches and boundary ridges [or: has people dying in ditches], it is as though the six directions were all utterly depleted. Therefore, ordinary people count what is small as benefit, whereas the sages count what is great as benefit; ordinary people take profit itself as benefit, whereas the sages take the whole world as benefit. The sages give benefit to the world, yet they never fail to reap its benefit; the world receives the sages'…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
人之利而未嘗以其利相競天下利之而不以
競汹汹穆穆日用飲食含德之厚溢爲泰和豈
不休哉胡氏以井田爲佐賛乾坤化育之功蓋
言比也夫乾坤旣已化育萬物矣而又舉夫佐
賛之功屬之聖人使聖人無所利於天下卽有
所利於天下而必待聖人之身何益也是故聖
人慮民之饑也爲火食粒食以養之慮民之寒
也爲桑麻布帛以煖之慮其不能相助也爲婚
姻往來以通之慮其不能遠害也爲宮室兵甲
===
以衛之慮其不知好惡也爲禮樂刑政以正之
是數者可以利天下矣然而聖人不能以其身
爲之衣食使之必相助不相遠而齊一其好惡
於是有井田之法井田者所以均天下之利也
語曰天下壤壤皆爲利往天下熙熙皆爲利來
士有不貲之軀而一旦受半通之綸則徇國忘
家不惜捐糜者爲厚祿也武夫悍卒袵金革蹈
白刃不避湯火之難者爲重賞也閭巷少年攻
剽椎埋任俠借名扞文罔者爲厚利也吏舞三
punctuated: 人之利，而未嘗以其利相競。天下利之而不以競，汹汹穆穆，日用飲食，含德之厚，溢爲泰和，豈不休哉！胡氏以井田爲佐賛乾坤化育之功，蓋言比也。夫乾坤旣已化育萬物矣，而又舉夫佐賛之功屬之聖人，使聖人無所利於天下，卽有所利於天下而必待聖人之身，何益也？是故聖人慮民之饑也，爲火食粒食以養之；慮民之寒也，爲桑麻布帛以煖之；慮其不能相助也，爲婚姻往來以通之；慮其不能遠害也，爲宮室兵甲以衛之；慮其不知好惡也，爲禮樂刑政以正之。是數者，可以利天下矣。然而聖人不能以其身爲之衣食，使之必相助、不相遠，而齊一其好惡，於是有井田之法。井田者，所以均天下之利也。語曰：「天下壤壤，皆爲利往；天下熙熙，皆爲利來。」士有不貲之軀，而一旦受半通之綸，則徇國忘家，不惜捐糜者，爲厚祿也；武夫悍卒，袵金革，蹈白刃，不避湯火之難者，爲重賞也；閭巷少年，攻剽椎埋，任俠借名，扞文罔者，爲厚利也；吏舞三
translation_en: … the benefits of the sages, yet never competed with one another over those benefits. When the world benefits from them without competing—harmonious and reverent, going about their daily food and drink, cherishing thick virtue that overflows into supreme harmony—how splendid is that! Master Hu [Hu Yin 胡寅] regarded the well-field system (jingtian 井田) as assisting in the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth; this was speaking of mutual association (bi 比). Now, Heaven and Earth have already transformed and nourished the myriad things, and yet to assign the work of assisting them to the sages—if the sages brought no benefit to the world, or even if they brought benefit to the world yet it had to depend upon the sages' own persons, what good would that be? Therefore, concerned that the people might starve, the sages instituted cooked food and grain meals to nourish them; concerned that the people might suffer from cold, they instituted mulberry, hemp, cloth, and silk to warm them; concerned that they might fail to help one another, they instituted marriage and social intercourse to connect them; concerned that they might fail to keep harm at a distance, they instituted dwellings, weapons, and armor to protect them; concerned that they might not know what to love and hate, they instituted rites, music, punishments, and governance to rectify them. These several measures were sufficient to benefit the world. Yet the sages could not in their own persons provide clothing and food for everyone, nor personally compel them to help one another, keep from estrangement [?], and unify their loves and hates; thus there arose the system of the well-fields. The well-field system is the means by which the benefits of the world are equalized. The proverb says: "All the world bustles to and fro, going after profit; all the world jostles in crowds, coming for profit." That a scholar possesses a body of priceless worth, yet once he receives the ribbon of even a minor seal, devotes himself to the state and forgets his family, not begrudging the sacrifice of his own life, is for the sake of a generous emolument; that martial men and fierce soldiers sleep on metal and leather, tread upon naked blades, and do not shrink from the perils of boiling water and fire, is for the sake of heavy rewards; that youths of the alleys rob and plunder, murder and bury their victims, act as knights-errant to trade on their reputations, and defy the net of the law, is for the sake of rich profit; that clerks manipulate the three-…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
尺飾喜惡以作威福身不免者爲行賂也弋射
漁獵蒙犯霜露馳驅阬谷者爲得味也百家衆
技焦神極思求精其業者爲博糈也夫是亦天
下之利也而聖人不以爲訓懼天下之各以其
利自勝也以利自勝則富無經業而貨無常主
天下逐于末矣逐末者衆必賤農人夫人不務
本而徒爭尺寸之利則大化何由而洽也故聖
人之治莫先於均利均利之政莫先於井田是
創自黃帝而三代遵之者也是故建步立畝正
===
其經界息爭端也六尺爲步步百爲夫夫三爲
屋屋三爲井井一里九夫八家共之協民力也二
十畝爲廬舍春夏居之秋冬則去節其勞也士
工商家受田五口乃當農夫一人平其法也種
必五穀備其災也民年二十受田六十歸田因
其時也七十以上上所養也十歲以下上所長
也十一以上上所疆也是天下之利也而聖人
不使爲天下私有也其取之于民也校數歲之
中以爲常則爲貢一井之地八家各私百畝同
punctuated: 尺，飾喜惡以作威福，身不免者，爲行賂也；弋射漁獵，蒙犯霜露，馳驅阬谷者，爲得味也；百家衆技，焦神極思，求精其業者，爲博糈也。夫是亦天下之利也，而聖人不以爲訓，懼天下之各以其利自勝也。以利自勝，則富無經業，而貨無常主，天下逐于末矣。逐末者衆，必賤農人。夫人不務本，而徒爭尺寸之利，則大化何由而洽也？故聖人之治，莫先於均利；均利之政，莫先於井田。是創自黃帝，而三代遵之者也。是故建步立畝，正其經界，息爭端也；六尺爲步，步百爲夫，夫三爲屋，屋三爲井，井一里九夫，八家共之，協民力也；二十畝爲廬舍，春夏居之，秋冬則去，節其勞也；士工商家受田，五口乃當農夫一人，平其法也；種必五穀，備其災也；民年二十受田，六十歸田，因其時也；七十以上，上所養也；十歲以下，上所長也；十一以上，上所疆也。是天下之利也，而聖人不使爲天下私有也。其取之于民也，校數歲之中以爲常，則爲貢；一井之地，八家各私百畝，同…
translation_en:
… [clerks who manipulate the three-]foot law code, disguising their personal likes and dislikes to wield arbitrary authority and dispense favors, even when they themselves do not escape punishment—do so for bribes; hunters and fishermen who brave frost and dew and gallop through ravines and valleys—do so to obtain delicacies; and practitioners of the hundred schools and myriad crafts who exhaust their spirits and push their thoughts to the limit, striving to perfect their arts—do so to gain a living. Now, these too are benefits of the world, yet the sages did not take them as teachings, fearing that everyone in the world would seek to outdo one another for their own private profit. When people seek to outdo one another for profit, wealth has no regular occupation and goods have no constant owner, so the world pursues secondary occupations. When those who pursue secondary occupations are numerous, farmers will certainly be despised. Now, if people do not attend to the fundamental occupation [agriculture], and merely contend for inches and feet of profit, how then can the great transformation spread harmoniously?

Therefore, in the governance of the sages, nothing takes precedence over equalizing profit; and in the administration of equalizing profit, nothing takes precedence over the well-field system (jingtian 井田). This was initiated by the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) and followed by the Three Dynasties. Thus, establishing paces and setting up acres (mu 畝) to rectify their boundaries was to put an end to causes of dispute. Six feet (chi 尺) made a pace (bu 步), a hundred paces made a plot (fu 夫), three plots made a hamlet (wu 屋), and three hamlets made a well-field (jing 井); a well-field of one square li (里) contained nine plots shared by eight families, which was to harmonize the people's strength. Twenty acres were set aside for field huts, where they dwelt in spring and summer and which they left in autumn and winter, in order to moderate their toil. When families of scholars, artisans, and merchants received land, five mouths were counted as equivalent to one farmer, in order to make the law equitable. Planting always included all five grains, in order to prepare against disasters. The people received land at the age of twenty and returned it at sixty, in accordance with their season of life. Those seventy and older were nourished by the state; those ten and younger were raised by the state; and those eleven and older were urged to work by the state [?]. This was the benefit of the world, yet the sages did not allow it to become the private possession of the world.

As for what they took from the people: comparing the average of several years to establish a constant quota was called the tribute system (gong 貢); on the land of one well-field, each of the eight families held a hundred acres in private while together…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
治公田則爲助不爲公田侯歲之成通以什一
之法助于百畝則爲徹車馬兵甲士旅之役于
焉取之府庫之充賜予之用于焉取之郊社宗
廟百神之祀于焉取之百官之養庶民之費于
焉取之非時者無藝者爲之厲禁是天下之利
也而聖人不以爲私有也天下大利也聖人得
之而不以自利聖人不以自利而亦不欲使天
下之自以爲利天地不與萬物爭利則物得其
平江海不與百川爭利則水得其平聖人不與
===
百姓爭利則民得其平雨露之施皇天主之長
養之功后土主之分田之制聖人主之不假稱
貸而倉庾實不待家給而衣食裕不採樵百里
而俯仰足不負販千里而饔飧少而不困多
而不亂無貪暴併兼之事無流離凍餒之苦無
呼號籲訴之聲衆寡强弱知愚賢不肖各食其
力遂其生不壞植而散羣治之以禮義而民歸
其極矣率之以興事而民從其令矣統之以官
府而民服其政矣斷之以刑威而民奉其法矣
punctuated:
治公田，則爲助；不爲公田，侯歲之成，通以什一之法助于百畝，則爲徹。車馬、兵甲、士旅之役于焉取之；府庫之充、賜予之用于焉取之；郊社、宗廟、百神之祀于焉取之；百官之養、庶民之費于焉取之。非時者、無藝者，爲之厲禁。是天下之利也，而聖人不以爲私有也。

天下，大利也。聖人得之而不以自利；聖人不以自利，而亦不欲使天下之自以爲利。天地不與萬物爭利，則物得其平；江海不與百川爭利，則水得其平；聖人不與百姓爭利，則民得其平。雨露之施，皇天主之；長養之功，后土主之；分田之制，聖人主之。不假稱貸而倉庾實，不待家給而衣食裕，不採樵百里而俯仰足，不負販千里而饔飧，少而不困，多而不亂，無貪暴併兼之事，無流離凍餒之苦，無呼號籲訴之聲。衆寡、强弱、知愚、賢不肖，各食其力，遂其生，不壞植而散羣。治之以禮義，而民歸其極矣；率之以興事，而民從其令矣；統之以官府，而民服其政矣；斷之以刑威，而民奉其法矣；
translation_en:
…cultivate the public field together, this is the “aid” (zhu) system; when no separate public field is set aside, waiting instead for the year’s harvest [reading 侯 as 候] and uniformly levying a tithe of one-tenth as aid from each hundred mu, this is the “all-through” (che) system. From this are drawn the levies for chariots and horses, armor and weapons, and military troops; from this are drawn the provisions for filling the treasuries and storehouses and the expenditures for imperial bestowals; from this are drawn the offerings for the sacrifices at the suburban altars, the altars of soil and grain, the ancestral temple, and to the hundred spirits; and from this are drawn the maintenance of the hundred officials and the expenses for the common people. Anything exacted out of season or without fixed measure is strictly prohibited. This is the benefit of the entire realm, yet the sages did not take it as their own private possession.

The realm is a great benefit. When the sages obtain it, they do not use it to benefit themselves; and just as the sages do not use it to benefit themselves, neither do they wish to let the people of the realm regard it as their own private benefit. When Heaven and Earth do not contend with the myriad things for benefit, all things attain their equilibrium; when the rivers and seas do not contend with the hundred streams for benefit, the waters attain their equilibrium; and when the sages do not contend with the common people for benefit, the people attain their equilibrium. Sovereign Heaven presides over the bestowal of rain and dew; Sovereign Earth presides over the work of nurturing and growth; and the sages preside over the institution of dividing the fields. Without resorting to borrowing at interest, the granaries and bins are full; without waiting for handouts to each household, food and clothing are abundant; without gathering firewood a hundred li away, there is enough to support parents above and wife and children below; and without peddling goods on one’s back a thousand li away, morning and evening meals [are supplied] [?]. Whether the harvest is meager, they are not in distress; whether it is plentiful, they do not fall into disorder. There are no acts of greedy violence or land annexation, no hardships of displacement, freezing, or starvation, and no cries of wailing or desperate appeals. The many and the few, the strong and the weak, the wise and the foolish, the worthy and the unworthy all live by their own labor and fulfill their livelihoods, without ruining their foundations or scattering from their communities. When governed through ritual and righteousness, the people return to the standard of perfection; when led in undertaking enterprises, the people obey the commands; when administered through official bureaus, the people submit to the governance; when adjudicated with the awe of punishments, the people uphold the laws;…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
加之以兵甲而民奮其威矣薄海內外未傳之
夫含生之類戴之如天履之如地環鄉稽首而
稱曰不有聖人則天無全覆地無全載卽所謂
乾坤者亦退然不敢自尸其化育之功諸福之
物可致之祥悉以萃諸聖人之身若曰彼能佐
贊我也是故堯遭九年之水而其洛之民不變
也禹定三壤之賦而昏墊之衆樂輸也湯之旱
七年而荼毒之孽無菜色也文王爲西伯而岐
周之鄙耕讓畔也大生大化比於乾坤協氣旁
===
流休嘉醉隱而聖人所以佐贊之者寧有它指
哉亦曰均利而已矣夫利世儒所諱言也而聖
人先之聖人知民之趨利猶水之就下不可止
也而天爲之立君以防其淫爲之立聖人之君
以平其施故井田行而利均利均而物各得所
物各得所而天下治其効至於贊化育參天地
易曰乾始能以美利利天下不言所利此之謂
也嗟乎乾坤之化育何所不均而必待井田以
佐贊其功是去上古之時遠矣故井田之政歷
punctuated:
加之以兵甲，而民奮其威矣。薄海內外，未傳之夫，含生之類，戴之如天，履之如地，環鄉稽首而稱曰：「不有聖人，則天無全覆，地無全載。」卽所謂乾坤者，亦退然不敢自尸其化育之功。諸福之物，可致之祥，悉以萃諸聖人之身，若曰：「彼能佐贊我也。」是故堯遭九年之水，而其洛之民不變也；禹定三壤之賦，而昏墊之衆樂輸也；湯之旱七年，而荼毒之孽無菜色也；文王爲西伯，而岐周之鄙耕讓畔也。大生大化，比於乾坤，協氣旁流，休嘉醉隱。而聖人所以佐贊之者，寧有它指哉？亦曰均利而已矣。

夫利，世儒所諱言也，而聖人先之。聖人知民之趨利，猶水之就下，不可止也。而天爲之立君以防其淫，爲之立聖人之君以平其施。故井田行而利均，利均而物各得所，物各得所而天下治，其効至於贊化育、參天地。《易》曰：「乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利。」此之謂也。

嗟乎！乾坤之化育何所不均，而必待井田以佐贊其功，是去上古之時遠矣。故井田之政，歷
translation_en:
…When applied to weapons and armor, the people rouse their martial might. Within and beyond the four seas, men not yet registered on the labor rolls [?] and all living creatures revere them as they do Heaven and tread upon their realm as they do Earth; turning toward them from all around, they bow their heads to the ground and declare: "Were it not for the sages, Heaven would not completely shelter us, and Earth would not completely sustain us!" Even what we call Qian and Kun [Heaven and Earth] would modestly step back and not dare to claim for themselves alone the merit of transformation and nurture. All auspicious things and attainable omens of good fortune gather completely upon the person of the sage, as if to say: "He is able to assist and aid us!" Therefore, Yao encountered nine years of floods, yet the people of Qi and Luo [?] did not change their ways; Yu fixed the tribute of the three grades of soil, and the multitudes who had been drowning in distress gladly paid their dues; Tang suffered seven years of drought, yet amid the calamity of bitter affliction the people showed no famished complexion; King Wen served as Earl of the West, and in the borderlands of Qi and Zhou those who plowed yielded the boundary ridges to one another. Great generation and great transformation were comparable to those of Qian and Kun; harmonious qi flowed forth on all sides, and auspicious excellence was richly and deeply present [?]. Yet as for that whereby the sages assisted and aided them, did it have any other aim? It was simply to equalize profit, and nothing more.

Now profit is something the scholars of the age shun speaking of, yet the sages put it first. The sages knew that the people's pursuit of profit is like water flowing downward: it cannot be stopped. Therefore Heaven established rulers for them to prevent their excess, and established sage rulers for them to make even its distribution. Thus, when the well-field system was practiced, profit was equalized; when profit was equalized, all things each found their proper place; when all things each found their proper place, the world was well governed, and its efficacy extended to aiding transformation and nurture and forming a triad with Heaven and Earth. The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Qian, the originating, is able with beauteous profit to benefit the whole world, without saying what it profits." This is what is meant.

Alas! In what respect are the transformation and nurture of Qian and Kun not equal, that they must await the well-field system to assist and aid their work? This shows how far removed things had become from the times of high antiquity. Therefore, the administration of the well-field system passed through…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
數代更數聖至周而後大備豈一日而興耶自
周轍一東而經界不正豪强亂作始開阡陌而
古制蕩然亦豈一日而廢耶井田廢而有代田
限田均田永業之制司田之官分口之業其法
紛紛亂矣於化育何裨耶無亦天地自然之運
不可强耶噫乾坤化育之功至今在也生財富
民之道聖人所以利天下者非一端也有能舉
而行之何必井田哉
表
擬河工告成廷臣
賀表
===
劉宇
同考試官學正劉　批〔河流原非人力能障咸由我〕
皇上一德格天神人受職故不踰春而告成子能推本而揄揚之且文直事核脫去粉粧豈示
竊比子長筆耶
考試官教諭王　批〔沖詞雅調風度灑然〕
考試官學正任　批〔模畫河上光景宛宛目中匠心〕
獨運之妙至是耶奇哉
punctuated:
數代，更數聖，至周而後大備，豈一日而興耶？自周轍一東，而經界不正，豪强亂作，始開阡陌，而古制蕩然，亦豈一日而廢耶？井田廢，而有代田、限田、均田、永業之制，司田之官、分口之業，其法紛紛亂矣，於化育何裨耶？無亦天地自然之運不可强耶？噫！乾坤化育之功，至今在也；生財富民之道，聖人所以利天下者，非一端也。有能舉而行之，何必井田哉！

表

擬河工告成廷臣賀表

劉宇
同考試官學正劉　批：〔河流原非人力能障，咸由我〕皇上一德格天，神人受職，故不踰春而告成。子能推本而揄揚之，且文直事核，脫去粉粧，豈示竊比子長筆耶？
考試官教諭王　批：〔沖詞雅調，風度灑然。〕
考試官學正任　批：〔模畫河上光景，宛宛目中，匠心〕獨運之妙至是耶！奇哉！
translation_en:
… several dynasties and passing through several sages, reaching complete perfection only in the Zhou—how could it have arisen in a single day? Once the Zhou court moved east, field boundaries were no longer rectified, the powerful and unruly arose in disorder, ridges and paths were first opened up, and the ancient system was swept away—how could it have been abolished in a single day either? After the well-field system was abolished, there came the systems of alternating fields (daitian), restricted fields (xiantian), equal-field (juntian), and lands in perpetuity (yongye); with officials in charge of fields and allotments distributed per capita, their methods fell into confused disorder. Of what benefit were they to the transforming and nurturing processes of nature? Is it not that the natural course of Heaven and Earth cannot be forced? Alas! The work of Heaven and Earth in transforming and nurturing remains present to this day, and the way of generating wealth and enriching the people—whereby the sages brought benefit to all under Heaven—does not consist of a single method. If there is someone capable of taking it up and putting it into practice, why must it be the well-field system!

Memorial

Proposed Congratulatory Memorial from Court Officials on the Completion of the Yellow River Conservancy Project

Liu Yu 劉宇
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Categorized Instructor (xuezheng) Liu comments: 〔The flow of the River is originally not something human strength can hold back; it is entirely because our〕 Sovereign’s pure virtue reaches Heaven, and spirits and men alike accept their charges, that the work was reported complete before the spring had passed. You are able to trace this to its root and extol it; moreover, the writing is straightforward and the facts are verified, shedding all cosmetic adornment. Does this not [?] venture to compare with the brush of Zichang (Sima Qian 司馬遷)?
Examiner and District Instructor (jiaoyu) Wang comments: 〔Modest phrasing and elegant tone; its bearing is free and unconstrained.〕
Examiner and Subprefectural Categorized Instructor Ren comments: 〔It depicts the scenes along the River as vividly as if right before one's eyes.〕 Could the marvel of solitary ingenuity reach such heights as this! Extraordinary indeed!

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
伏以
帝德格天懋贊川流之化
神功兩地光昭河翕之祥萬國朝宗四方謌頌
臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首竊惟黃河起於
崑崙通乎淮泗遡九折而上始窮其源自
屢遷以來蓋非其舊歷觀往蹟殊異今時
扼漕運之咽喉係
京師之命脉旣趨利而仍避害故舉事不易
成功水漲秋濤訝風雷之相薄歲咨昬墊
===
悲魚鱉之爲鄰或塞或疏人心之區畫靡
定隨築隨決河身之移徙無常況於政餙
虛文加以事非專任使數載盈庭之議似
三年作舍之謀生靈隱憂
國家大計未有甚於此者也茲蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
玄德淵涵
睿謀渙發
𢿱龢闡圖書之秘
punctuated: 伏以帝德格天，懋贊川流之化；神功兩地，光昭河翕之祥。萬國朝宗，四方謌頌。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟黃河起於崑崙，通乎淮泗。遡九折而上，始窮其源；自屢遷以來，蓋非其舊。歷觀往蹟，殊異今時。扼漕運之咽喉，係京師之命脉。旣趨利而仍避害，故舉事不易成功。水漲秋濤，訝風雷之相薄；歲咨昬墊，悲魚鱉之爲鄰。或塞或疏，人心之區畫靡定；隨築隨決，河身之移徙無常。況於政餙虛文，加以事非專任，使數載盈庭之議，似三年作舍之謀。生靈隱憂，國家大計，未有甚於此者也。茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，玄德淵涵，睿謀渙發。𢿱龢闡圖書之秘，
translation_en:
Humbly considering: the Emperor's virtue reaches to Heaven, grandly assisting the transformative power of the flowing streams; his divine achievements pair with the Earth [? 兩地], brilliantly manifesting the auspicious sign of the Yellow River's submission. The myriad states pay court in homage, and the four quarters sing praises. Your servants, truly joyful and truly elated, bow our heads to the ground.

We humbly reflect that the Yellow River rises in the Kunlun Mountains and connects with the Huai and Si rivers. Only by tracing it up through its nine bends can one reach its source; since its repeated shifts in course, it is no longer as it was of old. Reviewing past traces, they differ markedly from present circumstances. It holds the throat of the grain transport canal and is tied to the lifeline of the Capital. Because we seek to secure its benefits while simultaneously avoiding its harms, undertaking works upon it does not easily succeed. When the waters swell with autumn billows, one marvels as wind and thunder clash together; year after year the people sigh amid drowning and flood, grieving that they have fish and turtles for neighbors. Whether to dam it or to dredge it, human plans remain unsettled; no sooner are dikes built than they breach, and the shifting of the river's channel is unpredictable. Moreover, administration has been dressed up in empty formalities, and responsibility for the task has not been entrusted to a single authority, turning several years of court-filling deliberations into something like the proverbial plan of building a house by the roadside that remains uncompleted after three years. For the hidden anxieties of the living people and the great plans of the State, nothing is more urgent than this.

Now, we humbly encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, whose profound virtue is deep and all-embracing, and whose wise counsels shine forth. With harmonious vital energy he illuminates the mysteries of the River Chart and Luo Writing, …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
網羅畫舟楫之才
大地遍恩波潤澤寧惟九里
榮光浮德水澄清何啻三朝頃因河伯之橫流
特勑司空而平土行河使者首推九列之賢都
水長丞畢簡諸曹之彥授之方略假以便
宜謂千丈之陂易潰於蟻穴而八年之績
必始於龍門思防四溢之懷襄當藉兩涯
之盤束迺穿高堰再控遥隄
詔令重申率作無煩於沉璧
===
分須三至歡呼實倍於投醪驚畚臿之如雲快
經營之不日蛟龍蜿蟺應符漢帝之渠栗囷
兩鏤形可考夏王之鼎地靈效順天塹增
雄障狂瀾以東悉循故道自清河而北漸
號坦途金斗呂梁銜尾見舳艫竝進牙檣
錦纜歌喉與榜枻同聲貢
御府以駢塡總海錯山珍之盛賦太倉而絡繹
極墉崇櫛比之繁東南千里汀萊爰茲稼
穡西北九邊飛輓信若灌輸皆由我
punctuated: 網羅畫舟楫之才；大地遍恩波，潤澤寧惟九里；榮光浮德水，澄清何啻三朝。頃因河伯之橫流，特勑司空而平土。行河使者，首推九列之賢；都水長丞，畢簡諸曹之彥。授之方略，假以便宜。謂千丈之陂，易潰於蟻穴；而八年之績，必始於龍門。思防四溢之懷襄，當藉兩涯之盤束。迺穿高堰，再控遥隄。詔令重申，率作無煩於沉璧；分須三至，歡呼實倍於投醪。驚畚臿之如雲，快經營之不日。蛟龍蜿蟺，應符漢帝之渠；栗囷兩鏤，形可考夏王之鼎。地靈效順，天塹增雄。障狂瀾以東，悉循故道；自清河而北，漸號坦途。金斗、呂梁，銜尾見舳艫竝進；牙檣、錦纜，歌喉與榜枻同聲。貢御府以駢塡，總海錯山珍之盛；賦太倉而絡繹，極墉崇櫛比之繁。東南千里汀萊，爰茲稼穡；西北九邊飛輓，信若灌輸。皆由我
translation_en: …and nets in full the talents worthy to serve as boats and oars; over the great earth His waves of grace spread everywhere—how could their moistening benefit reach merely nine li? Resplendent light floats upon the Waters of Virtue—how is their limpid clarity limited to three mornings? Recently, because the River Lord overflowed wildly, He specially commanded the Minister of Works to pacify the land. As River-Inspecting Envoys, the worthiest among the Nine Ministers were foremost recommended; as Directors and Assistant Directors of the Bureau of Waterways, the finest talents from the various bureaus were all selected. He imparted to them strategic plans and granted them discretionary authority. Considering that a dike of a thousand fathoms is easily breached by an ant-hole, and that the achievement of eight years must begin at Longmen, to guard against flooding that engulfs the hills on all sides, one must rely on binding the waters tightly between both banks. Thus the Gaojiayan dike was excavated and distant embankments were further controlled. Imperial decrees were repeatedly issued, so that leading the work required no trouble of sinking jade disks into the river; imperial largesse was distributed thrice over, and the cheers of joy truly doubled those for casting spiced wine into the stream. Startling was the cloud-like gathering of baskets and spades; gratifying was the completion of the enterprise in no time. Flood-dragons coiled and glided, answering the auspicious omen of the Han Emperor's canal; grain-bins [?] and creatures [?] were doubly engraved, their shapes verifiable against the tripods of the Xia King. The spirits of the earth rendered obedience, and the natural moat grew in grandeur. Holding back the raging waves and guiding them eastward, the waters all followed their former course; from Qinghe northward, the route gradually came to be called a level thoroughfare. At Jindou and Lüliang, prows and sterns follow tail to tail as vessels advance side by side; among ivory masts and brocade hawsers, singing voices sound in unison with the beating of oars. Tribute fills the Imperial Household Treasury in dense abundance, gathering the profusion of delicacies from sea and mountain; grain taxes stream continuously to the Great Granary, reaching the utmost prosperity of stacks lofty as walls and ranged close as the teeth of a comb. Across a thousand li of marshland and overgrown fields in the southeast, sowing and reaping now take place here; rapid transport to the Nine Defense Commands of the northwest truly flows like water poured from a vessel. All this comes from our…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
皇上深惟億兆之安有備無患排此二三其說
惟斷乃成審勢操機利何爭於尺寸知人
善使事不襲乎尋常蓋禹勤由己之思德
斯遠矣惟堯切儆余之慮功自巍然刻三
犀牛宜勒碑而誦德來兩黃鵠合薦
廟以揚休臣等久屬涵濡未酬涓滴
皇猷允塞玄圭幸遘於虞庭史筆鋪張白馬羞
稱乎漢代伏願
心源常濬
===
道岸先登
修府事而九敘惟歌
若雨暘而庶徵來備
金繩玉牘百靈呈川至之符
紫闕朱宮萬載紀河清之瑞臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖懽躍忭營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
punctuated: 皇上深惟億兆之安，有備無患；排此二三其說，惟斷乃成。審勢操機，利何爭於尺寸？知人善使，事不襲乎尋常。蓋禹勤由己之思，德斯遠矣；惟堯切儆余之慮，功自巍然。刻三犀牛，宜勒碑而誦德；來兩黃鵠，合薦廟以揚休。臣等久屬涵濡，未酬涓滴。皇猷允塞，玄圭幸遘於虞庭；史筆鋪張，白馬羞稱乎漢代。伏願心源常濬，道岸先登；修府事而九敘惟歌，若雨暘而庶徵來備。金繩玉牘，百靈呈川至之符；紫闕朱宮，萬載紀河清之瑞。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，懽躍忭營之至，謹奉表稱賀以…
translation_en: …Your Majesty deeply considers the peace of the myriads of people, ensuring that with preparation there is no calamity; rejecting these wavering and divided opinions, only through decisive resolution was success achieved. Assessing the situation and grasping the critical moment, why contend over an inch or a foot of advantage? Knowing men and employing them well, the enterprise did not merely follow ordinary routines. Indeed, Yu was diligent in holding himself responsible for the drowned, and thus his virtue reached far; Yao was earnest in his concern that the floodwaters were warning him, and thus his achievement stood towering. Carving three stone rhinoceroses, it is fitting to inscribe a stele to praise Your virtue; the arrival of two yellow swans makes it proper to present an offering at the Ancestral Temple to extol Your blessings. Your servants have long been steeped in Your grace, yet have not repaid a single drop. The Imperial plan is truly fulfilled, and we are fortunate to witness the presentation of the dark jade tablet at the court of Yu; as the historian's brush elaborates on this, it would be shameful to even mention the white horse sacrifice of the Han dynasty. We humbly pray that the source of Your mind be ever dredged and clear, and that You ascend the shore of the Way before all others; that by cultivating the Six Treasuries and Three Businesses, all nine divisions be celebrated in song, and that with seasonable rain and sunshine, the various verifications all be complete. With golden cords and jade tablets, the hundred spirits present the auspicious tallies of swelling streams; in the purple towers and vermilion palaces, ten thousand years will record the auspicious sign of the Yellow River running clear. Your servants, unable to contain our extreme joy and elation as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to the Sage, respectfully present this memorial to offer congratulations and to…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
闈
第叁場
策
第一問
同考試官學正劉　批　劉宇
〔我〕
皇上
〔皇后繼美〕
〔列聖竝篤虞周其本乃在監成憲嗣徽音而末以好問好察亦保亦臨爲〕
===
〔聖修諸王尤見忠愛無已之意宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭王　批　〔對揚而不忘儆勸僧立朝必〕
〔大過人者敬服〕
考試官學正任　批　〔敷陳詳悉剴切具見忠悃錄之〕
觀大哉之乾元則知
帝道之所以爲大觀至哉之坤元則知
后道之所以爲至夫乾天也父道也而萬物資
始焉何如其大也
帝則統天御宇舉天下之民物而皆屬於覆冒
punctuated:
闈。

第叁場：策。

第一問。
同考試官學正劉　批：劉宇。〔我〕皇上、〔皇后繼美〕〔列聖，竝篤虞周。其本乃在監成憲、嗣徽音，而末以好問好察、亦保亦臨爲〕〔聖修諸王，尤見忠愛無已之意。宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭王　批：〔對揚而不忘儆勸，僧立朝必〕〔大過人者，敬服。〕
考試官學正任　批：〔敷陳詳悉剴切，具見忠悃，錄之。〕

觀大哉之乾元，則知帝道之所以爲大；觀至哉之坤元，則知后道之所以爲至。夫乾，天也，父道也，而萬物資始焉，何如其大也！帝則統天御宇，舉天下之民物而皆屬於覆冒
translation_en:
… [so Your Majesty may] hear [? 闈 for 聞].

Third Session: Policy Essays.

First Question.
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (Xuezheng) Liu, comments on Liu Yu 劉宇: 〔Our reigning Emperor and Empress succeed to the excellence of the Line of Sages, equaling the devotion of Yu (Shun) and Zhou. Its foundation lies in taking the established statutes as a mirror and inheriting the virtuous reputation [of the ancestors], while at the end taking the love of questioning and examining, and remaining ever-watchful whether protected [by unseen spirits] or approached [by others], as the basis for sagely self-cultivation and the admonition [? 諸王 for 規正] of the ruler; this especially reveals an inexhaustible spirit of loyalty and affection. It ought to be recorded as a model.〕
Examiner, County Instructor (Jiaoyu) Wang, comments: 〔In responding to and extolling [imperial virtue], he does not forget admonition and exhortation. When he [? 僧 for 他] stands at court, he will surely far surpass others; I admire him with respect.〕
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (Xuezheng) Ren, comments: 〔The exposition is detailed, thorough, and incisive, fully manifesting loyal sincerity. Record it.〕

When we contemplate the greatness of the Primal Creative (Qianyuan), we know whereby the Way of the Emperor is great; when we contemplate the perfection of the Primal Receptive (Kunyuan), we know whereby the Way of the Empress is perfect. Now Qian is Heaven, and the Way of the Father; the myriad things owe their beginning to it—how great it is! The Emperor governs Heaven and rules the universe, taking all the people and things under Heaven and placing them beneath his overarching canopy…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
文中其道同也是一乾元之大也坤地也
母道也而萬物資生焉何如其至也
后則翊天贊聖舉天下之民物而皆在於生成
之內其道同也是一坤元之至也知于此
則我
太祖高皇帝
成祖文皇帝
高皇后
文皇后之所以貽謀
===
穆宗莊皇帝
二皇太后之所以纘序及我
皇上
皇后之所以善繼善述可得而鋪張颺厲萬一
矣請遂陳之乾坤者萬物之大父母也帝
也者體天之乾以為天下父坤也者應地
之坤以為天下母者也是故帝曰皇后亦
曰皇其尊同也君總萬幾以撫綏萬邦后
總六宮以儀刑萬國其治同也君肅肅以
punctuated:
文中，其道同也，是一乾元之大也；坤，地也，母道也，而萬物資生焉，何如其至也！后則翊天贊聖，舉天下之民物而皆在於生成之內，其道同也，是一坤元之至也。知于此，則我太祖高皇帝、成祖文皇帝、高皇后、文皇后之所以貽謀，穆宗莊皇帝、二皇太后之所以纘序，及我皇上、皇后之所以善繼善述，可得而鋪張颺厲萬一矣，請遂陳之。

乾坤者，萬物之大父母也。帝也者，體天之乾以為天下父；坤也者，應地之坤以為天下母者也。是故帝曰皇，后亦曰皇，其尊同也；君總萬幾以撫綏萬邦，后總六宮以儀刑萬國，其治同也；君肅肅以
translation_en:
… within [His] canopy [?], His Way is the same—this is the same greatness as the Primal Creative (qianyuan). Kun (the Receptive) is Earth and the Way of the Mother, and from it the myriad things derive their birth—how supreme it is! The Empress assists Heaven and aids the Sage, so that all the people and things of the world are encompassed within Her nurturing and completion; Her Way is the same—this is the same supremeness as the Primal Receptive (kunyuan). Understanding this, how Our Grand Progenitor the Emperor Gao (Taizu), Our Accomplished Ancestor the Emperor Wen (Chengzu), Empress Gao, and Empress Wen handed down their plans; how Emperor Zhuang (Muzong) and the Two Empresses Dowager continued the line of succession; and how Our Sovereign and the Empress skillfully carry on their legacy and transmit their work—all of this may be set forth and extolled in some small measure. Allow me to present it in full.

Qian and Kun are the great father and mother of the myriad things. The Emperor embodies the Qian of Heaven to serve as father to the world; [the Empress, as] Kun, corresponds to the Kun of Earth to serve as mother to the world. Therefore, the Emperor is called August (huang), and the Empress is likewise called August; their exalted rank is the same. The Ruler oversees the myriad affairs of state to pacify the ten thousand realms, while the Empress oversees the Six Palaces to set a model for the ten thousand states; their governance is the same. The Ruler with solemn reverence …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
主鬯后莫莫以薦豆其祀先同也天子親
耕于南郊王后親蠶于北郊其率民同也
此其相須相成之道固如此故人見重華
協帝風動四方以爲虞舜之治若此其盛
也而不知釐降曰嬪者則其升聞之自也
人見丕冒西土咸和萬民以爲周文之化
若此其隆也而不知關雎好逑者則其刑
于之始也嗣是惟東京之美助於明德而
貞觀之治佐於長孫以及高曹向孟之賢
微有虞周之響其餘則寥寥無聞矣洪惟
===
我
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇攸敘彝倫而又得
高皇后以主內治是以風教訖于四海熙然一
虞周之盛也而猶欲即其明徵者世爲天
下道故著
皇明祖訓凡十三章首之以祖訓繼之以持守
與夫祭祀軍國之事纖悉具備而
高皇后亦有嘉言善行載諸方册如勸
punctuated: 主鬯，后莫莫以薦豆，其祀先同也；天子親耕于南郊，王后親蠶于北郊，其率民同也。此其相須相成之道固如此。故人見重華協帝、風動四方，以爲虞舜之治若此其盛也，而不知釐降曰嬪者，則其升聞之自也；人見丕冒西土、咸和萬民，以爲周文之化若此其隆也，而不知關雎好逑者，則其刑于之始也。嗣是惟東京之美助於明德，而貞觀之治佐於長孫，以及高、曹、向、孟之賢，微有虞、周之響，其餘則寥寥無聞矣。洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區宇，攸敘彝倫，而又得高皇后以主內治，是以風教訖于四海，熙然一虞、周之盛也。而猶欲即其明徵者，世爲天下道，故著《皇明祖訓》凡十三章，首之以祖訓，繼之以持守，與夫祭祀、軍國之事，纖悉具備；而高皇后亦有嘉言善行載諸方册，如勸
translation_en:
… presides over the sacrificial wine, while the Empress reverently presents the ritual vessels; their worship of the ancestors is the same. The Son of Heaven personally plows in the southern suburb, while the Empress personally tends silkworms in the northern suburb; their leading of the people is the same. Such indeed is the Way by which they depend upon and complete one another.

Thus, people see Chonghua [Shun] harmonizing with the Emperor [Yao] and his moral wind stirring the four quarters, and consider the governance of Shun of Yu to be so flourishing; yet they do not know that the sending down of the two daughters as wives was the very source from which his reputation rose to be heard above. People see the grand overspreading of the western lands and the complete harmonizing of the myriad people, and consider the transforming influence of King Wen of Zhou to be so eminent; yet they do not know that the "good mate" of the "Guanju" ode was the very beginning of the model he set for his family. After this, only the excellence of the Eastern Capital [Later Han] was aided by Empress Mingde [Ma], and the governance of the Zhenguan reign [of Tang] was assisted by Empress Zhangsun, down to the worthiness of Empresses Gao, Cao, Xiang, and Meng [of Song], which faintly echoed Yu and Zhou; as for the rest, they are few and unheard of.

Reflecting upon our Taizu, Emperor Gao, he founded the realm and set the constant human relationships in order, and furthermore obtained Empress Gao [Ma] to preside over the inner governance. Therefore, his moral instruction reached to the four seas, brightly matching the flourishing ages of Yu and Zhou. Yet still wishing to take what had been clearly proven and make it the Way for the empire for generations, he composed the Ancestral Injunctions of the August Ming (Huang Ming zuxun) in thirteen chapters in all, beginning with the "Ancestral Injunctions," continuing with "Maintaining Guard," and including matters of sacrifices, the military, and the state, complete in every detail; meanwhile, Empress Gao also had admirable words and virtuous deeds recorded in the historical tablets, such as encouraging…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
太祖以進學訓諸王以孝友者與
祖訓之書相彪炳也美哉洋洋乎典謨之作何
以異焉我
成祖文皇帝誕膺鴻運肇修人紀而又得
文皇后以主內治是以德教加于百姓沛然一
舜文之業也而猶欲即其保定者世爲天
下法故著
聖學心法二十八篇始于君道終于臣道與夫
禮樂名分之類本末具舉而
===
文皇后亦作內訓二十篇首德性次修身以至
慈幼逮下數千餘言與
心法之傳相輝映也美哉纚纚乎訓誥之文何
以殊焉肆我
穆宗莊皇帝睿明恭儉祇續
先猷而天下享和平之福我
仁聖
慈聖
二太后貞靜幽閑昭示宮則而天下仰慈惠之
punctuated: 太祖以進學，訓諸王以孝友者，與《祖訓》之書相彪炳也。美哉洋洋乎！典謨之作，何以異焉？我成祖文皇帝誕膺鴻運，肇修人紀，而又得文皇后以主內治，是以德教加于百姓，沛然一舜、文之業也。而猶欲即其保定者，世爲天下法，故著《聖學心法》二十八篇，始于《君道》，終于《臣道》，與夫禮樂、名分之類，本末具舉；而文皇后亦作《內訓》二十篇，首《德性》，次《修身》，以至《慈幼》、《逮下》，數千餘言，與《心法》之傳相輝映也。美哉纚纚乎！訓誥之文，何以殊焉？肆我穆宗莊皇帝睿明恭儉，祇續先猷，而天下享和平之福；我仁聖、慈聖二太后貞靜幽閑，昭示宮則，而天下仰慈惠之
translation_en:
… [encouraging] the Grand Progenitor (Taizu) to advance in learning and instructing the imperial princes in filial piety and brotherly affection—shine forth alongside the book of Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun). How splendid and vast! How does this differ from the compositions of the Canons and Counsels?

Our Accomplished Emperor, the Martial Ancestor (Chengzu Wen Huangdi), grandly received the great destiny and set in order the human relationships, while also having the Accomplished Empress (Wen Huanghou) to preside over the inner governance. Therefore, moral teaching extended to the common people—abundantly, the very enterprise of Shun and King Wen! Yet still wishing that what he had secured and stabilized should serve for generations as a model for the realm, he composed the Method of the Mind in Imperial Learning (Shengxue xinfa) in twenty-eight chapters, beginning with "The Way of the Ruler" and ending with "The Way of the Subject," together with such matters as rites and music and names and statuses, setting forth both root and branch in full. Meanwhile, the Accomplished Empress likewise composed the Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun) in twenty chapters, beginning with "Moral Nature," followed by "Cultivating the Self," and extending to "Kindness to the Young" and "Generosity to Inferiors"—several thousand words in all—which shine in mutual splendor with the transmission of the Method of the Mind. How splendid and well-ordered! How is this different from the writings of the Instructions and Announcements?

Thus our Reverent Emperor, the Majestic Ancestor (Muzong Zhuang Huangdi), wise, discerning, respectful, and frugal, reverently continued the plans of his predecessors, so that the realm enjoyed the blessings of peace and harmony; and our Two Empresses Dowager, the Benevolent and Sage (Rensheng) and the Compassionate and Sage (Cisheng), chaste, serene, secluded, and composed, have clearly manifested the regulations of the palace, so that the realm looks up to the…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
宣蓋
二祖之德卽虞舜周文之德也惟
皇考則善繼于不窮
二后之德卽英皇太姒之德也惟
二后則善述于不替同符千古昭有烈光有由
然矣我
皇上毓德青宮已躬親夫
嚴訓而嗣膺
乾統又日保于
===
===
慈寧我
聖后大婚禮成既親膺夫
寶冊而
正位中宮又時承乎
溫諭則不必著之典章垂之彝訓而我
祖宗
列后之相授受者已面命而心領之矣故言乎
其內治也定省之儀修而
兩宮之歡洽矣出閣之講設而友于之情著矣
punctuated: 宣。蓋二祖之德，卽虞舜、周文之德也，惟皇考則善繼于不窮；二后之德，卽英、皇、太姒之德也，惟二后則善述于不替。同符千古，昭有烈光，有由然矣！我皇上毓德青宮，已躬親夫嚴訓；而嗣膺乾統，又日保于慈寧。我聖后大婚禮成，既親膺夫寶冊；而正位中宮，又時承乎溫諭。則不必著之典章、垂之彝訓，而我祖宗、列后之相授受者，已面命而心領之矣。故言乎其內治也：定省之儀修，而兩宮之歡洽矣；出閣之講設，而友于之情著矣；
translation_en:
…dissemination. For the virtue of the Two Ancestors [Taizu and Taizong] is none other than the virtue of Yu Shun and King Wen of Zhou, and our Imperial Deceased Father [Emperor Muzong] was able to succeed to it well without exhaustion; the virtue of the Two Empresses [Empresses Xiaocigao and Renxiaowen] is none other than the virtue of Ehuang, Nüying, and Taisi, and the Two Empresses Dowager [Rensheng and Cisheng] have been able to transmit it well without decline. That they match the standards of remote antiquity and shine with radiant glory truly has its source!

While our Sovereign nurtured his virtue in the Heir Apparent's Palace, he already personally received stern instruction; and since succeeding to the heavenly throne, he has been daily protected and guided at the Cining Palace. Since the grand wedding rites of our Sacred Empress were completed, she has personally received the precious investiture book and seal; and having taken her rightful place in the Central Palace, she also constantly receives warm admonitions. Thus, there is no need to commit these teachings to written statutes or hand them down as formal instructions, for what our Imperial Ancestors and successive Empresses have passed down and received has already been enjoined face-to-face and comprehended in the heart.

Therefore, if we speak of the governance of the inner court: the rites of morning and evening inquiries after health are cultivated, and the joy of the Two Palaces [the Two Empresses Dowager] is harmonious; the princely lectures upon leaving the inner quarters are established, and fraternal affection is made manifest; …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
粢盛之禮恪而事
先之孝昭矣嫡庶之分明而宮闈之體肅矣齊
家之善章章較著不有以基天下之治耶
言乎其外治也任賢之志專而相臣之職
得矣褻賓之政行而吏治之績奏矣經費
之制定而財用之需節矣馭夷之策勝而
重譯之朝至矣治平之盛卓卓可紀不有
以廣齊家之化耶信乎熙洽宇內維持陰
敎有以光
===
祖烈而軼虞周雖甚盛德蔑以加矣而執事以
爲必有本焉愚以爲內外之治本于
君后之德而君后之德成于訓迪之勤蓋
祖訓之昭垂不一而足也惟于其傳之爲家法
者日振勵焉則身修家齊而刑于之化出
之有本而不窮
列聖之遺範世守而在也惟于其傳之爲治法
者日率由焉則篤近舉遠而風敎之流施
之有本而不匱人知
punctuated: 粢盛之禮恪，而事先之孝昭矣；嫡庶之分明，而宮闈之體肅矣。齊家之善，章章較著，不有以基天下之治耶？言乎其外治也，任賢之志專，而相臣之職得矣；褻賓之政行，而吏治之績奏矣；經費之制定，而財用之需節矣；馭夷之策勝，而重譯之朝至矣。治平之盛，卓卓可紀，不有以廣齊家之化耶？信乎熙洽宇內，維持陰敎，有以光祖烈而軼虞、周，雖甚盛德，蔑以加矣。而執事以爲必有本焉，愚以爲內外之治，本于君、后之德，而君、后之德，成于訓迪之勤。蓋祖訓之昭垂，不一而足也，惟于其傳之爲家法者，日振勵焉，則身修家齊，而刑于之化，出之有本而不窮；列聖之遺範，世守而在也，惟于其傳之爲治法者，日率由焉，則篤近舉遠，而風敎之流，施之有本而不匱。人知
translation_en:
… the rites of sacrificial grain offerings are reverently observed, and filial piety in serving the ancestors is made manifest; the distinction between principal and secondary consorts is clear, and the decorum of the palace quarters is solemn. The excellence of regulating the family is brilliantly evident—does it not serve as the foundation for the governance of the Empire?

Speaking of external governance: the resolve to employ the worthy is single-minded, and the duties of the grand ministers are fulfilled; the policy of verifying name and reality [?] is carried out, and the achievements of official administration are realized; the regulations for regular expenditures are established, and the demands on financial resources are economized; the strategies for controlling the border peoples prevail, and tribute missions arriving through multiple interpreters come to court.
