The flourishing of order and peace is eminently worthy of record—does it not serve to broaden the transformative influence of regulating the family? Truly, bringing harmony to the entire world and upholding the feminine teachings suffices to glorify the meritorious業 of the Ancestors and surpass Yu and Zhou; even the most abundant virtue could add nothing more to this.

Yet Your Excellency considers that there must be a fundamental root to it. In my humble view, the governance of the inner and outer realms is rooted in the virtue of the Sovereign and the Empress, and the virtue of the Sovereign and the Empress is brought to completion through diligence in instruction and guidance. Indeed, the luminous precepts handed down in the Ancestral Injunctions are more than one; only by rousing and exerting oneself daily in what has been transmitted as family law will the person be cultivated and the family regulated, so that the transformative influence of setting an example for one's consort issues from a root and is inexhaustible. The legacy and models of the Successive Sages are preserved from generation to generation and remain present; only by daily following and abiding by what has been transmitted as the law of governance will those near be treated with devotion and those far away be uplifted, so that the flow of moral instruction is dispensed from a root and never runs dry. People know…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖德之修矣而不知
皇上以天縱之資墾于成憲此乾元之所以常
大也人知后德之備矣而不知
聖后以思齋之德嗣乎徽音此坤元之所以常
至也內外交治遠邇同風位育咸臻陰陽
合德寧非太平極治之
主而萬世無疆之休也哉雖然君之與后猶天
之于地也天地竝列而天之形則包乎地
之外君后竝治而君之道則兼乎后之全
===
故獨觀萬化之原者不能不于吾
君屬望焉蓋鳌降之風溫恭之塞先之也關雎
之化敬止之純始之也其必好問好察以
擴此心之明若舜之大知而不偏亦臨亦
保以存此心之敬若文之緝熙而罔閒
經筵之御不徒爲聞見之資如我
太祖與宋善講家人而曰朕觀其要只在誠實
而有威嚴者可繹思也
顧問之勤不徒爲章句之末如我
punctuated: 聖德之修矣，而不知皇上以天縱之資，墾于成憲，此乾元之所以常大也；人知后德之備矣，而不知聖后以思齋之德，嗣乎徽音，此坤元之所以常至也。內外交治，遠邇同風，位育咸臻，陰陽合德，寧非太平極治之主，而萬世無疆之休也哉！雖然，君之與后，猶天之于地也。天地竝列，而天之形則包乎地之外；君后竝治，而君之道則兼乎后之全。故獨觀萬化之原者，不能不于吾君屬望焉。蓋鳌降之風，溫恭之塞先之也；關雎之化，敬止之純始之也。其必好問好察，以擴此心之明，若舜之大知而不偏；亦臨亦保，以存此心之敬，若文之緝熙而罔閒。經筵之御，不徒爲聞見之資，如我太祖與宋善講《家人》，而曰「朕觀其要只在誠實而有威嚴」者，可繹思也；顧問之勤，不徒爲章句之末，如我
translation_en:
…that the Imperial virtue is cultivated, yet do not know that His Majesty, with heaven-endowed talents, models himself [墾, for 監?] upon the established statutes—this is why the creative origin of Heaven (Qianyuan) is ever great. People know that the Empress's virtue is complete, yet do not know that the Sacred Empress, with the reverent and莊-like virtue celebrated in the ode "Siqi" [written 思齋], succeeds to the admirable legacy of her predecessors—this is why the receptive origin of Earth (Kunyuan) is ever supreme. When the inner and outer realms are both well-governed, far and near share the same moral customs, proper order and nourishment (weiyu) are both achieved, and yin and yang unite in their virtues—is he not indeed a sovereign of supreme peace and ultimate governance, bringing boundless blessings for ten thousand generations!

Even so, the ruler in relation to the empress is like Heaven in relation to Earth. Heaven and Earth stand side by side, yet the form of Heaven encompasses Earth from without; the ruler and the empress govern side by side, yet the Way of the ruler comprehends the entirety of the empress's role. Therefore, one who looks solely to the source of the ten thousand transformations cannot but place his hopes in our Sovereign. For the moral wind of sending down his two daughters in marriage at the Gui River [鳌降, for 釐降] was preceded by the fullness of Shun's gentle reverence; and the transforming influence of the ode "Guanju" was initiated by the purity of King Wen's reverent resting in perfection.

He must surely delight in questioning and delight in examining, so as to broaden the clarity of this mind, like Shun in his great wisdom without partiality; he must act as though approaching a deity and as though guarded by a protector, so as to preserve the reverence of this mind, like King Wen in his continuous radiance without interruption. Presiding over the Classics Colloquium (Jingyan) should not merely serve as a means of acquiring broad learning: as when our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) expounded the "Family" (Jiaren) hexagram with Song Shan 宋善 [for Song Lian 宋濂?] and said, "As We see it, its essential point lies solely in being sincere and truthful while maintaining august dignity"—this is worthy of deep reflection. Diligence in seeking counsel should not merely concern the trivialities of chapter and phrase: as when our…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
成祖與解縉論大學而得正心修身內外合一
之義者可推類也始終務典學之勤自強
法天行之健則聖德日懋而威如之吉永
孚于休道揆以端而絜矩之施愈神于化
矣一得之愚不識可轉聞于
上否
第二問
王守禮
同考試官訓導賓　批〔今天下吏治病在亡實是作援古證今推見敝始末陳內爭神久任允推本之論錄之〕
===
考試官教諭王　批〔吏治得失與所以馭吏之法評駁精詳是識治之士也〕
考試官學正任　批〔吏治之敝世未有識者吾令聞探本之論焉〕
君設官而任之職與官之受職而理民也
可徒以法制爲哉要在崇實效而已矣上
以實求下則殿最黜陟悉於民之利病覈
之而矯飾者無倖進下以實應上則其進
punctuated:
成祖與解縉論《大學》而得正心修身、內外合一之義者，可推類也。始終務典學之勤，自強法天行之健，則聖德日懋，而威如之吉永孚于休；道揆以端，而絜矩之施愈神于化矣。一得之愚，不識可轉聞于上否？

第二問
王守禮
同考試官訓導賓批：〔今天下吏治，病在亡實。是作援古證今，推見敝始，末陳內爭神、久任，允推本之論。錄之。〕
考試官教諭王批：〔吏治得失，與所以馭吏之法，評駁精詳，是識治之士也。〕
考試官學正任批：〔吏治之敝，世未有識者，吾令聞探本之論焉。〕

君設官而任之職，與官之受職而理民也，可徒以法制爲哉？要在崇實效而已矣。上以實求下，則殿最黜陟，悉於民之利病覈之，而矯飾者無倖進；下以實應上，則其進
translation_en:
… Emperor Chengzu discussing the Great Learning (Daxue) with Xie Jin 解縉 and grasping the principle of rectifying the mind and cultivating the person in a unity of inner and outer—from this one may reason by analogy. If from beginning to end he devotes himself to diligence in classical learning, strengthening himself in emulation of the unceasing vigor of Heaven's course, then his sagely virtue will daily flourish, and the auspiciousness of dignified majesty will forever inspire confidence in its blessings; the measuring of principle will thereby be made upright, and the application of the measuring square will become ever more miraculous in its transforming influence. In my humble understanding of a single point, I do not know whether this may be transmitted to His Majesty's hearing or not?

Second Question
Wang Shouli 王守禮
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Bin 賓, comments: "Today the governance of officials throughout the realm suffers from a lack of substance. This essay cites antiquity to verify the present, tracing the origins of the abuses, and at the end sets forth focusing the spirit inwardly [?] and long tenure in office. It is truly an argument that gets to the root of the matter. Recorded."
Examiner, Instructor Wang 王, comments: "The successes and failures of official governance, as well as the methods for managing officials, are evaluated and critiqued with precision and thoroughness. This is a scholar who understands governance."
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor Ren 任, comments: "The abuses of official governance have not been understood by the world; now [?] I have heard an argument that probes the root."

When the ruler establishes offices and assigns them responsibilities, and when officials accept those responsibilities and govern the people, can this be accomplished merely through laws and regulations? The key lies solely in esteeming substantial results. When the superior seeks substance from those below, then evaluations of merit and demotions or promotions are all verified against what benefits or harms the people, and those who practice pretense and ostentation have no way to advance by luck; when those below respond to the superior with substance, then those who advance …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者必其益於民者也其退者必其病乎民
者也不必聲華譽聞之彰奇功偉績之紀
而聲也譽也奇也偉也卒亦未有出此者
何也不采名而采實者之效也實可以利
民亦可以獲上然則爲吏者何必于見奇
樹異而上亦何必以法制驅之哉達乎此
則郡邑之民綏柔海寓之化寧謐唐虞三
代之盛不難致矣何論漢吏也愚嘗考覽
古今見守令之責爲至重焉古者分茅胙
===
土建國親侯天子以民事託諸侯諸侯勤
民事以荅天子巡狩述職各以時行而君
民之間不至闊絶者此道行也秦罷侯置
守裂天下地郡邑之而謷然軒然以鐫磨
其民天下吏治若救火揚沸然非武健嚴
酷惡能勝其任而愉快乎哉是故吏如秋
荼法如凝脂而姦有逸於法之外者法何
可恃也漢興懲秦之暴破觚而爲圓斲琱
而爲樸而所與民約者法惟三章耳殺人
punctuated:
者必其益於民者也，其退者必其病乎民者也。不必聲華譽聞之彰、奇功偉績之紀，而聲也、譽也、奇也、偉也，卒亦未有出此者。何也？不采名而采實者之效也。實可以利民，亦可以獲上，然則爲吏者何必于見奇樹異，而上亦何必以法制驅之哉？達乎此，則郡邑之民綏柔，海寓之化寧謐，唐、虞、三代之盛不難致矣，何論漢吏也！
愚嘗考覽古今，見守令之責爲至重焉。古者分茅胙土，建國親侯，天子以民事託諸侯，諸侯勤民事以荅天子。巡狩述職，各以時行，而君民之間不至闊絶者，此道行也。秦罷侯置守，裂天下地郡邑之，而謷然、軒然以鐫磨其民。天下吏治若救火揚沸然，非武健嚴酷，惡能勝其任而愉快乎哉？是故吏如秋荼，法如凝脂，而姦有逸於法之外者，法何可恃也！漢興，懲秦之暴，破觚而爲圓，斲琱而爲樸，而所與民約者，法惟三章耳：殺人
translation_en:
… those who are promoted will certainly be those who benefit the people, and those who are demoted will certainly be those who harm the people. There will be no need for the display of glorious renown and reputation, or the recording of extraordinary feats and great achievements, and yet renown, reputation, extraordinary feats, and great achievements will ultimately never go beyond this. Why is this? It is the effect of selecting for substance rather than selecting for name. When substance can both benefit the people and win the confidence of superiors, why then must those who serve as officials seek to display novelty and establish eccentricity, and why must superiors drive them with legal regulations? Once one comprehends this, the people of the commanderies and districts will be pacified and comforted, the transformation of the realm within the seas will be tranquil and serene, and the flourishing of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties will not be difficult to attain—what need is there even to speak of the officials of Han!

I have examined antiquity and the present, and I see that the responsibility of commandery governors and district magistrates is of the utmost weight. In antiquity, when rushes of different colors were apportioned to invest rulers with territory, states were established and feudal lords were treated with familial closeness. The Son of Heaven entrusted the affairs of the people to the feudal lords, and the feudal lords labored diligently at the affairs of the people in order to answer to the Son of Heaven. Tours of inspection and audiences to report on duties were each conducted according to season, and the reason that sovereign and people did not become estranged and cut off from one another was that this Way was in practice. Qin abolished the feudal lords and established commandery governors, carving up the land of the empire into commanderies and districts, and clamorously and arrogantly chiseled and ground down its people. Local administration across the empire was like fighting a fire with boiling water; unless an official was martial, vigorous, stern, and harsh, how could he be equal to his office and take pleasure in his work? Consequently, officials were as dense as autumn flowering reeds and the laws were as thick as congealed fat, yet the wicked still escaped outside the reach of the law—how then can laws be relied upon? When Han arose, it took warning from the tyranny of Qin, breaking what was angular to make it round, hewing away carved ornament to return to uncarved simplicity, and the law it agreed upon with the people consisted of only three articles: he who kills a person …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者無赦傷人及盜抵罪而萬民說焉且不
敢犯焉此豈有峻法繩之哉蓋上焉者令
不煩而馭吏也有要下焉者法可守而治
民也不勞漢之吏所以稱極盛而漢之治
所以稱近古者本以此也積而至於宣帝
之世而循吏者益可稱數試舉一二爲執
事評之文翁祭舉爲蜀郡守蜀僻陋有蠻
夷風而翁誘進飭厲繇是大化此豈以嚴
致理耶仁愛教化有以導之耳龔遂以丞
===
相御史舉爲渤海太守時左右郡歲饑盜
賊竝起遂以單車至盜悉罷去此豈以武
戡定耶其曰治亂民猶治亂繩不可急也
固有所以安之耳黃霸歷河南潁川宣布
詔令吏民鄉化興行治爲時第一矣而温
恭有讓其本焉王成相膠東戶口日增蒙
顯賞矣而勞來不怠其本焉朱邑廉平不
苛則所至愛敬信臣視民如子則召父興
歌吏之稱良也固有所以致之矣夫漢氏
punctuated: 者無赦，傷人及盜抵罪，而萬民說焉，且不敢犯焉。此豈有峻法繩之哉？蓋上焉者令不煩，而馭吏也有要；下焉者法可守，而治民也不勞。漢之吏所以稱極盛，而漢之治所以稱近古者，本以此也。積而至於宣帝之世，而循吏者益可稱數。試舉一二，爲執事評之。文翁祭舉爲蜀郡守，蜀僻陋有蠻夷風，而翁誘進飭厲，繇是大化。此豈以嚴致理耶？仁愛教化有以導之耳。龔遂以丞相、御史舉爲渤海太守，時左右郡歲饑，盜賊竝起，遂以單車至，盜悉罷去。此豈以武戡定耶？其曰：「治亂民猶治亂繩，不可急也。」固有所以安之耳。黃霸歷河南、潁川，宣布詔令，吏民鄉化興行，治爲時第一矣，而温恭有讓其本焉。王成相膠東，戶口日增，蒙顯賞矣，而勞來不怠其本焉。朱邑廉平不苛，則所至愛敬；信臣視民如子，則召父興歌。吏之稱良也，固有所以致之矣。夫漢氏
translation_en:
… [those who killed] were not pardoned, and those who injured others or stole were punished according to their crimes. Yet the myriad people rejoiced in this and moreover did not dare to violate it. Was this achieved by restraining them with harsh laws? Indeed, when those above issue commands that are not burdensome, they hold the essential key to managing officials; when those below have laws that can be observed, they govern the people without toil. That the officials of the Han are praised as having reached the utmost flourishing, and that the governance of the Han is praised as approaching antiquity, was fundamentally due to this.

As this accumulated down to the reign of Emperor Xuan, the upright officials (xunli) became even more worthy of enumeration. Let me cite one or two to evaluate them for Your Excellency. Wen Weng 文翁 was selected through examination [?] to serve as Grand Administrator (守) of Shu Commandery. Shu was remote and rustic, with the customs of southern and eastern barbarians, yet Weng guided, advanced, admonished, and encouraged them, whereby they were greatly transformed. Was good order here brought about by severity? It was simply that benevolent love and moral instruction provided a way to lead them. Gong Sui 龔遂, upon the recommendation of the Counselor-in-Chief (丞相) and the Censor-in-Chief (御史), was appointed Grand Administrator (太守) of Bohai. At the time, neighboring commanderies suffered from annual famines and bandits rose up all together, yet when Sui arrived in a single carriage, the bandits all dispersed and departed. Was this pacified by military force? As he said, "Governing disorderly people is like untangling a knotted rope; one must not be hasty." Truly, he had a means by which to settle them. Huang Ba 黃霸 served successively in Henan and Yingchuan, proclaiming imperial decrees and ordinances; subofficial functionaries and the common people turned toward moral transformation and rose up in good conduct, so that his administration ranked first of the age—and being gentle, respectful, and yielding was its foundation. Wang Cheng 王成 served as Chancellor (相) of Jiaodong; the number of households and individuals increased daily, and he received illustrious rewards—and his untiring encouragement and comfort of the people was its foundation. Zhu Yi 朱邑 was incorrupt, fair, and not harsh, so wherever he went he was loved and respected; Shao Xinchen 召信臣 regarded the people as his children, so songs praising "Father Shao" arose. That these officials were praised as good truly had that by which it was brought about. Now, the Han house…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
尚吏治吏爭自矜奮者不少而固之傳循
吏也止此豈非以循良之政獨取奉法循
理而武健材明者固無所稱數哉是故敎
民禮讓定著儀品可謂好古敎化矣然而
車服踰制失之僭姦邪有籍取一警百可
謂譽滿朝廷矣然而披籍取人失之煩投
巫鄴水長老傍驚禁令非不駭俗也而治
化謫矣敎吏鈎�royal
punctuated: 尚吏治，吏爭自矜奮者不少，而固之傳《循吏》也止此，豈非以循良之政，獨取奉法循理，而武健材明者，固無所稱數哉？是故敎民禮讓，定著儀品，可謂好古敎化矣，然而車服踰制，失之僭；姦邪有籍，取一警百，可謂譽滿朝廷矣，然而披籍取人，失之煩；投巫鄴水，長老傍驚，禁令非不駭俗也，而治化謫矣；敎吏鈎royal
translation_en: …valued the administration of officials, and there were not a few officials who vied to take pride in and exert themselves, yet when [Ban] Gu 班固 compiled his "Biographies of Upright Officials" (Xunli zhuan 循吏傳), he stopped at just these men. Was this not because the governance of upright and good officials took solely compliance with the law and adherence to principle as its standard, whereas those who were martial, vigorous, talented, and shrewd were indeed unworthy of being praised and counted? Therefore, teaching the people ritual propriety and deference, and establishing fixed ceremonial grades, may be called loving antiquity and moral transformation; yet when carriages and garments exceeded the regulations, the fault was usurpation [alluding to Han Yan 韓延壽]. Keeping registers of the wicked and perverse, and seizing one to warn a hundred, may be called winning renown that filled the court; yet opening the registers to arrest people erred in being overly troublesome [alluding to Zhang Chang 張敞]. Throwing the shamans into the waters of Ye 鄴 while the elders stood by in alarm—such prohibitions were not unshocking to popular customs, yet transformative governance was faulted [alluding to Ximen Bao 西門豹]. Teaching sub-officials to use "hook-and-[probe]" (gouding 鉤距) [alluding to Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢] [?]…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
德澤之施且壅閼不欲下也是則大可懼矣嗟
乎天之愛民亦甚矣選用賢良固將安之
耳至使民不得蒙實惠而布在郡邑者往
往皆是何耶嘗稽民情而得其故矣蓋下
之利病有常而上之好惡靡定執有常之
利病以求宜乎民而應靡常之好惡則必
違忤抵拂叢猜怒以危其身於是媕婀脂
韋之術行焉而爲之上者忽不加察驟然
而與之曰某良吏也其於民之利病豈惟
===
秦越人之視肥瘠哉又不獨此也其最儇
媮者則或勉飾初政以盜民譽而售上采
及最薦一聞則遂磔然恣肆無復忌憚其
誰能禁之是故薦列難盡據也夫守令之
於郡邑若家長然細鉅皆其事也苟身視
乎民家視乎鄰邑竭忠盡謀不辭勞勩民
焉有不宜哉惟夫趾疎於草野目絕於蔀
屋而田野之闢蕪無聞顏不顰于孤惸慮
不動於暵溢而歲入之豐凶罔問即簿書
punctuated: 德澤之施，且壅閼不欲下也，是則大可懼矣！嗟乎！天之愛民亦甚矣，選用賢良，固將安之耳。至使民不得蒙實惠，而布在郡邑者往往皆是，何耶？嘗稽民情而得其故矣。蓋下之利病有常，而上之好惡靡定。執有常之利病以求宜乎民，而應靡常之好惡，則必違忤抵拂，叢猜怒以危其身；於是媕婀脂韋之術行焉，而爲之上者忽不加察，驟然而與之曰：「某良吏也。」其於民之利病，豈惟秦越人之視肥瘠哉？又不獨此也，其最儇媮者，則或勉飾初政，以盜民譽而售上采；及最薦一聞，則遂磔然恣肆，無復忌憚，其誰能禁之？是故薦列難盡據也。夫守令之於郡邑，若家長然，細鉅皆其事也。苟身視乎民，家視乎鄰邑，竭忠盡謀，不辭勞勩，民焉有不宜哉？惟夫趾疎於草野，目絕於蔀屋，而田野之闢蕪無聞；顏不顰于孤惸，慮不動於暵溢，而歲入之豐凶罔問；即簿書…
translation_en: … the bestowal of benevolent grace is blocked and kept from reaching below—this is truly something to be greatly feared! Alas! Heaven loves the people deeply indeed; in selecting and appointing the worthy and good, the intention is surely to bring them peace. Why is it, then, that the people are prevented from receiving real benefits, and those spread across the prefectures and counties are everywhere like this? I have examined the conditions of the people and found the reason for it. What is beneficial or harmful to those below is constant, whereas the likes and dislikes of superiors are unsettled. If one holds fast to the constant benefits and harms in order to seek what is suitable for the people while responding to unsettled likes and dislikes, one will inevitably clash and give offense, accumulating suspicion and anger so as to endanger oneself. Thereupon, the arts of indecisive flattery and pliant accommodation prevail, while their superiors negligently fail to examine the matter and rashly approve of them, saying, "So-and-so is a good official." As for their attitude toward the benefits and harms of the people, is it merely like the people of Qin and Yue looking upon each other's fatness or leanness with indifference? Nor is this all. Those who are most nimble and opportunistic may exert themselves to dress up their initial administration in order to steal popular praise and win selection by their superiors; yet once a top merit recommendation is reported, they suddenly cast off all restraint and act wantonly without further scruple—and who can stop them? For this reason, recommendation lists cannot be wholly relied upon. Now, prefects and magistrates stand in relation to their prefectures and counties like the head of a household: matters small and great are all their responsibility. If they regarded the people as their own bodies and the neighboring districts [?] as their own families, exhausting their loyalty and utmost counsel without shrinking from toil and weariness, how could anything fail to suit the people? Only when their footsteps rarely reach the rustic countryside and their eyes never see the thatched hovels do they hear nothing of whether the fields are opened up or left to go to waste; when their brows do not furrow over the orphaned and solitary and their thoughts are unmoved by drought and flood, do they ask nothing of whether the annual harvest is abundant or poor. Even if, in registers and account books…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
期會柱後惠文豈無一二稱善者要不過
爲斷爲紛而統之乎爲名焉耳心未必誠
也而況未善者且十而九哉此執事所謂
吏不盡良而馭吏之道亦有未盡者是也
夫上之旌懲如彼吏之自爲如此而欲治
之超越於漢也可得乎凡此則虛文之爲
害也爲今之計莫若略虛文而崇實效欲
崇實效莫如先博大之令嚴貪黷之懲核
舉刺之典重簡任之道而久任其要焉何
===
也任不久則淑慝莫辨任既久則志意悉
舒是故土風民俗久則習之規畫幾宜久
則定之細微曲折久則窮之功勤勞閥久
則驗之而言官所疏與銓曹所具列者義
既備矣第千里之馭急衘轡者必蹶而急
節繁響之樂清廟無取焉故汲黯守淮陽
其治責大指不苛小而蓋公相齊無擾獄
市此清淨畫一無所變更之明效也今天
下吏治率尚精敏而舞文巧詆以輔法者
punctuated: 期會、柱後惠文，豈無一二稱善者？要不過爲斷、爲紛，而統之乎爲名焉耳，心未必誠也，而況未善者且十而九哉！此執事所謂「吏不盡良，而馭吏之道亦有未盡者」是也。夫上之旌懲如彼，吏之自爲如此，而欲治之超越於漢也，可得乎？凡此則虛文之爲害也。爲今之計，莫若略虛文而崇實效。欲崇實效，莫如先博大之令、嚴貪黷之懲、核舉刺之典、重簡任之道，而久任其要焉。何也？任不久則淑慝莫辨，任既久則志意悉舒。是故土風民俗，久則習之；規畫幾宜，久則定之；細微曲折，久則窮之；功勤勞閥，久則驗之。而言官所疏與銓曹所具列者，義既備矣。第千里之馭，急衘轡者必蹶，而急節繁響之樂，清廟無取焉。故汲黯守淮陽，其治責大指，不苛小；而蓋公相齊，無擾獄市。此清淨畫一、無所變更之明效也。今天下吏治率尚精敏，而舞文巧詆以輔法者，
translation_en: …deadlines, and the enforcement of law with censorial caps, could there not be one or two who are praised as capable? Yet in the end, this is nothing more than acting with harsh decisiveness or creating busywork, and all of it is done merely for the sake of reputation; their hearts are not necessarily sincere. How much more so when those who are not even capable make up nine out of ten! This is precisely what you, sir, meant by saying, "officials are not all good, and the way of governing officials has also not been fully realized." Now, when rewards and punishments from above are like that, and the conduct of officials themselves is like this, if we wish for our governance to surpass that of the Han dynasty, how could that be achieved? All of this is the harm caused by empty formalism. For the present plan, nothing is better than setting aside empty formalism and prizing practical results. If we wish to prize practical results, nothing is better than giving priority to broad and magnanimous ordinances, strictly punishing greed and corruption, verifying the statutes for recommendation and impeachment, and valuing the way of selective appointment—with long tenure in office being the most essential point. Why is this? If tenure is not long, then the good and the wicked cannot be distinguished; once tenure is long, one's intentions and ambitions can be fully unfolded. Therefore, as for local customs and popular mores, with long tenure one becomes familiar with them; as for plans and timely measures, with long tenure one settles them; as for subtle details and intricate complexities, with long tenure one thoroughly masters them; and as for meritorious service and diligent achievements, with long tenure one verifies them. What the speaking officials have memorialized and what the Ministry of Personnel has set forth in detail have already exhausted the principles of this matter. However, in driving a thousand-li horse, one who pulls too tightly on the bit and reins will surely make it stumble, and music of rapid tempo and intricate notes is not chosen for the Pure Temple. Thus, when Ji An 汲黯 served as Grand Protector of Huaiyang 淮陽, his administration focused on the main essentials and was not harsh in small matters; and when Master Gai 蓋公 advised the Chancellor of Qi 齊, he counselled against disturbing the courts and marketplaces. These are the clear effects of pure tranquility, uniformity, and refraining from constant changes. Today, administrative governance throughout the empire generally prizes shrewdness and agility, and those who manipulate the letter of the law and craftily level accusations to bolster the regulations…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
往往而是且日事於急切請易科條以表
暴其能卒使民畏之而不愛將焉用父母
爲也此博大之令所當先也周官六計弊
羣吏首以廉稱而今則度才品而處速退
者日爲囊槖之計其相習爲風也猶水之
走下不重隄防之不止也奈何吏以賍敗
乃罪止削仕籍令爲編氓其甚者又僅以
計免矣夫人情嗜利也無厭卽削籍且甘
心焉而況其他哉近例貪有指驗者臺臣
得按劾之甚則逮治此其法至善誠一一
===
行之卽貪墨之不懲未之有也若夫舉刺
之未盡核前所言已槩之矣然猶未盡也
愛憎殊情則毀譽失實臧否任意則好惡
違常甚亦有悃愊之吏德惠浹民而上之
人遠不之察者未必盡無也是得爲太公
之治哉是故司舉刺之權者不可不愼也
至若簡任之不重則又有可言焉唐虞用
人諸艱歷試而孔門高弟仕未有不爲邑
punctuated: 往往而是，且日事於急切，請易科條以表暴其能，卒使民畏之而不愛，將焉用父母爲也？此博大之令所當先也。《周官》六計弊羣吏，首以廉稱；而今則度才品而處速退者，日爲囊槖之計，其相習爲風也，猶水之走下，不重隄防之不止也。奈何吏以賍敗，乃罪止削仕籍、令爲編氓，其甚者又僅以計免矣！夫人情嗜利也無厭，卽削籍且甘心焉，而況其他哉？近例：貪有指驗者，臺臣得按劾之，甚則逮治。此其法至善，誠一一一行之，卽貪墨之不懲，未之有也。若夫舉刺之未盡核，前所言已槩之矣，然猶未盡也。愛憎殊情，則毀譽失實；臧否任意，則好惡違常。甚亦有悃愊之吏，德惠浹民，而上之人遠不之察者，未必盡無也。是得爲太公之治哉？是故司舉刺之權者，不可不愼也。至若簡任之不重，則又有可言焉。唐虞用人，諸艱歷試，而孔門高弟，仕未有不爲邑
translation_en:
… are found everywhere. Moreover, they daily busy themselves with urgent demands, requesting changes to the statutory regulations in order to display their own abilities. In the end, they cause the people to fear them rather than love them—what use, then, are they as “father and mother” officials to the people? Thus, broad-minded and magnanimous governance is what ought to be prioritized first.

In the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), when the six criteria of evaluation were used to judge the body of officials, integrity was cited first. Today, however, those who measure their own talents and rank and expect a swift retirement spend their days scheming to fill their pouches and sacks. Their mutual adoption of this as a custom is like water flowing downward: unless one builds heavy dikes to hold it back, it will not stop. How is it that when officials are ruined by bribery and corruption, their punishment goes no further than striking their names from the official register and reducing them to registered commoners, or in egregious cases, merely dismissing them during the triennial evaluation! Human nature is insatiable in its craving for profit; even if they are stripped of their official status, they gladly accept it—how much more so with lesser penalties! Under recent precedents, when there is concrete evidence of venality, Censorate officials are empowered to investigate and impeach the offenders, and in severe cases to arrest and punish them. This law is utterly admirable; if it were truly carried out in every single instance, there would never be a case where corrupt and venal officials were not deterred.

As for recommendations and impeachments not being thoroughly verified, what I have said previously has already outlined the matter, yet it has not exhausted it. When affection and animosity diverge in sentiment, slander and praise lose touch with reality; when commendation and censure follow personal whim, likes and dislikes violate constant norms. Indeed, it is not entirely unknown for there to be sincere and unpretentious officials whose virtue and kindness saturate the people, yet whose superiors are too distant to take notice of them. Can this be called governance of supreme impartiality? Therefore, those who wield the authority of recommendation and impeachment cannot fail to be cautious.

As for the lack of weight given to selection and appointment, there is still more that can be said. When Tang and Yu employed men, they tested them through all manner of difficulties, and among the foremost disciples of Confucius’s school, none entered official service without becoming a district …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
宰者今士一釋褐即輕外任不欲就即就
矣日夕惟遷改是冀此何異受人牛羊不
爲牧之而惟主之謝牧事望哉此始于任
之不重之過也且設官分職凡以爲民而
況郡守縣令其於民爲尤親乎愚切謂宜
倣
國初故事新進之士悉試理民毋遽以清華
授之而其委之以民也則假以便宜毋拘
以文法而又隨其材器不必求備撫字果
===
勞矣催科不過責寵辱無驚矣漕餉不苛
求而一眚之吏不遂督過人未有不感焉
思奮者此簡任之所當重也久任以王之
慎斯四者以輔之而又以超遷考課變通
之令之吏有不殫忠上之訏謨而奏安民
之實惠者鮮矣不然則操切者競進而摶
擊者爭馳是龔黃文召之流有長不獲一
表見也孰謂
聖明在上而可使今之吏治不漢氏若哉雖然
punctuated: 宰者。今士一釋褐，即輕外任不欲就；即就矣，日夕惟遷改是冀。此何異受人牛羊，不爲牧之，而惟主之謝牧事望哉？此始于任之不重之過也。且設官分職，凡以爲民，而況郡守、縣令，其於民爲尤親乎？愚切謂宜倣國初故事，新進之士，悉試理民，毋遽以清華授之。而其委之以民也，則假以便宜，毋拘以文法；而又隨其材器，不必求備。撫字果勞矣，催科不過責；寵辱無驚矣，漕餉不苛求。而一眚之吏，不遂督過，人未有不感焉思奮者。此簡任之所當重也。久任以王之，慎斯四者以輔之，而又以超遷考課變通之，令之吏有不殫忠上之訏謨，而奏安民之實惠者，鮮矣。不然，則操切者競進，而摶擊者爭馳，是龔、黃、文、召之流，有長不獲一表見也。孰謂聖明在上，而可使今之吏治不漢氏若哉？雖然，
translation_en: …steward. Today, as soon as scholars shed their commoner's clothes to enter office, they look down on provincial appointments and do not wish to take them up; and even if they do take them up, morning and evening they hope only for transfer and reassignment. How is this any different from receiving someone's cattle and sheep and, instead of herding them, merely hoping that the master will relieve one of the herding duties? This originates from the error of not attaching importance to their appointment. Moreover, establishing offices and dividing duties are all for the sake of the people—how much more so in the case of Commandery Governors and District Magistrates, who are especially close to the people? I earnestly believe that we should follow the precedent of the beginning of the dynasty: newly advanced scholars should all be tested in governing the people, and should not hastily be granted prestigious posts at court. And when entrusting the people to them, grant them discretionary power and do not bind them with the letter of the law; furthermore, employ them according to their talents and capacities without demanding perfection in everything. If they are truly diligent in caring for the people, do not excessively fault them in tax collection; if they are unmoved by favor or disgrace, do not make harsh demands of them regarding grain transport and military provisions. And if an official with a single unintentional slip is not immediately censured for the fault, there will be no one who is not moved to rouse himself to action. This is why selection and appointment ought to be given weight. By making long tenure the foundation [reading 主 for 王], carefully attending to these four matters to support it, and further adapting performance evaluations through exceptional promotions, it will be rare indeed for today's [reading 今 for 令] officials not to exhaust their loyalty in serving the grand counsels of the ruler above and achieve real benefits in bringing peace to the people. Otherwise, those who govern with harshness and urgency will compete for advancement, and those who strike out fiercely will vie to race ahead; thus men of the caliber of Gong Sui, Huang Ba, Wen Weng, and Shao Xinchen will forever be unable to distinguish themselves even once. Who would say that with a sage and enlightened ruler above, the administrative governance of today could be allowed to fall short of that of the Han dynasty? Even so,…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
又有說焉名實之際辨之爲難若其廉與
不廉惠與不惠則有可以自信者上方以
實之不副虞我而我又以名之不達自虞
乃舉其廉且惠者而弁髦之是又漢吏之
所不與也故一意廉惠即民受賜多矣民
受賜多即上意稱矣古有壺飧不發而餉
耨如賔者彼豈以求知爲也故吏治之敝
起於速化而速化之敝起於求知使夫人
而不求知焉則上之知眞矣此其責不專
===
於上也
第三問
同考試官教諭方　批〔雍州人物品格殊科子能歷擧　縱論評騭曲當且尚孜有素者耶宜錄以式〕
彪準
考試官教諭王　批〔品第昔賢而事功節義我獨取汾　陽道德文章獨取橫渠可以占所緼矣〕
考試官學正任　批〔譚昔賢行實如在掌上且斷案　不爽宛奮有卷之士也〕
punctuated:
又有說焉。名實之際，辨之爲難；若其廉與不廉、惠與不惠，則有可以自信者。上方以實之不副虞我，而我又以名之不達自虞，乃舉其廉且惠者而弁髦之，是又漢吏之所不與也。故一意廉惠，即民受賜多矣；民受賜多，即上意稱矣。古有壺飧不發而餉耨如賔者，彼豈以求知爲也？故吏治之敝起於速化，而速化之敝起於求知。使夫人而不求知焉，則上之知眞矣。此其責不專於上也。

第三問
同考試官教諭方　批〔雍州人物，品格殊科，子能歷擧縱論，評騭曲當，且尚孜有素者耶？宜錄以式。〕
彪準
考試官教諭王　批〔品第昔賢，而事功節義我獨取汾陽，道德文章獨取橫渠，可以占所緼矣。〕
考試官學正任　批〔譚昔賢行實如在掌上，且斷案不爽，宛奮有卷之士也。〕
translation_en:
… there is a further point to be made. At the boundary between reputation and reality, distinguishing the two is difficult; yet as to whether one is incorruptible or corrupt, benevolent or unbenevolent, that is something in which one can have confidence within oneself. When superiors worry about us on the grounds that our actual performance does not match our reputation, and we in turn worry for ourselves that our reputation does not reach above, if we then take our own incorruptibility and benevolence and cast them aside like a useless cap, this too is something the officials of the Han dynasty would not have approved of. Therefore, if one devotes oneself single-mindedly to incorruptibility and benevolence, the people will receive abundant blessings; and when the people receive abundant blessings, the ruler's wishes are fulfilled. In antiquity there were those who left gifted jars of food unopened, and those who brought meals to the weeding fields treating one another like honored guests—did they do so in order to seek recognition? Thus, the corruption of official administration arises from the desire for rapid advancement, and the evil of rapid advancement arises from seeking recognition. Suppose everyone refrained from seeking recognition; then the recognition from above would be genuine. Responsibility for this does not rest solely with those above.

Third Question
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Fang, comments: "The notable figures of Yongzhou belong to distinct categories of character and standing. You are able to enumerate them one by one and discuss them extensively, with evaluations that are nuanced and apt—surely you are one who has long been diligent in admiring and studying the ancients [? 尚孜/尚友]? It is fitting to record this as a model."
Biao Zhun 彪準
Examiner, County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Wang, comments: "In ranking the worthies of the past, for practical achievements and righteous integrity to single out the Prince of Fenyang [Guo Ziyi 郭子儀] (reading 我獨取 as 義獨取 [?], or 'I uniquely approve of your selecting Fenyang'), and for moral virtue and literary learning to single out Hengqu [Zhang Zai 張載]—from this one may gauge the depth of your inner cultivation."
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Ren, comments: "Discussing the deeds and realities of past worthies as if they were right in the palm of his hand, with judgments that never miss the mark—truly a scholar of well-stocked learning [? 宛奮有卷之士]."

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
古之君子隨材以立事因時以明志要皆
行其所自得而已君子當尚友之日奮好
修之志孰不欲掩迹前猷炳丹青之業希
光後模振金石之聲哉顧材之所賦通塞
殊其具而時之所值顯晦偶其遭於是各
因其所自得者而立之於事究生平之藴
明之於志宣性分之真是故根極道原敷
析大義非以肆辯也苞粹羣史擷芳六藝
非以炫博也亮猷炳績出將入相非以燁
===
寵也幽棲嘉遯捐榮集枯非以名高也要
皆行其所自得者而已學者即其所得而
反觀以自樹則前哲之標𥳑後事之砥淑
也奚必遡古之是而近世之非哉嘗聞穆
叔有言太上立德其次立功其次立言是
道德文章事功節義之所由著而埀之不
朽者也三代以前毋贅已以雍自后稷而
下文武成康培其基菁莪棫樸沃其化豐
鎬岐隴之間詩所稱王國多士克生者也
punctuated:
古之君子，隨材以立事，因時以明志，要皆行其所自得而已。君子當尚友之日，奮好修之志，孰不欲掩迹前猷，炳丹青之業；希光後模，振金石之聲哉？顧材之所賦，通塞殊其具；而時之所值，顯晦偶其遭。於是各因其所自得者，而立之於事，究生平之藴；明之於志，宣性分之真。是故根極道原，敷析大義，非以肆辯也；苞粹羣史，擷芳六藝，非以炫博也；亮猷炳績，出將入相，非以燁寵也；幽棲嘉遯，捐榮集枯，非以名高也；要皆行其所自得者而已。學者即其所得，而反觀以自樹，則前哲之標𥳑，後事之砥淑也，奚必遡古之是而近世之非哉？

嘗聞穆叔有言：「太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。」是道德、文章、事功、節義之所由著，而埀之不朽者也。三代以前，毋贅已。以雍自后稷而下，文、武、成、康培其基，「菁莪」、「棫樸」沃其化，豐、鎬、岐、隴之間，《詩》所稱「王國多士克生」者也。
translation_en:
The gentlemen of antiquity established their achievements in accordance with their talents and made manifest their aspirations in response to their times; in sum, they simply acted upon what they had personally attained. When a gentleman, in the days of befriending the ancients, rouses his resolve to cultivate excellence, who would not wish to surpass the plans of predecessors and make resplendent a career worthy of the annals of history, or to aspire to the glory of providing a model for posterity and ring out a reputation as enduring as metal and stone? Yet in the endowment of talent, the capacities for success or hindrance differ; and in the encounter with the times, the lot of prominence or obscurity is a matter of chance. Thus each, on the basis of what he has personally attained, establishes it in deeds to exhaust the store of his lifelong learning, or makes it manifest in his aspirations to declare the truth of his innate nature. Therefore, probing to the very source of the Way and analyzing great principles is not done to indulge in disputation; gathering the essence of the various histories and plucking the blossoms of the Six Arts is not done to show off erudition; displaying bright plans and radiant merits, going out as a general and entering court as a minister, is not done to bask in glorious favor; dwelling in seclusion in admirable withdrawal, casting aside榮 glory and embracing hardship, is not done for a lofty reputation. In sum, all simply act upon what they have personally attained. If scholars examine what those men attained and reflect upon themselves in order to establish their own standing, then the standards recorded of former sages serve as the whetstone for the refinement of later endeavors—why must one look back to antiquity as right and regard recent ages as wrong?

I have heard that Mushu 穆叔 once said: "The highest is to establish virtue; the next is to establish功 meritorious deeds; the next is to establish words." This is how moral virtue, literary composition, practical achievement, and righteous integrity become manifest and are handed down to immortality. Of the period before the Three Dynasties, there is no need to speak further. Take Yongzhou 雍州 from the time of Hou Ji 后稷 onward: Kings Wen 文, Wu 武, Cheng 成, and Kang 康 cultivated its foundations, the transformative influence celebrated in the odes "Jing'e" 菁莪 and "Yupu" 棫樸 enriched its culture, and the region between Feng 豐, Hao 鎬, Qi 岐, and Long 隴 was what the Classic of Poetry (Shi 詩) praises as a royal domain capable of bringing forth a multitude of worthy men.

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
當其時碩彥雲蒸鴻才林萃元聖而篤棐
者當制禮作樂之任隱居而屠釣者亮應
天順人之師其他濟濟思皇藹藹吉士類
皆潤色王猷張皇聖武敦詩說禮探性命
之原秉義全仁植綱常之重人有全德士
皆眞才豈非千古獨盛哉迨夫光岳既分
王教日遠士生其間非復成周之品而道
德文章事功節義分而爲四矣至漢晉唐
宋之世人才間出據其所得各有可述請
===
因執事所及者而上下其議論可乎當宣
帝之綜核名實也羣臣無能佐下風矣弱
翁身總衆職厲之以嚴所以賞罰信必克
稱上意也孝宣中興丙魏有聲班氏豈溢
美與當太宗之削除僭亂也軍興日爲之
叢脞矣如晦任居帷幄濟之以斷所以人
各稱職事無流滯也唐室賢相前稱房杜
柳芳殆實錄與韓休之相玄宗也數以直
諫人主之貌雖瘦而天下則肥開元之治
punctuated:
當其時，碩彥雲蒸，鴻才林萃。元聖而篤棐者，當制禮作樂之任；隱居而屠釣者，亮應天順人之師。其他濟濟思皇，藹藹吉士，類皆潤色王猷，張皇聖武，敦《詩》說《禮》，探性命之原，秉義全仁，植綱常之重。人有全德，士皆眞才，豈非千古獨盛哉？迨夫光岳既分，王教日遠，士生其間，非復成周之品，而道德、文章、事功、節義分而爲四矣。至漢、晉、唐、宋之世，人才間出，據其所得，各有可述。請因執事所及者，而上下其議論，可乎？

當宣帝之綜核名實也，羣臣無能佐下風矣。弱翁身總衆職，厲之以嚴，所以賞罰信必，克稱上意也。孝宣中興，丙、魏有聲，班氏豈溢美與？當太宗之削除僭亂也，軍興日爲之叢脞矣。如晦任居帷幄，濟之以斷，所以人各稱職，事無流滯也。唐室賢相，前稱房、杜，柳芳殆實錄與？韓休之相玄宗也，數以直諫，人主之貌雖瘦而天下則肥，開元之治…
translation_en:
At that time,eminent worthies rose like clouds and great talents gathered like forests. The great sage who rendered devoted assistance undertook the responsibility of instituting rites and creating music [the Duke of Zhou]; the recluse who had been a butcher and angler [Lü Shang, i.e., Taigong Wang] guided the armies that responded to Heaven and accorded with men. As for the others—the numerous and august multitude, the genial and refined gentlemen—they all alike embellished the royal plans, displayed the sacred martial prowess, devoted themselves to the Odes (Shi) and expounded the Rites (Li), probed the origins of human nature and destiny, upheld righteousness and perfected benevolence, and established the weighty principles of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues. Men possessed complete virtue, and scholars were all of genuine talent—was this not uniquely flourishing for all antiquity? When thevital energy of the realm (guangyue) became divided and the kingly teachings grew daily more distant, the scholars born in this region were no longer of the caliber of the flourishing Zhou, and morality, literary expression, statecraft, and righteous integrity split into four separate pursuits. Down to the eras of Han, Jin, Tang, and Song, men of talent appeared from time to time; based on what each attained, each has something worth recounting. May I take up those whom Your Excellency has mentioned and discuss them from past to present?

When Emperor Xuan of Han [r. 74–49 BCE] was verifying that names matched realities, the assembled ministers were scarcely able to assist him from below. Ruoweng [Wei Xiang 魏相, courtesy name Ruoweng] personally oversaw the myriad offices and spurred them on with strictness, so that rewards and punishments were trustworthy and certain, and he was able to fulfill the sovereign's intentions. In the restoration under the Filial Emperor Xuan, Bing [Bing Ji 丙吉] and Wei [Wei Xiang] won renown—was Ban Gu's praise of them in the History of the Han an exaggeration? When Emperor Taizong of Tang [r. 626–649] was sweeping away usurpers and rebels, military mobilization made daily affairs vexingly繁雜 [petty and crowded]. Ruhui [Du Ruhui 杜如晦] held responsibility within the command tent and aided the effort with decisive judgment, so that every man suited his office and affairs suffered no delay or stagnation. Among the worthy chief councilors of the Tang house, Fang [Fang Xuanling 房玄齡] and Du [Du Ruhui] were praised first of all—was Liu Fang's account not a veritable record? When Han Xiu 韓休 served as chief councilor to Emperor Xuanzong [r. 712–756], he frequently offered forthright remonstrance; though the ruler's countenance grew thin, the realm grew fat, and the governance of the Kaiyuan era [713–741]…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
庶幾貞觀休之守正不阿有助矣此宋璟
深嘆其賢也寇準之相眞宗也力贊親征
澶淵之役雖危而中國卒定景德之間契
丹畏服準之忘身徇國居多矣此畢士安
亟薦其義也先零肆侮漢廷無定畫矣充
國上金城之畧而罕开坐困老成謀國初
議不揺也营平其賢將哉回紇再入唐京
非舊物矣子儀奮單騎之勇而社稷重安
天性忠義神明扶持也汾陽眞大臣哉此
===
皆將相之表表者也以儒者言之敎授生
徒名震關西馬融也而作三傳以行於世
義何傳乎隱居不仕號稱大儒賈逵也而
著書百萬餘言志何篤乎杜元凱作長曆
因編年以寓褒貶春秋之旨明矣蓋可稱
武庫者與張子厚作西銘因事親以明事
天仁孝之道備矣蓋前聖未發者與以隱
士言之躬耕谷口慕采薇之風鄭子眞也
辭王鳳而不就身尤潔焉牧豕上林作五
punctuated:
庶幾貞觀，休之守正不阿有助矣，此宋璟深嘆其賢也。寇準之相眞宗也，力贊親征，澶淵之役雖危而中國卒定；景德之間，契丹畏服，準之忘身徇國居多矣，此畢士安亟薦其義也。先零肆侮，漢廷無定畫矣，充國上金城之畧而罕开坐困；老成謀國，初議不揺也，营平其賢將哉！回紇再入，唐京非舊物矣，子儀奮單騎之勇而社稷重安；天性忠義，神明扶持也，汾陽眞大臣哉！此皆將相之表表者也。
以儒者言之：敎授生徒，名震關西，馬融也，而作《三傳》以行於世，義何傳乎！隱居不仕，號稱大儒，賈逵也，而著書百萬餘言，志何篤乎！杜元凱作《長曆》，因編年以寓褒貶，《春秋》之旨明矣，蓋可稱武庫者與！張子厚作《西銘》，因事親以明事天，仁孝之道備矣，蓋前聖未發者與！
以隱士言之：躬耕谷口，慕采薇之風，鄭子眞也，辭王鳳而不就，身尤潔焉；牧豕上林，作《五
translation_en:
… nearly rivaled the Zhenguan era; [Han] Xiu's adherence to rectitude without flattery contributed to this, which is why Song Jing 宋璟 deeply admired his worthiness. When Kou Zhun 寇準 served as Grand Councilor to Emperor Zhenzong 眞宗, he vigorously urged the emperor to lead the campaign in person, so that although the campaign at Chanyuan 澶淵 was perilous, China was ultimately pacified; during the Jingde 景德 era, the Khitan stood in awe and submitted, which owed much to Zhun's selflessness in giving himself to the state, and this is why Bi Shi'an 畢士安 earnestly recommended his righteousness. When the Xianlian 先零 Qiang acted with rampant insolence, the Han court had no settled plan; [Zhao] Chongguo 趙充國 submitted his strategy for Jincheng 金城, and the Hanhan 罕开 tribes were trapped without a fight. As a seasoned veteran planning for the state, his initial proposal did not waver—truly the Marquis of Yingping 營平 was a worthy general! When the Uyghurs invaded once again, the Tang capital was no longer its former self; [Guo] Ziyi 郭子儀 summoned the courage to ride out as a lone horseman, and the altars of soil and grain were restored to peace. Endowed by nature with loyalty and righteousness, he was sustained by the gods—truly the Prince of Fenyang 汾陽 was a great minister! All of these were the most illustrious of generals and chancellors.

To speak of Confucian scholars: Teaching disciples and making his name resound throughout Guanxi 關西—that was Ma Rong 馬融; and in composing his commentaries on the Three Traditions (Sanzhuan 三傳) to circulate in the world, how widely his meaning was transmitted! Living in seclusion without taking office and being hailed as a great Confucian—that was Jia Kui 賈逵; and in authoring works totaling over a million words, how earnest was his resolve! Du Yuankai 杜元凱 [Du Yu 杜預] compiled the Long Calendar (Changli 長曆), using a chronological arrangement to lodge praise and blame, whereby the import of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) was made clear—surely he deserved to be called an "armory" of learning! Zhang Zihou 張子厚 [Zhang Zai 張載] composed the Western Inscription (Ximing 西銘), drawing upon the service to parents to elucidate the service to Heaven, whereby the Way of benevolence and filial piety was made complete—surely this was what former sages had not yet articulated!

To speak of recluses: Personally plowing at Gukou 谷口 and admiring the ethos of "gathering薇 ferns"—that was Zheng Zizhen 鄭子眞 [Zheng Pu 鄭樸]; in declining the summons of Wang Feng 王鳳 and refusing to take office, his personal integrity was especially pure. Herding swine in the Shanglin 上林 Park and composing the "Song of Five…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
噫之歌梁鴻也入會稽而不返志尤峻焉
田游巖安貧樂道而屢辭高宗之聘泉石
膏肓蓋其所自命者豈終南之疾徑耶种
司諫讀書養母而不赴太宗之辟雲溪退
士若將終身者豈北山之移誚耶合而觀
之數君子者材有通塞若難兼集所長時
有顯晦未能竝著于世要之行其所自得
則一而已矣夫其所自得者何也堅貞其
慮正固其守理義素明于中知識不眩乎
===
外也是以輔成保泰則宜弼直之猷定亂
扶傾則著匡襄之略當著述而立言以明
道當退處而抗節以秉貞道德事功文章
節義皆以垂不朽殆與華岳爭高渭流竝
長矣孰事欲別而言之且以觀先哲之標
準則生何適從哉蓋君子之尚論貴博而
其取則貴精不可不辨也今觀橫渠之學
精思力踐羽翼周程可以言道德矣至於
西銘正蒙又文章之尤著者也汾陽之勳
punctuated: 噫之歌》，梁鴻也；入會稽而不返，志尤峻焉。田游巖安貧樂道，而屢辭高宗之聘，「泉石膏肓」，蓋其所自命者，豈終南之疾徑耶？种司諫讀書養母，而不赴太宗之辟，「雲溪退士」，若將終身者，豈北山之移誚耶？合而觀之，數君子者，材有通塞，若難兼集所長；時有顯晦，未能竝著于世。要之，行其所自得，則一而已矣。夫其所自得者何也？堅貞其慮，正固其守，理義素明于中，知識不眩乎外也。是以輔成保泰，則宜弼直之猷；定亂扶傾，則著匡襄之略；當著述，而立言以明道；當退處，而抗節以秉貞。道德、事功、文章、節義，皆以垂不朽，殆與華岳爭高、渭流竝長矣。執事欲別而言之，且以觀先哲之標準，則生何適從哉？蓋君子之尚論貴博，而其取則貴精，不可不辨也。今觀橫渠之學，精思力踐，羽翼周、程，可以言道德矣；至於《西銘》、《正蒙》，又文章之尤著者也。汾陽之勳，
translation_en: … "Song of the Five Sighs" (Wuyi zhi ge) was Liang Hong 梁鴻; he entered Guiji 會稽 and never returned, his resolve all the more lofty. Tian Youyan 田游巖 was content in poverty and delighted in the Way, repeatedly declining the summonses of Emperor Gaozong 高宗; "an incurable passion for springs and rocks" was how he described himself—how could that be the "shortcut via Mount Zhongnan" [to officialdom]? Policy Critic (sijian) Chong [Chong Fang 种放] studied books and supported his mother, refusing to answer the summons of Emperor Taizong 太宗; styling himself the "Retired Scholar of Cloud Creek" (Yunxi tuishi) as though he would remain so for life—how could he be subject to the ridicule of the "Proclamation on Mount Bei" (Beishan yiwen)? Viewed together, among these several gentlemen, their talents met with either success or obstruction, as if it were difficult to combine all their strengths; their times were either illustrious or obscure, so they could not all be equally prominent in the world. Yet in essence, in practicing what they had personally attained, they were one and the same. And what was it that they had personally attained? They made their deliberations firm and pure, kept their integrity upright and steadfast, had principle and righteousness long illuminated within, and did not let their understanding be dazzled by externals. Therefore, when assisting in governance and preserving peace, they put forth counsels of rectitude and aid; when settling disorder and supporting the tottering, they manifested strategies of rescue and assistance; when called to write, they established words to illuminate the Way; and when called to withdraw into retirement, they upheld their integrity to maintain purity. Their moral virtue, practical achievements, literary writings, and upright integrity have all been handed down to immortality, almost vying in height with Mount Hua 華岳 and matching the length of the Wei River 渭流. Since Your Excellency [? text has 執事 written as 孰事] wishes to distinguish and discuss them, and thereby observe the standards set by the former worthies, what course should this student follow? Broadness is valued when a gentleman appraises figures of the past, yet precision is valued when he chooses his models; this must be carefully discriminated. Now, if we observe the learning of Hengqu 橫渠 [Zhang Zai 張載], he thought with precision and practiced with vigor, serving as wings to Zhou [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤] and the Chengs [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤]—this can truly be called moral virtue; as for his Western Inscription (Ximing) and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), they are moreover the most distinguished of literary writings. The meritorious deeds of Fenyang 汾陽 [Guo Ziyi 郭子儀], …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
旋乾轉坤左右爴代可以言事功矣至於
功成身退又節義之獨完者也下此則萊
公大節斯其次乎若壯侯之長畧韓林之
峭直君子取節焉弱翁之刑名基禍如晦
之賛成喋血蓋不能無遺議矣諸所立之
事功所謂血氣用事非耶馬融開絳帳而
身附梁冀之惡三傳何取焉貫逵專門君
子以爲固矣杜預嗜學君子以爲癖矣豈
聖門之文章哉子眞也梁鴻也游巖也潔
===
身避亂高矣實非通圓之軌种放遇有道
之主而僞隱沽名他日變塞重以致嗣宗
之笑節義又安在哉嗟乎愼别而嚴從者
尚論之凖也節取而竝觀者得師之益也
由弱翁而下皆人才之傑出者使其遊於
聖人之門則淵源所漸卽以登求路游夏
之科與逸民竝列焉可也君子本其行事
以定之矩考其立志以照之的皆吾人砥
淑之資也愼毋曰此非三代以上人物姑
punctuated: 旋乾轉坤，左右爴代，可以言事功矣；至於功成身退，又節義之獨完者也。下此則萊公大節，斯其次乎？若壯侯之長畧，韓林之峭直，君子取節焉。弱翁之刑名基禍，如晦之賛成喋血，蓋不能無遺議矣。諸所立之事功，所謂血氣用事，非耶？馬融開絳帳而身附梁冀之惡，三傳何取焉？貫逵專門，君子以爲固矣；杜預嗜學，君子以爲癖矣，豈聖門之文章哉？子眞也，梁鴻也，游巖也，潔身避亂，高矣，實非通圓之軌；种放遇有道之主，而僞隱沽名，他日變塞，重以致嗣宗之笑，節義又安在哉？嗟乎！愼别而嚴從者，尚論之凖也；節取而竝觀者，得師之益也。由弱翁而下，皆人才之傑出者，使其遊於聖人之門，則淵源所漸，卽以登求、路、游、夏之科，與逸民竝列焉可也。君子本其行事以定之矩，考其立志以照之的，皆吾人砥淑之資也，愼毋曰此非三代以上人物，姑
translation_en: … reversed the course of heaven and earth and assisted Emperors Suzong and Daizong [爴代 for 肅代], which can truly be called practical achievements; and when his功 merits were accomplished and he retired in person, his integrity and righteousness were moreover uniquely complete. Below this, does the great integrity of the Duke of Lai (Kou Zhun 寇準) come next? As for the far-reaching strategy of Marquis Zhuang (Wei Qing 衛青 [?]) and the stern uprightness of Han and Lin [?], the gentleman takes their good points selectively. Yet Ruoweng's (Wei Xiang 魏相) reliance on Penal Names (Legalism) laid the foundation for disaster, and Ruhui's (Du Ruhui 杜如晦) abetting of bloodshed cannot be free from lingering criticism. Are not the various practical achievements they established what one calls acting out of mere physical vigor and passion? Ma Rong 馬融 set up his crimson curtain to teach, yet personally attached himself to the wickedness of Liang Ji 梁冀—what is there to commend in his commentaries on the Three Traditions? Jia Kui 賈逵 [貫逵] specialized narrowly in a single school, which the gentleman regards as obstinate; Du Yu 杜預 was obsessed with learning, which the gentleman regards as an addiction—how could these be the literary culture of the Sage's gate? Zizhen (Zheng Pu 鄭樸), Liang Hong 梁鴻, and Youyan (Tian Youyan 田游巖) kept themselves pure and fled disorder; lofty as they were, theirs was truly not an all-encompassing, adaptable path. Chong Fang 种放 encountered a ruler who possessed the Way, yet feigned reclusion to buy fame; when later he changed what he had held to in obscurity, he further incurred the ridicule of Sizong (Ruan Ji 阮籍)—where then were his integrity and righteousness? Alas! To distinguish carefully and follow strictly is the standard for evaluating figures of the past; to select partial merits and observe them side by side is the benefit of finding teachers. From Ruoweng on down, all were outstanding talents; had they roamed within the gate of the Sage, then through the gradual influence of that deep source, they could have ascended to the categories of Ran Qiu 冉求, Zilu 子路, Ziyou 子游, and Zixia 子夏, or been ranked alongside the worthy recluses. If the gentleman bases himself on their deeds to fix a carpenter's square, and examines their aspirations to illuminate a target, they are all resources for us to whet and refine our virtue. Let us by no means say, "These are not personages from above the Three Dynasties, so for now…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
舍是哉
第四問
曹思聰
同考試官教諭涂　批〔馬政極敝而關陝為甚諸生類能敷陳周漢唐宋及我〕
國初舊法而於此中事多未之及即有議及者亦常談耳子能根究敝源真要緊也宜錄
之以備
采擇
考試官教諭王　批〔敘事詳酌議當而豪邁之氣溢於筆端自是有用文字〕
===
考試官學正任　批〔是集能發人所未發此其所以為奇〕〔佀當□文占耶〕
古今之談馬政者其說有二曰牧之官牧
之民而已祖公馬之說者主於官而不知
典守非其人是以使年病法也襲國馬之
說者主於民而不知法制有未盡是以多
事病民也權衡於二者之間以求宜官宜
民之道則得人要矣任法急焉是故慎簡
punctuated:
舍是哉？

第四問
曹思聰
同考試官教諭涂批：〔馬政極敝，而關陝為甚。諸生類能敷陳周、漢、唐、宋及我〕國初舊法，而於此中事多未之及；即有議及者，亦常談耳。子能根究敝源，真要緊也。宜錄之以備采擇。
考試官教諭王批：〔敘事詳，酌議當，而豪邁之氣溢於筆端，自是有用文字。〕
考試官學正任批：〔是集能發人所未發，此其所以為奇。〕〔佀當□文占耶？〕

古今之談馬政者，其說有二：曰牧之官、牧之民而已。祖公馬之說者，主於官，而不知典守非其人，是以使年病法也；襲國馬之說者，主於民，而不知法制有未盡，是以多事病民也。權衡於二者之間，以求宜官宜民之道，則得人要矣，任法急焉。是故慎簡
translation_en:
… set these aside?

Fourth Policy Question
Cao Sicong 曹思聰
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Tu 涂: [Horse administration has fallen into extreme decay, and it is worst in Guanzhong and Shaanxi. The candidates are generally able to set forth the practices of the Zhou, Han, Tang, Song, and the] old regulations from the founding of our dynasty, yet most fail to touch upon the actual affairs within this region; even when some do discuss them, it is merely commonplace talk. You are able to thoroughly investigate the roots of this decay, which is truly vital. It is fitting to record this essay so as to present it for selection.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wang 王: [The narrative of events is detailed, the deliberations and proposals are sound, and a heroic, vigorous spirit overflows from the tip of the brush; this is naturally a piece of practical, useful writing.]
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Ren 任: [This essay succeeds in bringing to light what others have failed to express, which is what makes it extraordinary.] [Could it perhaps take a place among the model essays [?]?]

Those who have discussed horse administration in ancient and modern times hold two views: namely, pasturing by the state and pasturing by the people, and nothing more. Those who follow the doctrine of "public horses" (gongma) favor management by officials, without realizing that when those in charge are not the right men, corrupt officials [reading 吏 for 年] [?] undermine the laws. Those who inherit the doctrine of "state horses" (guoma) favor management by the people, without realizing that when institutional regulations are less than thorough, excessive demands harm the people. If one weighs the balance between the two in order to seek a way that suits both the state and the people, then obtaining the right men is essential, and relying on sound regulations is urgent. Therefore, if one carefully selects…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以重其選變通以盡其利不徇乎今不泥
乎古而法唯人焉任之則官可牧也民亦
可牧也而於馬政有裨矣方今治教修明
馬政具舉而當事諸臣圖維計畫者又復
周至執事可謂無慮矣乃復筴諸生以經
國籌邊之畧甚盛心也愚請先言往事後
及
國朝新舊之制而終之以陜西唯執事擇焉
夫馬之爲政載在周禮者甚詳蓋其以丘
===
十六井出乘車而駕車馬牛皆有定數及
馬之具也長帥牧正董其事而得牧者則
賜姓賜邑傳之無窮以故成周之世藉國
馬以行軍資公馬以稱賦而周官法度燦
然具矣此豈有異故哉周公以關雎麟趾
之意弘經綸制作之猷故法善而人可守
耳由周以來蓋又有可言者漢牧于民而
用于官則衆庶蕃育唐牧于官而用于民
則賤可易縑此其效之可睹者而要所休
punctuated:
以重其選，變通以盡其利，不徇乎今，不泥乎古，而法唯人焉任之，則官可牧也，民亦可牧也，而於馬政有裨矣。方今治教修明，馬政具舉，而當事諸臣圖維計畫者又復周至，執事可謂無慮矣，乃復筴諸生以經國籌邊之畧，甚盛心也。愚請先言往事，後及國朝新舊之制，而終之以陜西，唯執事擇焉。

夫馬之爲政，載在《周禮》者甚詳。蓋其以丘十六井出乘車，而駕車馬牛皆有定數；及馬之具也，長帥、牧正董其事，而得牧者則賜姓賜邑，傳之無窮。以故成周之世，藉國馬以行軍，資公馬以稱賦，而周官法度燦然具矣。此豈有異故哉？周公以《關雎》、《麟趾》之意，弘經綸制作之猷，故法善而人可守耳。由周以來，蓋又有可言者：漢牧于民而用于官，則衆庶蕃育；唐牧于官而用于民，則賤可易縑。此其效之可睹者，而要所休
translation_en:
… to attach weight to their selection, and adapting flexibly to exhaust their benefits—neither conforming blindly to the present nor clinging rigidly to antiquity, and entrusting the laws solely to capable men—then horses can be pastured by the officials, and they can also be pastured by the people, which will be beneficial to horse administration. At present, governance and instruction are well-ordered and clear, horse administration is fully implemented, and the plans and deliberations of the officials in charge are moreover thorough and complete. Your Excellency might be said to have nothing to worry about, yet you still question the candidates on strategies for ordering the state and planning for the frontiers; this is a most magnanimous intention. I beg to speak first of past affairs, then touch upon the old and new institutions of our dynasty, and conclude with Shaanxi, leaving it to Your Excellency to select from among them.

Now, the administration of horses is recorded in great detail in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). In its system, a district (qiu) of sixteen well-fields (jing) supplied a war chariot, and the horses and oxen harnessed to the chariots all had fixed numbers. As for the provision of horses, the Commandants (zhangshuai) and Pasturage Directors (muzheng) supervised the affair, and those who succeeded in pasturing were bestowed surnames and fief-towns to be passed down without end. For this reason, in the age of Glorious Zhou, they relied on state horses (guoma) to march the armies and drew upon ducal horses (gongma) to match the military levies, so that the laws and regulations of the Offices of Zhou were resplendently complete. Was there any unusual reason for this? The Duke of Zhou used the spirit of the "Guanju" and "Linzhi" odes to broaden his plans for statecraft and institutional creation; thus the laws were good and men could uphold them. From the Zhou onward, there are also things worth mentioning: the Han pastured horses among the people and used them for the officials, so the populace bred them in abundance; the Tang pastured them under the officials and used them among the people, so horses became cheap enough to be traded for a bolt of silk. These are the visible results, yet in essence what gave rest and…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
息不專在于馬也至宋則畜監牧市邊關
而官馬戎馬之名立矣散編戶責孳生而
戶馬保馬之法興矣然妨政病民唯保馬
爲甚而周之良法始無復有存焉者宜執
事之重慨於熙寧而謂民翻以病也我
國家稽古定制仰法周官國初謀議之臣殫
忠竭猷固有不在周公下者豈於馬政爲
不備哉是故計戶以養馬計丁以課駒而
生之內者富茶易于西番絹市于遼左而
===
致之外者多其在陝西則地無頃畝計分
論駒地之利雖廣而駒之課仍寬是以地
得耕穫馬得飼養地漸沃壤馬漸蕃息所
以養之於官與民者法至善已夫其養之
官也所以給衛所之用也謂非周之設官
分治不可也其養之民也所以備諸邊之
乏也謂非周之寓兵于農不可也迨乎弘
正之間屢爲疏議而牧地之以公用徵者
銀以八百計矣嘉隆之際時爲釐正而牧
punctuated: 息不專在于馬也。至宋，則畜監牧、市邊關，而官馬、戎馬之名立矣；散編戶、責孳生，而戶馬、保馬之法興矣。然妨政病民，唯保馬爲甚，而周之良法始無復有存焉者。宜執事之重慨於熙寧，而謂民翻以病也。我國家稽古定制，仰法周官。國初謀議之臣，殫忠竭猷，固有不在周公下者，豈於馬政爲不備哉？是故計戶以養馬，計丁以課駒，而生之內者富；茶易于西番，絹市于遼左，而致之外者多。其在陝西，則地無頃畝，計分論駒。地之利雖廣，而駒之課仍寬。是以地得耕穫，馬得飼養，地漸沃壤，馬漸蕃息，所以養之於官與民者，法至善已。夫其養之官也，所以給衛所之用也，謂非周之設官分治不可也；其養之民也，所以備諸邊之乏也，謂非周之寓兵于農不可也。迨乎弘、正之間，屢爲疏議，而牧地之以公用徵者，銀以八百計矣；嘉、隆之際，時爲釐正，而牧
translation_en:
… [what was nurtured and] given rest did not lie solely in horses. Coming to the Song dynasty, they raised horses in pasturage directorates and purchased them at frontier passes, and thus the designations of "official horses" (guanma) and "military horses" (rongma) were established; they distributed them among registered households and exacted quotas of foals, and thus the systems of "household horses" (huma) and "security-group horses" (baoma) arose. Yet in obstructing governance and harming the people, nothing was worse than the baoma system, and the good laws of the Zhou for the first time had nothing left remaining of them. It is fitting that Your Excellency sighs deeply over the Xining era (1068–1077) and says that the people instead suffered from it.

Our State examined antiquity to establish its institutions, looking up to model itself on the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). At the founding of the dynasty, the ministers who planned and deliberated exhausted their loyalty and poured forth their counsels; indeed they were not inferior to the Duke of Zhou—how could they have been unprepared in horse administration? Therefore, households were calculated in order to raise horses, and adult males were calculated in order to levy foals, so that those bred within the interior were abundant; tea was traded with the Western Barbarians (Xifan) and silk was marketed in Liaodong, so that those brought in from the outside were numerous.

As for Shaanxi, the pastureland was not measured by the qing or mu, and foals were assessed by calculating shares. Although the profits of the land were broad, the quota of foals remained lenient. Because of this, the land could be plowed and harvested, and the horses could be fed and tended; the land gradually became fertile soil, and the horses gradually multiplied and thrived. The laws by which they were raised by both officials and the people were supreme in their excellence! Now, their being raised by officials was the means to supply the needs of the Guards and Battalions (weisuo); one cannot say this is not the Zhou principle of establishing offices and dividing governance. Their being raised by the people was the means to prepare against shortages along the various frontiers; one cannot say this is not the Zhou principle of lodging soldiers among the farmers.

When it came to the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) eras, memorials and deliberations were repeatedly submitted, and the silver levied on pasturelands for public expenses was reckoned in the eight hundreds; during the transition between the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras, reforms and rectifications were periodically made, and the pasture…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
地有山原坡川之等爲牧養多寡之數矣
時則銀雖徵而軍未稱苦也唯加至萬餘
而軍始病數雖限而馬未稱逋也唯定以
一頃有半之地而法始嚴遂有遺馬數十
匹棄地數十頃而散而之四方者此牧臣
所以目擊而議而省臣不容已于言也是
曷以故哉弊也久矣愚生更悉言之而執
事聽焉漢世民牧姑毋論唐人所稱牧於
官者監牧之官唯司芻牧一切孳養生息
===
官爲董之今之監牧則但較其孳生之數
徵其備用之馬而已而所以芻與牧者不
問也但以養之監苑養之衛所者爲養于
官而不知監苑衛所之軍之養與州縣之
民之養法令不同要之均養于民而已矣
嗟乎熙寧保馬之法固執事所爲長太息
者而今日馬政之行其害則有甚焉何也
宋人以馬給民唯其所願而又復其身給
其草束折變緣納之錢今則唯問其丁不
punctuated: 地有山原坡川之等，爲牧養多寡之數矣。時則銀雖徵而軍未稱苦也，唯加至萬餘而軍始病；數雖限而馬未稱逋也，唯定以一頃有半之地而法始嚴。遂有遺馬數十匹、棄地數十頃，而散而之四方者。此牧臣所以目擊而議，而省臣不容已于言也。是曷以故哉？弊也久矣，愚生更悉言之，而執事聽焉。漢世民牧姑毋論，唐人所稱牧於官者，監牧之官唯司芻牧，一切孳養生息，官爲董之。今之監牧，則但較其孳生之數，徵其備用之馬而已，而所以芻與牧者不問也；但以養之監苑、養之衛所者爲養于官，而不知監苑、衛所之軍之養與州縣之民之養，法令不同，要之均養于民而已矣。嗟乎！熙寧保馬之法，固執事所爲長太息者，而今日馬政之行，其害則有甚焉。何也？宋人以馬給民，唯其所願，而又復其身，給其草束折變緣納之錢；今則唯問其丁，不
translation_en: …pasturelands were graded into mountains, plateaus, slopes, and valleys to determine the quotas for raising more or fewer horses. At that time, although silver was levied, the soldiers did not yet complain of hardship; it was only when the levy was increased to over ten thousand taels that the soldiers began to suffer. Although quotas were fixed, horse deliveries were not yet in arrears; it was only when the rule was set at one and a half qing of land that the law became harsh. Consequently, there were those who left behind dozens of horses, abandoned dozens of qing of land, and scattered in all directions. This is why the officials in charge of horse pasturage, witnessing this with their own eyes, have deliberated on it, and why the supervising secretaries cannot refrain from speaking out. Why is this so? The abuses are of long standing. Your humble student will speak of them in greater detail, if Your Excellency will deign to listen. Setting aside the civilian pasturage of the Han dynasty for the moment, in what the men of the Tang called raising horses through the state, the officials of the Directorate of Horse Pasturage only managed fodder and grazing, while all matters of breeding and rearing were supervised by the officials themselves. In today's Directorates of Horse Pasturage, however, they merely audit the quotas of foals bred and requisition the reserve horses, without asking how they are fed and pastured. They merely regard horses raised in the Directorates and Pasturages or in the Guards and Battalions as being raised by the state, failing to realize that although the rearing of horses by soldiers in the Directorates, Pasturages, Guards, and Battalions differs in statutory regulations from the rearing of horses by commoners in the subprefectures and counties, in essence both amount to nothing other than raising them among the people. Alas! The horse-guarantee system of the Xining era (1068–1077) is indeed something over which Your Excellency heaves a long sigh, yet in the implementation of horse administration today, its harms are even worse. Why is that? When the men of the Song distributed horses to the people, it was purely voluntary, and moreover they exempted the keepers from personal labor service and granted them commutation cash for bundles of fodder and incidental dues. Today, however, one asks only about their adult male丁 status, not…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
問其願矣飼養芻牧之費其餘無幾而其
他賦役日益甚焉何望乎身之復也宋之
保馬不供他設而今他設如故矣監正圉
長臨之羣長小甲從而統之上下交征剝
求無猒而養馬之外役復叢然加也既供
糧稅以給公家又備芻秣以養官馬視宋
之害誠有甚焉者矣且馬之生也有報駒
之令馬之損也有責償之條日有生日有
斃而地之所出不勝其所償也況乎簿書
===
啓科派之隙印俵開需索之門而軍之困
也有不至流離轉徙不止者欲馬政之興
也得乎昔宋文彥博謂戶配一馬繫之維
之不能蕃息今之牧不獨縶維已也望其
蕃息可得哉故愚以為欲馬之蕃不問其
牧于官也牧于民也其議有三而得人任
法其要焉周官趣巫牧圉之職皆以德行
道藝之士為之而今外之苑太非直趣巫
牧圉也小之監正圉長亦非閹人關吏也
punctuated:
問其願矣。飼養芻牧之費，其餘無幾，而其他賦役日益甚焉，何望乎身之復也？宋之保馬不供他設，而今他設如故矣。監正、圉長臨之，羣長、小甲從而統之，上下交征，剝求無猒，而養馬之外役復叢然加也。既供糧稅以給公家，又備芻秣以養官馬，視宋之害誠有甚焉者矣。且馬之生也，有報駒之令；馬之損也，有責償之條。日有生，日有斃，而地之所出不勝其所償也。況乎簿書啓科派之隙，印俵開需索之門，而軍之困也，有不至流離轉徙不止者，欲馬政之興也，得乎？昔宋文彥博謂：「戶配一馬，繫之維之，不能蕃息。」今之牧不獨縶維已也，望其蕃息，可得哉？

故愚以為欲馬之蕃，不問其牧于官也、牧于民也，其議有三，而得人、任法其要焉。周官趣、巫、牧、圉之職，皆以德行道藝之士為之，而今外之苑、太，非直趣、巫、牧、圉也；小之監正、圉長，亦非閹人、關吏也。
translation_en:
…not asking whether they are willing. Of the allowances for feeding and pasturing, almost nothing remains, while other taxes and labor services grow heavier by the day—what hope is there of personal exemption from corvée? Under the Song bao-ma system, households were not subject to other impositions, whereas today other impositions remain just as before. Directors of Pasturage Directorates (jianzheng) and Stable Heads (yuzhang) oversee them from above, while Herd Heads (qunzhang) and Tithing Chiefs (xiaojia) supervise them in turn; superiors and subordinates alike engage in mutual exactions and endless extortion, and on top of raising horses, additional labor services are piled upon them in profusion. Having already paid grain taxes to supply the state, they must also prepare fodder and grain to raise government horses; compared to the evils of the Song, this is truly far worse. Moreover, when foals are born, there is the order to report them; when horses are lost, there is the statute requiring compensation. Every day some are born and every day some die, yet what the land produces is not enough to cover what must be compensated. How much more so when account books open loopholes for arbitrary surcharges, and branding and distribution open the door to extortionate demands! The distress of the military households does not stop until they are driven to destitution and flight—if one wishes horse administration to flourish under such conditions, how can that be achieved? Formerly, Wen Yan博 文彥博 of the Song said, "If each household is assigned a horse and keeps it tied and tethered, they cannot multiply." Today's pasturing is not merely a matter of tethering them; to hope that they will multiply—how could that be possible?

Therefore, I humbly believe that if we wish horses to multiply, regardless of whether they are pastured by the government or pastured by the people, there are three proposals to consider, and obtaining the right men and relying on sound laws are the essentials. Among the Zhou offices (Zhouguan), the posts of Masters of the Royal Stables (quma), Horse Veterinarians (wu), Herdsmen (mu), and Grooms (yu) were all filled by men of moral conduct, learning, and practical skill. Today, in the provinces, the Pasturage offices (Yuanma si) and Courts of the Imperial Stud (Taipu si) are not merely Masters of the Stables, Veterinarians, Herdsmen, and Grooms; even down to the minor Directors of Pasturage Directorates and Stable Heads, they are not mere doorkeepers and barrier clerks…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遷其秩者以爲置身于散地而人之目之
復以爲散而忽焉即屢申屢飭竟莫有效
覩易聽者以故怨望之心生橐槖之私起
矣是故比苑太以京寺之重處正長以科
貢之途如楊文襄之議可行也唐牧地起
隴右金城平涼天水東至樓煩外暨河曲
內則涇寧豳岐坊監錯置牧養有法而牧
地則堇千二百三十頃耳今邠涇寧州與
汧渭之境即其故地而閑田不耕者何止
一千二百三十也况洪永間所定草場自
東勝至河西抵古北口葢幾十萬里其饒
水草便牧馬者又不啻如唐人而已是故
擇地以立監牧設法以爲俵散如丘文莊
之議可行也
===
國初諸番納馬以茶酬之今番馬猶故而
聖天子威德遠被即俺酋桀黠亦歲貢名馬唯
謹斯固千載一時也已但金牌之制未復
而商茶所易安得霜蹏宜大延綏歲有互
punctuated: 遷其秩者，以爲置身于散地，而人之目之，復以爲散而忽焉。即屢申屢飭，竟莫有效覩易聽者。以故怨望之心生，橐槖之私起矣。是故比苑、太以京寺之重，處正、長以科、貢之途，如楊文襄之議可行也。唐牧地起隴右、金城、平涼、天水，東至樓煩，外暨河曲，內則涇、寧、豳、岐，坊、監錯置，牧養有法，而牧地則堇千二百三十頃耳。今邠、涇、寧州與汧、渭之境，即其故地，而閑田不耕者，何止一千二百三十也？况洪、永間所定草場，自東勝至河西，抵古北口，葢幾十萬里，其饒水草、便牧馬者，又不啻如唐人而已。是故擇地以立監牧，設法以爲俵散，如丘文莊之議可行也。國初，諸番納馬，以茶酬之。今番馬猶故，而聖天子威德遠被，即俺酋桀黠，亦歲貢名馬唯謹，斯固千載一時也已。但金牌之制未復，而商茶所易，安得霜蹏？宜大、延綏歲有互…
translation_en:
…Yet those who are transferred to these ranks regard themselves as placed in idle posts, and others who look upon them likewise consider them idle and treat them with neglect. Even though instructions and admonitions are repeatedly issued, in the end there is no effect that changes what people see and hear. Because of this, feelings of resentment arise and private pilfering begins. Therefore, equating the Pasturage Office and the Branch Court of the Imperial Stud with the prestige of the capital courts, and filling the posts of Directors of Pasturage Directorates and Herdsmen-in-Chief from the ranks of provincial graduates and tribute students—as proposed by Yang Wenxiang (Yang Yiqing 楊一清)—is feasible.

In the Tang dynasty, pasturelands stretched from Longyou, Jincheng, Pingliang, and Tianshui eastward to Loufan, extending outward to the Bend of the Yellow River (Hequ) and inward to Jing, Ning, Bin, and Qi. Corrals and directorates were interspersed and there were proper methods for pasturing and rearing, yet the pastureland totaled barely 1,230 qing. Today, Bin, Jing, and Ning Subprefectures, along with the regions of the Qian and Wei rivers, are those very same former lands, and how could the uncultivated idle fields there be merely 1,230 qing? Moreover, the pasturelands established during the Hongwu (1368–1398) and Yongle (1403–1424) eras, stretching from Dongsheng to Hexi and reaching Gubeikou, cover nearly a hundred thousand li; those areas rich in water and grass and convenient for pasturing horses far surpass what the men of the Tang possessed. Therefore, selecting lands to establish pasturage directorates and devising methods to distribute horses—as proposed by Qiu Wenzhuang (Qiu Jun 丘濬)—is feasible.

At the beginning of our dynasty, the various Tibetan and western tribes submitted horses and were rewarded with tea. Today, the tribal horses are still as before, and the august Son of Heaven's majesty and virtue reach afar; even the unruly and cunning chieftain Altan Khan respectfully presents famous horses in annual tribute. This is truly an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. However, the system of gold tallies has not been restored, and when horses are bartered for merchant tea, how can one obtain "frost-hoofed" steeds? In Xuanfu-Datong [reading 宣大 for 宜大] and Yansui, there are annual mutual [markets]…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
市然我以敝繒給之彼以玄黃償之足甫
出邊而已不詰水草待斃矣欲以養之監
苑而試之於行陳十而二三耳是故增馬
直以啖羣胡捐微利以收奇駿如李文正
之議可行也乃其法之在西土者則又有
可言焉諸臣所論疏
上業已下有司議矣今欲減銀以寬之則軍餉
何可缺欲增地以充之則銀額何可更法
之弊也亡已時已計莫若做
===
國初之制而酌時宜行之屬公平通變之人
修丈勘均齊之法某也督亢獲可畝一鍾
某也磽确十不二三息者夫然後簡牧軍
而以馬給之每地三頃令養馬一匹而又
爲肥瘠搭配之法專令餧養諸以他故差
者悉已之其以餘地徵銀者量減十七載
之籍略如民屯故事兩限完徵以給軍餉
斯地有餘利民有餘力牧不稱苦馬不稱
乏上可以復
punctuated: 市，然我以敝繒給之，彼以玄黃償之，足甫出邊而已不詰水草、待斃矣。欲以養之監苑而試之於行陳，十而二三耳。是故增馬直以啖羣胡，捐微利以收奇駿，如李文正之議，可行也。乃其法之在西土者，則又有可言焉。諸臣所論，疏上，業已下有司議矣。今欲減銀以寬之，則軍餉何可缺？欲增地以充之，則銀額何可更？法之弊也，亡已時已。計莫若做國初之制，而酌時宜行之。屬公平通變之人，修丈勘均齊之法：某也督亢，獲可畝一鍾；某也磽确，十不二三息者。夫然後簡牧軍而以馬給之，每地三頃，令養馬一匹，而又爲肥瘠搭配之法，專令餧養，諸以他故差者悉已之。其以餘地徵銀者，量減十、七，載之籍，略如民屯故事，兩限完徵，以給軍餉。斯地有餘利，民有餘力，牧不稱苦，馬不稱乏，上可以復
translation_en:
… markets, yet when we supply them with worn-out silks, they repay us with sickly, exhausted horses; their hooves have barely crossed the frontier before they are already ignoring water and grass and waiting to die. If one wishes to raise them in the Directorate Pastures and test them in battle formations, scarcely two or three out of ten will serve. Therefore, increasing the price paid for horses to entice the various northern tribes and sacrificing petty profit to acquire extraordinary steeds, as proposed by Li Wenzheng (Li Dongyang 李東陽), is practicable.

As for the methods practiced in the western regions, there is also something to be said. The memorials discussing this by various officials have been submitted to the Emperor and already handed down to the competent authorities for deliberation. Now, if we wish to reduce the silver commutations to grant relief, how can military rations be left short? If we wish to increase the land allotments to make them sufficient, how can the fixed silver quotas be altered? The abuses of the system will never come to an end. The best plan is to model ourselves [on? Text has 做 for 倣] the system of the beginning of the dynasty while adapting it to the needs of the times. We should entrust fair-minded and adaptable men to institute a method of surveying and equalizing the land: noting that a certain tract is fertile like Dukang, capable of yielding a zhong per mu, while another tract is stony and barren, yielding a return of not even two or three parts in ten. Only then should we select the pasturage soldiers and issue horses to them, ordering that for every three qing of land, one horse be raised, while also instituting a method of pairing fertile and barren lands. They should be exclusively assigned to feeding and tending the horses, and all requisitions for other labor services should be completely abolished. For the remaining land on which silver is levied, the rate should be reduced after consideration by a tenth or up to seven-tenths [or: reduced to seven-tenths] and recorded in the registers; roughly following the precedent of civilian military-agricultural colonies (mintun), the levy should be completed in two installments to supply military rations. Thus the land will yield surplus profit, the people will have spare strength, the herdsmen will not complain of hardship, and the horses will not be spoken of as scarce. At the highest level, we can restore …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
國初之盛追成周之富而下陋漢唐宋於不
居矣即不然而曰地不可倍增量加焉可
也銀不可太減量𨷖焉可也雖日一點印
日一比徵而雇倩逃賣之姦終不可革又
安望修丘文莊李文正楊文襄之議而行
之今日也哉善乎李覺之言曰猶頓買人
子也朱公教以畜五牸十年之間其息無
筭況以今日之馬而得人焉盡法以養之
其所蕃息當與成周不異矣何虞不可制
===
何九邊諸關之勢不可重乎雖然生所復
執事者法耳張萬歲王毛仲彼已何人然
坊監畜牧勤勞不憚故貞觀至麟德間馬
七十萬六千匹而王之牧也亦已至于四
十三萬焉此其小者也魯僖思無邪而駉
牡之盛衛文公騋牝三千之富
說者謂秉心塞淵基之彼直一國君小吏
耳且猶若此況
聖天子主持于上至誠所動天地可格而況于
punctuated: 國初之盛，追成周之富，而下陋漢、唐、宋於不居矣。即不然而曰：「地不可倍增，量加焉可也；銀不可太減，量𨷖焉可也。」雖日一點印，日一比徵，而雇倩、逃賣之姦終不可革，又安望修丘文莊、李文正、楊文襄之議而行之今日也哉！善乎李覺之言曰：「猶頓，買人子也。朱公教以畜五牸，十年之間，其息無筭。況以今日之馬而得人焉，盡法以養之，其所蕃息當與成周不異矣。」何虞不可制，何九邊諸關之勢不可重乎？雖然，生所復執事者，法耳。張萬歲、王毛仲，彼已何人？然坊監畜牧，勤勞不憚，故貞觀至麟德間，馬七十萬六千匹；而王之牧也，亦已至于四十三萬焉。此其小者也。魯僖「思無邪」而駉牡之盛，衛文公「騋牝三千」之富，說者謂「秉心塞淵」基之。彼直一國君、小吏耳，且猶若此；況聖天子主持于上，至誠所動，天地可格，而況于
translation_en:
… the flourishing state of the early years of our dynasty, rival the wealth of the perfected Zhou, and look down upon the Han, Tang, and Song as unworthy of comparison. If instead one refuses to do this and says, "The land allocation cannot be doubled, though a modest increase is permissible; the silver commutation cannot be greatly reduced, though a slight remission is permissible," then even if horses are inspected and branded daily and silver arrears are compared and flogged daily, the abuses of hiring substitutes, absconding, and illicit selling can never be eradicated. How then could we ever hope to revive the proposals of Qiu Wenzhuang (Qiu Jun 丘濬), Li Wenzheng (Li Dongyang 李東陽), and Yang Wenxiang (Yang Yiqing 楊一清) and put them into practice today?

Well put were the words of Li Jue 李覺: "猗頓 [transcribed 猶頓, Yi Dun] was the son of a commoner [or merchant, 賈人, transcribed 買人]. Lord Zhu (Fan Li 范蠡) taught him to raise five breeding females, and within ten years their offspring were beyond count. How much more so if with the horses of today we obtain the right men and exhaustively apply the methods to rear them—their multiplication would surely not differ from that of the perfected Zhou!" What northern adversary could not then be subdued, and how could the strategic strength of the passes along the Nine Frontiers not be reinforced?

Even so, what I, a student, have presented in reply to Your Excellency is merely the institutional method. Who were Zhang Wansui 張萬歲 and Wang Maozhong 王毛仲? Yet in the pasturage directorates they tended the herds without shirking toil; thus from the Zhenguan (627–649) to the Linde (664–665) eras, the horses numbered 706,000, and under Wang's herding they also reached 430,000. And these are the lesser examples. Duke Xi of Lu 魯僖公 "had no depraved thoughts" and enjoyed a multitude of sturdy stallions; Duke Wen of Wei 衛文公 possessed the wealth of "three thousand tall mares," which commentators say was founded upon his "holding a heart sincere and deep." Those were merely feudal lords of single states or minor officials, and yet they achieved such results. How much more so when our Sacred Son of Heaven presides above, whose utmost sincerity can move and reach Heaven and Earth—let alone…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
馬乎賢百執事交警于下忠敬所孚無勛
不樹而況一牧事乎生固知天下之馬無
不盛天下之馬政無不舉而不獨陜以西
也
第五問
南企仲
同考試官教諭薛　批〔指陳虜酋情態洞然自中雲長慮却顧訏謨遠略令讀者惕然有省特此以籌百不失一矣蓋不徒文字古也〕
===
考試官教諭王　批〔數百言非故諳虜情不能有此即老將不如也錄之〕
考試官學正任　批〔忠懇之情慷慨之氣具見乎詞予以書生而當甲兵者乎〕
令之計者曰俺酋耄年好佛率所部十萬
衆而久牧河外張掖酒泉之間欲佛之福
利而私其身耳非有他也不然則瓦剌之
種彼所深讎三以其衆覆之而無一矢之
利彼所欲甘心而一當焉者蓋鑒往時輕
punctuated:
馬乎？賢百執事交警于下，忠敬所孚，無勛不樹，而況一牧事乎？生固知天下之馬無不盛，天下之馬政無不舉，而不獨陜以西也。

第五問
南企仲
同考試官教諭薛　批〔指陳虜酋情態，洞然自中雲。長慮却顧，訏謨遠略，令讀者惕然有省。特此以籌，百不失一矣，蓋不徒文字古也。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔數百言，非故諳虜情，不能有此，即老將不如也。錄之。〕
考試官學正任　批〔忠懇之情，慷慨之氣，具見乎詞。予以書生而當甲兵者乎！〕

令之計者曰：「俺酋耄年好佛，率所部十萬衆而久牧河外張掖、酒泉之間，欲佛之福利而私其身耳，非有他也。不然，則瓦剌之種，彼所深讎，三以其衆覆之而無一矢之利，彼所欲甘心而一當焉者。蓋鑒往時輕
translation_en:
…horses? When the worthy officials of all ranks mutually admonish one another below, through the trust inspired by their loyalty and reverence, there is no merit that cannot be established—and how much more so for the single matter of horse pasturage! This student therefore knows for certain that the horses throughout the realm will all flourish, and the horse administration throughout the realm will be fully upheld, not merely in the regions west of Shaan!

Fifth Question
Nan Qizhong 南企仲
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Xue 薛 comments: [His exposition of the chieftain's circumstances and attitude hits the mark with complete clarity [?]. Looking far ahead and considering behind, with grand counsels and far-reaching strategy, it makes the reader wake up with vigilance. Relying on this to lay plans, not one in a hundred will fail; indeed, it is not merely that its literary style is antique.]
Examiner, County Director of Studies Wang 王 comments: [Several hundred words that could not have been written without a seasoned familiarity with the caitiffs' situation; even a veteran general could not surpass this. Record it.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Ren 任 comments: [Loyal and earnest feeling, and an impassioned and resolute spirit, are both fully visible in his words. Could this be a scholar who serves as the equal of armored soldiers!]

Those who make plans today [?] say: "The chieftain Altan (Anqiu 俺酋) is in his extreme old age and fond of Buddhism. He has led his horde of a hundred thousand men to pasture for a long time beyond the Yellow River between Zhangye 張掖 and Jiuquan 酒泉, merely desiring the blessings and benefits of the Buddha for his own person; he has no other motive. Otherwise, it is because the Oirat (Wala 瓦剌) tribes are his deep enemies; thrice their forces have defeated him without his gaining the advantage of a single arrow, and it is they against whom he wishes to slake his vengeance and have a reckoning. For he has taken warning from the mistake of his past rash…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
舉之誤而傾其巢穴移駐近境以示先聲
然後伺其便以曳落何嘗之耳所謂夷狄
相攻中國之利幸彼之愚不知自解耳亦
非有他也不然則
貢市之利已七八年憑藉寵靈而威行塞外
彼豈匪茹而不以爲中國之惠且彼之所
好者佛而中國爲之通其意彼之所希者
賞而中國爲之順其情是我有大造於彼
也虜雖獰獷豈不知中國之大雖不屑屑
===
夷狄之治而紀綱法度可恃以維城者猶
足爲萬年之固而敢無故自敗其約以僥
倖萬不可必之擄掠而啓我疆埸之謀以
爲彼肘腋之患哉必不然矣然明計者不
以淺深而逃其情彼既以禮佛而來則當
以禮佛而去佛既禮矣東西南北自在也
即中國一家未有不畫野分州者如以爲
辭不能號之而遽去胡能號之而畢來乎
况互市之地益增屬番之挾益甚茶馬之
punctuated:
舉之誤，而傾其巢穴，移駐近境以示先聲，然後伺其便以曳落何嘗之耳。所謂「夷狄相攻，中國之利」，幸彼之愚不知自解耳，亦非有他也。不然，則貢市之利已七八年，憑藉寵靈而威行塞外，彼豈匪茹而不以爲中國之惠？且彼之所好者佛，而中國爲之通其意；彼之所希者賞，而中國爲之順其情，是我有大造於彼也。虜雖獰獷，豈不知中國之大，雖不屑屑夷狄之治，而紀綱法度可恃以維城者，猶足爲萬年之固，而敢無故自敗其約，以僥倖萬不可必之擄掠，而啓我疆埸之謀，以爲彼肘腋之患哉？必不然矣。」

然明計者不以淺深而逃其情。彼既以禮佛而來，則當以禮佛而去。佛既禮矣，東西南北自在也。即中國一家，未有不畫野分州者，如以爲辭不能號之而遽去，胡能號之而畢來乎？况互市之地益增，屬番之挾益甚，茶馬之
translation_en:
…mistake of acting rashly, he is emptying out his lair and moving his encampment near the frontier to project an intimidating reputation in advance, and will then wait for an opportunity to test them at Yeluoho [?曳落何]. As the saying goes, "When barbarian tribes attack one another, it is to China's advantage"—we are fortunate that in their folly they do not know how to resolve their own feuds; there is nothing more to it than this. Or else, he has enjoyed the profits of tribute and border markets for seven or eight years now, relying on imperial favor and prestige to project his authority beyond the frontiers; how could he fail to reckon this and not regard it as China's generosity? Moreover, what he delights in is the Buddha, and China facilitates his wishes; what he hopes for is rewards, and China indulges his desires—thus we have conferred great grace upon him. Though the caitiffs are fierce and savage, how could they not know that great China, even if it does not bother itself with governing barbarians in detail, still possesses institutions, laws, and discipline that can be relied upon as a bulwark sufficient for ten thousand years of security? Would he dare without cause to break his own covenant, gambling on plunder that is utterly uncertain, thereby provoking strategic countermeasures on our frontiers and creating a threat right at his own elbow and ribs? Surely it is not so."

Yet a clear-sighted strategist does not let the depth or shallowness of appearances cause him to miss the true situation. Since he came in the name of worshiping the Buddha, he ought to depart once he has worshiped the Buddha. Now that the Buddha has been worshiped, he is free to go east, west, south, or north. Even within China, which is a single family, there is no place that is not demarcated into territories and provinces. If he makes the excuse that he cannot issue orders to make his hordes depart suddenly, how was he able to issue orders to make them all come together in the first place? Furthermore, the locations for border markets are increasingly multiplied, the coercion of our tributary Tibetan tribes grows ever more severe, and their demands for tea and horses…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
請益驕凡此皆覬覦之萌或者有中行說
之徒為之煽誘又或有如喜寧之屬為之
蠱惑皆未可知也故天下有外癡而中黠
者其情不可不察也遠料者不以强弱而
爽其勢自古鄰國之交猶有假道之禮借
云彼之有事於瓦剌也何不以情輸我而
先為乞哀乃遽載其穹廬驅其羊馬使投
鞭之衆絡繹於國門之外比之蜂屯蟻聚
我見其不足與校而彼以為不敢誰何能
===
必彼之慊然而內懼曰中國一旦遂我我
且為窮寇乎此其勢不可不虞也蓋嘗讀
匈奴傳而知彼之為中國患自周以來郎
未有得上策者我
太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元
成祖文皇帝三犁虜庭然倏順倏叛奄入奄遯
情態萬狀未嘗帖然傾心也我
穆宗莊皇帝以天覆地載之恩為
宗社無疆之計遂使俛首稱藩誓堅
punctuated: 請益驕，凡此皆覬覦之萌。或者有中行說之徒為之煽誘，又或有如喜寧之屬為之蠱惑，皆未可知也。故天下有外癡而中黠者，其情不可不察也。遠料者不以强弱而爽其勢。自古鄰國之交，猶有假道之禮。借云彼之有事於瓦剌也，何不以情輸我而先為乞哀？乃遽載其穹廬，驅其羊馬，使投鞭之衆絡繹於國門之外，比之蜂屯蟻聚。我見其不足與校，而彼以為不敢誰何，能必彼之慊然而內懼曰：「中國一旦遂我，我且為窮寇」乎？此其勢不可不虞也。蓋嘗讀《匈奴傳》，而知彼之為中國患，自周以來，郎未有得上策者。我太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元，成祖文皇帝三犁虜庭，然倏順倏叛，奄入奄遯，情態萬狀，未嘗帖然傾心也。我穆宗莊皇帝以天覆地載之恩，為宗社無疆之計，遂使俛首稱藩，誓堅
translation_en:
…demands [for tea and horses] grow ever more arrogant—all these are the sprouts of covetous ambitions. Perhaps there are people like Zhonghang Yue 中行說 instigating and enticing them, or perhaps there are those of the ilk of Xi Ning 喜寧 bewitching and deluding them; all of this is impossible to know for certain. Thus in the world there are those who appear foolish on the outside yet are cunning within; their true intentions cannot go unexamined.

Those who calculate far ahead do not misjudge the strategic situation on account of strength or weakness. Since antiquity, in relations between neighboring states there has at least been the courtesy of requesting right of passage. Even supposing that they had military business with the Oirats (Wala 瓦剌), why did they not convey the truth to us and first plead for sympathy?
