Instead, they suddenly loaded up their felt tents and drove their sheep and horses, causing a multitude numerous enough to dam a river with their whips to stream endlessly outside our frontier gates, gathering like swarms of bees and colonies of ants. We view them as not worth reckoning with, while they take it that we dare not challenge them at all. How can we be certain that they feel dissatisfied and inwardly fearful, saying to themselves, "If one day China drives us out [? 遂我, for 逐我], we shall become desperate bandits"? This strategic situation is one we cannot fail to guard against.

Indeed, I have read the "Account of the Xiongnu" (Xiongnu zhuan 匈奴傳) and know that in the menace they have posed to China since the Zhou dynasty, no one has ever attained the supreme strategy [? 郎, for 誠/即]. Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi 太祖高皇帝, the Hongwu Emperor), swept away the barbarian Yuan, and our Accomplished Progenitor, Emperor Wen (Chengzu Wenhuangdi 成祖文皇帝, the Yongle Emperor), thrice plowed up the caitiffs' court. Yet they were one moment submissive and the next rebellious, suddenly invading and suddenly fleeing, their attitudes and dispositions taking myriad forms, never once docilely devoting their hearts to us. Our Majestic Ancestor, Emperor Zhuang (Muzong Zhuanghuangdi 穆宗莊皇帝, the Longqing Emperor), with grace as all-encompassing as Heaven and Earth, made boundless plans for the ancestral altars and altars of soil and grain, thereby causing them to bow their heads, declare themselves vassals, and swear to firmly maintain…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
貢市
皇上內順治而外威嚴修
二祖之政而揚
穆考之烈所以赤子視之而不以塞垣限之者
誠以守在四夷而兩階自舞且謂彼之未
敢生心也然
廟筭不可深測而封疆之臣念在多壘者亦惟
示三可疑以使之必去講三可恃以待其
不去而已何以故諸番之曲意於彼而爲
===
之鄉導非無飲恨之情也積威所刼欲報
而不能且無以爲歸耳今竭力事之且踰
年矣能無怨望之意乎聞古人有能使回
紇反攻吐蕃者因而撫之結之又爲之詷
其隙而諜以間之若欲相糾而判虜者然
虜能無疑乎虜衆離其巢穴已經寒暑射
獵少獲且其習俗惡疫而畏痘獨不可以
人力爲之乎聞昔人有毒涇上流者因而
倣之或於餱糧或於水草善藏其用而不
punctuated: 貢市。皇上內順治而外威嚴，修二祖之政而揚穆考之烈，所以赤子視之而不以塞垣限之者，誠以守在四夷而兩階自舞，且謂彼之未敢生心也。然廟筭不可深測，而封疆之臣念在多壘者，亦惟示三可疑以使之必去，講三可恃以待其不去而已。何以故？諸番之曲意於彼而爲之鄉導，非無飲恨之情也，積威所刼，欲報而不能，且無以爲歸耳。今竭力事之，且踰年矣，能無怨望之意乎？聞古人有能使回紇反攻吐蕃者，因而撫之結之，又爲之詷其隙而諜以間之，若欲相糾而判虜者然，虜能無疑乎？虜衆離其巢穴，已經寒暑，射獵少獲，且其習俗惡疫而畏痘，獨不可以人力爲之乎？聞昔人有毒涇上流者，因而倣之，或於餱糧，或於水草，善藏其用而不
translation_en: … tribute and border markets. His Majesty maintains harmonious rule within and stern majesty without, cultivating the governance of the Two Ancestors (Taizu and Chengzu) and exalting the illustrious achievements of His Late Father, Emperor Muzong. The reason he regards them as infants and does not bar them with the frontier walls is truly because when the Son of Heaven's defense lies among the four barbarian peoples, shield-and-feather dances are performed of themselves between the two staircases, and furthermore because it is held that they dare not harbor treacherous intentions. Yet the calculations of the imperial court cannot be deeply fathomed, and frontier officials whose thoughts dwell on the multitude of ramparts can only display three grounds for suspicion to compel them inevitably to depart, and cultivate three things to rely upon in preparation for their refusal to depart—nothing more. Why is this so? When the various Tibetan tribes (Fan) bend to their will and serve as their guides, it is not that they lack swallowed resentment; coerced by accumulated menace, they wish to avenge themselves but cannot, and moreover have nowhere to turn for refuge. Now they have exhausted their strength in serving them for over a year—how could they be without feelings of grievance and discontent? We hear that among the ancients there were those who could induce the Uyghurs (Huihe) to turn and attack the Tibetans (Tubo). If we avail ourselves of this to pacify and win them over, and furthermore spy out their rifts and use secret agents to sow discord among them, making it appear as though they intend to band together and rebel against the Caitiffs (lu), how could the Caitiffs not be suspicious? The Caitiff hordes have been away from their lairs through winter and summer; their hunting yields little catch, and moreover by custom they abhor pestilence and dread smallpox—can this alone not be brought about by human effort? We hear that among men of old there were those who poisoned the upper reaches of the Jing River. If we pattern ourselves after this—whether in dry provisions or in water and pasture—skillfully concealing its application without…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
露其機使彼士馬喪亡而不得其故虜能
無疑乎彼之切齒於瓦剌亦猶之瓦剌切
齒於彼也古有鷸蚌之喻今其時矣厚募
明辯有膽略者速之使鬪而又東西誤之
或誑以巢穴之覆或誑以仇讎之至虜能
無疑乎如是而又恩結藏僧許以虜退則
優其禮利招通事約以虜退則賞之官皆
聽彼之自爲術而吾不與焉虜其有維縶
者乎不然則堅壁清野昔人已有定筭而
===
===
預爲收斂又
朝廷不忍鋒刃之成法
勅甘肅守臣熟計而預待之且今之城守視昔
金湯矣今之堡寨視昔扃鑰矣此其定不
可恃乎竝邊要害稍增屯戍若慮糧餉不
給首惟汰其老弱不必別爲調度而又時
時飭之使之終日欽欽常如對陳即腹裏
郡縣有苦饑寒欲流離者慎擇良守令以
時撫定之不至輕爲搖動此其預不可恃
alt_text:
露其機使彼彼士馬喪亡而不得其故虜能
無疑乎彼之切齒於兀剌亦猶之兀剌切
齒於彼也古有鷸蚌之喻今其時矣厚募
明辯有膽略者速之使鬭而又東西誤之
或誑以巢穴之覆或誑以仇讎之至虜能
無疑乎如是而又思結藏僧許以虜退則
優其禮利招通事約以虜退則賞之官皆
聽彼之自爲術而吾不與焉虜其有維喙
者乎不然則堅壁清野昔人已有定弄而
===

齒於彼也古有鷸蚌之喻今其時矣厚募
明辯有膽略者速之使鬭而又東西誤之
或誑以巢穴之覆或誑以仇讎之至虜能
無疑乎如是而又思結藏僧許以虜退則
優其禮利招通事約以虜退則賞之官皆
聽彼之自爲術而吾不與焉虜其有維喙
者乎不然則堅壁清野昔人已有定弄而
===
預爲牧斂又
朝廷不忍鋒刃之成法
勑甘肅守臣熟計而預待之且今之城守視昔
金湯矣今之堡寨視昔扃鑰矣此其定不
可恃乎茲邊要害稍增屯戍若慮糧餉不
給首惟汰其老弱不必别爲調度而又時
時飭之使之終日欽欽常如對陳即腹裏
郡縣有苦饑寒欲流離者愼擇良守令以
時撫定之不至輕爲搖動此其預不可恃
punctuated: 露其機，使彼士馬喪亡而不得其故，虜能無疑乎？彼之切齒於瓦剌，亦猶之瓦剌切齒於彼也。古有鷸蚌之喻，今其時矣。厚募明辯有膽略者，速之使鬪，而又東西誤之，或誑以巢穴之覆，或誑以仇讎之至，虜能無疑乎？如是而又恩結藏僧，許以虜退則優其禮；利招通事，約以虜退則賞之官。皆聽彼之自爲術，而吾不與焉，虜其有維縶者乎？不然，則堅壁清野，昔人已有定筭，而預爲收斂，又朝廷不忍鋒刃之成法。勅甘肅守臣熟計而預待之。且今之城守視昔金湯矣，今之堡寨視昔扃鑰矣，此其定不可恃乎？竝邊要害，稍增屯戍；若慮糧餉不給，首惟汰其老弱，不必別爲調度。而又時時飭之，使之終日欽欽，常如對陳。即腹裏郡縣有苦饑寒欲流離者，慎擇良守令以時撫定之，不至輕爲搖動，此其預不可恃
translation_en:
…reveal the mechanism, causing their soldiers and horses to perish without knowing the reason—could the caitiffs not be filled with suspicion? Their gnashing of teeth at the Oirats (Wala) is just like the Oirats' gnashing of teeth at them. In antiquity there was the parable of the snipe and the clam; now is just such a time! If we generously recruit eloquent and courageous men to prod them into fighting one another, while also misleading them east and west—deceiving them either with reports that their lairs have been overturned, or with word that their mortal enemies have arrived—could the caitiffs not be filled with suspicion? Working in this manner, if we also bind the Tibetan monks to us with favor, promising them lavish ritual treatment once the caitiffs withdraw, and entice the interpreters with profit, agreeing to reward them with official posts once the caitiffs withdraw—letting them devise their own stratagems while we remain uninvolved—would anything still tether the caitiffs here?

Failing that, strengthening the walls and clearing the fields is a settled strategy of men of the past; and gathering in the people and livestock beforehand is also the established method of a Court that cannot bear the clash of blades. Let an imperial command order the defending officials of Gansu to deliberate thoroughly and make advance preparations for them. Moreover, today's city defenses are like walls of metal and moats of boiling water compared to the past, and today's forts and stockades are like bolted locks compared to the past—can this settled readiness not be relied upon? At strategic points along the frontier, slightly increase the garrison troops; if there is concern that grain rations will not suffice, first simply weed out the old and weak without needing to make separate logistical arrangements. Furthermore, instruct and drill them constantly, keeping them reverently alert all day long as if facing a battle line. Even if in the interior prefectures and counties there are people suffering from hunger and cold who wish to flee as refugees, carefully select good prefects and magistrates to soothe and settle them in a timely manner so that they are not lightly shaken into unrest—can this advance preparation not be relied upon…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
乎然後威福在己緩急隨宜虜之有名號
能統領者或隆殺之異禮或喜怒之異情
而又慎烽火以節其勞嚴操練以精其技
厚恩信以得其死簡文法以盡其才使兵
識將意將識士情撫臣密之於內而無所
撓鎮臣喻之於外而無所拂務若身使臂
臂使指而元氣爲之常運焉此其威不可
恃乎由是而有喜寧中行說其人者可以
他事按矣雖然無慮焉昔武帝之登單于
臺也使使告匈奴曰單于能戰天子自將
待邊而匈奴爲之遠遁其臣之使於匈奴
者怵以頭懸北闕屠爲九郡數語匈奴即
不敢動蓋兵貴先聲而北虜又故可恐喝
走者今遼東大創露布屢宣此虜聞之其
亦有嚴心而魄之褫也久矣況鎖鑰之嚴
者不言而信爪牙之奮者不怒而威則
聖天子之所誕敷眞有出於借箸之外者愚生
何足以知之
punctuated: 乎？然後威福在己，緩急隨宜，虜之有名號能統領者，或隆殺之異禮，或喜怒之異情。而又慎烽火以節其勞，嚴操練以精其技，厚恩信以得其死，簡文法以盡其才，使兵識將意，將識士情，撫臣密之於內而無所撓，鎮臣喻之於外而無所拂，務若身使臂、臂使指，而元氣爲之常運焉，此其威不可恃乎？由是而有喜寧、中行說其人者，可以他事按矣。雖然，無慮焉。昔武帝之登單于臺也，使使告匈奴曰：「單于能戰，天子自將待邊。」而匈奴爲之遠遁。其臣之使於匈奴者，怵以「頭懸北闕，屠爲九郡」數語，匈奴即不敢動。蓋兵貴先聲，而北虜又故可恐喝走者。今遼東大創，露布屢宣，此虜聞之，其亦有嚴心而魄之褫也久矣。況鎖鑰之嚴者，不言而信；爪牙之奮者，不怒而威。則聖天子之所誕敷，眞有出於借箸之外者，愚生何足以知之？
translation_en:
… be relied upon? Only then will the power to punish and reward rest with us, and we can respond to emergencies or periods of calm as appropriate. As for those among the caitiffs who hold prestigious titles and are capable of commanding troops, we may treat them with varying degrees of ritual—either generous or curtailed—and show them differing dispositions of favor or anger. Furthermore, we should exercise caution with beacon fires so as to spare the troops unnecessary toil, enforce strict training to refine their martial skills, bestow generous grace and good faith to win their readiness to die, and simplify bureaucratic regulations to allow them to fully exercise their talents. Thus the soldiers will understand the intentions of their generals, and the generals will understand the feelings of their men; the Grand Coordinators will plan closely within and face no obstruction, while the Regional Commanders will make instructions clear without and meet no resistance. All efforts will operate as the body moves the arm and the arm moves the fingers, while the vital energy circulates constantly throughout. Can such awe-inspiring might not be relied upon?

From this position, should there be individuals like Xi Ning 喜寧 or Zhonghang Yue 中行說, they can be investigated and dealt with on the pretext of other matters. Even so, there is no cause for worry. In the past, when Emperor Wu [of Han] ascended the Chanyu Terrace, he sent an envoy to announce to the Xiongnu: "If the Chanyu is able to fight, the Son of Heaven himself is leading troops and waiting at the frontier." Because of this, the Xiongnu fled far away. And when his ministers went as envoys to the Xiongnu and intimidated them with a few words—warning that their heads would be hung at the northern palace gates and their lands slaughtered and carved into nine commanderies—the Xiongnu immediately dared not make a move. This is because in warfare, establishing an advance reputation is paramount, and the northern caitiffs are by nature susceptible to being frightened off by threats. Now, great victories have been won in Liaodong, and proclamations of triumph have been repeatedly announced. Hearing of this, these caitiffs have surely felt dread in their hearts and been robbed of their nerve for a long time. How much more so when our frontier defenses are so strictly secured that they command trust without a word, and our martial defenders are so roused that they inspire awe without displaying anger! Thus, what the Sacred Son of Heaven has broadly promulgated truly transcends any stratagems that could be devised by borrowing the sovereign's chopsticks. How could a foolish student such as I be worthy of fathoming it?

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄後序
萬曆己卯陝西旣遵往例舉
士而鄉書告成矣〔居仁〕以職
事宜序簡末序曰夫人情自
淳之漓易旣漓而復淳則難
由質趨文易旣文而返質則
難寰宇地勢原於西北而萬
===
世之文肇自羲皇人人言之
矣太華終南之雄峙黃河涇
渭之浩流渾淪旁礴本固而
源遠精英之所孕孰非惇大
朴直士哉陝以西羲皇而下
文武之豐鎬今固有遺趾也
恪守朴直豈獨其地氣然哉
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄後序

萬曆己卯，陝西旣遵往例舉士，而鄉書告成矣。〔居仁〕以職事，宜序簡末。序曰：夫人情自淳之漓易，旣漓而復淳則難；由質趨文易，旣文而返質則難。寰宇地勢原於西北，而萬世之文肇自羲皇，人人言之矣。太華、終南之雄峙，黃河、涇、渭之浩流，渾淪旁礴，本固而源遠，精英之所孕，孰非惇大朴直士哉？陝以西，羲皇而下，文、武之豐、鎬，今固有遺趾也。恪守朴直，豈獨其地氣然哉？
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the jimao year of the Wanli reign (1579), once Shaanxi had selected scholars in accordance with established precedent and the provincial examination register was brought to completion, by virtue of my official duties, I, [Juren], ought to write a postface at the end of the volume. The postface reads: Now, in human sentiment, it is easy to pass from pure simplicity to thin superficiality, but once thin, to return to purity is difficult; it is easy to move from unadorned substance toward literary ornament, but once ornamented, to revert to substance is difficult. That the topography of the realm originates in the northwest, and that the culture of ten thousand generations began with the august Fuxi, is something everyone says. With the majestic peaks of Mount Taihua and Mount Zhongnan, and the vast currents of the Yellow, Jing, and Wei rivers—all-encompassing and boundless, firm in root and distant in source—among those nurtured by this finest essence, who is not a generous, great, simple, and upright scholar? West of Shan, coming down from the august Fuxi, the capitals of Feng and Hao of Kings Wen and Wu indeed still have their remaining sites today. In strictly preserving simplicity and uprightness, how could this be due solely to the terrestrial vital energy of the region? …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
流風遺俗直道而行亦崇尚
之不可誣也故比屋而考德
道有夷隆要之歸於淳也執
簡而譚藝學有麤密要之歸
於質也蓋〔居仁〕既應聘而來
以快觀其地遂得縱觀諸士
之文既又接所拔之儁乃
===
竊自幸曰美哉秦之產也瑞
世之人文其在兹乎其在兹
乎夫川谷異齊民生其間異
俗士之所習尚不可强而同
也彼括聚片言湊泊爛錦非
不觀美苟竊言無當錄用謂
何今觀諸士所為文本之乎
punctuated: 流風遺俗，直道而行，亦崇尚之不可誣也。故比屋而考德，道有夷隆，要之歸於淳也；執簡而譚藝，學有麤密，要之歸於質也。蓋〔居仁〕既應聘而來，以快觀其地，遂得縱觀諸士之文，既又接所拔之儁，乃竊自幸曰：「美哉秦之產也！瑞世之人文，其在兹乎！其在兹乎！」夫川谷異齊，民生其間異俗，士之所習尚，不可强而同也。彼括聚片言，湊泊爛錦，非不觀美，苟竊言無當，錄用謂何？今觀諸士所為文，本之乎
translation_en: … Their lingering traditions and handed-down customs—walking the straight path—are likewise values they revere, which cannot be denied. Therefore, when one examines virtue from house to house, though the Way may rise or decline, in essence it returns to pure simplicity; when one holds the tablets and discusses literary art, though scholarship may be coarse or refined, in essence it returns to substance. After I, 〔Juren〕, accepted the invitation and came here, taking delight in beholding this land, I was then able to survey at length the writings of the scholars, and subsequently met the outstanding talents who had been selected. I then secretly rejoiced to myself, saying: "How admirable are those born of Qin! The cultural refinement that augurs an auspicious age—is it not right here? Is it not right here?" Now, rivers and valleys differ in their alignment, and the people born among them differ in their customs; what scholars practice and value cannot be forced into uniformity. Those who scrape together fragmentary phrases and piece together flashy brocades are not unpleasant to look at, yet if they plagiarize words without substance, what would be the point of selecting and employing them? Now, looking at the essays composed by these scholars, they are rooted in…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天眞出之以獨見洪纖意鑄
好醜性形故觀其文如見其
貌偉而偉姸而姸無秋毫爽
也我
皇上稽古右文作新士類頊者納
言官之請布功令釐文體曾
未踰年而秦人士所爲文輒
===
已根極理要而歸之於純正
亦本其所賦之淳而所習以
質勝故變而之道有易易者
觀所爲文而其所効用可諒
也顧諸士所執以進者藝也
素所服習也今羅而貢之南
宮行且爲
punctuated: 天眞，出之以獨見，洪纖意鑄，好醜性形；故觀其文如見其貌，偉而偉、姸而姸，無秋毫爽也。我皇上稽古右文，作新士類，頊者納言官之請，布功令、釐文體，曾未踰年，而秦人士所爲文輒已根極理要，而歸之於純正。亦本其所賦之淳，而所習以質勝，故變而之道有易易者。觀所爲文，而其所効用可諒也。顧諸士所執以進者，藝也，素所服習也。今羅而貢之南宮，行且爲
translation_en:
…natural genuineness and bring them forth from independent insight; large and small are cast by intent, and beauty and ugliness take shape from their very nature. Thus, reading their writings is like seeing their countenances—what is grand appears grand, what is graceful appears graceful, without the slightest discrepancy.

Our Emperor examines antiquity and esteems civil culture, renewing the body of scholars. Recently [reading 頃 for 頊], accepting the petition of the speaking officials, he promulgated examination regulations to rectify literary style. Scarcely a year has passed, and yet the writings composed by the scholars of Qin have already penetrated to the essentials of principle and returned to purity and correctness. This too stems from the unadulterated nature with which they are endowed and from habits in which substance prevails; hence their transformation so as to reach the Way has been most easy. By observing the writings they have composed, one can trust the service they will render.

Yet that which the scholars hold fast in order to advance is literary skill—what they have long practiced and been accustomed to. Now that they have been gathered in and presented as tribute to the Southern Palace [the Ministry of Rites, for the Metropolitan Examination], they are about to be…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
一人用矣効用將何以哉秦中之
往哲鏗鍧炳耀以樹勳于前
而垂光于後者〔居仁〕不遑縷
陳近世涵濡聖眞篤行古道
動以賢聖爲期則有若呂文
簡竭忠殫猷勤功鼎彝則有
若王端毅抗節不撓奮爭國
===
是則富平于今稱之矣是皆
秉誠矢公以淳朴質直之心
出其身爲天下用故以表士
類則道德稱高以弘建樹則
勳庸耀世以出議論則聳聞
振聽故海內望其人如麟如
鳳目爲世之所罕覯也諸士
punctuated: 一人用矣，効用將何以哉？秦中之往哲，鏗鍧炳耀，以樹勳于前而垂光于後者，〔居仁〕不遑縷陳。近世涵濡聖眞，篤行古道，動以賢聖爲期，則有若呂文簡；竭忠殫猷，勤功鼎彝，則有若王端毅；抗節不撓，奮爭國是，則富平于今稱之矣。是皆秉誠矢公，以淳朴質直之心，出其身爲天下用。故以表士類，則道德稱高；以弘建樹，則勳庸耀世；以出議論，則聳聞振聽。故海內望其人如麟如鳳，目爲世之所罕覯也。諸士
translation_en: … the One Man [the Emperor]. By what means will they render effective service? As for the former worthies of Qin [Shaanxi]—resounding and brilliant, who established meritorious deeds in the past and cast their radiance down to posterity—I, [Ju-ren], have not the leisure to recount them in detail. In recent ages, for immersing oneself in sage truth, earnestly practicing the ancient Way, and taking the worthies and sages as one's standard in every action, there was one such as Lü Wenjian [Lü Nan 呂柟]; for exhausting loyalty and plans, and laboring at achievements worthy of being inscribed on sacrificial tripods and vessels, there was one such as Wang Duanyi [Wang恕 Wang Shu]; for upholding integrity without bending and vigorously contending over the great policies of the state, he of Fuping [Sun Piyang 孫丕揚 or Yang Jue 楊爵 / Li Kechou, i.e., the worthy of Fuping] is praised to this day. All of these men held fast to sincerity and pledged themselves to the public good; with unadorned, simple, and upright hearts, they brought themselves forth to be of use to the empire. Thus, when they stood as models for the scholar class, their moral virtue was acclaimed as lofty; when they broadened their achievements, their meritorious service illuminated the age; when they put forth their deliberations, they startled and roused all who heard them. Therefore, within the seas people looked up to such men as unicorns (lin) and phoenixes (feng), regarding them as rarely seen in the world. Now the gentlemen…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
且出而服官政矣職任雖殊
要皆三君子所嘗有事也諸
士自視其身與三君子所執
持何如夫因皐爲高則崇基
立就執柯施伐則取法不遠
近取諸身旣稟賦若此遠稽
諸人又芳躅若彼故諸士之
===
儀刑非不足也亦惟執淳質
之心以往而罔弗濟矣今譚
者謂補偏救弊莫若稍減其
文而秦人士之自爲尚則莫
若獨守其質乃或自厭其淳
質之不文直欲從事于靡文
縟節謂足以諧衆情而宜流
punctuated: 且出而服官政矣。職任雖殊，要皆三君子所嘗有事也。諸士自視其身，與三君子所執持何如？夫因皐爲高，則崇基立就；執柯施伐，則取法不遠。近取諸身，旣稟賦若此；遠稽諸人，又芳躅若彼。故諸士之儀刑非不足也，亦惟執淳質之心以往，而罔弗濟矣。今譚者謂補偏救弊，莫若稍減其文；而秦人士之自爲尚，則莫若獨守其質。乃或自厭其淳質之不文，直欲從事于靡文縟節，謂足以諧衆情而宜流
translation_en: …are about to go forth and take up official administration. Although their posts and responsibilities may differ, in essence these are all matters in which those three gentlemen once engaged. When you scholars examine yourselves, how do you compare with the principles held fast by those three gentlemen? Now, if one builds high by taking advantage of a hill, a lofty foundation is immediately achieved; if one holds an axe-handle to hew another, the model is not far off. Drawing near at hand from yourselves, your natural endowments are already like this; examining afar in others, their fragrant footsteps are moreover like that. Therefore, models for you scholars to emulate are by no means lacking; you need only hold fast to a pure and unadorned mind as you go forward, and there will be nothing you cannot accomplish. Nowadays, commentators say that to remedy imbalances and rescue the age from abuses, nothing is better than slightly reducing its華麗 embellishment (wen); whereas for the scholars and gentlemen of Qin [Shaanxi] in what they personally esteem, nothing is better than solely preserving their substantive simplicity (zhi). Yet some may grow dissatisfied with their own pure simplicity as being unrefined, and wish instead to devote themselves to extravagant embellishment and elaborate ceremony, supposing this sufficient to harmonize with popular sentiment and suit current…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
俗也則棄其所不當無而慕
其所不必有譬則售珠而還
櫝其毋乃不善變乎守其常
則兩得之渝所守則兩失之
故習不可不愼也若曰先進
彬彬斯稱全德篤實而輝光
淵中而彪外此固諸士之自
===
待而亦主司之所望也且發
跡岐周流聲宇宙內爲政于
國而外宣布於諸侯協心夾
輔佐成周泰和之治兹又非
秦產哉郎諸士不敢侈言自
負望前茅以爲依歸亦非異
人任矣尚懋勉乎主司者更
punctuated: 俗也。則棄其所不當無，而慕其所不必有，譬則售珠而還櫝，其毋乃不善變乎？守其常則兩得之，渝所守則兩失之，故習不可不愼也。若曰先進彬彬，斯稱全德，篤實而輝光，淵中而彪外，此固諸士之自待，而亦主司之所望也。且發跡岐周，流聲宇宙，內爲政于國，而外宣布於諸侯，協心夾輔，佐成周泰和之治，兹又非秦產哉？郎諸士不敢侈言自負，望前茅以爲依歸，亦非異人任矣。尚懋勉乎！主司者更
translation_en: …prevailing customs. To thus cast aside what one ought not to lack while coveting what one has no need to possess—like buying the casket and returning the pearl—is that not a poor way to change? If one holds fast to one's constant nature, one attains both [substance and refinement]; if one betrays what one holds fast to, one loses both. Therefore, one cannot but be cautious regarding habits and customs. As for saying that the men of former times were balanced in substance and refinement, and that this is what constitutes complete virtue—being earnest and solid yet shining forth brilliantly, deep within yet patterned without—this is indeed what you scholars expect of yourselves, and it is also what the examiners hope for. Moreover, those who rose to prominence in Qi and Zhou, whose renown spread throughout the universe, who administered the government within the state and proclaimed its virtue abroad to the feudal lords, uniting their hearts in shared assistance to help bring about the grand harmony of the Zhou dynasty—were they not also natives of Qin? Even if [reading 郎 as 即] you scholars dare not boast extravagantly in self-conceit, looking toward those vanguard models as your standard to follow is surely not a responsibility that belongs to others! Strive earnestly! Those who serve as examiners further…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
有厚望矣
直隷大名府滑縣儒學敎諭
王〔庶仁〕謹序
punctuated:
有厚望矣。
直隷大名府滑縣儒學敎諭王〔庶仁〕謹序。
translation_en:
… have even higher hopes.
Respectfully prefaced by Wang Shuren 王庶仁, Instructor of the Confucian School of Hua County, Daming Prefecture, in the Southern or Northern Metropolitan Area (Zhili).

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄序
上萬曆之七年天下復當大比士
於鄉巡按陝西監察御史張
憲翔〔衡〕
上命晨夜馳入關無何迫試事乃
以前御史沈〔涵〕禮聘學正〔宗〕
湯教諭王〔居仁〕爲考試官學
===
正劉〔淑唐〕教諭涂〔案〕方〔思賢〕
薛〔彥卿〕訓導石〔珮〕賓〔中孚〕爲
同考試官提調則左布政使
朱〔炳如〕右布政使張〔國彥〕監
試則副使李〔時漸〕王〔體復〕諸
執事靡弗慎擇充者於是合
河西巡按御史趙〔楫〕提學副
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄序
上萬曆之七年，天下復當大比士於鄉。巡按陝西監察御史張憲翔〔衡〕上命，晨夜馳入關。無何，迫試事，乃以前御史沈〔涵〕禮聘學正〔宗〕湯、教諭王〔居仁〕爲考試官，學正劉〔淑唐〕、教諭涂〔案〕、方〔思賢〕、薛〔彥卿〕、訓導石〔珮〕、賓〔中孚〕爲同考試官。提調則左布政使朱〔炳如〕、右布政使張〔國彥〕，監試則副使李〔時漸〕、王〔體復〕，諸執事靡弗慎擇充者。於是合河西巡按御史趙〔楫〕、提學副
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the seventh year of the reigning Emperor's Wanli reign (1579), the empire was once again due for the triennial examination of scholars in the provinces. Regional Inspector of Shaanxi and Investigating Censor Zhang Xianxiang 张宪翔, bearing [reading 衡 as 銜] the Imperial mandate, rode day and night to enter the pass. Before long, as the examination affairs pressed near, in accordance with the courteous invitations already extended by the former Censor Shen Han 沈涵, Department Director of Schools [Zhou] Zongtang [周]宗汤 and District Director of Schools Wang Juren 王居仁 were engaged to serve as Examiners, while Department Director of Schools Liu Shutang 刘淑唐, District Directors of Schools Tu An 涂案, Fang Sixian 方思贤, and Xue Yanqing 薛彦卿, and Assistant Instructors Shi Pei 石珮 and Bin Zhongfu 宾中孚 were engaged to serve as Associate Examiners. As for the Proctors, they were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhu Bingru 朱炳如 and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Guoyan 张国彦; as for the Surveillance Officials of the Examination, they were Surveillance Vice Commissioners Li Shijian 李时渐 and Wang Tifu 王体复. There were none among the various functionaries who were not carefully selected to fill their posts. Thereupon, combining the scholars selected by Regional Inspector of Hexi and Investigating Censor Zhao Ji 赵楫 and Education-intendant Surveillance Vice…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
使李〔維楨〕所選士一千九百
有奇三試之遵
制額舉六十五人錄其氏名若
文以
獻〔宗湯〕宜序首簡蓋漢人之言
曰秦形勝之國也帶河阻山
縣隔千里持戟百萬秦得百
===
二焉秦之雄於天下自古記
之矣〔宗湯〕則請言
今日自
國家建都于燕俯而臨天下如
北辰然分野萬里郡縣星列
天下有相制之形而無偏重
之處秦雖大直當之一隅安
punctuated: 使李〔維楨〕所選士一千九百有奇，三試之。遵制額，舉六十五人，錄其氏名若文以獻。〔宗湯〕宜序首簡。蓋漢人之言曰：「秦，形勝之國也。帶河阻山，縣隔千里，持戟百萬，秦得百二焉。」秦之雄於天下，自古記之矣。〔宗湯〕則請言今日：自國家建都于燕，俯而臨天下，如北辰然。分野萬里，郡縣星列，天下有相制之形，而無偏重之處。秦雖大，直當之一隅，安
translation_en: … Education Intendant Vice Commissioner Li Weizhen 李維楨, numbering one thousand nine hundred and more, and examined them across three sessions. In compliance with the statutory quota, sixty-five men were selected as provincial graduates, and their surnames and given names, together with their model essays, have been recorded for presentation to the throne. It falls to me, Zongtang 宗湯, to write the preface for the opening pages. Now, a man of the Han dynasty once said: "Qin is a state of strategic terrain. Girdled by the Yellow River and guarded by mountains, it is suspended a thousand li away from the rest of the realm; against a million halberd-bearers, Qin holds the advantage of two against a hundred." That Qin stood supreme in the realm has been recorded since antiquity. Yet I, Zongtang, beg leave to speak of the present day: Since our dynasty established its capital at Yan, it looks down upon and governs the realm just like the North Star. Across apportioned domains spanning ten thousand li, commanderies and counties are arrayed like stars; the realm possesses a configuration of mutual checks and balances, with no region holding disproportionate weight. Although Qin is vast, it merely constitutes a single corner of the empire—how…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
所名其雄乎秦不能以其大
而雄天下則將奚以夫人固
有以地重地亦有以人重必
得士焉與天下絜長比大而
秦得百二而後可也今夫天
下非小狹也秦士非益多而
天下非少也有人於此遽而
===
號於衆曰秦之士與天下之
士絜長比大而得百二衆有
不失笑者乎〔宗湯〕請譬之鄧
林之植也不必皆干霄拂雲
蔽青天而蔭原畝之木也然
而求干霄拂雲蔽青天而蔭
原畝之木非鄧林無有也燕
punctuated: 所名其雄乎？秦不能以其大而雄天下，則將奚以？夫人固有以地重，地亦有以人重，必得士焉，與天下絜長比大，而秦得百二，而後可也。今夫天下非小狹也，秦士非益多而天下非少也。有人於此，遽而號於衆曰：「秦之士與天下之士，絜長比大而得百二。」衆有不失笑者乎？〔宗湯〕請譬之：鄧林之植也，不必皆干霄拂雲、蔽青天而蔭原畝之木也；然而求干霄拂雲、蔽青天而蔭原畝之木，非鄧林無有也。燕
translation_en: …can it claim preeminence? If Qin cannot be preeminent in the empire by virtue of its size, then by what means will it be so? Now, just as men assuredly gain importance from their land, a land also gains importance from its men. Only when it obtains scholars who, when measured in excellence and compared in greatness against those of the whole empire, give Qin a two-to-a-hundred advantage [lit. "two parts equivalent to a hundred"], will it do. Now the empire is neither small nor narrow; the scholars of Qin are not growing ever more numerous while those of the rest of the empire are few. If someone here were suddenly to proclaim to the crowd, "When the scholars of Qin are measured in excellence and compared in greatness against the scholars of the empire, they hold a two-to-a-hundred advantage," would anyone in the crowd not burst out laughing? Allow me [Zongtang 宗湯] to illustrate this with an analogy: among the trees growing in the Forest of Deng (Denglin 鄧林), not all are necessarily trees that reach into the sky and brush the clouds, screening the blue heavens and shading the plains and fields; yet if one seeks trees that reach into the sky and brush the clouds, screening the blue heavens and shading the plains and fields, they are to be found nowhere else but in the Forest of Deng. Of the [horses of] Yan…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
代之馬不必皆追風掣電一
日而千里然脫有追風掣電
一日而千里者必燕代馬也
秦亦士之鄧林之圃而燕代
之野也渠寧無士昔人之論
曰才過千人謂之豪過萬人
謂之傑夫此一人耳而才度
===
越千萬人則豪傑之名歸焉
矣豪傑之士雖無文王猶興
矧生於文王之鄉而爲思皇
之遺者乎方今
神聖在御日出之地光耀明德治
登乎大猷唯是勸學育才招
延茂異勤於中懷誠幾得豪
punctuated: 代之馬，不必皆追風掣電，一日而千里；然脫有追風掣電、一日而千里者，必燕、代馬也。秦亦士之鄧林之圃，而燕、代之野也，渠寧無士？昔人之論曰：「才過千人謂之豪，過萬人謂之傑。」夫此一人耳，而才度越千萬人，則豪傑之名歸焉矣。豪傑之士，雖無文王猶興，矧生於文王之鄉，而爲思皇之遺者乎？方今神聖在御，日出之地，光耀明德，治登乎大猷，唯是勸學育才，招延茂異，勤於中懷，誠幾得豪
translation_en: …and Dai need not all chase the wind and flash like lightning, covering a thousand li in a single day; yet if perchance there is one that chases the wind and flashes like lightning, covering a thousand li in a single day, it will surely be a horse of Yan and Dai. Qin is likewise the Denglin grove and the pasture of Yan and Dai for scholars—how could it possibly lack men of worth? A saying of the ancients goes: "One whose talent surpasses a thousand men is called a stalwart (hao 豪); one who surpasses ten thousand is called a hero (jie 傑)." Now this is but a single person, yet when his talent transcends a thousand or ten thousand men, the name of stalwart and hero accrues to him. A heroic scholar rises up even when there is no King Wen—how much more so those who are born in the homeland of King Wen and are the legacy of the "splendid multitude of royal men" (sihuang 思皇) celebrated in the Odes! At present, a divine sage is on the throne; to the very places where the sun rises, his resplendent virtue shines forth, and his governance ascends to the Great Plan. He is devoted in his innermost heart solely to encouraging learning and nurturing talent, summoning and welcoming those of flourishing and extraordinary ability, genuinely hoping to obtain heroic…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
傑之士而用之士誰有不敬
應者乎秦渠寧無士蓋〔宗湯〕
之初應聘而來也私覩夫挾
策懷器雲翔而待校於車下
者無慮數千百人也進而觀
其所爲文辭陳之以疑以觀
其學雜設之事以觀其才紛
===
難之以觀其識漫引之以觀
其守旁詰射之以觀其辯如
此而不失得六十五人而止
爾夫此六十五人者一旦而
穎脫於數千百人之上若所
謂豪傑云者而言者曰是不
離爾之鄉爾早暮續食偕計
punctuated: 傑之士而用之，士誰有不敬應者乎？秦渠寧無士？蓋〔宗湯〕之初應聘而來也，私覩夫挾策懷器、雲翔而待校於車下者，無慮數千百人也。進而觀其所爲文辭：陳之以疑，以觀其學；雜設之事，以觀其才；紛難之，以觀其識；漫引之，以觀其守；旁詰射之，以觀其辯。如此而不失，得六十五人而止爾。夫此六十五人者，一旦而穎脫於數千百人之上，若所謂豪傑云者，而言者曰：「是不離爾之鄉爾。」早暮續食，偕計
translation_en: …outstanding scholars (haojie) and employ them—which among the scholars would not reverently respond? How could Qin (Shaanxi) really lack scholars? When I, [Zongtang], first arrived in response to the invitation to serve as examiner, I privately observed those holding their writing tablets and cherishing their talents, gathering like clouds to await evaluation beneath my carriage—without doubt numbering several thousand. Going further to examine the literary compositions they produced: we set forth doubtful points to observe their learning; we posed varied affairs to observe their talent; we challenged them with complexities to observe their insight; we led them with broad, unrestrained prompts to observe their steadfastness of principle; and we probed and questioned them from oblique angles to observe their powers of argumentation. Tested in this manner without faltering, we obtained sixty-five men and no more. Now, these sixty-five men have in a single day stood out sharply above several thousand others, seeming to be what are called outstanding heroes; yet a critic might say, "This is merely without leaving your own home province." Soon, supplied with provisions along the way, you will travel with the tribute reports…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
與四方名下之士角於春官
更進而踐
文石履
赤墀奉
臨軒之制對稱曰子大夫也當此
之時不佞即不敢過望爾人
人而舉顧豈無絕塵而奔者
===
於其間乎有之謂足當豪傑
非耶而言者又曰是藝止爾
可以爲先資而未可以成信
則所爲豪傑者大略可覩矣
太上立德其次立功其次立
言周召尚矣自周而漢而唐
宋窺前聖之奧樹將相之勳
punctuated: 與四方名下之士角於春官，更進而踐文石、履赤墀，奉臨軒之制對，稱曰「子大夫」也。當此之時，不佞即不敢過望爾人人而舉，顧豈無絕塵而奔者於其間乎？有之，謂足當豪傑非耶？而言者又曰：「是藝止爾，可以爲先資，而未可以成信。」則所爲豪傑者，大略可覩矣。太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。周、召尚矣，自周而漢、而唐、宋，窺前聖之奧，樹將相之勳，
translation_en: …to compete at the Ministry of Rites against renowned scholars from all quarters; and advancing even further to tread upon the patterned stones and walk the vermilion steps of the palace court, receiving in person the Emperor's policy questions at the Palace Examination and being addressed in reply as "My High Officials." At that time, although this unworthy one would not dare to expect too much—that every single one of you will succeed—could there yet fail to be those among you who gallop ahead, leaving the dust behind? If there are such men, would it not be fitting to consider them outstanding heroes? Yet the critic says again: "This is merely literary craft; it may serve as an initial pledge of service, but it cannot yet establish true trustworthiness." From this, what constitutes an outstanding hero can be seen in general outline. The highest course is to establish virtue; the next is to establish meritorious service; and the next is to establish enduring words. The Dukes of Zhou and Shao are of course unsurpassed in antiquity; from the Zhou down through the Han, and on to the Tang and Song, those who peered into the profound mysteries of the former sages, who established the meritorious achievements of generals and chief councilors,…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
富名山之藏者何可指數然
太半炳烺於爾秦之圖籍也
爾如不以豪傑自命則可如
以豪傑自命典刑具在奚所
擇而處焉夫遇
光華之旦圖不朽之業修此三
者故全也德不至而功立功
===
不至而言立隨性之所近而
務臻其極流聲無窮者名世
之軌也而總之不在名高而
在致實不在材具而在所養
爾多士勉矣氣欲完神欲定
心欲密才欲練措之為德行
發之為事業擬議之為變化
punctuated: 富名山之藏者，何可指數？然太半炳烺於爾秦之圖籍也。爾如不以豪傑自命則可；如以豪傑自命，典刑具在，奚所擇而處焉？夫遇光華之旦，圖不朽之業，修此三者，故全也。德不至而功立，功不至而言立，隨性之所近而務臻其極，流聲無窮者，名世之軌也。而總之，不在名高而在致實，不在材具而在所養。爾多士勉矣！氣欲完，神欲定，心欲密，才欲練，措之為德行，發之為事業，擬議之為變化，
translation_en: …and enrich the repositories of famous mountains—how could they all be counted on the fingers? Yet more than half of them shine brilliantly in the records and books of your land of Qin. If you do not regard yourselves as heroes of extraordinary talent, then so be it; if you do regard yourselves as heroes, the classic models are all present—which among them will you choose to abide in? Now, meeting with this glorious dawn and planning for an imperishable enterprise, to cultivate all three of these is thus completeness. If one falls short of establishing virtue yet establishes merit, or falls short of establishing merit yet establishes words—following what is congenial to one's nature and striving to reach its ultimate limit, so as to hand down an endless reputation—this is the path of those renowned in their generation. In sum, it lies not in lofty fame, but in attaining substance; not in mere endowment of talent, but in what one nourishes. Exert yourselves, all you scholars! Your vital energy should be whole, your spirit should be settled, your mind should be meticulous, and your talent should be tempered; put them into practice as moral conduct, manifest them as achievements and enterprises, and deliberate upon them to bring about transformation,…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
則養盛而實至實至而名隨
之矣上之與周召爲徒次無
墜爾先哲之典刑矣先資成
信而不第爲一鄉士矣昔宋
太宗嘗言士非望拔十得五
得一二人亦可爲致理之具
蓋其難也宗湯不佞業以爾
===
多士進多士寧無意乎俾談
者曰三秦豪傑唯爾多士曰
秦無人亦唯爾多士曰豪傑
則以一人而度越千萬人雖
謂秦士於天下得百二亦宜
曰無人則太華誠高洪河誠
深安所託其重于天下耶宗
punctuated: 則養盛而實至，實至而名隨之矣。上之與周、召爲徒，次無墜爾先哲之典刑矣；先資成信，而不第爲一鄉士矣。昔宋太宗嘗言：「士非望拔十得五，得一二人亦可爲致理之具。」蓋其難也。宗湯不佞，業以爾多士進，多士寧無意乎？俾談者曰「三秦豪傑」，唯爾多士；曰「秦無人」，亦唯爾多士。曰豪傑，則以一人而度越千萬人，雖謂秦士於天下得百二亦宜；曰無人，則太華誠高，洪河誠深，安所託其重于天下耶？宗
translation_en: …then your self-cultivation will be abundant and true substance will be achieved; when true substance is achieved, reputation will follow it. At the highest, you will be peers of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao; next to that, you will not let fall the exemplary models of your former worthies. Your initial presentation of yourselves as a pledge of service will establish good faith, and you will not merely be scholars of a single locality. In the past, Emperor Taizong of the Song (Song Taizong 宋太宗) once said: "With scholars, one does not hope to select ten and obtain five; if one obtains even one or two, they can still serve as instruments for bringing about good governance." Such is the difficulty of it! Unworthy though I, Zongtang (宗湯), am, I have already recommended you many scholars for advancement—how could you many scholars not take this to heart? Whether commentators say "The Three Qin region has heroic talents" depends entirely on you many scholars; whether they say "Qin has no men" also depends entirely on you many scholars. If they speak of heroic talents, then through a single person surpassing tens of millions of others, even to say that the scholars of Qin hold a two-to-a-hundred advantage over the rest of the realm would be fitting. If they say there are no men, then even though Mount Taihua is truly high and the great Yellow River is truly deep, upon what can they entrust their weight in the realm? I, Zong…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
湯自度淺薄無以相長爾多
士第借形勝之輕重述才賢
之所產明
主上之至意闡豪傑之名實以與
爾多士勗焉多士耳目所覩
記至孰必有能辨此矣是舉
也總督軍務則兵部左侍郎
===
兼右僉都御史郜〔光先　久弘〕
文德雅厲士習巡撫陝西地
方則右副都御史近陞戶部
右侍郎傅〔希　摯〕風敎淪浹仐
右僉都御史李〔堯　德〕聲猷夙
暨甘肅則兵部右侍郎兼右
僉都御史侯〔東　萊〕寧夏則右
punctuated: 湯自度淺薄，無以相長爾多士，第借形勝之輕重，述才賢之所產，明主上之至意，闡豪傑之名實，以與爾多士勗焉。多士耳目所覩記至孰，必有能辨此矣。是舉也，總督軍務則兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史郜〔光先　久弘〕文德，雅厲士習；巡撫陝西地方則右副都御史、近陞戶部右侍郎傅〔希　摯〕風敎淪浹，仐右僉都御史李〔堯　德〕聲猷夙暨；甘肅則兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史侯〔東　萊〕，寧夏則右
translation_en:
… [Zong]tang, measuring my own shallow attainments, have nothing with which to help advance you gentlemen; I merely borrow the relative weight of our strategic topography, recount the men of talent and worth this land has produced, set forth the Sovereign's utmost intent, and expound the name and reality of true heroes, so as to join in mutual encouragement with you gentlemen. That which your eyes and ears have witnessed and remembered is thoroughly familiar, and there will surely be those among you able to discern this.

In this undertaking, as Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, the Left Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Gao [Guangxian 光先], long enlarging civil virtue, has refined and encouraged the customs of the literati; as Grand Coordinator of the Shaanxi Region, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief recently promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue Fu [Xizhi 希摯], whose moral teaching has deeply permeated the land, and the present Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li [Yaode 堯德], whose reputation and statesmanship have long reached afar; in Gansu, the Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Hou [Donglai 東萊]; in Ningxia, the Right …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
政陳〔棐〕李〔汶〕董〔汝漢〕左叅議
徐〔汝翼〕韓〔應元〕右叅議徐〔學〕
詩〔忻〕洪〔弘德〕袁〔作〕文副使張
〔更化〕李〔日强〕姚〔繼可〕張〔孫繩〕
覃〔應元〕張〔九一〕宋〔孟震〕解〔學〕
禮〔維高〕僉事桑〔有光〕周〔館〕貫
王〔君賞〕李〔尚淳〕苑馬寺卿趙
===
少卿梁〔許〕申〔維岱〕行太僕寺
卿武〔尚賢〕馬〔出圖〕少卿馬〔特〕

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
瀛〔以〕先期按察使孫〔坤〕以先
任皆入賀
萬壽副使王〔湘〕以遷秩僉事咸〔懷〕
〔良〕以調任近方出闈皆始事
有勞者得備書云
直隸滁州儒學學正任〔宗〕〔湯〕
謹序
punctuated:
瀛〔以〕先期、按察使孫〔坤〕以先任，皆入賀萬壽；副使王〔湘〕以遷秩、僉事咸〔懷〕〔良〕以調任，近方出闈：皆始事有勞者，得備書云。
直隸滁州儒學學正任〔宗〕〔湯〕謹序。
translation_en:
…ying, who departed ahead of time, and Surveillance Commissioner Sun Kun 孫坤, who held the post previously, had all gone to court to offer congratulations on the Imperial Birthday; Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Xiang 王湘, due to promotion, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xian Huailiang 咸懷良, due to transfer, had just recently left the examination compound—all of these contributed their labor at the inception of the undertaking, and thus merit being fully recorded here.

Respectfully prefaced by Ren Zongtang 任宗湯, Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Chuzhou 滁州 in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸).

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰吾十有五而志于學三十而立四十
而不惑五十而知天命六十而耳順七
十而從心所欲不踰矩
苟不固聰明聖知達天德者其孰能知之
孟子曰禹惡旨酒而好善言湯執中立賢
無方文王視民如傷望道而未之見武
王不泄邇不忘遠周公思兼三王以施
四事其有不合者仰而思之夜以繼日
幸而得之坐以待旦
===
易
聖人作而萬物覩本乎天者親上本乎地
者親下則各從其類也
王假有家交相愛也
乾知大始坤作成物乾以易知坤以簡能
書
百官以治萬民以察
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲不踰矩。」
苟不固聰明聖知達天德者，其孰能知之？
孟子曰：「禹惡旨酒而好善言。湯執中，立賢無方。文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。周公思兼三王，以施四事；其有不合者，仰而思之，夜以繼日；幸而得之，坐以待旦。」

易
聖人作而萬物覩，本乎天者親上，本乎地者親下，則各從其類也。
王假有家，交相愛也。
乾知大始，坤作成物。乾以易知，坤以簡能。

書
百官以治，萬民以察。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

1. The Master said: "At fifteen, I set my heart on learning. At thirty, I stood firm. At forty, I had no doubts. At fifty, I knew the decree of Heaven. At sixty, my ear was attuned. At seventy, I could follow my heart's desires without transgressing the square." (Analects 2.4)

2. Unless one truly possesses keenness of hearing and sight, sagely wisdom, and reaches all the way to Heavenly virtue, who could know him? (Doctrine of the Mean 32)

3. Mencius said: "Yu disliked fine wine and loved good words. Tang held fast to the Mean and employed the worthy without regard to their origins. King Wen looked upon the people as if they were wounded, and gazed toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. King Wu did not treat the near with familiarity and did not forget the distant. The Duke of Zhou sought to combine the virtues of the Three Kings in order to carry out these four courses of action. Whenever anything did not accord with them, he looked up and thought about it, continuing from day into night; and when by good fortune he grasped it, he sat waiting for the dawn." (Mencius 4B.20)

Classic of Changes (Yi)

1. The sage arises and the myriad things behold him. What is rooted in heaven draws close to what is above; what is rooted in earth draws close to what is below: thus each follows its own kind. (Hexagram 1, Qian, Wenyan Commentary)

2. "The king approaches his family": they love one another mutually. (Hexagram 37, Jiaren, Xiang Commentary)

3. Qian directs the great beginning; Kun brings things to completion. Qian directs through ease; Kun is capable through simplicity. (Xici Commentary A.1)

Classic of Documents (Shu)

1. The hundred officials are thereby regulated; the myriad people are thereby clearly distinguished. ("Canon of Yao" / "Counsels of the Great Yu")

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
野無遺賢萬邦咸寧
有言逆于汝心必求諸道有言遜于汝志
必求諸非道
曰其稽我古人之德矧曰其有能稽謀自
天
小大之臣咸懷忠良其侍御僕從罔匪正
人以旦夕承弼厥辟
詩
南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子福履成之
===
靡室靡家玁狁之故不遑啓居玁狁之故
采薇采薇薇亦柔止曰歸曰歸心亦憂
止憂心烈烈載飢載渴我戍未定靡使
歸聘采薇采薇薇亦剛止曰歸曰歸歲
亦陽止王事靡盬不遑啓處憂心孔疚
我行不來
迺慰迺止迺左迺右迺疆迺理迺宣迺畝
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方
春秋
punctuated:
野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。
有言逆于汝心，必求諸道；有言遜于汝志，必求諸非道。
曰其稽我古人之德，矧曰其有能稽謀自天。
小大之臣，咸懷忠良；其侍御僕從，罔匪正人。以旦夕承弼厥辟。
《詩》
南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。
靡室靡家，玁狁之故；不遑啓居，玁狁之故。采薇采薇，薇亦柔止。曰歸曰歸，心亦憂止。憂心烈烈，載飢載渴。我戍未定，靡使歸聘。采薇采薇，薇亦剛止。曰歸曰歸，歲亦陽止。王事靡盬，不遑啓處。憂心孔疚，我行不來。
迺慰迺止，迺左迺右，迺疆迺理，迺宣迺畝。
儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。
《春秋》
translation_en:
"No men of worth are left neglected in the countryside, and all the myriad states enjoy peace."

"When words run counter to your mind, you must seek their meaning in the Way; when words conform to your will, you must test whether they depart from the Way."

"When it is said that he examines the virtue of our ancients, how much more when it is said that he is able to examine and take counsel from Heaven!"

"Ministers great and small all cherish loyalty and goodness; his attendants, grooms, and followers are none of them other than upright men, who morning and evening attend upon and assist their sovereign."

Classic of Poetry (Shi)

"In the south there are trees with drooping branches, and the creepers and vines twine around them. Happy be the lord: may happiness and禄-fortune make him complete!"

"We have no house, no home, because of the Xianyun; we have no leisure to kneel or sit at rest, because of the Xianyun. We gather the thorn-ferns, gather the thorn-ferns, while the thorn-ferns are still tender. We say, 'Let us return, let us return!' and our hearts are full of sorrow. Our sorrowing hearts burn fiercely; we are hungry and thirsty. Our garrison duty is not yet settled, and we have no one to send home to inquire after our families. We gather the thorn-ferns, gather the thorn-ferns, and the thorn-ferns have grown coarse and stiff. We say, 'Let us return, let us return!' and the year is already in the tenth month. The king's business allows no slackening; we have no leisure to kneel or rest. Our sorrowing hearts are sorely distressed, yet we march on and do not come home."

"So he comforted them, so he settled them; so he placed them on the left and on the right; so he defined their boundaries and laid out their divisions; so he drained the land and marked out the acres."

"We revere, take as our model, and imitate the statutes of King Wen, daily bringing peace and order to the four quarters."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
春正月己卯烝　夏五月丁丑烝〔桓公八〕
〔年〕
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
〔僖公元年〕秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于
陽穀〔僖公三年〕春王正月公會齊侯宋
公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰
遂伐楚次于陘　楚屈完來盟于師盟
于召陵　齊人執陳轅濤塗　秋及江
人黃人伐陳　冬十有二月公孫茲帥
===
師會齊人宋人衛人鄭人許人曹人侵
陳〔僖公四年〕
三月作丘甲〔成公元年〕春用田賦〔哀公十〕
〔有二年〕
春王正月季孫宿叔老會晉士匄齊人宋
人衛人鄭公孫蠆曹人莒人邾人滕人
薛人杞人小邾人會吳于向〔襄公十有〕
〔四年〕
禮記
punctuated:
春正月己卯，烝。夏五月丁丑，烝。〔桓公八年〕
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。〔僖公元年〕秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕春王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰；遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。齊人執陳轅濤塗。秋，及江人、黃人伐陳。冬十有二月，公孫茲帥師會齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭人、許人、曹人侵陳。〔僖公四年〕
三月，作丘甲。〔成公元年〕春，用田賦。〔哀公十有二年〕
春王正月，季孫宿、叔老會晉士匄、齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭公孫蠆、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人會吳于向。〔襄公十有四年〕
禮記
translation_en:
In spring, in the first month, on the day jimao, the winter sacrifice (zheng) was performed. In summer, in the fifth month, on the day dingchou, the winter sacrifice (zheng) was performed. [8th year of Duke Huan]
In the eighth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and an officer of Zhu at Cheng. [1st year of Duke Xi] In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, an officer of Jiang, and an officer of Huang met at Yanggu. [3rd year of Duke Xi] In spring, in the King's first month, the Duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in making an incursion into Cai, whereupon Cai collapsed; they then attacked Chu and halted at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army, and they covenanted at Shaoling. The people of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen. In autumn, we joined the people of Jiang and the people of Huang in attacking Chen. In winter, in the twelfth month, Gongsun Zi led a force to join the people of Qi, the people of Song, the people of Wei, the people of Zheng, the people of Xu, and the people of Cao in making an incursion into Chen. [4th year of Duke Xi]
In the third month, the district military levy (qiujia) was instituted. [1st year of Duke Cheng] In spring, the land tax for military service (tianfu) was introduced. [12th year of Duke Ai]
In spring, in the King's first month, Jisun Su and Shu Lao joined Shi Gai of Jin, an officer of Qi, an officer of Song, an officer of Wei, Gongsun Chai of Zheng, an officer of Cao, an officer of Ju, an officer of Zhu, an officer of Teng, an officer of Xue, an officer of Qi, and an officer of Little Zhu in meeting Wu at Xiang. [14th year of Duke Xiang]
Record of Rites (Liji)

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
凡爲君使者已受命君言不宿於家
天下大定然後正六律和五聲弦歌詩頌
此之謂德音德音之謂樂
君子之所謂義者貴賤皆有事於天下天
子親耕粢盛秬鬯以事上帝故諸侯勤
以輔事於天子
天下莫不貴者道也
論
第貳場
===
佐賛乾坤化育之功
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢戒俗吏矯飾者詔〔元和二年〕
擬唐以陸贄爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔貞元八年〕
擬河工告成廷臣
賀表
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
punctuated:
凡爲君使者，已受命，君言不宿於家。
天下大定，然後正六律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌，此之謂德音，德音之謂樂。
君子之所謂義者，貴賤皆有事於天下。天子親耕，粢盛秬鬯以事上帝，故諸侯勤以輔事於天子。
天下莫不貴者道也。

第貳場
論
佐賛乾坤化育之功。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢戒俗吏矯飾者詔〔元和二年〕。
擬唐以陸贄爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔貞元八年〕。
擬河工告成，廷臣賀表。

判語〔五條〕
官吏給由。
translation_en:
"Whenever one serves as an envoy for the ruler, once he has received his charge, the ruler's words do not stay overnight in his house."
"When all under heaven was greatly settled, only then did he rectify the six pitch-standards, harmonize the five tones, and sing the Odes and Hymns to string accompaniment. This is called virtuous sound; virtuous sound is called music."
"What the gentleman calls righteousness means that both the noble and the lowly have their duties in the world. The Son of Heaven plows in person, providing the sacrificial grain and black-millet aromatic wine with which to serve the Lord on High; therefore the feudal lords labor diligently in order to assist the Son of Heaven in his duties."
"That which nothing in the world fails to prize is the Way."

Second Session
Discourse (lun):
"Assisting in the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth."

Edicts, Mandates, and Memorials (zhao, gao, biao) [candidates are examined on one]:
Imitation of a Han-dynasty edict admonishing vulgar officials who engage in pretentious artifice [2nd year of the Yuanhe era (85 CE)].
Imitation of a Tang-dynasty mandate appointing Lu Zhi (陸贄) as Vice Director of the Secretariat (zhongshu shilang) and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery (tong pingzhangshi) [8th year of the Zhenyuan era (792 CE)].
Imitation of a congratulatory memorial (biao) from the court officials upon the reported completion of the Yellow River conservancy works.

Legal Judgments (panyu) [five items]:

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
收支留難
禁止迎送
優恤軍屬
帶造段匹
第叁場
策五道
問古今稱極治者必曰虞周以今觀之重
華之勲始於釐降二南之化肇自關雎
風敎本原顧不重耶我
===
太祖高皇帝肇造區宇
成祖文皇帝誕膺鴻運創述巍煥流光八埏郎
彛文無異揆焉乃
皇明祖訓
聖學心法二書所以貽厥孫謀者至爲閎具可
指而言與我
高皇后母儀天下嘉言懿行載在方策嗣我
文皇后作內訓以敎宮闈蓋釐降關雎一轍也
略亦可殫述與我
punctuated:
收支留難。
禁止迎送。
優恤軍屬。
帶造段匹。

第叁場：
策五道。

問：古今稱極治者，必曰虞、周。以今觀之，重華之勲，始於釐降；《二南》之化，肇自《關雎》。風敎本原，顧不重耶？我太祖高皇帝肇造區宇，成祖文皇帝誕膺鴻運，創述巍煥，流光八埏，郎彛、文無異揆焉。乃《皇明祖訓》、《聖學心法》二書，所以貽厥孫謀者，至爲閎具，可指而言與？我高皇后母儀天下，嘉言懿行，載在方策；嗣我文皇后作《內訓》以敎宮闈，蓋釐降、《關雎》一轍也，略亦可殫述與？我
translation_en:
Obstructing receipts and disbursements.
Prohibiting ceremonial welcoming and sending off.
Showing compassionate care to military dependents.
Making unauthorized additions to quotas in the weaving of satin bolts.

Third Session:
Five Policy Questions.

Question: Those in antiquity and the present who speak of the pinnacle of good governance invariably cite Yu [Shun] and Zhou. Viewed from the present, the meritorious achievements of Chonghua [Shun] began with the marriage of the two royal daughters sent down to him, and the moral transformation celebrated in the Two Nan [of the Classic of Poetry] originated with the "Guanju" ode. Is not the fountainhead of moral instruction through custom weighty indeed?

Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), founded the realm, and our Accomplished Progenitor, Emperor Wen (Chengzu, the Yongle Emperor), grandly received the great mandate. Their founding and continuation of the dynastic enterprise were lofty and glorious, shedding radiance to the eight extremities of the world; truly [reading 郎 as 卽?] their principles are no different from those of Yao [or Shun, reading 彛 as 堯/舜?] and King Wen. Now, the two books Ancestral Injunctions of the August Ming (Huang Ming zuxun) and Method of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), by which they bequeathed plans to their descendants, are most vast and comprehensive; can you point to their essentials and discuss them?

Our Empress Gao (Empress Ma) was a motherly model to all under Heaven, her admirable words and virtuous deeds recorded in the historical tablets; subsequently, our Empress Wen (Empress Xu) composed the Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun) to instruct the palace women. These follow the very same track as the royal daughters' marriage to Shun and the "Guanju" ode; can their outlines also be recounted in full? Our…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
穆宗莊皇帝睿明恭儉祇續
先猷
仁聖懿安
慈聖宣文
二皇太后貞靜徽柔昭示宮則視我
二祖
二后貽謀規範不先後同符與我
皇上
皇后躬親訓迪今二載于玆矣其熙洽寓內維
===
祖烈而軼虞周者必有本也願鋪張而揚厲之
持除敎光
以鳴
今日之盛
問秦罷封建置郡縣法甚具也而禁網益
密姦僞萌起漢除秦苛與民約法惟三
章耳而郡若縣兢兢守之何與夫漢法
行漢吏業已稱盛矣乃班之敘傳也僅
僅見五六抑以何道取之與夫定儀披
punctuated:
穆宗莊皇帝睿明恭儉，祇續先猷；仁聖懿安、慈聖宣文二皇太后貞靜徽柔，昭示宮則：視我二祖、二后貽謀規範，不先後同符與？我皇上、皇后躬親訓迪，今二載于玆矣。其熙洽寓內、維祖烈而軼虞周者，必有本也。願鋪張而揚厲之，持除敎光，以鳴今日之盛。

問：秦罷封建，置郡縣，法甚具也，而禁網益密，姦僞萌起；漢除秦苛，與民約法惟三章耳，而郡若縣兢兢守之，何與？夫漢法行，漢吏業已稱盛矣；乃班之敘傳也，僅僅見五六，抑以何道取之與？夫定儀披
translation_en:
…the Emperor Muzong Zhuang (r. 1567–1572), wise, discerning, reverent, and frugal, respectfully carried forward the plans of his predecessors; and the Two Empresses Dowager, Rensheng Yi'an and Cisheng Xuanwen, chaste, tranquil, virtuous, and gentle, have clearly manifested the regulations of the palace: compared with the plans and standards bequeathed by our Two Progenitors and Two Empresses, do they not tally across time like two halves of a tally? Our reigning Emperor and Empress have personally received their instruction and guidance for two years now. That by which they bring harmony to all within the realm, uphold the meritorious achievements of the ancestors, and surpass the eras of Yu and Zhou must have a fundamental root. I hope you will elaborate upon and extol this—upholding and spreading the radiance of their teaching [?]—in order to proclaim the flourishing magnificence of the present day.

Question: When Qin abolished feudal enfeoffment and established commanderies and counties, its laws were exceedingly comprehensive; yet as the net of prohibitions grew ever denser, treachery and deceit sprouted up. When Han swept away the harshness of Qin, it agreed upon a legal code of only three articles with the people, and yet the commanderies and counties cautiously and reverently abided by them—why was this? Now, as Han laws were put into practice, the officials of Han were already celebrated as flourishing; yet when Ban Gu (32–92) composed his biographical narratives [of Upright Officials in the Book of Han], only five or six men appear—by what principle did he select them? Moreover, those who established court ritual or examined…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
籍者聲稱有赫投巫擿伏者民畏如神
而乃不得與五六人竝傳何與士平居
譚治道輒欲姑舍漢吏而近世法令益
修未見超越漢治豈吏之未盡良耶抑
所以馭吏者道未盡也頃言官建白謂
久任不行吏數更易以故鮮實效耳今
任不爲不久矣何效之不可睹與此其
法必有不盡于此者而補偏救弊之說
不可不亟講也諸士習世故亦必有槩
于中矣願相與揚搉之以俟經世者擇
焉
===
問道德文章事功節義士論褎然重之全
雍以姬教穠沃河山鬱蒸才臣碩彥鱗
砌而出諸列在詩書毋贅已嗣是有總
衆職稱上意者忝帷幄剖決如流者守
正不阿者忘身徇國者坐困先零者克
復兩京者三傳竝行於世者著書百萬
餘言者有長厯作而春秋之義著西銘
punctuated:
籍者，聲稱有赫；投巫擿伏者，民畏如神；而乃不得與五六人竝傳，何與？士平居譚治道，輒欲姑舍漢吏；而近世法令益修，未見超越漢治。豈吏之未盡良耶？抑所以馭吏者道未盡也？頃言官建白，謂久任不行，吏數更易，以故鮮實效耳。今任不爲不久矣，何效之不可睹與？此其法必有不盡于此者，而補偏救弊之說，不可不亟講也。諸士習世故，亦必有槩于中矣，願相與揚搉之，以俟經世者擇焉。

問：道德、文章、事功、節義，士論褎然重之。全雍以姬教穠沃，河山鬱蒸，才臣碩彥，鱗砌而出。諸列在《詩》、《書》，毋贅已。嗣是有總衆職稱上意者，忝帷幄剖決如流者，守正不阿者，忘身徇國者，坐困先零者，克復兩京者，三傳竝行於世者，著書百萬餘言者；有《長厯》作而《春秋》之義著，《西銘》
translation_en:
… consult registers had lustrous reputations, and those who cast witches into rivers or exposed hidden crimes were revered by the people like gods—yet they were not included alongside those five or six men in the biographies. Why is that? When scholars in ordinary life discuss the way of governance, they are always inclined to set aside the officials of the Han; yet in recent ages, though laws and ordinances have been ever more elaborated, we have not seen governance surpass that of the Han. Is it because the officials are not all good? Or is it because the way of managing officials has not been fully realized? Recently, speaking officials made proposals arguing that because long tenure is not practiced and officials are frequently replaced, actual results are rare. Now tenure in office cannot be considered short, so why are results still not to be seen? In this matter, the method surely does not end with tenure alone, and doctrines for rectifying imbalances and remedying abuses must be urgently discussed. You gentlemen are well acquainted with worldly affairs and must certainly have formed views on this in your hearts. I hope we may examine and discuss the matter together, awaiting selection by those who order the world.

Question: Moral virtue, literary attainment, practical achievement, and principled integrity are held in the highest esteem in scholarly discourse. The entire Yongzhou region [Shaanxi], enriched by the teachings of the Zhou house and nurtured by its lush rivers and mountains, has produced talented ministers and eminent worthies in dense succession like overlapping scales. Those already arrayed in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) need not be repeated here. Thereafter, there was one who oversaw all offices and suited the sovereign's wishes; one who participated in council within the command tent and made decisions like a flowing stream; one who upheld rectitude without flattery; one who forgot himself to die for the state; one who subdued the Xianlian [Qiang] tribes while remaining seated; one who recovered the two capitals; one whose commentaries on the Three Traditions circulated together in the world; one who authored writings totaling more than a million words; one who composed the Long Calendar (Changli) so that the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) was made manifest, and one whose Western Inscription (Ximing)…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
出而仁孝之理明者躬耕谷口者牧豕
上林者泉石膏肓雲溪退士者之數子
者於道德文章事功節義可別而言之
與歷將既邈載籍可稽數子嘉言善行
果信然與夫學者談唐虞而述三代率
卑漢唐宋曰勿論也能自得師即媺惡
錯居亦多砥淑先哲如數子後事標矱
自在吾將以諗諸士之所適
問馬政軍國重務載在周禮纖悉具備今
可舉而言之與由周而來言馬政者凡
幾變矣漢初稍爲復古遂致阡陌成羣
唐制府兵貞觀後天下以一縑易一馬
今其法固在可倣而行之與宋初有官
馬戶馬戍馬之設至熙寧吏保馬之法
而民翻以病其視漢唐之制有優劣與
===
我
國朝馬政計地課駒牧不稱苦馬不稱乏與
周制有異同與弘正嘉隆之間先後有
punctuated:
出而仁孝之理明者；躬耕谷口者；牧豕上林者；泉石膏肓、雲溪退士者。之數子者，於道德、文章、事功、節義，可別而言之與？歷將既邈，載籍可稽，數子嘉言善行，果信然與？夫學者談唐、虞而述三代，率卑漢、唐、宋，曰勿論也。能自得師，即媺惡錯居，亦多砥淑。先哲如數子，後事標矱自在，吾將以諗諸士之所適。
問：馬政，軍國重務，載在《周禮》，纖悉具備，今可舉而言之與？由周而來，言馬政者凡幾變矣。漢初稍爲復古，遂致阡陌成羣；唐制府兵，貞觀後天下以一縑易一馬，今其法固在，可倣而行之與？宋初有官馬、戶馬、戍馬之設，至熙寧吏保馬之法，而民翻以病，其視漢、唐之制有優劣與？我國朝馬政，計地課駒，牧不稱苦，馬不稱乏，與周制有異同與？弘、正、嘉、隆之間，先後有
translation_en:
… came forth so that the principles of benevolence and filial piety were made clear; there was one who personally plowed at Gukou; one who herded swine in the Shanglin Park; and those known for an "incurable passion for springs and rocks" or as the "Retired Scholar of Yunxi." Regarding these several masters, can you distinguish and discuss them in terms of their moral virtue, literary achievement, practical accomplishment, and integrity and righteousness? Though the passage of time [?] is already remote, the historical records can be examined: are the admirable words and virtuous deeds of these several masters indeed credible and true? Now, when scholars discuss Yao and Shun and recount the Three Dynasties, they generally disparage the Han, Tang, and Song, saying they are not worth discussing. Yet if one is able to find a teacher for oneself, even where beauty and ugliness are intermingled, there is much by which to whet and refine oneself into virtue. With former worthies such as these several masters, their models and standards for later affairs naturally remain; by this I shall observe what direction you gentlemen take.

Question: Horse administration is a vital affair of the military and the state. As recorded in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), it was complete in every minute detail; can you cite and discuss it today? From the Zhou onward, how many times have policies regarding horse administration changed! In the early Han, there was a slight restoration of antiquity, which consequently led to horses forming herds along the field paths. The Tang established the Garrison Militia (fubing), and after the Zhenguan era (627–649), throughout the realm one bolt of fine silk could be exchanged for one horse. Since those regulations still survive in the records today, can they be emulated and put into practice? In the early Song, there was the establishment of government horses (guanma), household horses (huma), and frontier-garrison horses (shuma); by the Xining era (1068–1077), when the method was changed [?] to the tithing-group horse system (baoma), the people instead suffered from it. Compared with the systems of the Han and Tang, what were its relative merits and defects? In our reigning dynasty's horse administration, foals were assessed according to land, so that herders did not complain of hardship and horses were not spoken of as scarce; how does this compare in similarities and differences with the Zhou system? title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
題屢爲清補屢爲釐革未復其舊近牧臣目
擊而條議省臣熟計而
上陳皆亹亹數千言甚爲激切今皆下其議於
所司將次第其要緊者以復其備
廟堂采擇萬一第不知
國初之舊法尚可復行以濟牧軍之急近日
之節議亦可少損以捄馬政之敝與無
已尚有經國籌邊之略如昔丘文莊李
文正楊文襄之議更酌漢唐宋之中而
上求周官之遺意俾夫有定役地有常
數輸直有規差撥無苦內以重邊關之
勢外以寓制虜之機諸士生長百二之
鄉習聞而籌之熟矣願著于篇將采以
轉聞于
上
===
問北虜爲患中國往牒所載甚詳由周以
降漢唐之强竟莫能摧輪而繫其頸者
豈其時謀國者乏馭戎之上策耶迨我
punctuated:
題，屢爲清補，屢爲釐革，未復其舊。近牧臣目擊而條議，省臣熟計而上陳，皆亹亹數千言，甚爲激切。今皆下其議於所司，將次第其要緊者以復，其備廟堂采擇萬一。第不知國初之舊法，尚可復行以濟牧軍之急？近日之節議，亦可少損以捄馬政之敝與？無已，尚有經國籌邊之略，如昔丘文莊、李文正、楊文襄之議，更酌漢、唐、宋之中，而上求《周官》之遺意，俾夫有定役，地有常數，輸直有規，差撥無苦，內以重邊關之勢，外以寓制虜之機。諸士生長百二之鄉，習聞而籌之熟矣。願著于篇，將采以轉聞于上。

問：北虜爲患中國，往牒所載甚詳。由周以降，漢、唐之强，竟莫能摧輪而繫其頸者，豈其時謀國者乏馭戎之上策耶？迨我
translation_en:
…memorials on the subject, and although there have been repeated clearances and replacements, and repeated reforms and rectifications, the old standards have not been restored. Recently, the officials in charge of horse pasturage, having witnessed the situation firsthand, submitted itemized proposals, while the metropolitan supervising secretaries, after careful deliberation, presented their views to the Emperor. All of these ran tirelessly to several thousand words and were exceedingly impassioned and urgent. Now, all their deliberations have been sent down to the competent authorities, who are about to rank the most essential points in order and reply, so as to provide them for the imperial court's possible selection and adoption. Yet one wonders: can the old methods of the beginning of the dynasty still be revived and put into practice to relieve the urgent plight of the pasturage soldiers? Can the recent proposals for retrenchment also be slightly modified to rescue the horse administration from its abuses? Or, failing that, are there still grand strategies for governing the state and planning for the frontiers—such as the proposals of the former Qiu Wenzhuang (Qiu Jun 丘濬), Li Wenzheng (Li Dongyang 李東陽), and Yang Wenxiang (Yang Yiqing 楊一清)—that further strike a balance among the systems of the Han, Tang, and Song, while reaching back to seek the legacy of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), so as to ensure that corvée laborers have fixed duties, pastures have constant quotas, the payment of commutation fees follows regulations, and the assignment and dispatch of horses entail no hardship, thereby internally strengthening the position of the frontier passes and externally embedding the means to control the northern caitiffs? You gentlemen were born and raised in this region of "two against a hundred" [Shaanxi], where you have long heard of these matters and planned for them thoroughly. I hope you will set your thoughts down in your essays, so that I may select from them to transmit for the hearing of the Emperor.

Question: That the northern caitiffs have been a scourge to China is recorded in great detail in past documents. From the Zhou dynasty onward, despite the might of the Han and the Tang, they were ultimately unable to smash their chariot wheels and bind their necks—could it be that those who planned for the state in those times lacked the supreme strategy for controlling the barbarians? title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元
成祖文皇帝三犂虜庭鴻猷駿烈曠古稱盛然
倐順倐叛奄入奄遯虜情桀黠亦未帖
然傾心也邇者俺酋納款輸貢其部落
往來內地我
皇上猶赤子視之邊臣不以塞垣限之豈非千
古一時
國家之極盛哉然狼子野心中懷叵測頃以
禮佛建寺盤據河外往來張掖酒泉威
劫屬番睥睨茶馬至亡厭也凡此豈效
順者所宜有耶夫虜所駐足咸為要塞
儻久此不返猶梏腹而堅前好乎此地
者全陝之屏翰而全陝者九邊之肩背
也諸士生長於玆宜懷請纓之志願詳
言之俟石畫者採焉
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元，成祖文皇帝三犂虜庭，鴻猷駿烈，曠古稱盛。然倐順倐叛，奄入奄遯，虜情桀黠，亦未帖然傾心也。邇者俺酋納款輸貢，其部落往來內地，我皇上猶赤子視之，邊臣不以塞垣限之，豈非千古一時，國家之極盛哉！然狼子野心，中懷叵測，頃以禮佛建寺，盤據河外，往來張掖、酒泉，威劫屬番，睥睨茶馬，至亡厭也。凡此，豈效順者所宜有耶？夫虜所駐足，咸為要塞，儻久此不返，猶梏腹而堅前好乎？此地者，全陝之屏翰；而全陝者，九邊之肩背也。諸士生長於玆，宜懷請纓之志，願詳言之，俟石畫者採焉。
translation_en: … [When it came to our] Grand Progenitor the Exalted Emperor (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), he swept away the northern-barbarian Yuan; the Accomplished Progenitor the Cultured Emperor (Chengzu, the Yongle Emperor) thrice plowed up the caitiffs' royal courts. Their grand plans and magnificent achievements have been praised as flourishing beyond anything in antiquity. Yet, now submitting and now rebelling, suddenly invading and suddenly fleeing, the caitiffs' disposition remained unruly and cunning, nor did they ever docilely incline their hearts toward us. Recently, the chieftain Anda (Altan Khan) offered submission and paid tribute. As his tribes go back and forth within the interior territories, our August Emperor regards them like newborn infants, and frontier officials do not restrict them with the border walls. Is this not a once-in-an-eternity moment and the ultimate flourishing of the dynasty? However, these wolf cubs have wild hearts and harbor unfathomable intentions within. Of late, under the pretext of worshiping the Buddha and building a monastery, they have entrenched themselves beyond the Yellow River, going back and forth around Zhangye and Jiuquan, intimidating and plundering our tributary Tibetan tribes, and casting greedy eyes on the tea-and-horse trade, to the point of utter insatiability. Could any of this be proper for one who pledges allegiance? Now, the places where the caitiffs have planted their feet are all strategic strongholds. Should they linger here for long and not return, will they really restrain their appetites [?] and hold fast to the former amity? This region is the protective screen of all Shaanxi, and all Shaanxi is the shoulders and back of the Nine Frontiers. You gentlemen, born and raised here, ought to cherish the ambition of requesting a long cord [to bind the enemy]. I hope you will speak of this in full detail, awaiting selection by those who devise rock-solid plans.
