title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
噫之歌梁鴻也入會稽而不返志尤峻焉
田游巖安貧樂道而屢辭高宗之聘泉石
膏肓蓋其所自命者豈終南之疾徑耶种
司諫讀書養母而不赴太宗之辟雲溪退
士若將終身者豈北山之移誚耶合而觀
之數君子者材有通塞若難兼集所長時
有顯晦未能竝著于世要之行其所自得
則一而已矣夫其所自得者何也堅貞其
慮正固其守理義素明于中知識不眩乎
===
外也是以輔成保泰則宜弼直之猷定亂
扶傾則著匡襄之略當著述而立言以明
道當退處而抗節以秉貞道德事功文章
節義皆以垂不朽殆與華岳爭高渭流竝
長矣執事欲別而言之且以觀先哲之標
變則生何適從哉蓋君子之尚論貴博而
其取則貴精不可不辨也今觀橫渠之學
精思力踐羽翼周程可以言道德矣至於
西銘正蒙又文章之尤著者也汾陽之勳
punctuated: 噫之歌，梁鴻也，入會稽而不返，志尤峻焉。田游巖安貧樂道，而屢辭高宗之聘，「泉石膏肓」蓋其所自命者，豈終南之疾徑耶？种司諫讀書養母，而不赴太宗之辟，「雲溪退士」若將終身者，豈北山之移誚耶？合而觀之，數君子者，材有通塞，若難兼集所長；時有顯晦，未能竝著于世。要之，行其所自得，則一而已矣。夫其所自得者何也？堅貞其慮，正固其守，理義素明于中，知識不眩乎外也。是以輔成保泰，則宜弼直之猷；定亂扶傾，則著匡襄之略。當著述而立言以明道，當退處而抗節以秉貞。道德、事功、文章、節義，皆以垂不朽，殆與華岳爭高、渭流竝長矣。執事欲別而言之，且以觀先哲之標變，則生何適從哉？蓋君子之尚論貴博，而其取則貴精，不可不辨也。今觀橫渠之學，精思力踐，羽翼周、程，可以言道德矣；至於《西銘》、《正蒙》，又文章之尤著者也。汾陽之勳，
translation_en: … the "Song of Five Sighs" (Wuyi zhi ge)—this was Liang Hong; he entered Guiji and never returned, his resolve being even more lofty. Tian Youyan was content in poverty and delighted in the Way, repeatedly declining the summonses of Emperor Gaozong [of Tang]. An "incurable passion for springs and rocks" was what he claimed for himself—how could his have been a "shortcut via Mount Zhongnan" [to officialdom]? Policy Critic (sijian) Chong [Chong Fang] studied books and cared for his mother, refusing to answer the summons of Emperor Taizong [of Song]. Calling himself the "Retired Scholar of Cloud Creek" (Yunxi tuishi) as though he would remain so for life—how could he be mocked by a "Proclamation on Mount Bei"? Viewed together, among these several gentlemen, their circumstances varied between advancement and hindrance, as if it were difficult for them to combine every excellence; and their times varied between prominence and obscurity, so they could not all be equally illustrious in the world. Yet in essence, in carrying out what they had genuinely attained within themselves, they were one and the same. And what was it that they had attained within themselves? They made their deliberations firm and pure, kept their integrity upright and steadfast, had principle and righteousness ever clear within, and did not let their understanding be dazzled by external things. Therefore, in assisting the accomplished and preserving peace, they put forward counsels of upright aid [?]; in quelling disorder and supporting the tottering, they displayed strategies of rectification and assistance. When it was time to write, they established words to illuminate the Way; when it was time to withdraw into retirement, they upheld their integrity to maintain purity. Their moral virtue, practical achievements, literary writings, and lofty integrity have all been handed down to immortality, almost vying in height with Mount Hua and matching the length of the Wei River's flow. Now Your Excellency wishes to discuss them by distinct categories, and moreover to observe the standards and adaptations [?] of these former worthies—what, then, should this student follow? Broadness is valued when a gentleman appraises figures of the past, yet refinement is valued when he chooses models to emulate; this must be carefully distinguished. If we now observe the learning of Hengqu [Zhang Zai], with his incisive thought and strenuous practice, serving as wings to Zhou [Dunyi] and the Cheng brothers [Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi], one may truly speak of his moral virtue; and as for his Western Inscription (Ximing) and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), they are furthermore among the most eminent of literary writings. The meritorious deeds of Fenyang [Guo Ziyi] …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
旋乾轉坤左右肅代可以言事功矣至於
功成身退又節義之獨完者也下此則萊
公大節斯其次乎若壯侯之長略韓林之
峭直君子取節焉弱翁之刑名基禍如晦
之賛成喋血蓋不能無遺議矣諸所立之
事功所謂血氣用事非耶馬融開絳帳而
身附梁冀之惡三傳何取焉賈逵專門君
子以爲固矣杜預嗜學君子以爲癖矣豈
聖門之文章哉子眞也梁鴻也游巖也潔
===
身避亂高矣實非通圓之軌种放遇有道
之主而僞隱沽名他日變塞重以致嗣宗
之笑節義又安在哉嗟乎慎別而嚴從者
尚論之準也節取而竝觀者得師之益也
由弱翁而下皆人才之傑出者使其游於
聖人之門則淵源所漸卽以登求路游夏
之科與逸民竝列焉可也君子本其行事
以定之矩考其立志以昭之的皆吾人砥
淑之資也慎毋曰此非三代以上人物姑
punctuated: 旋乾轉坤，左右肅、代，可以言事功矣；至於功成身退，又節義之獨完者也。下此則萊公大節，斯其次乎？若壯侯之長略，韓、林之峭直，君子取節焉。弱翁之刑名基禍，如晦之賛成喋血，蓋不能無遺議矣。諸所立之事功，所謂血氣用事，非耶？馬融開絳帳，而身附梁冀之惡，三傳何取焉？賈逵專門，君子以爲固矣；杜預嗜學，君子以爲癖矣，豈聖門之文章哉？子眞也，梁鴻也，游巖也，潔身避亂，高矣，實非通圓之軌。种放遇有道之主，而僞隱沽名，他日變塞，重以致嗣宗之笑，節義又安在哉？嗟乎！慎別而嚴從者，尚論之準也；節取而竝觀者，得師之益也。由弱翁而下，皆人才之傑出者，使其游於聖人之門，則淵源所漸，卽以登求、路、游、夏之科，與逸民竝列焉可也。君子本其行事以定之矩，考其立志以昭之的，皆吾人砥淑之資也。慎毋曰：「此非三代以上人物，姑…
translation_en: … reversed the course of heaven and earth and assisted Emperors Suzong and Daizong of Tang; this may truly be called practical achievement! As for retiring once his work was accomplished, in moral integrity he alone was complete. Below him, the great integrity of Duke Lai [Kou Zhun 寇準] would be next, would it not? As for the far-reaching strategy of the Martial Marquis [Ban Chao 班超, Marquis of Dingyuan, posthumously Zhuanghou 壯侯] and the stern uprightness of Han [Han Yu 韓愈?] and Lin [Lin Fu 林甫? or Han Qi 韓琦 and Fan Zhongyan?], the gentleman selects their good points. As for Ruoweng [Bing Ji 丙吉, or Wei Xiang 魏相, courtesy name Ruoweng] laying the foundations of disaster through his reliance on penal law and name-and-reality [刑名], and Ruhui [Du Ruhui 杜如晦] assisting in the bloodshed [at Xuanwu Gate], they cannot be free from lingering criticism. Are not the various achievements they established what one calls acting out of mere vigour and passion? Ma Rong 馬融 set up his crimson curtain to teach, yet personally attached himself to the wickedness of Liang Ji 梁冀—what is there to commend in his commentaries on the Three Traditions? Jia Kui 賈逵 specialized in a single school, which the gentleman considers obstinate; Du Yu 杜預 was addicted to learning [specifically the Zuo Tradition], which the gentleman considers an obsession—how could these be the literary culture of the Sage's school? As for Zizhen [Zheng Pu 鄭樸], Liang Hong 梁鴻, and Youyan [Tian Youyan 田游巖], they kept themselves pure and fled disorder; lofty as they were, theirs was truly not a path of comprehensive adaptability. Chong Fang 种放 encountered a ruler who possessed the Way, yet feigned reclusion to fish for fame; when later he changed his principles from when he was in obscurity, he only incurred the mockery of a Sizong [Ruan Ji 阮籍]—where then was his moral integrity? Alas! To distinguish carefully and follow strictly is the standard for evaluating figures of the past; to select particular merits and observe them side by side is the benefit of finding teachers. From Ruoweng on down, all were outstanding talents; had they roamed within the gates of the Sage, then, steeped in that fountainhead, they could have ascended to the disciplines of Ran Qiu 冉求, Zilu 子路, Ziyou 子游, and Zixia 子夏, or been ranked alongside the virtuous recluses [逸民]. When the gentleman bases himself on their deeds to establish a standard and examines their aspirations to clarify his target, all of them serve as resources for our own self-cultivation and refinement. Let us by no means say, "These are not figures from the Three Dynasties or earlier, so for now let us…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
舍是哉
第四問
曹思聰
同考試官教諭涂　批〔馬政極敝而關陝爲甚諸生類能歎陳周漢唐宋及我〕
國初舊法而於此中事多未之及即有議及者亦常談耳子能根究敝源眞要緊也宜錄
之以備
采擇
考試官教諭王　批〔敘事詳盡議當而豪逸之氣溢〕
於筆端自是有用文字
===
考試官學正任　批〔是策能發人所未發且辭氣嚴〕
行最宜文古耶
古今之策馬政者其說有二曰牧之官牧
之民而已祖公馬之說者主於官而不知
典守非其人是以侵牟病法也襲國馬之
說者主於民而不知法制有未盡是以多
事病民也權衡於二者之間以求宜官宜
民之道則得人要矣任法急焉是故愼簡
punctuated:
舍是哉！

第四問

曹思聰

同考試官教諭涂批：〔馬政極敝，而關陝爲甚。諸生類能歎陳周、漢、唐、宋及我〕國初舊法，而於此中事多未之及；即有議及者，亦常談耳。子能根究敝源，眞要緊也，宜錄之以備采擇。

考試官教諭王批：〔敘事詳盡，議當，而豪逸之氣溢〕於筆端，自是有用文字。

考試官學正任批：〔是策能發人所未發，且辭氣嚴〕行，最宜文古耶。

古今之策馬政者，其說有二：曰牧之官、牧之民而已。祖公馬之說者，主於官，而不知典守非其人，是以侵牟病法也；襲國馬之說者，主於民，而不知法制有未盡，是以多事病民也。權衡於二者之間，以求宜官宜民之道，則得人要矣，任法急焉。是故愼簡
translation_en:
…set them aside!

Fourth Question

Cao Sicong 曹思聰

Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Tu 涂 comments: Horse administration has fallen into extreme decay, and in Guanzhong and Shaanxi it is at its worst. The candidates generally know how to lament and set forth the old institutions of the Zhou, Han, Tang, Song, and the beginning of our own dynasty, yet regarding the affairs right here in this region they mostly fail to touch upon them; even when someone discusses them, it is merely commonplace talk. You are able to trace the root of the abuses to their source, which is truly hit upon what is essential. It ought to be recorded and printed to be ready for imperial selection.

Examiner Instructor Wang 王 comments: The exposition of facts is thorough and detailed, the arguments are fitting, and a vigorous, unrestrained spirit overflows from the tip of his brush. It is naturally a piece of practical, useful writing.

Examiner Director of Studies (xuezheng) Ren 任 comments: This policy essay is able to bring to light what others have failed to express; moreover, its diction and tone are rigorous and flowing [?], most fittingly archaic in style [?].

Among those past and present who have devised policies for horse administration, their theories have been two: namely, pasturing them through the officials, and pasturing them through the people—nothing more. Those who follow the theory of "public horses" (gongma) place the responsibility mainly on the officials, without realizing that when those in charge are not the right men, peculation and encroachment ruin the system. Those who inherit the theory of "state horses" (guoma) place the responsibility mainly on the people, without realizing that when the regulations and institutions are not fully perfected, excessive demands ruin the people. If one weighs the balance between these two in order to seek a way that suits both the officials and the people, then obtaining the right men is crucial, and putting the laws into effect is urgent. Therefore, if we carefully select…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以重其選變通以盡其利不徇乎今不泥
乎古而法唯人焉任之則官可牧也民亦
可牧也而於馬政有裨矣方今治教修明
馬政具舉而當事諸臣圖維計畫者又復
周至執事可容無慮矣乃復筴諸生以經
國籌邊之略甚盛心也愚請先言往事後
及
國朝新舊之制而終之以陜西唯執事擇焉
夫馬之爲政載在周禮者甚詳蓋其以丘
===
十六井出乗車而駕車馬牛皆有定數及
馬之具也長帥牧正董其事而得牧者則
賜姓賜邑傳之無窮以故成周之世藉國
馬以行軍資公馬以稱賦而周官法度燦
然具矣此豈有異故哉周公以關雎麟趾
之意弘經綸制作之猷故法善而人可守
耳由周以來蓋又有可言者漢牧于民而
用于官則衆庶蕃育唐牧于官而用于民
則賤可易緣此其效之可睹者而要所休
punctuated:
以重其選，變通以盡其利，不徇乎今，不泥乎古，而法唯人焉任之，則官可牧也，民亦可牧也，而於馬政有裨矣。方今治教修明，馬政具舉，而當事諸臣圖維計畫者又復周至，執事可容無慮矣。乃復筴諸生以經國籌邊之略，甚盛心也。愚請先言往事，後及國朝新舊之制，而終之以陜西，唯執事擇焉。

夫馬之爲政，載在《周禮》者甚詳。蓋其以丘十六井出乗車，而駕車馬牛皆有定數。及馬之具也，長帥、牧正董其事，而得牧者則賜姓賜邑，傳之無窮。以故成周之世，藉國馬以行軍，資公馬以稱賦，而《周官》法度燦然具矣。此豈有異故哉？周公以《關雎》、《麟趾》之意，弘經綸制作之猷，故法善而人可守耳。由周以來，蓋又有可言者：漢牧于民而用于官，則衆庶蕃育；唐牧于官而用于民，則賤可易緣。此其效之可睹者，而要所休
translation_en:
… in order to give weight to their selection, and adapt flexibly in order to exhaust its benefits—neither blindly following the present nor being bogged down in the past, and entrusting the laws solely to the right men—then horses can be pastured by the state, and they can also be pastured by the people, which will be beneficial to horse administration. At present, governance and instruction are well-ordered and enlightened, horse administration is fully implemented, and the plans and deliberations of the officials in charge are moreover thorough and complete; Your Excellency might well be free of concern. Yet you still question us students on strategies for ordering the state and planning for the frontiers, which is a most generous intention. Allow this humble student to speak first of past affairs, then touch upon the old and new institutions of our Dynasty, and conclude with Shaanxi, for Your Excellency to choose from.

Now, the administration of horses is recorded in great detail in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). In its system, a qiu of sixteen well-fields (jing) supplied one war chariot, and the horses and oxen drawing the chariots were all of a fixed number. When the horses were supplied, Directors (zhangshuai) and Herdsmen-in-Chief (muzheng) supervised the affair, and those who succeeded in pasturing were granted surnames and fief-towns to pass down endlessly. For this reason, in the era of the flourishing Zhou, they relied on state horses (guoma) to march the armies and drew upon public horses (gongma) to match the military levies, and the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) were brilliantly complete. Was there any unusual reason for this? The Duke of Zhou used the spirit of the "Guanju" and "Linzhi" odes to broaden his plans for statecraft and institutional creation; thus the laws were good and people could uphold them. From the Zhou onward, there are also things worth mentioning: the Han pastured horses among the people and used them in the state, and the common folk bred them in abundance; the Tang pastured horses in the state and used them among the people, so that horses were cheap and could be traded for a bolt of silk [?]. These are the visible results, though in essence what gave rest and…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
息不專在于馬也至宋則畜監牧市邊關
而官馬戎馬之名立矣散編戶責孳生而
戶馬保馬之法興矣然妨政病民唯保馬
爲甚而周之良法始無復有存焉者宜執
事之重慨於熙寧而謂民翻以病也我
國家稽古定制仰法周官國初謀議之臣殫
忠竭猷固有不在周公下者豈於馬政爲
不備哉是故計戶以養馬計丁以課駒而
生之內者富茶易于西番絹市于遼左而
===
致之外者多其在陝西則地無頃畝計分
論駒地之利雖廣而駒之課仍寬是以地
得耕穫馬得飼養地漸沃壤馬漸蕃息所
以養之於官與民者法至善已夫其養之
官也所以給衛所之用也謂非周之設官
分治不可也其養之民也所以備諸邊之
乏也謂非周之寓兵于農不可也迨乎弘
正之間屢爲疏議而牧地之以公用徵者
銀以八百計矣嘉隆之際時爲釐正而牧
punctuated: 息，不專在于馬也。至宋，則畜監牧、市邊關，而官馬、戎馬之名立矣；散編戶、責孳生，而戶馬、保馬之法興矣。然妨政病民，唯保馬爲甚，而周之良法始無復有存焉者。宜執事之重慨於熙寧，而謂民翻以病也。我國家稽古定制，仰法《周官》，國初謀議之臣，殫忠竭猷，固有不在周公下者，豈於馬政爲不備哉？是故計戶以養馬，計丁以課駒，而生之內者富；茶易于西番，絹市于遼左，而致之外者多。其在陝西，則地無頃畝，計分論駒。地之利雖廣，而駒之課仍寬，是以地得耕穫，馬得飼養，地漸沃壤，馬漸蕃息，所以養之於官與民者，法至善已。夫其養之官也，所以給衛所之用也，謂非周之設官分治不可也；其養之民也，所以備諸邊之乏也，謂非周之寓兵于農不可也。迨乎弘、正之間，屢爲疏議，而牧地之以公用徵者，銀以八百計矣；嘉、隆之際，時爲釐正，而牧
translation_en:
… nourished did not lie solely in the horses themselves. By the Song dynasty, horses were bred in Pasturages (Jianmu) and purchased at frontier passes, establishing the designations of "official horses" (guanma) and "military horses" (rongma); they were distributed among registered households and quotas were imposed for breeding foals, giving rise to the systems of "household horses" (huma) and "baojia horses" (baoma). Yet in obstructing governance and harming the people, the baojia horse system was the worst of all, and for the first time nothing remained of the fine laws of the Zhou. It is fitting that you, sir, lament so deeply over the Xining era (1068–1077) and say that the people instead suffered from it.

Our Dynasty examined antiquity to establish its institutions, looking up to emulate the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). At the founding of the dynasty, the ministers who deliberated and planned exhausted their loyalty and poured forth their counsels; truly they were not inferior to the Duke of Zhou—how could they have left the horse administration incomplete? Therefore, households were counted to raise horses and adult males were counted to assess quotas of foals, so that those bred in the interior were abundant; tea was traded with the Western Borderlands (Xifan) and silk was bartered in Liaodong, so that those brought in from the exterior were numerous.

As for Shaanxi, pasturage land was not measured by qing and mu, but foals were assessed according to allotted shares. Although the profits of the land were broad, the foal quotas remained lenient. Thus the land could be plowed and harvested, and the horses could be fed and tended; the land gradually became fertile soil, and the horses gradually multiplied. The methods by which they were raised by both officials and the people were supreme indeed. That they were raised by the officials was to supply the needs of the Guards and Battalions (weisuo)—one cannot say this was not the Zhou principle of establishing offices with divided responsibilities. That they were raised by the people was to prepare against shortages along the various frontiers—one cannot say this was not the Zhou principle of lodging the military among the peasantry.

When it came to the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) eras, memorials and deliberations were repeatedly submitted, and the silver levied from pasturage lands for public expenses was counted by the eight hundreds. During the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras, rectifications were periodically made, and pasturage…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
地有山原坡川之等爲牧養多寡之數矣
時則銀雖徵而軍未稱苦也唯加至萬餘
而軍始病數雖限而馬未稱逋也唯定以
一頃有半之地而法始嚴遂有遺馬數十
匹棄地數十頃而散而之四方者此牧臣
所以目擊而議而省臣不容已于言也是
曷以故哉弊也久矣愚生更悉言之而執
事聽焉漢世民牧姑毋論唐人所稱牧於
官者監牧之官唯司芻牧一切孳養生息
===
官爲董之令之監牧則但較其孳生之數
徵其備用之馬而已而所以芻與牧者不
問也但以養之監苑養之衛所者爲養于
官而不知監苑衛所之軍之養與州縣之
民之養法令不同要之均養于民而已矣
嗟乎熙寧保馬之法固執事所爲長太息
者而今日馬政之行其害則有甚焉何也
宋人以馬給民唯其所願而又復其身給
其草束折變緣納之錢今則唯問其丁not
punctuated: 地有山原坡川之等，爲牧養多寡之數矣。時則銀雖徵而軍未稱苦也，唯加至萬餘而軍始病；數雖限而馬未稱逋也，唯定以一頃有半之地而法始嚴。遂有遺馬數十匹、棄地數十頃，而散而之四方者。此牧臣所以目擊而議，而省臣不容已于言也。是曷以故哉？弊也久矣，愚生更悉言之，而執事聽焉。漢世民牧姑毋論，唐人所稱牧於官者，監牧之官唯司芻牧，一切孳養生息，官爲董之。令之監牧，則但較其孳生之數，徵其備用之馬而已，而所以芻與牧者不問也。但以養之監苑、養之衛所者爲養于官，而不知監苑、衛所之軍之養，與州縣之民之養，法令不同，要之均養于民而已矣。嗟乎！熙寧保馬之法，固執事所爲長太息者，而今日馬政之行，其害則有甚焉。何也？宋人以馬給民，唯其所願，而又復其身，給其草束、折變緣納之錢；今則唯問其丁，不
translation_en:
… pasturelands were graded into mountains, plateaus, slopes, and plains to determine the quotas for raising more or fewer horses. At those times, although silver was levied, the soldiers did not yet complain of hardship; it was only when the levy was increased to over ten thousand taels that the soldiers began to suffer. Although quotas were fixed, the horses were not yet reported as in arrears; it was only when the rule of assigning one and a half qing of land per horse was established that the law became harsh. Consequently, there were those who left behind dozens of horses, abandoned dozens of qing of land, and scattered in all directions. This is why the horse-administration officials witnessed it with their own eyes and deliberated on it, and why the supervising secretaries could not refrain from speaking out.

Why is this so? The abuses are of long standing. Allow this humble student to explain it in further detail, and may Your Excellency listen. Setting aside the civilian horse-raising of the Han era for now, in what the men of the Tang called "official horse-raising," the officials of the Directorate of Horse Pastures were solely in charge of fodder and grazing, and all matters of breeding, rearing, and multiplying were supervised by the officials themselves. In today's [reading 今 for 令] pasture directorates, however, they merely audit the quotas of breeding and requisition horses for reserve use, without inquiring at all into the means of providing fodder and grazing. People merely regard raising horses in the directorates and pasturages or in the guards and battalions as "raising by the state," without realizing that although the regulations differ between raising by soldiers in the directorates, pasturages, guards, and battalions and raising by commoners in the subprefectures and counties, in essence both amount to nothing more than raising by the people!

Alas! The horse-guarantee system (baoma fa) of the Xining reign (1068–1077) is indeed something over which Your Excellency heaves a long sigh, yet in the implementation of horse administration today, its harms are even worse. Why? When the Song distributed horses to the people, it was done only according to their willingness; moreover, they exempted the keepers from personal service and supplied them with bundles of hay as well as commuted cash for incidental tax payments. Nowadays, however, the authorities only ask about a household's adult males and do not …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
問其願矣飼養芻牧之費其餘無幾而其
他賦役日益甚焉何望乎身之復也宋之
保馬不供他設而今他設如故矣監正圉
長臨之羣長小甲從而統之上下交征剝
求無猒而養馬之外役復叢然加也既供
糧稅以給公家又備芻秣以養官馬視宋
之害誠有甚焉者矣且馬之生也有報駒
之令馬之損也有責償之條日有生日有
斃而地之所出不勝其所償也况乎簿書
===
啓科派之隙印俵關需索之門而軍之困
也有不至流離轉徙不止者欲馬政之興
也得乎昔宋文彥博謂戶配一馬縶之維
之不能蕃息今之牧不獨縶維已也望其
蕃息可得哉故愚以爲欲馬之蕃不問其
牧于官也牧于民也其議有三而得人任
法其要焉周官趣巫牧圉之職皆以德行
道藝之士爲之而今外之苑太非直趣巫
牧圉也小之監正圉長亦非闒人闒吏也
punctuated:
問其願矣。飼養芻牧之費，其餘無幾，而其他賦役日益甚焉，何望乎身之復也？宋之保馬，不供他設，而今他設如故矣。監正、圉長臨之，羣長、小甲從而統之，上下交征，剝求無猒，而養馬之外，役復叢然加也。既供糧稅以給公家，又備芻秣以養官馬，視宋之害，誠有甚焉者矣。且馬之生也，有報駒之令；馬之損也，有責償之條。日有生，日有斃，而地之所出，不勝其所償也。况乎簿書啓科派之隙，印俵關需索之門，而軍之困也，有不至流離轉徙不止者，欲馬政之興也，得乎？昔宋文彥博謂戶配一馬，縶之維之，不能蕃息。今之牧，不獨縶維已也，望其蕃息，可得哉？
故愚以爲欲馬之蕃，不問其牧于官也、牧于民也，其議有三，而得人任法其要焉。《周官》趣、巫、牧、圉之職，皆以德行道藝之士爲之。而今外之苑、太，非直趣、巫、牧、圉也；小之監正、圉長，亦非闒人、闒吏也。
translation_en:
…asking whether they are willing! After the expenses of feeding and pasturing, very little remains, while other taxes and labor services grow heavier by the day—how could they hope for personal exemption from corvée? Under the Song horse-maintenance system (baoma), households were not subjected to other imposts, whereas today other imposts remain just as before. Directors of Pasturage Directorates (jianzheng) and Corral Heads (yuzhang) oversee them from above, while Herd Heads (qunzhang) and Petitory Tithing Chiefs (xiaojia) supervise them in turn. Superiors and subordinates alike exact levies, fleecing them insatiably, and on top of raising horses, further labor services are piled upon them in profusion. Having already provided grain taxes to supply the state, they must also prepare fodder and grain to raise government horses; compared to the harms of the Song, this is truly far worse. Moreover, when foals are born, there is the regulation for reporting foals; when horses are lost, there is the statute demanding compensation. Every day some are born and every day some die, yet what the land produces is not enough to cover what must be compensated. How much more so when registers and account books open loopholes for arbitrary surcharges, and the branding and distribution of horses open the gates to extortion! The distress of the military households does not cease until they are driven to vagrancy and flight—if one wishes for the horse administration to flourish under such conditions, how can it be achieved? In the past, Wen Yan博 (文彥博) of the Song said that when each household is assigned a horse and tethers and ties it up, the horses cannot multiply. Today's pasturing is not merely a matter of tethering and tying them up; how can we hope for them to multiply?

Therefore, I humbly hold that if we wish horses to multiply—regardless of whether they are pastured by the government or pastured by the people—there are three proposals, and securing the right men to carry out the laws is the most essential. In the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the posts of stablemaster (zou), horse-doctor (wu), herdsman (mu), and groom (yu) were all filled by gentlemen of virtuous conduct and mastery of the arts. Today, in the provinces, the officials of the Pasturage Directorates (Yuanma si) and Courts of the Imperial Stud (Taipu si) are far more than mere stablemasters, horse-doctors, herdsmen, and grooms; even the lesser Directors of Pasturage Directorates and Corral Heads are not supposed to be worthless men or base clerks…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遷其秩者以爲置身于散地而人之目之
復以爲散而忽焉卽屢申屢飭竟莫有歐
觀易聽者以故怨望之心生槖橐之私起
矣是故比苑太以京寺之重處正長以科
貢之途如楊文襄之議可行也唐牧地起
隴右金城平涼天水東至樓煩外暨河曲
內則涇寧豳岐坊監錯置牧養有法而牧
地則堇千二百三十頃耳今邠涇寧州與
汧渭之境卽其故地而閑田不耕者何止
一千二百三十也況洪永閒所定草塲自
東勝至河西抵古北口蓋幾十萬里其饒
水草便牧馬者又不啻如唐人而已是故
擇地以立監牧設法以爲倸散如丘文莊
之議可行也
===
國初諸番納馬以茶酬之今番馬猶故而
聖天子威德遠被卽俺酋桀黠亦歲貢名馬唯
謹斯固千載一時也已但金牌之制未復
而商茶所易安得霜蹏宣大延綏歲有互
punctuated: 遷其秩者以爲置身于散地，而人之目之復以爲散而忽焉。卽屢申屢飭，竟莫有歐觀易聽者，以故怨望之心生，槖橐之私起矣。是故比苑太以京寺之重，處正長以科貢之途，如楊文襄之議可行也。唐牧地起隴右、金城、平涼、天水，東至樓煩，外暨河曲，內則涇、寧、豳、岐，坊監錯置，牧養有法，而牧地則堇千二百三十頃耳。今邠、涇、寧州與汧、渭之境，卽其故地，而閑田不耕者何止一千二百三十也？況洪、永閒所定草塲，自東勝至河西，抵古北口，蓋幾十萬里，其饒水草、便牧馬者，又不啻如唐人而已。是故擇地以立監牧，設法以爲倸散，如丘文莊之議可行也。國初諸番納馬，以茶酬之。今番馬猶故，而聖天子威德遠被，卽俺酋桀黠，亦歲貢名馬唯謹，斯固千載一時也已。但金牌之制未復，而商茶所易，安得霜蹏？宣、大、延綏歲有互
translation_en:
…Those transferred to these posts consider themselves relegated to idle positions, and others who look upon them likewise regard the posts as idle and slight them. Even though injunctions and reprimands are issued again and again, in the end there is no one who changes his view or alters his hearing [? 歐觀易聽, for 改觀易聽]; for this reason, feelings of resentment arise and private pocketing and embezzlement spring up. Therefore, matching the Pasturage Seals and Branch Courts of the Imperial Stud with the weight of the Capital Courts, and filling the posts of Directors and Chiefs through the routes of examination graduates and tribute students, as proposed by Yang Wenxiang (Yang Yiqing 楊一清), is feasible.

In the Tang dynasty, pasturelands stretched from Longyou, Jincheng, Pingliang, and Tianshui eastward to Loufan, reaching Hequ on the outside and Jing, Ning, Bin, and Qi on the inside. Stables and Directorates were interspersed, and grazing and rearing had set methods, yet the pasturelands amounted to barely 1,230 qing. Today, Bin, Jing, and Ning Prefectures, along with the regions of the Qian and Wei Rivers, are those very former lands, and how could the uncultivated idle fields there be merely 1,230 qing? Moreover, the grazing grounds established during the Hongwu (1368–1398) and Yongle (1403–1424) eras, stretching from Dongsheng to Hexi and reaching Gubeikou, cover nearly a hundred thousand li; those areas rich in water and grass and convenient for pasturing horses far surpass what the people of the Tang had. Therefore, selecting land to establish herds and directorates, and devising methods to manage their gathering and dispersal [? 倸散, for 聚散], as proposed by Qiu Wenzhuang (Qiu Jun 丘濬), is feasible.

At the beginning of our dynasty, the various Tibetan tribes presented horses and were compensated with tea. Today, the Tibetan horses remain as before, and the august Son of Heaven's majesty and virtue extend far—even so unruly and crafty a chieftain as Anda (Altan Khan) reverently presents famed horses in annual tribute. This is truly an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. However, the system of gold tallies has not been restored, and in what is traded for merchant tea, how can one obtain "frost-hoofed" steeds? In Xuanfu, Datong, and Yansui, there are annual mutual…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
市然我以緞繒給之彼以玄黄償之足甫
出邊而已不諳水草待斃矣欲以養之監
苑而試之於行陳十而二三耳是故增馬
直以啖羣胡捐微利以收奇駿如李文正
之議可行也乃其法之在西土者則又有
可言焉諸臣所論疏
上業已下有司議矣今欲減銀以寛之則軍餉
何可缺欲增地以充之則銀額何可更法
之弊也亡已時已計莫若倣
===
國初之制而酌時宜行之屬公平通變之人
修丈勘均齊之法某也督亢獲可畝一鍾
某也磽确十不二三息者夫然後簡牧軍
而以馬給之每地三頃令養馬一匹而又
爲肥瘠搭配之法專令餧養諸以他故差
者悉已之其以餘地徵銀者量減十七載
之籍略如民屯故事兩限完徵以給軍餉
斯地有餘利民有餘力牧不稱苦馬不稱
乏上可以復
punctuated: 市，然我以緞繒給之，彼以玄黄償之，足甫出邊，而已不諳水草、待斃矣。欲以養之監苑，而試之於行陳，十而二三耳。是故增馬直以啖羣胡，捐微利以收奇駿，如李文正之議，可行也。乃其法之在西土者，則又有可言焉。諸臣所論疏，上業已下有司議矣。今欲減銀以寛之，則軍餉何可缺？欲增地以充之，則銀額何可更？法之弊也，亡已時已。計莫若倣國初之制，而酌時宜行之。屬公平通變之人，修丈勘均齊之法：某也督亢，獲可畝一鍾；某也磽确，十不二三息者。夫然後簡牧軍而以馬給之，每地三頃，令養馬一匹，而又爲肥瘠搭配之法，專令餧養，諸以他故差者悉已之。其以餘地徵銀者，量減十七載之籍，略如民屯故事，兩限完徵，以給軍餉。斯地有餘利，民有餘力，牧不稱苦，馬不稱乏，上可以復
translation_en:
…markets; yet while we supply them with satins and silks, they repay us with sickly and exhausted horses. Their hooves have barely crossed the frontier before they are already unaccustomed to the water and grass and awaiting death. If we wish to raise them in the Directorate Pastures and test them in battle formations, only two or three out of ten survive. Therefore, increasing the price paid for horses to entice the various northern tribes and relinquishing petty profits in order to acquire extraordinary steeds, as proposed by Li Wenzheng 李文正 (Li Dongyang 李東陽), is feasible.

As for the regulations in the western regions, there is also something that can be said. The memorials discussed by various officials have already been sent down by His Majesty to the competent authorities for deliberation. Now, if we wish to reduce the silver commutations to grant them relief, how can military rations be left short? If we wish to increase the land allotments to replenish them, how can the fixed silver quotas be altered? The abuses of the system will never come to an end. The best plan is to model ourselves upon the system of the beginning of the dynasty and implement it according to the suitability of the times. We should entrust fair-minded and adaptable men to institute methods for surveying, inspecting, and equalizing the land: determining which lands are fertile like Dukang 督亢, capable of yielding one zhong per mu, and which are stony and barren, yielding scarcely two or three parts in ten. Only then should we select the pasturage soldiers and issue horses to them, ordering one horse to be raised for every three qing of land, while also establishing a method for pairing fertile and barren lands. They should be exclusively assigned to feeding and rearing the horses, and all requisitions for other corvée duties should be completely abolished. As for the surplus land on which silver is levied, the assessments registered over the past十七 [seventeen / Jiazhi-Longqing?] years should be appropriately reduced, roughly following the precedent of civilian military-agricultural colonies (mintun), with collections completed in two installments to supply military rations. Thus the land will yield surplus profit, the people will have surplus strength, the herdsmen will not complain of hardship, and the horses will not be in short supply. Above, we can restore…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
馬乎賢百執事交警于下忠敬所孚無勛
不樹而況一牧事乎生固知天下之馬無
不盛天下之馬政無不舉而不獨陜以西
也
第五問
南企仲
同考試官教諭薛　批〔備陳虜酋情態洞然目中而長慮卻顧訏謨遠略令讀者惕然有省〕
〔持此以往將百不失一矣蓋不徒文字古也〕
考試官教諭王　批〔究極虜情言言非故爲虛詞不能〕
〔有此卽老將不如也錄之〕
考試官學正任　批〔忠懇之情激發之氣具見乎詞〕
〔于以書生而富甲兵者乎〕
===
今之計者曰俺酋耄年好佛率所部十萬
衆而久牧河外張掖酒泉之間欲佛之福
利而私其身耳非有他也不然則瓦剌之
種彼所深讎三以其衆覆之而無一矢之
利彼所欲甘心而一當焉者蓋鑒往時輕
punctuated:
馬乎？賢百執事交警于下，忠敬所孚，無勛不樹，而況一牧事乎？生固知天下之馬無不盛，天下之馬政無不舉，而不獨陜以西也。
第五問
南企仲
同考試官教諭薛　批〔備陳虜酋情態，洞然目中，而長慮卻顧，訏謨遠略，令讀者惕然有省。〕〔持此以往，將百不失一矣，蓋不徒文字古也。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔究極虜情，言言非故，爲虛詞不能〕〔有此，卽老將不如也，錄之。〕
考試官學正任　批〔忠懇之情，激發之氣，具見乎詞，〕〔于以書生而富甲兵者乎！〕
今之計者曰：「俺酋耄年好佛，率所部十萬衆，而久牧河外張掖、酒泉之間，欲佛之福利而私其身耳，非有他也。不然，則瓦剌之種，彼所深讎，三以其衆覆之而無一矢之利，彼所欲甘心而一當焉者，蓋鑒往時輕
translation_en:
… horses alone? When worthy officials in all their various duties mutually admonish one another below, and loyalty and reverence inspire trust, there is no merit that cannot be established—how much more so the single matter of horse pasturage! This student therefore knows for certain that horses throughout the realm will all flourish, and horse administration throughout the realm will be fully upheld, not merely in the region west of Shaan!

Fifth Policy Question

Nan Qizhong 南企仲

Associate Examiner, Instructor Xue, comments: "He sets forth the conditions and dispositions of the caitiff chieftain in full detail, making them clearly visible before one's eyes; meanwhile, his far-reaching foresight and grand, distant strategy cause the reader to reflect with vigilant awareness. If one holds to these principles in going forward, there will not be a single misstep in a hundred; indeed, its merit lies not merely in the antiquity of its prose."

Examiner, Instructor Wang, comments: "He thoroughly investigates the caitiffs' situation; every word is grounded in substance, something empty rhetoric could never achieve. Even a veteran general could not surpass this. Selected for inclusion."

Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Ren, comments: "Loyal, earnest sentiment and roused, spirited vigor are both fully manifest in his words. Is he not a scholar whose mind is richly stocked with armor and weaponry?"

Those who devise plans today say: "In his advanced old age, the chieftain Altan Khan (An qiu 俺酋) has grown fond of Buddhism. He leads his horde of a hundred thousand men and has long pastured them beyond the Yellow River between Zhangye 張掖 and Jiuquan 酒泉 simply because he desires the blessings and benefits of the Buddha for his own person, and for no other reason. Otherwise, it is because the Oirat (Wala 瓦剌) tribes are his deep enemies; three times they ambushed him with their forces so that he gained not the advantage of a single arrow, and he longs to have his revenge and meet them once more in battle. Thus, taking warning from the mistake of his past rash…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
舉之誤而傾其巢穴移駐近境以示先聲
然後伺其便以曳落何嘗之耳所謂夷狄
相攻中國之利幸彼之愚不知自解耳亦
非有他也不然則
貢市之利已七八年憑藉寵靈而威行塞外
彼豈匪茹而不以爲中國之患且彼之所
好者佛而中國爲之通其意彼之所希者
賞而中國爲之順其情是我有大造於彼
也虜雖獰獷豈不知中國之犬雖不屑屑
===
夷狄之治而紀綱法度可恃以維城者猶
足爲萬年之固而敢無故自敗其約以僥
倖萬不可必之擄掠而啓我疆場之謀以
爲彼肘腋之患哉必不然矣然明計者不
以淺深而逃其情彼既以禮佛而來則當
以禮佛而去佛既禮矣東西南北自在也
即中國一家未有不盡野分州者如以爲
辭不能號之而遽去胡能號之而畢來乎
况互市之地益增屬番之挾益甚茶馬之
punctuated: 舉之誤，而傾其巢穴，移駐近境以示先聲，然後伺其便以曳落何嘗之耳。所謂夷狄相攻，中國之利，幸彼之愚，不知自解耳，亦非有他也。不然，則貢市之利已七八年，憑藉寵靈而威行塞外，彼豈匪茹，而不以爲中國之患？且彼之所好者佛，而中國爲之通其意；彼之所希者賞，而中國爲之順其情，是我有大造於彼也。虜雖獰獷，豈不知中國之犬，雖不屑屑夷狄之治，而紀綱法度可恃以維城者，猶足爲萬年之固，而敢無故自敗其約，以僥倖萬不可必之擄掠，而啓我疆場之謀，以爲彼肘腋之患哉？必不然矣。然明計者不以淺深而逃其情。彼既以禮佛而來，則當以禮佛而去。佛既禮矣，東西南北自在也，即中國一家，未有不盡野分州者，如以爲辭不能號之而遽去，胡能號之而畢來乎？况互市之地益增，屬番之挾益甚，茶馬之
translation_en:
…the mistake of their previous rash actions, and so they have emptied out their lairs and moved to camp near the border in order to project advance momentum, after which they will wait for an opportunity to test the waters at Yeluogai [transcription reads 曳落何, for 拽落該]. As the saying goes, when barbarians attack one another, it is to China's advantage; we are fortunate in their folly that they do not know how to resolve their own feuds, and there is nothing else to it. Otherwise, consider that the benefits of tribute and border markets have lasted for seven or eight years now; relying on imperial favor and prestige, their authority holds sway beyond the passes—how could they fail to weigh matters carefully and instead make themselves a menace to China? Moreover, what he delights in is the Buddha, and China facilitates his wishes in this; what he hopes for is rewards, and China accommodates his desires. Thus we have conferred great grace upon him. Though the caitiffs are fierce and unruly, how could they not know the greatness [transcription reads 犬 for 大] of China? Even if we do not trouble ourselves overmuch with governing the barbarians, the institutions, discipline, and laws on which we rely as our defensive bulwark are still sufficient to provide ten thousand years of security. Would they dare, without cause, break the treaty themselves to gamble on plundering that is by no means guaranteed to succeed, thereby provoking military countermeasures on our frontiers that would become a threat right at their own flank? Surely not!

Yet those who calculate clearly do not let the enemy's true condition escape them on account of whether appearances are superficial or deep. Since he came in the name of worshiping the Buddha, he ought to depart once he has worshiped the Buddha. Now that the Buddha has been worshiped, he is free to go east, west, south, or north; even within China as a single family, there is no place that is not divided into bounded territories and provinces. If he makes the excuse that he cannot issue the command to make his followers depart at once, how then was he able to issue the command to make them all come here together? Furthermore, the sites for mutual trade are increasingly multiplied, their coercion of the tributary Tibetan tribes grows ever more severe, and their demands in the tea-and-horse trade…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
請益驕凡此皆覬覦之萌或者有中行說
之徒爲之煽誘又或有如喜寧之屬爲之
蠱惑皆未可知也故天下有外癡而中黠
者其情不可不察也遠料者不以强弱而
爽其勢自古鄰國之交猶有假道之禮借
云彼之有事於瓦剌也何不以情輸我而
先爲乞哀乃遽載其穹廬驅其羊馬使投
鞭之衆絡繹於國門之外比之蜂屯蟻聚
我見其不足與校而彼以爲不敢誰何能
必彼之慊然而內懼曰中國一旦逐我我
且爲窮寇乎此其勢不可不慮也蓋嘗讀
匈奴傳而知彼之爲中國患自周以來即
未有得上策者我
===
太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元
成祖文皇帝三犁虜庭然倏順倏叛奄入奄遯
情態萬狀未嘗帖然傾心也我
穆宗莊皇帝以天覆地載之恩爲
宗社無疆之計遂使俛首稱藩誓堅
punctuated: 請益驕。凡此皆覬覦之萌，或者有中行說之徒爲之煽誘，又或有如喜寧之屬爲之蠱惑，皆未可知也。故天下有外癡而中黠者，其情不可不察也。遠料者不以强弱而爽其勢。自古鄰國之交，猶有假道之禮。借云彼之有事於瓦剌也，何不以情輸我而先爲乞哀，乃遽載其穹廬、驅其羊馬，使投鞭之衆絡繹於國門之外，比之蜂屯蟻聚。我見其不足與校，而彼以爲不敢誰何。能必彼之慊然而內懼，曰「中國一旦逐我，我且爲窮寇」乎？此其勢不可不慮也。蓋嘗讀《匈奴傳》，而知彼之爲中國患，自周以來即未有得上策者。我太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元，成祖文皇帝三犁虜庭；然倏順倏叛，奄入奄遯，情態萬狀，未嘗帖然傾心也。我穆宗莊皇帝以天覆地載之恩，爲宗社無疆之計，遂使俛首稱藩，誓堅
translation_en: … requests have grown ever more arrogant. All of these are the nascent sprouts of covetous ambition. Perhaps there are people like Zhonghang Yue 中行說 instigating and enticing them, or perhaps there are those of the ilk of Xi Ning 喜寧 bewitching and deluding them—all of this is impossible to know. Therefore, in the world there are those who appear foolish on the outside yet are cunning within; their true dispositions must be examined. Those who plan with far-sightedness do not misjudge the strategic situation on the basis of strength or weakness. Since antiquity, in relations between neighboring states there has still been the ritual of requesting right of passage. Even supposing, as is claimed, that they have military business with the Oirats (Wala 瓦剌), why did they not first report their true circumstances to us and beg for sympathy, instead of suddenly loading up their felt tents and driving along their sheep and horses, causing a multitude numerous enough to dam a river with their whips to stream continuously outside the gates of our state, massing like swarming bees and gathering ants? We view them as not worth reckoning with, yet they take it to mean that we dare not challenge them at all. Can we be certain that they feel dissatisfied with themselves and inwardly fearful, saying, "Once China expels us, we shall become desperate bandits"? This strategic situation is one that must be viewed with concern. Indeed, I have read the "Account of the Xiongnu" (Xiongnu zhuan 匈奴傳) and know that in the menace they have posed to China, since the Zhou dynasty there has never been anyone who attained the supreme strategy. Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi 太祖高皇帝), swept away the barbarian Yuan, and the Accomplished Progenitor, Emperor Wen (Chengzu Wenhuangdi 成祖文皇帝), thrice plowed up the caitiffs' court; yet one moment they submitted and the next they rebelled, suddenly invading and suddenly fleeing, their dispositions and antics taking a myriad forms, never once docilely turning their hearts to us in allegiance. Our Emperor Muzong Zhuang (Muzong Zhuanghuangdi 穆宗莊皇帝), with grace that covers like Heaven and supports like Earth, formed a boundless plan for the ancestral temples and altars of state, thereby causing them to bow their heads, declare themselves vassals, and swear to firmly maintain …

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
貢市
皇上內順治而外威嚴修
二祖之政而揚
穆考之烈所以赤子視之而不以塞垣限之者
誠以守在四夷而兩階自舞且謂彼之未
敢生心也然
廟筭不可深測而封疆之臣念在多壘者亦惟
示三可疑以使之必去講三可恃以待其
不去而已何以故諸番之曲意於彼而爲
===
之鄉導非無飲恨之情也積威所刼欲郄
而不能且無以爲歸耳今竭力事之且踰
年矣能無怨望之意乎聞古人有能使回
紇反攻吐蕃者因而撫之結之又爲之詷
其隙而諜以間之若欲相糾而判虜者然
虜能無疑乎虜衆離其巢穴已經寒暑射
獵少獲且其習俗惡疲而畏痘獨不可以
人力爲之乎聞昔人有毒涇上流者因而
倣之或於餱糧或於水草善藏其用而不
punctuated: 貢市。皇上內順治而外威嚴，修二祖之政而揚穆考之烈，所以赤子視之而不以塞垣限之者，誠以守在四夷而兩階自舞，且謂彼之未敢生心也。然廟筭不可深測，而封疆之臣念在多壘者，亦惟示三可疑以使之必去，講三可恃以待其不去而已。何以故？諸番之曲意於彼而爲之鄉導，非無飲恨之情也，積威所刼，欲郄而不能，且無以爲歸耳。今竭力事之，且踰年矣，能無怨望之意乎？聞古人有能使回紇反攻吐蕃者，因而撫之結之，又爲之詷其隙而諜以間之，若欲相糾而判虜者然，虜能無疑乎？虜衆離其巢穴，已經寒暑，射獵少獲，且其習俗惡疲而畏痘，獨不可以人力爲之乎？聞昔人有毒涇上流者，因而倣之，或於餱糧，或於水草，善藏其用而不
translation_en: …tribute and frontier markets. His Majesty maintains harmonious order within and stern majesty without, cultivating the governance of the Two Ancestors (Taizu and Chengzu) and exalting the illustrious achievements of his Imperial Father Muzong. The reason he views them as infants and does not bar them with the frontier walls is truly because when defense lies among the four barbarian tribes, ritual dances naturally take place between the two staircases of the court, and furthermore because it is thought that they do not yet dare to harbor treacherous intentions. Yet the strategic calculations of the imperial court cannot be fathomed deeply, and as for the frontier officials whose minds are occupied by the many fortifications, they should simply display three causes for suspicion to compel them to depart, and cultivate three things to rely upon in preparation for their not departing—that is all. For what reason? That the various Tibetan tribes bend their wills to them and act as their guides does not mean they are without swallowed resentment; coerced by accumulated menace, they wish to withdraw [?] but cannot, and moreover have nowhere to turn for allegiance. Now they have exhausted their strength in serving them for over a year—how could they be without feelings of grievance and resentment? We hear that among the ancients there was one (Guo Ziyi 郭子儀) who was able to cause the Uyghurs to turn and attack the Tibetans; if we accordingly pacify them and form ties with them, and furthermore spy out their rifts for them and use espionage to drive a wedge between them, making it appear as though they wish to band together and rebel against the caitiffs, how could the caitiffs not be suspicious? Since the caitiff hordes left their lairs, they have already passed through winter and summer; their hunting yields little catch, and moreover by custom they hate exhaustion and fear smallpox—could this alone not be brought about by human effort? We hear that among men of the past there were those who poisoned the upper reaches of the Jing River; if we accordingly imitate this, whether in dry provisions or in water and pasture, skillfully concealing its application without…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
乎然後威福在已緩急隨宜虜之有名號
能統領者或隆殺之異禮或喜怒之異情
而又愼烽火以節其勞嚴操練以精其技
厚恩信以得其死簡文法以盡其才使兵
識將意將識士情撫臣密之於內而無所
撓鎭臣諭之於外而無所拂務若身使臂
臂使指而元氣爲之常運焉此其威不可
恃乎由是而有喜寧中行說其人者可以
他事按矣雖然無慮焉昔武帝之登單于
===
臺也使使告匈奴曰單于能戰天子自將
待邊而匈奴爲之遠遁其臣之使於匈奴
者怵以頭懸北闕屠爲九郡數語匈奴即
不敢動蓋兵貴先聲而北虜又故可恐喝
走者今遼東大創露布屢宣此虜聞之其
亦有嚴心而魄之褫也久矣況鎖鑰之嚴
者不言而信爪牙之奮者不怒而威則
聖天子之所誕敷眞有出於借箸之外者愚生
何足以知之
punctuated: 乎？然後威福在已，緩急隨宜。虜之有名號能統領者，或隆殺之異禮，或喜怒之異情。而又愼烽火以節其勞，嚴操練以精其技，厚恩信以得其死，簡文法以盡其才。使兵識將意，將識士情；撫臣密之於內而無所撓，鎭臣諭之於外而無所拂。務若身使臂、臂使指，而元氣爲之常運焉，此其威不可恃乎？由是而有喜寧、中行說其人者，可以他事按矣。雖然，無慮焉。昔武帝之登單于臺也，使使告匈奴曰：「單于能戰，天子自將待邊。」而匈奴爲之遠遁。其臣之使於匈奴者，怵以「頭懸北闕，屠爲九郡」數語，匈奴即不敢動。蓋兵貴先聲，而北虜又故可恐喝走者。今遼東大創，露布屢宣，此虜聞之，其亦有嚴心而魄之褫也久矣。況鎖鑰之嚴者不言而信，爪牙之奮者不怒而威，則聖天子之所誕敷，眞有出於借箸之外者，愚生何足以知之！
translation_en:
… Only then will the power to awe and to reward rest with us, and we may act with urgency or leniency as fits the occasion. Toward those among the caitiffs who hold notable titles and are capable of commanding others, we may show differing degrees of ceremony, now elevated and now diminished, or display differing moods of pleasure and anger. Moreover, we must be cautious with the beacon fires so as to spare our troops unnecessary toil, strict in military drills so as to perfect their skills, generous in grace and good faith so as to win their willingness to die, and concise in legalistic regulations so as to allow them to exhaust their talents. Cause the soldiers to know the intentions of their generals, and the generals to know the sentiments of their men; let the Grand Coordinators plan secretly within without obstruction, and the Regional Commanders issue instructions without defiance on the frontier. Ensure that it operates just as the body moves the arm and the arm moves the fingers, with the vital vigor circulating constantly throughout—could such majesty as this not be relied upon?

From this position, should there be men like Xi Ning 喜寧 or Zhonghang Yue 中行說, they can be investigated and dealt with on other pretexts. Even so, there is no cause for anxiety. In former times, when Emperor Wu [of Han] ascended the Chanyu Terrace (Chanyu tai 單于臺), he sent an envoy to tell the Xiongnu: "If the Chanyu is able to fight, the Son of Heaven is personally leading his forces and waiting at the frontier"—whereupon the Xiongnu fled far away. And when his minister went as an envoy to the Xiongnu and intimidated them with a few words about having their heads hung at the Northern Watchtower and their lands carved up into nine commanderies, the Xiongnu immediately dared not make a move. For in warfare, preemptive reputation is prized, and the northern caitiffs are by nature susceptible to being frightened off by threats. Now that we have inflicted great defeats upon them in Liaodong and repeatedly proclaimed unsealed dispatches of victory, when these caitiffs hear of it, they too must long since have felt dread in their hearts and had their spirits stripped away. How much more so when those who guard the strategic passes with strictness command trust without speaking, and those who rouse themselves as the throne's claws and teeth inspire awe without rage! Thus that which the Sacred Son of Heaven broadly spreads forth truly surpasses anything that could be devised by borrowing chopsticks to plan for him—how could this foolish student be worthy of knowing it!

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
流風遺俗直道而行亦崇尚
之不可誣也故比屋而考德
道有夷隆要之歸於淳也執
簡而譚藝學有麤密要之歸
於質也蓋〔居仁〕既應聘而來
以快覩其地遂得縱觀諸士
之文旣又接所拔之儁乂乃
===
竊自幸曰美哉秦之產也瑞
世之人文其在玆乎其在玆
乎夫川谷異齊民生其間異
俗士之所習尚不可强而同
也彼括聚片言湊泊爛錦非
不觀美苟竅言無當錄用謂
何今觀諸士所爲文本之乎
punctuated: 流風遺俗，直道而行，亦崇尚之不可誣也。故比屋而考德，道有夷隆，要之歸於淳也；執簡而譚藝，學有麤密，要之歸於質也。蓋〔居仁〕既應聘而來，以快覩其地，遂得縱觀諸士之文，旣又接所拔之儁乂，乃竊自幸曰：「美哉！秦之產也，瑞世之人文其在玆乎！其在玆乎！」夫川谷異齊，民生其間異俗，士之所習尚，不可强而同也。彼括聚片言，湊泊爛錦，非不觀美，苟竅言無當，錄用謂何？今觀諸士所爲文，本之乎
translation_en: …inherited customs and surviving traditions, walking the straight path; this too shows that what is esteemed cannot be falsified. Therefore, when one examines virtue from household to household, although the Way has its times of decline and flourishing, in essence it comes back to unadulterated simplicity; when one holds up the writing slips to discuss literary arts, although learning varies in coarseness and refinement, in essence it comes back to unadorned substance. Now, after I, Juren, accepted the invitation to come here and had the pleasure of beholding this land, I was then able to survey freely the writings of the various scholars, and subsequently to meet the outstanding talents who had been selected. Thereupon I privately rejoiced to myself, saying: "Splendid indeed are the products of Qin! Does not the cultural flowering that serves as an auspicious omen for the age lie right here? Does it not lie right here?" Now, rivers and valleys differ in their configurations, and the people born among them differ in their customs; what scholars practice and esteem cannot be forced into uniformity. As for those who gather up fragmentary phrases and piece together dazzling brocades, it is not that they are unpleasant to look at, yet if their hollow words lack substance, what would be the point of selecting and employing them? Now, observing the compositions written by these scholars, they root them in…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天眞出之以獨見洪纖意鑄
好醜性形故觀其文如見其
貌偉而偉妍而妍無秋毫爽
也我
皇上稽古右文作新士類頃者納
言官之請布功令釐文體曾
未踰年而秦人士所爲文輒
已根極理要而歸之於純正
亦本其所賦之淳而所習以
===
質勝故變而之道有易易者
觀所爲文而其所効用可諒
也顧諸士所執以進者藝也
素所服習也今羅而貢之南
宮行且爲
punctuated: 天眞，出之以獨見，洪纖意鑄，好醜性形；故觀其文如見其貌，偉而偉，妍而妍，無秋毫爽也。我皇上稽古右文，作新士類，頃者納言官之請，布功令，釐文體。曾未踰年，而秦人士所爲文，輒已根極理要而歸之於純正，亦本其所賦之淳而所習以質勝，故變而之道有易易者。觀所爲文，而其所効用可諒也。顧諸士所執以進者，藝也，素所服習也。今羅而貢之南宮，行且爲
translation_en: …natural genuineness and bring them forth from independent insight; large and small are cast by their own thought, fair and foul take shape from their own nature. Thus, reading their writings is like seeing their countenances: what is grand appears grand, what is graceful appears graceful, without a hair's breadth of discrepancy. Our Emperor examines antiquity and esteems civil culture, renewing the body of scholars. Recently, accepting the request of speaking officials, he promulgated examination regulations to rectify literary style. Scarcely a year has passed, and the writings produced by the scholars of Qin [Shaanxi] are already thoroughly rooted in essential principles and have returned to purity and correctness. This too stems from the simplicity of their natural endowment and the fact that in their habits substance prevails; therefore, changing and coming to the Way came most easily to them. By observing the writings they have produced, the service they will render can be trusted. Yet what the gentlemen hold to advance themselves is literary craft, which they have long practiced and mastered. Now they have been gathered and presented as tribute to the Southern Palace [Ministry of Rites], and soon they will be…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
一人用矣効用將何以哉秦中之
往哲鏗鍧炳耀以樹勳于前
而垂光于後者〔居仁〕不遑縷
陳近世涵濡聖真篤行古道
動以賢聖爲期則有若呂文
簡竭忠殫猷勒功鼎彝則有
若王端毅抗節不撓奮爭國
===
是則富平于今稱之矣是皆
秉誠矣公以淳朴質直之心
出其身爲天下用故以表士
類則道德稱高以弘建樹則
勳庸耀世以出議論則聳聞
振聽故海内望其人如麟如
鳳目爲世之所罕覯也諸士
punctuated: 一人用矣，効用將何以哉？秦中之往哲，鏗鍧炳耀，以樹勳于前而垂光于後者，〔居仁〕不遑縷陳。近世涵濡聖真，篤行古道，動以賢聖爲期，則有若呂文簡；竭忠殫猷，勒功鼎彝，則有若王端毅；抗節不撓，奮爭國是，則富平于今稱之矣。是皆秉誠矣公，以淳朴質直之心，出其身爲天下用。故以表士類則道德稱高，以弘建樹則勳庸耀世，以出議論則聳聞振聽。故海内望其人如麟如鳳，目爲世之所罕覯也。諸士
translation_en: …employed by the Sovereign himself! By what means, then, will they render service? As for the past worthies of Shaanxi (Qinzhong 秦中) whose resounding and brilliant achievements established merit in former times and left a lasting radiance to posterity, I, [Ju Ren 居仁], have no leisure to recount them in detail. In recent ages, for immersing oneself in sagely truth, earnestly practicing the ancient Way, and taking the worthies and sages as one's standard in every action, there was someone like Lü Wenjian 呂文簡 [Lü Nan 呂柟]; for exhausting loyalty and plans and having one's merits inscribed on ritual bronzes, there was someone like Wang Duanyi 王端毅 [Wang Shu 王恕]; and for upholding integrity without bending and boldly contending over the policies of the state, the gentleman of Fuping 富平 [Yang Jue 楊爵] is praised to this day. All of these men held fast to sincerity and public-mindedness [reading 矣公 as 秉公?], and with pure, simple, and upright hearts came forth in person to be of service to the empire. Thus, when they stood as models for the literati, their moral virtue was acclaimed as lofty; when they expanded their achievements, their meritorious service illuminated the age; and when they put forth their arguments and counsel, they stirred and awakened all who heard them. Therefore, people within the seas looked up to such men as unicorns (lin 麟) and phoenixes (feng 鳳), regarding them as rarities seldom seen in the world. Now the scholars…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
且出而服官政矣職任雖殊
要皆三君子所嘗有事也諸
士自視其身與三君子所執
持何如夫因阜爲高則崇基
立就執柯施伐則取法不遠
近取諸身旣稟賦若此遠稽
諸人又芳躅若彼故諸士之
===
儀刑非不足也亦惟執淳質
之心以往而罔弗濟矣今譚
者謂補偏救弊莫若稍減其
文而秦人士之自爲尚則莫
若獨守其質乃或自厭其淳
質之不文直欲從事于靡文
縟節謂足以諧衆情而宜流
punctuated: 且出而服官政矣，職任雖殊，要皆三君子所嘗有事也。諸士自視其身，與三君子所執持何如？夫因阜爲高，則崇基立就；執柯施伐，則取法不遠。近取諸身，旣稟賦若此；遠稽諸人，又芳躅若彼。故諸士之儀刑非不足也，亦惟執淳質之心以往，而罔弗濟矣。今譚者謂補偏救弊，莫若稍減其文；而秦人士之自爲尚，則莫若獨守其質。乃或自厭其淳質之不文，直欲從事于靡文縟節，謂足以諧衆情而宜流
translation_en: …are about to go forth and take up the duties of official governance. Although your offices and responsibilities will differ, in essence they are all matters in which those three gentlemen once engaged. When you scholars examine yourselves, how do you compare with what those three gentlemen upheld? Indeed, if one builds height upon an existing mound, a lofty foundation is immediately achieved; if one holds an axe-handle while hewing another, the model is not far to seek. Drawing near from your own persons, your natural endowments are already like this; examining afar in others, their fragrant footsteps are furthermore like that. Therefore, models for you scholars to emulate are by no means lacking; you need only hold fast to a simple, unadorned heart as you go forward, and there is nothing you will not accomplish. Today, commentators say that to rectify imbalances and remedy abuses, nothing is better than slightly reducing cultural refinement; and as for what the scholars and people of Qin should prize in themselves, nothing is better than steadfastly preserving their unadorned substance. Yet some, disdaining their own simple substance as lacking in refinement, wish instead to devote themselves to extravagant ornament and elaborate ceremonial, thinking this sufficient to harmonize with popular sentiment and suit the current…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
俗也則棄其所不當無而慕
其所不必有譬則售珠而還
櫝其毋乃不善變乎守其常
則兩得之渝所守則兩失之
故習不可不慎也若曰先進
彬彬斯稱全德篤實而輝光
弸中而彪外此固諸士之自
===
待而亦主司之所望也且發
跡岐周流聲宇宙內爲政于
國而外宣布於諸侯協心夾
輔佐成周泰和之治玆又非
秦產哉卽諸士不敢侈言自
負望前茅以爲依歸亦非異
人任矣尚懋勉乎主司者更
punctuated: 俗也，則棄其所不當無，而慕其所不必有。譬則售珠而還櫝，其毋乃不善變乎？守其常則兩得之，渝所守則兩失之，故習不可不慎也。若曰：「先進彬彬，斯稱全德；篤實而輝光，弸中而彪外。」此固諸士之自待，而亦主司之所望也。且發跡岐周，流聲宇宙，內爲政于國，而外宣布於諸侯，協心夾輔，佐成周泰和之治，玆又非秦產哉？卽諸士不敢侈言自負，望前茅以爲依歸，亦非異人任矣。尚懋勉乎！主司者更
translation_en: …customs, then they cast aside what they ought not to lack and yearn for what they do not need to possess. This is like selling the casket and returning the pearl—is that not a poor way to change? By holding to their constant nature, they attain both [substance and refinement]; by abandoning what they hold to, they lose both. Therefore, one cannot be too cautious about habits and customs. As for saying that the men of former times were well-balanced in substance and refinement and thus稱 praised for complete virtue—steadfast and sincere yet shining with brilliance, filled within and patterned without—this is indeed what you scholars expect of yourselves, and it is also what the examiners hope for. Moreover, those who rose to prominence in Qizhou, whose renown spread throughout the universe, who administered the government within the state and proclaimed its virtue abroad to the feudal lords, uniting their hearts to assist and support the ruler in achieving the supreme harmony of the Zhou dynasty—were they not also natives of Qin? Even if you scholars dare not speak extravagantly in self-conceit, looking to those vanguard exemplars as models to follow is surely not a responsibility to be left to others. Strive diligently! The examiners even…

title: 萬曆七年陝西鄉試錄
text:
有厚望矣
直隸大名府滑縣儒學教諭
王〔岢〕居仁謹序
punctuated:
有厚望矣。
直隸大名府滑縣儒學教諭王〔岢〕居仁謹序。
translation_en:
…have even higher hopes.

Respectfully written as a postface by Wang [Ke] Juren 王〔岢〕居仁, Instructor of the Confucian School of Hua County, Daming Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili).
